#### The ℓ-adic tame character t_ℓ : I_K → Z_ℓ(1)

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/ell-adic-tame-character`. Kind: construction. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.GaloisRep` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/TameCharacter`). Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2`.

Let K be a nonarchimedean local field with residue field of characteristic p and cardinality q, and ℓ ≠ p a prime. Let θ : I_K/P_K ≅ Ẑ^{(p')}(1) = lim_{p ∤ m} μ_m(K̄) be the tame character of LocalFieldsRamification layer 4 and Z_ℓ(1) = lim_n μ_{ℓ^n}(K̄) (R01.1/tate-twist). Define t_ℓ : I_K → Z_ℓ(1) as θ composed with the projection to the ℓ-component; explicitly t_ℓ(σ) = (σ(π^{1/ℓ^n})/π^{1/ℓ^n})_n for a uniformiser π and a compatible system of roots. Then: (i) t_ℓ is a continuous surjective homomorphism, independent of π and the roots, trivial on P_K; (ii) Kummer reductions: t_ℓ mod ℓ^n is σ ↦ σ(π^{1/ℓ^n})/π^{1/ℓ^n} ∈ μ_{ℓ^n}; (iii) equivariance: t_ℓ(wσw^{-1}) = χ_ℓ(w)·t_ℓ(σ) for w ∈ G_K, σ ∈ I_K; for w ∈ W_K this is q^{weilDegree(w)}·t_ℓ(σ); (iv) every continuous homomorphism from I_K (or from an open subgroup J of I_K) to a pro-ℓ group factors through t_ℓ (through t_ℓ|_J); in particular I_K has exactly one quotient of order ℓ, namely t_ℓ mod ℓ : I_K ↠ μ_ℓ; (v) for L/K finite with ramification index e, t_{ℓ,K}|_{I_L} = e·t_{ℓ,L}; (vi) a trivialisation T : Z_ℓ(1) ≅ Z_ℓ (a choice of compatible primitive ℓ^n-th roots of unity) gives T∘t_ℓ : I_K → Z_ℓ, and changing T multiplies it by a unit of Z_ℓ. t_ℓ does not extend to a homomorphism on G_K or W_K (by (iii) such an extension would be invariant under conjugation by Frobenius, which multiplies t_ℓ by q ≠ 1).

**Hypotheses.**

- ℓ ≠ p
- K has finite residue field (a nonarchimedean local field); the construction for henselian traits with other residue fields stays with LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles LPV.0
- t_ℓ is a character of inertia only

**Construction and proof.**

1. (i)–(ii): LocalFieldsRamification layer 4 (the tame character, its independence of choices, its finite-level form) followed by the projection Ẑ^{(p')}(1) → Z_ℓ(1).
2. (iii): the G_K-equivariance statement of layer 4 (conjugation acts through the cyclotomic action), with χ_ℓ from cyclotomic-and-dirichlet-characters; on W_K, χ_ℓ(w) = q^{weilDegree w} because χ_ℓ = λ(q) on G_K.
3. (iv): a pro-ℓ quotient kills the pro-p group P_K and factors through the abelian group I_K/P_K ≅ ∏_{ℓ' ≠ p} Z_{ℓ'}(1), whose maximal pro-ℓ quotient is the ℓ-factor; the order-ℓ quotients correspond to Hom(Z_ℓ(1), Z/ℓ), a line over F_ℓ.
4. (v): with π_K = u·π_L^e, σ ∈ I_L fixes the ℓ^n-th roots of the unit u (they generate an unramified extension), so σ(π_K^{1/ℓ^n})/π_K^{1/ℓ^n} = (σ(π_L^{1/ℓ^n})/π_L^{1/ℓ^n})^e.

**Prerequisites.** `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/LocalFieldsRamification#layer-4-the-tame-quotient-of-the-absolute-galois-group`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/LocalFieldsRamification#layer-3-ramification-the-tame-and-wild-cases-and-the-filtration`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ClassFieldTheory#layer-9-the-local-weil-group`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/tate-twist`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/cyclotomic-and-dirichlet-characters`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/unramified-character-lambda`.

**Uses.**

- ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/grothendieck-quasi-unipotence: ρ(σ) = exp(N·t_ℓ(σ)) on an open subgroup of inertia
- ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/grothendieck-monodromy-and-the-weil-deligne-functor: ρ'(F^nσ) = ρ(F^nσ)exp(−t_ℓ(σ)N)
- LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles:LPV.1/finite-extension-and-logarithm-rescaling: restriction of t_ℓ along a ramified extension multiplies it by e, so N′ = eN
- LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles:LPV.1/twisted-monodromy-equivariance: equivariance of t_ℓ under Frobenius gives NF = qFN
- ClassicalSerreModularity:R33.3/dp-dyadic-transition-and-the-order-three-type: the unique quotient of order 3 of I_2
- Deligne 1973, 2.2.2(b): t_ℓ : I → Z_ℓ(1) is the ℓ-component of the tame character

**API.**

- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.tameCharacter` (constructor): t_ℓ : I_K →ₜ* Z_ℓ(1).
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.tameCharacter_surjective` (characterisation): t_ℓ is surjective and kills P_K.
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.tameCharacter_apply_uniformizer` (simp): t_ℓ(σ) mod ℓ^n = σ(π^{1/ℓ^n})/π^{1/ℓ^n} for any uniformiser π and any root.
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.tameCharacter_conj` (relation): t_ℓ(wσw^{-1}) = χ_ℓ(w)·t_ℓ(σ).
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.tameCharacter_factor_of_proEll` (universal-property): a continuous homomorphism from an open subgroup J ≤ I_K to a pro-ℓ group factors uniquely through t_ℓ|_J.
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.tameCharacter_restrict` (functoriality): t_{ℓ,K}|_{I_L} = e(L/K)·t_{ℓ,L}.
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.tameCharacterTriv` (data): T ∘ t_ℓ : I_K → Z_ℓ for a trivialisation T; tameCharacterTriv_smul for T ↦ aT.
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.tameCharacter_eq_tame` (compatibility): t_ℓ is the ℓ-component of LocalFieldsRamification layer 4's I_K/P_K ≅ Ẑ^{(p')}(1).

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.tameCharacter_mod_ell_Qp` (computation): For K = Q_p, t_ℓ(σ) mod ℓ = σ(p^{1/ℓ})/p^{1/ℓ}.
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.tameCharacter_wild` (degenerate): t_ℓ(σ) = 0 for σ ∈ P_K.
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.tameCharacter_not_extend` (non-example): There is no continuous homomorphism G_K → Z_ℓ(1) restricting to t_ℓ on I_K; a definition of t_ℓ as a character of G_K fails.
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.unique_quotient_order_ell` (characterisation): Every surjection I_K → Z/ℓ is a unit multiple of t_ℓ mod ℓ composed with μ_ℓ ≅ Z/ℓ.
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.tameCharacter_restrict_ramified` (compatibility): For L = K(π^{1/e}) with p ∤ e, t_{ℓ,K}|_{I_L} = e·t_{ℓ,L}.

**Acceptance.**

- For K = Q_p and σ ∈ I with σ(p^{1/ℓ}) = ζ_ℓ p^{1/ℓ}, t_ℓ(σ) ≡ ζ_ℓ in μ_ℓ.
- For K = Q_2 and ℓ = 3, the unique quotient of order 3 of I_2 is t_3 mod 3 : I_2 ↠ μ_3, through which every unipotent action of I_2 on an F_3-vector space factors (ClassicalSerreModularity R33.3 at (q, N) = (3, 2)).

**Sources.**

- deligne73-constantes, 2.2.2(b), Del-22, printed p. 522 (read on the page image): “Pour ℓ ≠ p premier, on note t_ℓ l'application composée t_ℓ : I → Ẑ'(1)(k̄) → Z_ℓ(1)(k̄)” — The ℓ-adic tame character is the ℓ-component of the tame character I → Ẑ'(1) whose kernel is P.
- fsy22, §5.3.1, arXiv v5 p. 54 (text layer): “by Grothendieck’s quasi-unipotency theorem, there exists a unique nilpotent endomorphism N” — FSY's statement of quasi-unipotence used to build the Weil–Deligne representation.

#### Tame inertia, the level of a character, and the fundamental characters of levels one and two

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/tame-inertia-and-fundamental-characters`. Kind: definition. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.GaloisRep` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/FundamentalCharacters`). Planet: **Fundamental characters**. Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2`.

Let K be a nonarchimedean local field with residue field k of characteristic p, I_K ⊃ P_K and I_t = I_K/P_K (LocalFieldsRamification layer 4), k̄ the residue field of K̄. For n ≥ 1 and Q = p^n, the fundamental character of level n is θ_{Q−1} : I_t → μ_{Q−1}(K̄) ≅ F_Q^× ⊂ k̄^× (reduction modulo the maximal ideal), σ ↦ σ(π^{1/(Q−1)})/π^{1/(Q−1)}, independent of the uniformiser and the root; the fundamental characters of level n are its n conjugates θ_{Q−1}^{p^i}, 0 ≤ i < n, and, for a field k_1 of characteristic p, a character I_t → k_1^× is fundamental of level n if it is θ_{Q−1} followed by an embedding F_Q ↪ k_1. These induce I_t ≅ lim F_{p^n}^× (transition maps the norms). A character of I_t is of level n if it factors through F_{p^n}^× (via θ_{p^n−1}) and through no F_{p^m}^× with m a proper divisor of n. Conjugation by an arithmetic Frobenius lift s acts on I_t by u ↦ u^{#k}, so θ(sus^{-1}) = θ(u)^{#k} for every fundamental character θ. For K = Q_p: the level-1 fundamental character is ω = θ_{p−1} = χ̄_p|_{I}; the two level-2 fundamental characters ψ = ω_2, ψ' = ω_2^p satisfy ψψ' = ω_2^{p+1} = ω; for a finite extension K/Q_p with ramification index e, χ̄_p|_{I_K} = θ_{p−1}^e. The residual character ω_{p,2}, its Teichmüller lift [ω_{p,2}] : I_t → W(F_{p^2})^× (TauCeti.teichmuller) and its ℓ-adic incarnations are three distinct declarations, although the sources use one symbol.

**Hypotheses.**

- level is a property of a character of I_t, not of a representation of G_K
- the level-1/level-2 dichotomy is specific to dimension two (tame-semisimple-residual-local-representations)
- the comparison with local class field theory has a sign: Serre 1972 Proposition 3 shows the tame character and the reciprocity map on units are opposite

**Construction and proof.**

1. θ_{Q−1} is the Q−1 component of LocalFieldsRamification layer 4's tame character I_K/P_K ≅ Ẑ^{(p')}(1), read in the residue field: reduction μ_{Q−1}(K̄) ≅ F_Q^× is the bijection of TauCeti.rootsOfUnityEquivResidueFieldUnits (inverse of the Teichmüller map); the inverse limit statement is Serre 1972 Proposition 2.
2. Conjugation: layer 4's equivariance (conjugation acts through the cyclotomic action), with the cyclotomic character of an arithmetic Frobenius acting on prime-to-p roots of unity by the #k-th power.
3. ω = θ_{p−1} on I_{Q_p}: K(μ_p) = K((−p)^{1/(p−1)}) and (ζ^a − 1)/(ζ − 1) ≡ a modulo the maximal ideal (Serre 1972 Proposition 8, recorded there as the e-th power for ramification index e).
4. ψψ' = ψ^{1+p} = θ_{p²−1}^{(p²−1)/(p−1)} = θ_{p−1} by the norm compatibility of the θ's.

**Prerequisites.** `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/LocalFieldsRamification#layer-4-the-tame-quotient-of-the-absolute-galois-group`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/LocalFieldsRamification#layer-3-ramification-the-tame-and-wild-cases-and-the-filtration`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/LocalFieldsRamification#layer-2-unramified-extensions-and-frobenius`; `tauceti:TauCeti.teichmuller`; `tauceti:TauCeti.rootsOfUnityEquivResidueFieldUnits`; `tauceti:TauCeti.residue_teichmuller`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/teichmuller-lift-of-a-residual-character`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/cyclotomic-and-dirichlet-characters`.

**Uses.**

- AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights:R15.4/tame-inertia-characters-of-a-local-residual-representation: the two tame characters of a local residual representation are of level 1 or 2
- AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights:R15.4/recipe-well-definedness-and-twisting: permuting niveau-2 fundamental characters and twisting
- OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting:R21.5/reduction-of-v-k-zero: V̄_{k,0} = ind(ω_2^{k−1})
- ClassicalSerreModularity:R33.2/dihedral-local-type-at-n: a character of G_{Q_{N²}} of niveau 2 on inertia
- EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.5/projective-inertia-order: fundamental characters bound the order of projective inertia
- Khare–Wintenberger I, 1.5: ω_p and ω_{p,2} with deliberate notational overloading

**API.**

- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.fundamentalCharacter` (constructor): θ_{p^n−1} : I_t → F_{p^n}^× for n ≥ 1.
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.fundamentalCharacter_indep` (characterisation): θ_{p^n−1} does not depend on the uniformiser or on the chosen root.
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.fundamentalCharacter_norm` (relation): θ_{p^{nm}−1}^{(p^{nm}−1)/(p^n−1)} = θ_{p^n−1}; the θ's induce I_t ≃ lim F_{p^n}^×.
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.fundamentalCharacter_conj` (relation): θ(sus^{-1}) = θ(u)^{#k} for an arithmetic Frobenius lift s.
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.IsFundamentalOfLevel` (constructor): predicate on χ : I_t → k_1^×; the n fundamental characters of level n are θ^{p^i}.
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.level` (data): the level of a character of I_t of finite order prime to p, with level_dvd_iff_factors.
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.fundamentalCharacter_one_eq_cyclotomic` (compatibility): θ_{p−1}^{e(K/Q_p)} = χ̄_p|_{I_K}.
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.fundamentalCharacter_two_mul_pow` (simp): for K = Q_p: ω_2 · ω_2^p = ω.
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.fundamentalCharacter_restrict` (functoriality): for L/K finite with ramification index e, θ^K restricted along I_{t,L} → I_{t,K} is (θ^L)^e.
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.teichmullerFundamentalCharacter` (coercion): the Teichmüller lift [θ_{p^n−1}] valued in W(F_{p^n})^× = μ_{p^n−1}, distinct from θ itself.

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.fundamentalCharacter_two_mul_conj` (computation): For K = Q_p, ω_2^{p+1} = ω on I_t.
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.level_trivial` (degenerate): The trivial character has level 1.
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.fundamentalCharacter_two_not_extend` (non-example): ω_2 does not extend to a character of G_{Q_p} (its Frobenius conjugate is ω_2^p ≠ ω_2), although it extends to G_{Q_{p²}}; a definition of fundamental characters as characters of G_{Q_p} fails.
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.fundamentalCharacter_one_Qp` (characterisation): For K = Q_p, θ_{p−1} = χ̄_p|_{I_{Q_p}}.
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.fundamentalCharacter_teichmuller` (compatibility): Reducing the Teichmüller lift [θ_{p^n−1}] modulo p gives θ_{p^n−1} (TauCeti.residue_teichmuller).

**Acceptance.**

- The product of the two level-2 fundamental characters of I_{Q_p} is the restriction of the mod-p cyclotomic character.
- On an explicit supersingular elliptic curve over Q_p with good reduction (p odd), the tame characters of E[p] are the two level-2 fundamental characters (Serre 1972 1.11; R01.6 supplies the curve).

**Sources.**

- serre87-duke, 2.1, printed p. 183 (decomposition excerpt, text layer): “Nous noterons I le groupe d'inertie de Gp , et Ip le plus grand prop-sous-groupe de I (groupe d'inertie sauvage) . Le quotient It = I/Ip est le groupe d'inertie modérée de G ; il s'identifie à lira . Fpn, cf. [41], prop . 2 .” — Tame inertia and its identification with lim F_{p^n}^*, quoted from Serre 1972 Prop. 2 (read here on the page image of Serre 1972).
- serre72-proprietes, 1.3, Proposition 2, printed p. 264 (read on the page image): “Proposition 2. Les isomorphismes θ_{q−1} définissent un isomorphisme θ: I_t → lim F_q^*, où F_q parcourt l'ensemble des sous-corps finis de k_s.” — The identification of tame inertia used for fundamental characters; it is Tau Ceti LocalFieldsRamification layer 4's tame character read through the residue field.
- serre72-proprietes, 1.7, Exemples: caractères fondamentaux, printed p. 267 (read on the page image): “On appelle caractère fondamental de niveau n tout caractère obtenu en composant le caractère θ_{q−1}: I_t → μ_{q−1} = F_q^*, avec un automorphisme du corps F_q” — Here q = p^n; there are n fundamental characters of level n, the conjugates θ_{q−1}^{p^i}.
- kw-serre-modularity-I, 1.5 Notation, p. 4 of the preprint (decomposition excerpt): “We also denote by ωp,2 a fundamental character of level 2 (valued in F∗p2 ) of Ip : it factors through the unique quotient of Ip that is isomorphic to F∗p2 . We denote by the same symbol” — The sentence continues: the same symbol denotes its Teichmüller lift and all its ℓ-adic incarnations (combining accents in the text layer). The deliberate notational overloading of ω_{p,2}; the formalisation keeps the residual character, its Teichmüller lift and its ℓ-adic incarnations as distinct declarations.

#### Semisimple residual local representations are tame; levels and induced representations in dimension two

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/tame-semisimple-residual-local-representations`. Kind: theorem. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.GaloisRep` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/TameResidual`). Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2`.

Let K be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, k_1 a field of characteristic p with the discrete topology and ρ̄ : G_K → GL(V) a continuous representation on a finite-dimensional k_1-vector space. (a) If ρ̄ is semisimple then ρ̄(P_K) = 1; hence for any ρ̄, P_K acts trivially on the semisimplification V^{ss} (R01.1/semisimplification) and I_K acts on V^{ss} through I_t; ρ̄(I_t) is cyclic of order prime to p, and over k̄_1 the action of I_t on V^{ss} is a sum of characters, each a product of powers of fundamental characters, the multiset of which is stable under χ ↦ χ^{#k}. (b) (K = Q_p, dim V = 2, k_1 = F̄_p) The two characters φ, φ' of I_t on V^{ss} are of level 1 or 2; if of level 2 they are conjugate: φ' = φ^p, φ = φ'^p, φ ≠ φ'. (c) If φ, φ' are of level 2, V is irreducible; conversely an irreducible two-dimensional ρ̄ has level 2. (d) Let Q_{p²} ⊂ Q̄_p be the unramified quadratic extension and χ : G_{Q_{p²}} → F̄_p^× continuous with χ|_{I} = ω_2^j. Then ind(χ) := Ind_{G_{Q_{p²}}}^{G_{Q_p}} χ restricted to I_{Q_p} is ω_2^j ⊕ ω_2^{pj}, and ind(χ) is irreducible iff (p+1) ∤ j; every irreducible two-dimensional ρ̄ is of this form. When (p+1) | j, χ extends to G_{Q_p} and ind(χ) ≅ χ̃ ⊕ χ̃η with η the unramified quadratic character.

**Hypotheses.**

- k_1 has characteristic p equal to the residue characteristic (residual representations at p)
- semisimplicity in (a) is with respect to G_K; P_K need not act trivially on V itself
- (b)–(d) are two-dimensional statements over Q_p; for K with residue field F_{p^f} the Frobenius acts by the p^f-th power

**Construction and proof.**

1. (a) Serre 1972 Proposition 4: ρ̄(P_K) is a finite p-group (open kernel), its invariants V' ≠ 0 form a G_K-stable subspace because P_K is normal; semisimplicity and induction on dimension give ρ̄(P_K) = 1. Then I_t acts through a finite cyclic group of order prime to p (I_t is procyclic of order prime to p), hence diagonalisably over k̄_1, through characters which are powers of fundamental characters (tame-inertia-and-fundamental-characters); stability under the #k-th power is conjugation by a Frobenius lift.
2. (b) Serre 1987 Proposition 1: conjugation by a Frobenius lift s satisfies sus^{-1} ≡ u^p mod I_p, so {φ, φ'} is stable under the p-th power; either both are fixed (level 1) or they are swapped (level 2).
3. (c) Serre 1987 2.2: a stable line would give a character of I_t extending to G_p, hence of level 1. Conversely let ρ̄ be irreducible (hence semisimple, so (a) applies) with φ, φ' of level 1: if φ = φ', twisting by a power of χ̄_p extending φ makes ρ̄ unramified, with procyclic image, hence reducible over F̄_p; if φ ≠ φ', conjugation by a Frobenius lift maps the φ-eigenline of I_t to the φ^{1/p} = φ eigenline, so both eigenlines are G_p-stable; either way ρ̄ is reducible.
4. (d) Mackey: Res_I Ind χ = χ|_I ⊕ χ^s|_I with s a Frobenius lift, and χ^s|_I = ω_2^{pj} by the conjugation rule; the Mackey irreducibility criterion (Tau Ceti InductionRestriction layer 4, applied to the finite image) gives irreducibility iff χ ≠ χ^s, i.e. iff ω_2^j ≠ ω_2^{pj} on I (unramified characters of G_{Q_{p²}} are s-invariant), i.e. iff (p² − 1) ∤ j(p − 1), i.e. (p+1) ∤ j. If (p+1) | j then ω_2^j = ω^{j/(p+1)} on I and χ = ω^{j/(p+1)}μ with μ unramified, which extends. Every irreducible ρ̄ has level 2 by (c), so I_t acts by ω_2^j ⊕ ω_2^{pj} with distinct characters; the Frobenius of Q_{p²} acts on I_t by the p²-th power and fixes both, so G_{Q_{p²}} preserves the two eigenlines, ρ̄|_{G_{Q_{p²}}} = χ ⊕ χ^s, and Frobenius reciprocity gives ρ̄ ≅ ind(χ).

**Prerequisites.** `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/tame-inertia-and-fundamental-characters`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/LocalFieldsRamification#layer-4-the-tame-quotient-of-the-absolute-galois-group`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/LocalFieldsRamification#layer-2-unramified-extensions-and-frobenius`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/semisimplification`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/finite-coefficients-and-finite-quotients`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/continuous-induction`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/mackey-decomposition`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/InductionRestriction#layer-4-intertwining-numbers-and-the-mackey-irreducibility-criterion`.

**Acceptance.**

- For 2 ≤ k ≤ p + 1, ind(ω_2^{k−1}) is irreducible (1 ≤ k − 1 ≤ p < p + 1), as used by OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting R21.5.
- For p = 3 and j = 4, ω_2^4 = ω on I and ind(χ) is reducible.

**Sources.**

- serre72-proprietes, 1.6, Proposition 4, printed p. 265 (read on the page image): “Proposition 4. Si ρ est semi-simple, on a ρ(I_p) = {1}.” — ρ is a continuous representation of G on a finite-dimensional vector space over a field of characteristic p (1.6).
- serre87-duke, 2.1, printed p. 183 (read on the page image): “le groupe I_p agit trivialement sur V^{ss} ([41], prop. 4)” — Wild inertia acts trivially on the semisimplification of a residual representation.
- serre87-duke, 2.1, Proposition 1, printed p. 183 (read on the page image): “Les caractères φ et φ' donnant l'action de I_t sur V^{ss} sont de niveau 1 ou 2. S'ils sont de niveau 2, ils sont conjugués: on a φ' = φ^p et φ = φ'^p.” — The level dichotomy for two-dimensional residual representations of G_{Q_p}.
- serre87-duke, 2.1, proof of Proposition 1, printed p. 183 (read on the page image): “la conjugaison par s opère sur I_t = I/I_p par u ↦ u^p” — Conjugation by an (arithmetic) Frobenius lift acts on tame inertia by the p-th power.
- serre87-duke, 2.2, printed p. 183 (read on the page image): “La représentation V est alors irréductible, car si elle contenait un sous-espace stable de dimension 1, l'action de I_t sur ce sous-espace se ferait par un caractère prolongeable à G_p, donc de niveau 1.” — Level 2 forces irreducibility.

#### Grothendieck's ℓ-adic monodromy theorem (arithmetic quasi-unipotence)

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/grothendieck-quasi-unipotence`. Kind: theorem. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.GaloisRep` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/Monodromy`). Planet: **Grothendieck's monodromy theorem**. Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2`.

Let K be a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q, q = p^f, W_K its Weil group with the Weil topology (ClassFieldTheory layer 9), ℓ ≠ p a prime, E a finite extension of Q_ℓ, V a finite-dimensional E-vector space and ρ : W_K → GL(V) continuous for the Weil topology and the ℓ-adic topology (for instance the restriction of a continuous representation of G_K). Then there is a unique nilpotent N ∈ Hom_{Z_ℓ}(Z_ℓ(1), End_E V) = End(V)(−1) and an open subgroup J ⊂ I_K such that ρ(σ) = exp(N(t_ℓ(σ))) for all σ ∈ J (exp of a nilpotent endomorphism, a finite sum). Moreover ρ(w)N(x)ρ(w)^{-1} = N(χ_ℓ(w)x) for w ∈ W_K, x ∈ Z_ℓ(1); after a trivialisation T of Z_ℓ(1), N' := N(T^{-1}1) satisfies ρ(w)N'ρ(w)^{-1} = q^{weilDegree(w)}N', i.e. ρ(Φ)N'ρ(Φ)^{-1} = qN' for an arithmetic Frobenius lift Φ and ρ(F)N'ρ(F)^{-1} = q^{-1}N' for a geometric one. Consequences: every ρ(σ), σ ∈ I_K, is quasi-unipotent (eigenvalues roots of unity); ρ(I_K) is finite iff N = 0; N is the same for ρ and for every restriction ρ|_{W_L}, L/K finite, up to the factor e(L/K) of t_ℓ (N_L = e·N_K); coefficients in Q̄_ℓ are covered after descent to a finite E (R01.1/baire-descent-to-a-finite-coefficient-field).

**Hypotheses.**

- ℓ different from the residue characteristic p
- finite residue field: the argument uses that Frobenius multiplies t_ℓ by q, which is not a root of unity; for K = C((t)) the character σ ↦ (1+ℓ)^{T(t_ℓ(σ))} of I_K = G_K is continuous and not quasi-unipotent, so the statement fails for algebraically closed residue fields (where LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles LPV.1 supplies the geometric theorem)
- quasi-unipotence holds on an open subgroup only; ρ need not be unipotent on I_K
- N is Tate-twisted; the untwisted N' depends on T and changes by a unit under a change of T

**Construction and proof.**

1. Deligne states the theorem as 8.2 and refers to Serre–Tate for the proof (not read); the argument planned here is the standard one.
2. Lattice: ρ(I_K) is compact, so it stabilises an O_E-lattice (R01.1/compact-subgroups-stabilise-lattices); J := ρ|_{I_K}^{-1}(1 + ℓ²M_n(O_E)) is open in I_K and ρ(J) is pro-ℓ.
3. Factorisation: by ell-adic-tame-character (iv), ρ|_J = h ∘ t_ℓ|_J for a continuous h : t_ℓ(J) → 1 + ℓ²M_n(O_E); t_ℓ(J) = ℓ^m Z_ℓ(1) is procyclic, and N(x) := ℓ^{-m} log h(ℓ^m x) (ℓ-adic logarithm, convergent on 1 + ℓ²M_n(O_E)) is Z_ℓ-linear with exp(N(t_ℓ(σ))) = ρ(σ) on J.
4. Nilpotence: for w ∈ W_K, conjugation by w preserves an open subgroup of J and t_ℓ(wσw^{-1}) = χ_ℓ(w)t_ℓ(σ) (ell-adic-tame-character (iii)), so ρ(w)N(x)ρ(w)^{-1} = N(χ_ℓ(w)x); with w an arithmetic Frobenius lift, N' is conjugate to qN', so its eigenvalues are stable under multiplication by q and are all 0.
5. Uniqueness: two pairs (N_1, J_1), (N_2, J_2) agree on J_1 ∩ J_2 because log is injective on unipotent elements, and linearity in x gives N_1 = N_2.
6. ρ(I_K) finite iff N = 0: if N = 0, ρ is trivial on the open J; if ρ(I_K) is finite, exp(N(x)) has finite order and is unipotent, hence trivial, and N = log of it is 0.

**Prerequisites.** `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/ell-adic-tame-character`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/cyclotomic-and-dirichlet-characters`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/continuous-representation`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/compact-subgroups-stabilise-lattices`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/baire-descent-to-a-finite-coefficient-field`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ClassFieldTheory#layer-9-the-local-weil-group`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/LocalFieldsRamification#layer-4-the-tame-quotient-of-the-absolute-galois-group`; `mathlib:IsNilpotent.exp`; `mathlib:IsNilpotent.exp_add_of_commute`.

**Acceptance.**

- For the Tate curve E_q over K with v(q) > 0, the representation on V_ℓE_q has N ≠ 0 with image the line Q_ℓ(1) ⊂ V_ℓE_q, and ρ(I_K) is infinite.
- For an abelian variety with potentially good reduction, or for any representation with finite image on inertia (e.g. a finite-order character), N = 0.

**Sources.**

- deligne73-constantes, Théorème 8.2, Del-66, printed p. 566 (decomposition excerpt, read on the page image): “Soit (V,ρ) une représentation λ-adique de W(K̄/K). Il existe N ∈ End(V)(-1), nilpotent, tel que pour σ dans un sous-groupe d'indice fini de I, on ait ρ(σ) = exp(N.t_ℓ(σ))” — Quasi-unipotence on a finite-index (= open) subgroup of inertia, with N Tate-twisted.
- deligne73-constantes, Théorème 8.2, displayed relation, Del-66, printed p. 566 (read on the page image): “Ce N ∈ End(V)(-1) est unique, donc invariant par Galois : pour w ∈ W(K̄/K), on a ρ(w) N ρ(w)^{-1} = q^{v'(w)}.N” — The conjugation relation with v' counting arithmetic-Frobenius powers (2.2.2).
- deligne73-constantes, 8.1, Del-66, printed p. 566 (read on the page image): “Le résultat suivant est démontré dans [13].” — Deligne quotes Grothendieck's theorem; its proof is in [13] = Serre–Tate, Good reduction of abelian varieties, which was not read.
- fsy22, §5.3.1, arXiv v5 p. 54 (text layer): “by Grothendieck’s quasi-unipotency theorem, there exists a unique nilpotent endomorphism N” — FSY's statement of quasi-unipotence used to build the Weil–Deligne representation.

#### Weil–Deligne representations of a local Weil group (arithmetic normalisation)

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/weil-deligne-representation`. Kind: definition. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/WeilDeligne/Basic`). Planet: **Weil–Deligne representation**. Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2`.

Let K be a nonarchimedean local field with residue cardinality q, W_K its Weil group with weilDegree : W_K → Z (kernel I_K, arithmetic Frobenius lifts of degree 1; ClassFieldTheory layer 9), and Ω a field of characteristic 0. A Weil–Deligne representation of W_K over Ω is a triple (V, r, N): V a finite-dimensional Ω-vector space, r : W_K → GL(V) a homomorphism whose restriction to I_K has open kernel (equivalently r is continuous for the discrete topology on GL(V)), and N ∈ End_Ω(V) nilpotent with r(w)Nr(w)^{-1} = q^{weilDegree(w)}N for all w ∈ W_K (Deligne (8.4.1.1)); equivalently r(Φ)Nr(Φ)^{-1} = qN for an arithmetic Frobenius lift Φ and r(F)Nr(F)^{-1} = q^{-1}N for a geometric lift F. Morphisms are Ω-linear maps f with f∘r(w) = r'(w)∘f and f∘N = N'∘f; they form an Ω-linear abelian category WD_Ω(K) with direct sums, tensor products (r⊗r', N⊗1 + 1⊗N'), internal Hom and duals (r^∨, −N^∨), determinant (det r, 0), coefficient extension Ω → Ω', restriction to W_L for L/K finite inside K̄ and induction from W_L (Ind r, with N acting on the induced space through the coset decomposition). The unramified character ω : W_K → Ω^×, ω(w) = q^{weilDegree(w)} (ω(Φ) = q), corresponds to Deligne's ω_1 = ‖·‖ and to Q_ℓ(1); the special representation Sp(n) has basis e_0, …, e_{n−1}, r(w)e_i = ω(w)^i e_i and Ne_i = e_{i+1} (Ne_{n−1} = 0). The inertial type of (V, r, N) is r|_{I_K} up to isomorphism.

**Hypotheses.**

- arithmetic normalisation (8.4.1.1); copying a geometric-Frobenius formula with q instead of q^{-1} gives the wrong objects
- r is required to have open kernel on inertia; the ℓ-adic topology of Ω plays no role (Deligne 8.3–8.4: the description is independent of the topology of E_λ)
- Ω has characteristic 0, needed for exp/log in the comparison with ℓ-adic representations

**Construction and proof.**

1. Category: kernels and cokernels of morphisms carry the restricted r and N, the relation is preserved; tensor products: r⊗r'(w)(N⊗1 + 1⊗N')r⊗r'(w)^{-1} = q^{deg w}(N⊗1 + 1⊗N'), and N⊗1 + 1⊗N' is nilpotent as a sum of commuting nilpotents.
2. Duals: with r^∨(w) the transpose of r(w)^{-1}, r^∨(w)X^∨r^∨(w)^{-1} = (r(w)Xr(w)^{-1})^∨ for X ∈ End V, so r^∨(w)(−N^∨)r^∨(w)^{-1} = q^{weilDegree(w)}(−N^∨).
3. Restriction to W_L: weilDegree_K = f(L/K)·weilDegree_L on W_L (ClassFieldTheory layer 9 weilDegree_weilTransfer) and q_L = q^{f(L/K)}, so the relation is preserved.
4. Sp(n): r(w)Nr(w)^{-1}e_i = ω(w)^{-i}r(w)e_{i+1} = ω(w)e_{i+1}.

**Prerequisites.** `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ClassFieldTheory#layer-9-the-local-weil-group`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/LocalFieldsRamification#layer-4-the-tame-quotient-of-the-absolute-galois-group`; `mathlib:Representation`; `mathlib:Representation.dual`; `mathlib:Representation.tprod`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/unramified-character-lambda`.

**Uses.**

- PadicHodgeTheory:R06.3/convention-comparison-with-r01: Weil–Deligne representations (r, N) over Ω in the arithmetic normalisation, with ⊗, duals, determinant, the twist by ω, restriction to I_K and (r,N) ≅ (r,aN)
- AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations:R19.4/hecke-versus-langlands-normalization-and-local-global-compatibility: Frobenius-semisimple representations of the Weil–Deligne group attached to π_p; F N F^{-1} = q^{-1}N for geometric F
- EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison:ET.6: full Frobenius-semisimple Weil–Deligne parameters σ ⊗ Sp_r with covariance r(w)Nr(w)^{-1} = |w|N
- PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:R24.5/compatible-system: Frobenius-semisimple WD data r_q over E at every finite q
- GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer:R16.3: rank-two specialisation of the canonical local correspondence imports the Weil–Deligne carrier
- Fresán–Sabbah–Yu 2022, §5.3.1: Weil–Deligne representations (ρ, N) with ρ(w)Nρ(w)^{-1} = p^{-v(w)}N, v(w) the power of geometric Frobenius

**API.**

- `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep` (structure): the structure (V, r, N) with r|_{I_K} of open kernel and the relation r(w)Nr(w)^{-1} = q^{weilDegree w}N.
- `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep.Hom` (structure): morphisms; WeilDeligneRep forms an Ω-linear abelian category.
- `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep.conj_monodromy_arith` (simp): r(Φ)Nr(Φ)^{-1} = qN for arithmetic Φ; conj_monodromy_geom: r(F)Nr(F)^{-1} = q^{-1}N.
- `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep.tensor` (instance): tensor product with monodromy N⊗1 + 1⊗N'; direct sum; unit (trivial, 0).
- `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep.dual` (instance): dual (r^∨, −N^∨); internal Hom; det (det r, 0).
- `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep.twist` (functoriality): twist by a character χ : W_K → Ω^× with open kernel on I_K, (r⊗χ, N).
- `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep.omega` (example): ω(w) = q^{weilDegree w}; ω corresponds to ‖·‖ under Deligne's normalisation of local class field theory.
- `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep.special` (example): Sp(n) as above; Sp(n)^∨ ≅ Sp(n) ⊗ ω^{1−n}.
- `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep.restrict` (functoriality): restriction to W_L, compatible with ⊗ and duals.
- `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep.induced` (functoriality): induction from W_L, Frobenius reciprocity with restriction.
- `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep.iso_smul_monodromy` (equivalence): (V, r, N) ≅ (V, r, aN) for every a ∈ Ω^× (Deligne, proof of Lemme 8.4.3).
- `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep.inertialType` (projection): r|_{I_K} up to isomorphism.
- `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep.baseChange` (functoriality): coefficient extension along Ω → Ω'.

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep.special_two_relation` (computation): Sp(2) = (1 ⊕ ω, Ne_0 = e_1) satisfies r(Φ)Nr(Φ)^{-1} = qN.
- `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep.geometric_copy_fails` (non-example): (ω ⊕ 1, Ne_0 = e_1) is not a Weil–Deligne representation: it satisfies r(Φ)Nr(Φ)^{-1} = q^{-1}N for arithmetic Φ.
- `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep.monodromy_zero` (degenerate): For N = 0 a Weil–Deligne representation is a representation of W_K with open kernel on I_K, and every such r gives one.
- `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep.iso_smul_monodromy_special` (characterisation): Sp(2) with monodromy N and with monodromy 2N are isomorphic via e_0 ↦ e_0, e_1 ↦ 2e_1.
- `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep.dual_special_two` (compatibility): Sp(2)^∨ ≅ Sp(2) ⊗ ω^{-1}, and det Sp(2) = ω.

**Acceptance.**

- Sp(2) = (1 ⊕ ω, N e_0 = e_1) satisfies the relation, and its kernel of N is the line on which arithmetic Frobenius acts by q, matching Q_ℓ(1) ⊂ V_ℓ(E_q) for a Tate curve.
- The pair (ω ⊕ 1, N e_0 = e_1), i.e. N lowering the ω-exponent, violates the relation: r(w)Nr(w)^{-1} = q^{-weilDegree(w)}N.

**Sources.**

- deligne73-constantes, Définition 8.4.1, Del-68, printed p. 568 (read on the page image): “(b) un endomorphisme nilpotent N de V, tel que (8.4.1.1) ρ'(w) N ρ'(w)^{-1} = q^{v'(w)} N” — The defining relation of a Weil–Deligne representation, in the arithmetic normalisation.
- deligne73-constantes, proof of Lemme 8.4.3, Del-69, printed p. 569 (read on the page image): “Changer T en aT change (ρ',N') en (ρ',aN'). Nous montrerons que pour toute représentation (ρ',N') de 'W(K̄/K) sur un corps E, et tout a ∈ E, (ρ',N') ⥲ (ρ',a N').” — The rescaling lemma (r,N) ≅ (r,aN); 'tout a ∈ E' must be read as a ≠ 0.
- fsy22, §5.3.1, arXiv v5 p. 54 (text layer): “A Weil-Deligne representation (ρ, N) on V consists of a Weil representation ρ on V as above and a nilpotent endomorphism N, called the logarithm of the unipotent part of the local monodromy, such that the equality ρ(w)Nρ(w)−1 = p−v(w) N holds for all w ∈ W (Qp /Qp ),” — FSY's v(w) counts powers of the GEOMETRIC Frobenius F_p, so p^{-v(w)} = p^{v'(w)}: the same relation as Deligne (8.4.1.1).
- deligne73-constantes, 2.2.4, Del-22, printed p. 522 (read on the page image): “est le sous-groupe de Gal(K̄/K) formé des σ tels que v'(σ) soit une puissance entière du Frobenius φ” — Deligne's Weil group; Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory layer 9 builds the same carrier with its Weil topology.

#### The Weil–Deligne representation of an ℓ-adic representation and its independence of choices

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/grothendieck-monodromy-and-the-weil-deligne-functor`. Kind: construction. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/WeilDeligne/OfEllAdic`). Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2`.

Let K be a nonarchimedean local field with residue field of cardinality q, ℓ ≠ p, E a finite extension of Q_ℓ and (V, ρ) a continuous representation of W_K (or of G_K, restricted to W_K) on a finite-dimensional E-vector space, with monodromy N ∈ End(V)(−1) from grothendieck-quasi-unipotence. Choose a geometric Frobenius lift F ∈ W_K and an isomorphism T : Q_ℓ(1) → Q_ℓ (Deligne 8.4.2). Define WD_{F,T}(ρ) = (V, ρ', N') by ρ'(F^nσ) = ρ(F^nσ)·exp(−t_ℓ(σ)N) for n ∈ Z, σ ∈ I_K (every w ∈ W_K is uniquely F^nσ), and N' ∈ End(V) the image of N under T. Then (V, ρ', N') is a Weil–Deligne representation over E in the sense of weil-deligne-representation (ρ'|_{I_K} has open kernel and ρ'(w)N'ρ'(w)^{-1} = q^{weilDegree(w)}N'), and its isomorphism class WD(ρ) depends only on ρ, not on F or T (Lemme 8.4.3): changing F to Fτ (τ ∈ I_K) conjugates by A = exp((1−q^{-1})^{-1}t_ℓ(τ)N), and changing T to aT replaces N' by aN', isomorphic to (ρ', N') for every a ∈ E^×. The construction is a functor from continuous ℓ-adic representations of W_K to WD_E(K), it is exact, faithful, compatible with ⊗, duals, det, direct sums, twists (WD(ρ⊗χ) = WD(ρ)⊗WD(χ)), coefficient extension, restriction to W_L and induction from W_L, and with V^{ρ(I_K)} = (ker N')^{ρ'(I_K)}; it induces a bijection between isomorphism classes of continuous ℓ-adic representations of W_K over E and isomorphism classes of Weil–Deligne representations over E (Deligne 8.3.7, in the form 8.4); a continuous representation of W_K extends continuously to G_K iff its image is bounded, i.e. iff the eigenvalues of r(Φ) are ℓ-adic units.

**Hypotheses.**

- λ must have residue characteristic different from that of K; this is the ℓ ≠ p hypothesis of the stage
- the nilpotent N of Theorem 8.2 lies in End(V)(−1), i.e. it is Tate-twisted; the untwisted N' of 8.4.2 depends on the choice of T, and changing T to aT replaces N' by aN'
- quasi-unipotence is only on a subgroup of finite index of inertia; ρ itself need not be unipotent on all of I
- the construction 8.4.2 depends on choosing a GEOMETRIC Frobenius F and a trivialization T of Z_ℓ(1); Lemme 8.4.3 removes the dependence only up to isomorphism
- the source's proof of Lemme 8.4.3 changes F to F.ρ (ρ in I), giving an isomorphic pair via conjugation by A = exp((1−q^{−1})^{−1} t_ℓ(ρ)), and T to aT, and shows (ρ', N') is isomorphic to (ρ', aN') for every a (printed 'a ∈ E', meaning a nonzero) by decomposing V into generalized eigenspaces V^α of F^n, with N V^α contained in V^{q^{−n} α}
- the bijection is for representations of W_K; Weil–Deligne representations whose Frobenius has non-unit eigenvalues come from representations of W_K that do not extend to G_K

**Construction and proof.**

1. The source states 8.2 as Grothendieck's theorem and refers to [13] = Serre–Tate, Good reduction of abelian varieties, Ann. of Math. 88 (1968), for the proof, which was NOT read here; grothendieck-quasi-unipotence plans that proof.
2. The exponent convention is fixed by the notation of 2.2.2–2.2.4: v' is reduction to Gal(k̄/k), whose Weil subgroup W(k̄/k) = Z is generated by the ARITHMETIC Frobenius φ, and F = φ^{-1} is the geometric Frobenius; so the displayed relation reads ρ(Φ)Nρ(Φ)^{-1} = qN for arithmetic Φ. This agrees with the stage text 'With arithmetic Frobenius the relation is r(F)Nr(F)^{-1}=qN'.
3. ρ' is a homomorphism because ρ(w)N(x)ρ(w)^{-1} = N(χ_ℓ(w)x) and t_ℓ(wσw^{-1}) = χ_ℓ(w)t_ℓ(σ) (grothendieck-quasi-unipotence, ell-adic-tame-character (iii)), so the correction factors exp(−t_ℓ(σ)N) multiply compatibly; ρ' is trivial on the open J where ρ = exp(t_ℓN).
4. 8.4.2 produces (ρ', N') from (V, ρ), and Lemme 8.4.3 proves independence of the choices of F and T up to isomorphism; 8.3.7 follows.
5. Compatibilities: N is unique, so the N of ρ⊗ρ' is N⊗1 + 1⊗N' and the N of ρ^∨ is −N^∨; restriction to W_L uses t_{ℓ,K}|_{I_L} = e·t_{ℓ,L} (ell-adic-tame-character (v)); induction: the monodromy of Ind ρ is the induced N because N is unique and Ind ρ restricted to an open subgroup of I_K is a sum of conjugates of ρ.
6. Invariants: σ ∈ I_K fixes v under ρ iff ρ'(σ)exp(t_ℓ(σ)N)v = v for all σ; taking σ ∈ J gives Nv = 0, and then ρ'(σ)v = v (Deligne 8.12, FSY §5.3.1).

**Prerequisites.** `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/grothendieck-quasi-unipotence`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/weil-deligne-representation`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/ell-adic-tame-character`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ClassFieldTheory#layer-9-the-local-weil-group`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/continuous-induction`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/restriction-dual-tensor-twist`; `mathlib:IsNilpotent.exp`; `mathlib:IsNilpotent.isUnit_exp`.

#### Frobenius semisimplification, semisimplification, and the three objects attached to a Weil–Deligne representation

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/frobenius-semisimplification`. Kind: construction. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/WeilDeligne/FrobeniusSemisimple`). Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2`.

Let (V, r, N) be a Weil–Deligne representation over a field Ω of characteristic 0 and F ∈ W_K a geometric Frobenius lift. Let r(F) = s·u be the multiplicative Jordan–Chevalley decomposition (s semisimple, u unipotent, commuting; Tau Ceti LinearMap.GeneralLinearGroup.jordanDecomposition, Ω perfect). Then u commutes with r(W_K) and with N (Deligne 8.5: u is a polynomial in r(F), a power r(F)^m is central in r(W_K) because F^m acts trivially on I_K modulo the open kernel of r, and N is an eigenvector of conjugation by r(F)); the Frobenius semisimplification is (V, r^{F-ss}, N) with r^{F-ss}(F^nσ) := r(F^nσ)u^{-n} (n ∈ Z, σ ∈ I_K) (Deligne (8.5.1)). It is a Weil–Deligne representation, independent of the choice of F, with r^{F-ss}(F) = s. (V, r, N) is Frobenius-semisimple if r = r^{F-ss}, equivalently if r(w) is semisimple for one (equivalently every) w ∈ W_K ∖ I_K. Three objects are distinguished: (1) the full (V, r, N); (2) its Frobenius semisimplification (V, r^{F-ss}, N), which keeps N; (3) its semisimplification in the abelian category WD_Ω(K), which is (V^{ss}, r^{ss}, 0): the simple objects have N = 0 because ker N is a sub-object, and r^{ss} is the semisimplification of r as a representation of W_K. On the Galois side, for an ℓ-adic ρ, WD(ρ^{ss}) is (3) for WD(ρ), whereas WD(ρ)^{F-ss} is (2). Every Frobenius-semisimple indecomposable Weil–Deligne representation over an algebraically closed Ω is r_0 ⊗ Sp(n) for an irreducible representation r_0 of W_K and n ≥ 1, and the decomposition of a Frobenius-semisimple object into such is unique up to order.

**Hypotheses.**

- Ω of characteristic 0 (perfect, so the Jordan decomposition exists over Ω)
- Frobenius semisimplification semisimplifies only Frobenius; it does not kill N and is not the semisimplification of the Weil–Deligne representation
- the classification of indecomposables needs Ω algebraically closed

**Construction and proof.**

1. Deligne 8.5: u is a polynomial in r(F) (Tau Ceti coe_semisimplePart_mem_adjoin); r(F)^m is central in r(W_K) modulo the open kernel I' of r on I_K for m with F^m acting trivially on I_K/I', so u (the unipotent part of r(F)^m to the power 1/m in the unipotent group) centralises r(W_K); N is an eigenvector of conjugation by r(F) (eigenvalue q^{-1}), so u commutes with N.
2. r^{F-ss} is a homomorphism with the same restriction to I_K and the relation for N holds because u commutes with N; independence of F: for w_1, w_2 ∉ I_K, r(w_1), r(w_2) have a common power up to the finite kernel, so u^n is the unipotent part of r(F^nσ) for every σ (Deligne 8.5).
3. Semisimplification: ker N is r-stable by the relation, so simple objects have N = 0; Jordan–Hölder in the finite-length category WD_Ω(K).
4. Classification: on an F-semisimple object, the monodromy filtration of N (the unique increasing filtration with N M_k ⊂ M_{k−2} and N^k : gr_k ≅ gr_{−k}) is r-stable with r(F) acting on the primitive parts; Deligne Proposition 8.9 uses the graded pieces; the decomposition r_0 ⊗ Sp(n) follows from the Jacobson–Morozov form of N (Ω characteristic 0).

**Prerequisites.** `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/weil-deligne-representation`; `tauceti:LinearMap.GeneralLinearGroup.jordanDecomposition`; `tauceti:LinearMap.GeneralLinearGroup.semisimplePart`; `tauceti:LinearMap.GeneralLinearGroup.unipotentPart`; `tauceti:LinearMap.GeneralLinearGroup.eq_jordanDecomposition_iff`; `tauceti:LinearMap.GeneralLinearGroup.coe_semisimplePart_mem_adjoin`; `tauceti:LinearMap.GeneralLinearGroup.IsUnipotent`; `mathlib:Module.End.exists_isNilpotent_isSemisimple`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/semisimplification`.

#### The local Euler factor of a Weil–Deligne or ℓ-adic representation (geometric Frobenius)

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/local-euler-factor`. Kind: definition. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/WeilDeligne/LFactor`). Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2`.

For a Weil–Deligne representation (V, r, N) over Ω and a geometric Frobenius lift Φ ∈ W_K, L(V, X) := det(1 − X·r(Φ) | (ker N)^{r(I_K)}) ∈ Ω[X], a polynomial with constant term 1 and degree dim (ker N)^{I_K}, independent of Φ (inertia acts trivially on the invariants); for Ω = C, L(V, s) = L(V, q^{-s})^{-1}. In Deligne's notation (3.5.1) Z(V; t) = det(1 − Ft^d, V^I)^{-1} with d = [k : F_p], so X = t^d = q^{-s}. For a continuous ℓ-adic representation ρ of G_K or W_K (ℓ ≠ p), L(ρ, X) := det(1 − Xρ(Φ) | V^{ρ(I_K)}) = L(WD(ρ), X) (Deligne 8.12). For F a number field, a finite place v and ρ a continuous representation of G_F over a field of characteristic 0 with v ∤ ℓ, L_v(ρ, X) := L(ρ|_{G_{F_v}}, X), independent of ι; if ρ is unramified at v, L_v(ρ, X) = det(1 − Xρ(Frob_v)^{-1}) = X^{dim V}·P_v(ρ^∨, X^{-1}). For a Tate module V_ℓA with H^1 = V_ℓA^∨: (V_ℓA^∨)^{I_v} is the dual of the coinvariants (V_ℓA)_{I_v}, so L_v(V_ℓA^∨, X) = det(1 − X·Frob_v | (V_ℓA)_{I_v}) with arithmetic Frob_v; this equals det(1 − X·Frob_v | V_ℓA^{I_v}) when I_v acts through a finite quotient, but not in general (Tate curve: 1 − X from coinvariants, 1 − qX from invariants).

**Hypotheses.**

- GEOMETRIC Frobenius in the Euler factor, arithmetic Frobenius in P_v; the two are related by duality
- (ker N)^{I} on the Weil–Deligne side, V^{ρ(I)} on the Galois side; these agree by the Weil–Deligne functor
- taking inertia invariants does not commute with reduction modulo ℓ, so L_v of a residual representation is not the reduction of L_v of a lift

**Construction and proof.**

1. Independence of Φ: two geometric lifts differ by an element of I_K, which acts trivially on (ker N)^{I_K}; (ker N)^{I_K} is r(W_K)-stable because I_K is normal and r(w) preserves ker N by the relation.
2. L(ρ) = L(WD(ρ)): grothendieck-monodromy-and-the-weil-deligne-functor gives V^{ρ(I_K)} = (ker N')^{ρ'(I_K)}, and ρ' = ρ on it.
3. Unramified case: ρ(Frob^{-1}) acts on V and det(1 − Xρ(Frob)^{-1}) = X^n det(X^{-1} − ρ^∨(Frob)) by transposition (frobenius-characteristic-polynomial).

**Prerequisites.** `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/weil-deligne-representation`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/grothendieck-monodromy-and-the-weil-deligne-functor`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/frobenius-characteristic-polynomial`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/local-restriction`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/frobenius-semisimplification`; `mathlib:Polynomial.reverse`; `mathlib:LinearMap.det`.

**Uses.**

- Fresán–Sabbah–Yu 2022, Lemma 5.40: equality of L-factors of r and r̄
- PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:R24.5/compatible-system: local L-factors of compatible systems
- PeriodsAndSpecialValues:PS.1: completed motivic L-functions from local Weil–Deligne data
- ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6/local-euler-factor-of-an-abelian-variety: the Euler factor of an abelian variety at every place

- `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep.localFactor_indep` (characterisation): independent of the geometric Frobenius lift.
- `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep.localFactor_directSum` (simp): L(V ⊕ V') = L(V)·L(V').
- `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep.localFactor_iso` (extensionality): isomorphic Weil–Deligne representations have equal local factors; L(V^{F-ss}) = L(V).
- `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep.localFactor_unramified_twist` (relation): for an unramified character λ_W(α), L(V ⊗ λ_W(α), X) = L(V, α^{-1}X).
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.localEulerFactor` (constructor): L(ρ, X) = det(1 − Xρ(Φ) | V^{ρ(I_K)}) for ℓ-adic ρ, and L_v(ρ, X) for global ρ.
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.localEulerFactor_eq_localFactor` (compatibility): L(ρ, X) = L(WD(ρ), X).
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.localEulerFactor_unramified` (compatibility): L_v(ρ, X) = Polynomial.reverse (P_v(ρ^∨, X)) at unramified v.
- `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep.localFactor_exact_monodromy_zero` (relation): on short exact sequences of Weil–Deligne representations with N = 0, L is multiplicative (inertia invariants are exact for open kernel); with N ≠ 0 it is not.

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep.localFactor_omega` (computation): L(ω, X) = 1 − q^{-1}X, since ω(F) = q^{-1} for a geometric Frobenius lift F.
- `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep.localFactor_special_two` (computation): L(Sp(2), X) = 1 − q^{-1}X and L(Sp(2)^∨, X) = 1 − X.
- `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep.localFactor_zero` (degenerate): L(0, X) = 1 and L(1, X) = 1 − X.
- `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep.localFactor_special_not_invariants` (non-example): Using V^{I_K} instead of (ker N)^{I_K} gives (1 − X)(1 − q^{-1}X) for Sp(2), and using arithmetic Frobenius gives 1 − qX for ω; both are wrong.
- `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep.localFactor_not_exact` (characterisation): For 0 → ω → Sp(2) → 1 → 0, L(Sp(2)) ≠ L(ω)L(1): L is not multiplicative on exact sequences with nonzero monodromy.

**Acceptance.**

- L(Q_ℓ(1), X) = 1 − q^{-1}X; for a Tate curve E_q over K, L(V_ℓE_q, X) = 1 − q^{-1}X and L(V_ℓE_q^∨, X) = 1 − X, the split multiplicative Euler factor.
- For a totally ramified character χ (χ|_{I_K} ≠ 1), L(χ, X) = 1.

**Sources.**

#### Local factors and Weil–Deligne representations of induced representations

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/local-factor-of-induced-representation`. Kind: theorem. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/WeilDeligne/Induction`). Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2`.

(a) Local: let L/K be a finite separable extension of nonarchimedean local fields with residue degree f, and (V, r, N) a Weil–Deligne representation of W_L over Ω. Then L(Ind_{W_L}^{W_K}(V, r, N), X) = L((V, r, N), X^f), and for an ℓ-adic representation ρ of W_L (or G_L), WD(Ind ρ) ≅ Ind WD(ρ), so L(Ind ρ, X) = L(ρ, X^f). (b) Global: let L/F be a finite extension of number fields, ρ a continuous representation of G_L over a field of characteristic 0 and v a finite place of F with v ∤ ℓ. Then L_v(Ind_{G_L}^{G_F} ρ, X) = ∏_{w | v} L_w(ρ, X^{f(w|v)}). If ρ is unramified at every w | v and L/F is unramified at v, Ind ρ is unramified at v and P_v(Ind ρ, X) = ∏_{w | v} P_w(ρ, X^{f(w|v)}).

**Hypotheses.**

- L/F finite (open subgroup G_L), places w of L above v with residue degrees f(w|v)
- for the P_v formula: L/F unramified at v and ρ unramified at all w | v; otherwise only the L-factor statement holds

**Construction and proof.**

1. (a) Deligne Proposition 3.8(ii): (Ind V)^{I_K} = Ind_{W(k̄/ℓ)}^{W(k̄/k)}(V^{I_L}) as W(k̄/k)-representations (both are covariant functions on W(k̄/k) with values in V^{I_L}), and Lemme 3.9: for F_n the endomorphism of V^{⊕n} permuting cyclically and applying F once, det(1 − F_n X) = det(1 − F X^n). On the Weil–Deligne side the monodromy of the induced object is induced, and ker of the induced N is induced from ker N.
2. WD(Ind ρ) ≅ Ind WD(ρ): grothendieck-monodromy-and-the-weil-deligne-functor (compatibility with induction).
3. (b) local-restriction gives (Ind ρ)_ι ≅ ⊕_{w|v} Ind_{G_{L_w}}^{G_{F_v}} ρ_{ι_w} (Mackey); apply (a) to each summand with f = f(w|v) and multiplicativity of L on direct sums.
4. P_v formula: at unramified v, L_v = reverse of P_v of the dual; apply the L-formula to ρ^∨ (Ind commutes with duals) and reverse, using that reversal is multiplicative and X ↦ X^f commutes with it.

**Prerequisites.** `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/local-euler-factor`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/grothendieck-monodromy-and-the-weil-deligne-functor`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/local-restriction`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/frobenius-characteristic-polynomial`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/mackey-decomposition`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/continuous-induction`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ClassFieldTheory#layer-9-the-local-weil-group`.

**Acceptance.**

- For L = Q(i), F = Q, ρ = 1: P_p(Ind 1, X) = (X − 1)² for p ≡ 1 mod 4 and X² − 1 = (X − 1)(X + 1) for p ≡ 3 mod 4.
- For K'/K unramified of degree f and ρ = 1, L(Ind 1, X) = 1 − X^f.

**Sources.**

- deligne73-constantes, Proposition 3.8 (ii), Del-30, printed p. 530 (read on the page image): “Soient L une extension finie séparable de K dans K̄ et V_L une représentation complexe de W(K̄/L). Soit V_K la représentation induite de W(K̄/K). On a (3.8.2) L(V_K) = L(V_L).” — Inductivity of local L-factors; the proof identifies V_K^{I_K} with the induced representation of W(k̄/l) and applies Lemme 3.9.
- deligne73-constantes, (3.5.1), Del-28, printed p. 528 (read on the page image): “(3.5.1) Z(V;t) = det(1 - Ft^d, V^I)^{-1}” — The local factor uses the GEOMETRIC Frobenius F on inertia invariants; t^d with d = [k:F_p] corresponds to X = q^{-s}.

#### The monodromy filtration and purity of Weil–Deligne representations

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/purity-of-weil-deligne-representations`. Kind: definition. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/WeilDeligne/Purity`). Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2`.

Let (V, r, N) be a Weil–Deligne representation over Ω, ι : Ω → C an embedding (or Ω = Q̄_ℓ with a fixed ι : Q̄_ℓ ≅ C), F a geometric Frobenius lift and w ∈ Z. The monodromy filtration M_• of N is the unique increasing filtration of V with N M_a ⊂ M_{a−2} and N^a : gr^M_a V ≅ gr^M_{−a} V for all a ≥ 0; it is stable under r(W_K), so W_K acts on each gr^M_a V. An element α ∈ Ω^× is a q-Weil number of weight m if α is algebraic over Q and |τ(α)| = q^{m/2} for every field embedding τ : Q(α) → C. (V, r, N) is pure of weight w if, for every a, every eigenvalue of r(F) on gr^M_a V is a q-Weil number of weight w + a (FSY §5.3.2, geometric Frobenius). An ℓ-adic representation ρ of G_K (ℓ ≠ p) is pure of weight w if WD(ρ) is; mixed if V has an r-stable filtration with pure graded pieces.

**Hypotheses.**

- geometric Frobenius: weights are measured with F, so Q_ℓ(1) = (ω, 0) is pure of weight −2
- purity depends only on the Frobenius semisimplification

**Construction and proof.**

1. Existence and uniqueness of the monodromy filtration for a nilpotent endomorphism of a finite-dimensional vector space (Deligne, Weil II 1.6.1; Jordan normal form in characteristic 0); its r-stability follows from uniqueness because r(w)Nr(w)^{-1} is a scalar multiple of N, which has the same monodromy filtration.
2. The Weil-number condition does not depend on the choice of F: two lifts differ by inertia, which acts through a finite group on each graded piece (N = 0 there).

**Prerequisites.** `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/weil-deligne-representation`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/frobenius-semisimplification`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/grothendieck-monodromy-and-the-weil-deligne-functor`.

**Uses.**

- Fresán–Sabbah–Yu 2022, §5.3.2 and Lemma 5.40: purity of the Weil–Deligne representations of r_{k,ℓ}
- AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations:R19.3/strict-compatibility-and-the-monodromy-weight-purity: monodromy-pure local WD parameters: ker N weight w−2, coker N weight w
- WeightsInEtaleCohomology:R34.1/purity-under-restriction-and-induction: purity and Frobenius weights
- DeligneWeightsAndPurity: weight-monodromy statements consume the monodromy filtration

**API.**

- `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep.monodromyFiltration` (constructor): the monodromy filtration M_• of N, with monodromyFiltration_unique.
- `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep.monodromyFiltration_stable` (structure): M_a is r(W_K)-stable.
- `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep.IsWeilNumber` (constructor): α is a q-Weil number of weight m with respect to ι.
- `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep.IsPure` (constructor): (V, r, N) is pure of weight w.
- `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep.isPure_frobeniusSemisimplification` (characterisation): IsPure V w ↔ IsPure V^{F-ss} w.
- `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep.isPure_tensor` (compatibility): pure of weights w, w' gives tensor product pure of weight w + w'; dual pure of weight −w; twist by ω shifts the weight by −2.
- `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep.isPure_restrict` (functoriality): purity is preserved by restriction to W_L (with q_L = q^f) and by induction.
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.IsPureAt` (constructor): an ℓ-adic representation is pure of weight w at v if WD(ρ|_{G_{F_v}}) is.

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep.isPure_special_two` (computation): Sp(2) is pure of weight −1.
- `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep.isPure_omega` (computation): ω = WD(Q_ℓ(1)) is pure of weight −2 (geometric Frobenius acts by q^{-1}).
- `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep.isPure_trivial` (degenerate): The trivial one-dimensional representation is pure of weight 0.
- `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep.not_isPure_split` (non-example): (1 ⊕ ω, 0) is not pure, although its Frobenius eigenvalues are those of the pure Sp(2): purity needs N.
- `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep.monodromyFiltration_special` (characterisation): For Sp(n), gr^M_a is one-dimensional for a ∈ {−n+1, −n+3, …, n−1}.

**Acceptance.**

- Sp(2) is pure of weight −1: a geometric Frobenius acts by q^{-1} (weight −2 = −1 + (−1)) on gr^M_{−1} = ker N and by 1 (weight 0 = −1 + 1) on gr^M_1 = V/ker N; hence V_ℓ(E_q) is pure of weight −1 and V_ℓ(E_q)^∨ of weight 1.
- 1 ⊕ ω with N = 0 is not pure (weights 0 and −2 on gr_0).

**Sources.**

- fsy22, §5.3.2, arXiv v5 p. 57 (text layer): “Recall that (ρ, N) is called pure of weight w if the eigenvalues of Frobenius Fp acting on V ⩽a /V ⩽a−1 are p-Weil numbers of weight w + a for all a.” — Purity through the monodromy filtration, with the geometric Frobenius F_p.

#### A representation with pure graded Weil–Deligne representation is pure, with the same L- and ε-factors (FSY Lemma 5.40)

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/pure-graded-weil-deligne`. Kind: theorem. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/WeilDeligne/Purity`). Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2`.

Let p ≠ ℓ be primes, K/Q_p finite (FSY: K = Q_p) and r : G_K → GL(V) a continuous ℓ-adic representation with a filtration 0 = V_0 ⊂ V_1 ⊂ ⋯ ⊂ V_c = V by G_K-stable subspaces such that the Weil–Deligne representation of r̄ on V̄ = ⊕_i V_i/V_{i−1} is pure of weight w. Then WD(r) is pure of weight w, and r and r̄ have the same local L-factor and the same ε-factor: L(r, X) = L(r̄, X) and ε(WD(r), ψ, dx) = ε(WD(r̄), ψ, dx) (local-epsilon-factor).

**Hypotheses.**

- ℓ ≠ p
- the filtration is by G_K-stable subspaces; V̄ is the associated graded, not the semisimplification (though the conclusion passes to it)
- the ε-statement is for complex coefficients after an embedding ι : Q̄_ℓ → C

**Construction and proof.**

1. FSY's proof (from a referee's sketch): the ε-factor of the Weil representation ρ in (5.33) depends only on the semisimplification of r by multiplicativity (local-epsilon-factor (1)).
2. With φ = ρ(F_p), the relation Nφ = pφN shows an eigenvalue α of φ on gr^M_a gives αp^{-b} on gr^M_{a−2b} with at least the same multiplicity, 0 ≤ b ≤ a.
3. By uniqueness of the monodromy operator (grothendieck-quasi-unipotence), N restricts to the monodromy of each V_i and induces the monodromy N̄ of V̄; det(1 − φT) = det(1 − φ̄T), and purity of (ρ̄, N̄) forces the monodromy filtrations of N and N̄ to have the same graded dimensions, so (ρ, N) is pure.
4. ρ|_{ker N} and ρ̄|_{ker N̄} have the same semisimplification; taking I_p-invariants is exact on Weil representations (I_p acts through finite quotients), giving equal det(1 − φT | ker(N)^{I}) and equal det(φT | V^{I}/ker(N)^{I}); hence equal L- and ε-factors by local-euler-factor and local-epsilon-factor.

**Prerequisites.** `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/purity-of-weil-deligne-representations`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/local-euler-factor`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/local-epsilon-factor`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/grothendieck-quasi-unipotence`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/grothendieck-monodromy-and-the-weil-deligne-functor`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/frobenius-semisimplification`.

**Acceptance.**

- For the Tate curve, the filtration Q_ℓ(1) ⊂ V_ℓE_q has associated graded (1 ⊕ ω, 0), which is not pure, so the lemma does not apply; and indeed L(V_ℓE_q, X) = 1 − q^{-1}X differs from L(1 ⊕ ω, X) = (1 − X)(1 − q^{-1}X): the purity hypothesis cannot be dropped.
- FSY apply the lemma for even k to replace {r_{k,ℓ}} by its semisimplification in the functional equation.

**Sources.**

- fsy22, Lemma 5.40, arXiv v5 p. 58 (text layer): “associated with r is pure as well, and r and r̄ have the same L and ε-factors.” — Conclusion of Lemma 5.40; the hypothesis is that the Weil–Deligne representation of the graded representation of a stable filtration is pure.
- fsy22, proof of Lemma 5.40, arXiv v5 p. 58 (text layer): “Finally, observe that taking Ip -invariants is exact on Weil representations since Ip acts through finite quotients, hence the identities” — The key exactness step of the proof.

#### Deligne–Langlands local constants ε(V, ψ, dx) of Weil and Weil–Deligne representations

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/local-epsilon-factor`. Kind: construction. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/WeilDeligne/Epsilon`). Planet: **Deligne–Langlands local constants**. Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2`.

Let K be a finite extension of Q_p, ψ : K → C^× a nontrivial continuous additive character, dx a Haar measure on K, and W_K the Weil group, with local class field theory normalised as in Deligne 2.3 (Art_K : K^× ≅ W_K^{ab} sending uniformisers to GEOMETRIC Frobenius lifts; the inverse of Tau Ceti's arithmetic artinMap normalisation). (Deligne Théorème 4.1) There is a unique function ε assigning to each isomorphism class of (K, K̄, ψ, dx, V, ρ), V a finite-dimensional complex representation of W_K with open kernel on I_K, a number ε(V, ψ, dx) ∈ C^×, such that: (1) ε is multiplicative in short exact sequences (hence defined on virtual representations); (2) ε(V, ψ, a·dx) = a^{dim V}ε(V, ψ, dx), so ε(V, ψ) is defined for virtual V of dimension 0; (3) for L/K finite inside K̄ and a virtual representation V_L of W_L of dimension 0, ε(Ind_{W_L}^{W_K} V_L, ψ) = ε(V_L, ψ ∘ Tr_{L/K}); (4) for dim V = 1, given by the quasi-character χ of K^× through Art_K, ε(V, ψ, dx) is Tate's local constant ε(χ, ψ, dx) (AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors AL.1, translated from its ε(s, ω, ψ) normalisation). For a Weil–Deligne representation (V, r, N) over C: ε((V, r, N), ψ, dx) := ε(r, ψ, dx)·det(−r(Φ) | V^{r(I_K)}/(ker N)^{r(I_K)}) with Φ a geometric Frobenius lift (equivalently Deligne (8.12.4) ε = ε_0(r)·det(−F | V^I)^{-1}, V^I = (ker N)^{r(I)}); with the s-variable, ε(V, s) = ε(V ⊗ ω_s) (FSY (5.31)–(5.33)). For an ℓ-adic representation ρ (ℓ ≠ p) and ι : Q̄_ℓ ≅ C, ε(ρ, ψ, dx) := ε(ι WD(ρ), ψ, dx); it depends only on the Frobenius semisimplification and its ε_0-part only on the semisimplification.

**Hypotheses.**

- K of characteristic 0 (finite over Q_p): the Tau Ceti reciprocity isomorphism of ClassFieldTheory layer 9 is available only there; Deligne's theorem itself also covers archimedean and equal-characteristic local fields, which are recorded as a gap
- normalisation of local class field theory: uniformiser ↔ geometric Frobenius (Deligne 2.3, CG18); Tau Ceti's artinMap must be inverted
- uniqueness is local (Brauer induction); existence (Deligne §4) is global and uses Artin L-functions of number fields, whose functional equation has no owner (gap)

**Construction and proof.**

1. Uniqueness: every irreducible representation of W_K is r_0 ⊗ χ with r_0 of finite image (Deligne 4.10) and the finite-image part factors through Gal(L/K) for L/K finite Galois; Brauer's induction theorem (Tau Ceti InductionRestriction layer 6) writes any virtual representation of a finite group as a Z-combination of representations induced from one-dimensional characters of subgroups; (1), (3), (4) then determine ε (Deligne 4.1–4.3).
2. Reduction for existence: Deligne 4.10–4.11 reduce by the type decomposition to the existence of an α-theory of constants for each finite Galois K'/K and each quasi-character α (4.9 (*)).
3. Existence (Deligne 4.12–4.16): globalise K'/K as the completion of a Galois extension of number fields at a non-split place (Lemme 4.13, Krasner and weak approximation), choose an idele class character with prescribed ramification (Lemme 4.14), and define the local constant at v as the global constant of 3.12 (functional equation of Artin L-functions, from Brauer induction and Hecke's functional equation, AL.1/hecke-l-functional-equation) divided by the product of the local constants at the other places, known by induction on ramification (Lemmes 4.15, 4.16 for unramified and highly ramified twists).
4. Weil–Deligne extension: the factor det(−r(Φ) | V^{I}/(ker N)^{I}) is multiplicative on Frobenius semisimplifications; FSY (5.33) and Deligne (8.12.4) agree because Deligne's ε_0(r) = ε(r)·det(−r(Φ) | V^{r(I)}) (Deligne (3.4.3.3) for characters).

**Prerequisites.** `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/weil-deligne-representation`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/frobenius-semisimplification`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/local-factor-of-induced-representation`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/grothendieck-monodromy-and-the-weil-deligne-functor`; `AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors:AL.1/local-epsilon-gamma-factors`; `AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors:AL.1/explicit-epsilon-factors`; `AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors:AL.1/local-quasicharacter-conductor`; `AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors:AL.1/hecke-l-functional-equation`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/InductionRestriction#layer-6-the-virtual-character-ring-artin-and-brauer-induction`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ClassFieldTheory#layer-9-the-local-weil-group`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ClassFieldTheory#layer-7-the-absolute-local-artin-map-its-normalizations-and-conductors`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/LocalFieldsRamification#layer-0-local-fields-and-their-finite-extensions`.

**Uses.**

- Fresán–Sabbah–Yu 2022, §5.3.1: ε((ρ,N), s) = ε_0(ρ,s)·ε_1((ρ,N),s) for the local factors of the Kloosterman motives; global ε_k(s) as a product
- Fresán–Sabbah–Yu 2022, Lemma 5.40: r and r̄ have the same ε-factors
- AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations:R19.4/hecke-versus-langlands-normalization-and-local-global-compatibility: ε(χ·σ̌(π_p)) = ε(χ·ω_p^{1/2}·π_p) characterises σ(π_p)
- EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison:ET.6: L/ε-factor compatibility of the local Langlands correspondence; local constants on the Weil–Deligne side
- GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer:R16.3: rank-two L/ε factors of the local correspondence

**API.**

- `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep.epsilonWeil` (constructor): ε(V, ψ, dx) ∈ C^× for complex representations of W_K with open kernel on I_K.
- `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep.epsilonWeil_exact` (simp): multiplicativity in short exact sequences; extension to the Grothendieck group.
- `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep.epsilonWeil_smul_measure` (simp): ε(V, ψ, a dx) = a^{dim V} ε(V, ψ, dx).
- `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep.epsilonWeil_induced` (functoriality): ε(Ind V_L, ψ) = ε(V_L, ψ ∘ Tr_{L/K}) for virtual V_L of dimension 0.
- `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep.epsilonWeil_character` (compatibility): for dim V = 1, ε equals Tate's local constant of the quasi-character χ = V ∘ Art_K (AL.1/local-epsilon-gamma-factors, after converting ε(s, ω, ψ) with s = 1/2 normalisation and self-dual dx).
- `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep.epsilonWeil_unique` (universal-property): any function satisfying (1)–(4) equals epsilonWeil.
- `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep.epsilon` (constructor): ε((V, r, N), ψ, dx) = ε(r, ψ, dx)·det(−r(Φ) | V^{I}/(ker N)^{I}).
- `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep.epsilon_frobeniusSemisimplification` (relation): ε depends only on the Frobenius semisimplification; ε(r, ψ, dx) depends only on the semisimplification.
- `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep.epsilon_unramified_twist` (relation): ε(V ⊗ ω_s, ψ, dx) = q^{−(a(V) + n(ψ)dim V)s}ε(V, ψ, dx), a(V) the Artin conductor (R01.3).
- `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep.epsilon_dual` (relation): ε(V, ψ, dx)ε(V^∨ ⊗ ω, ψ(−x), dx') = 1 for dual Haar measures dx, dx' (Deligne 5.7).

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep.epsilon_unramified_character` (computation): ε(χ, ψ, dx) = 1 for χ unramified, n(ψ) = 0, vol(O_K) = 1.
- `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep.epsilon_special_two` (computation): ε(Sp(2), ψ, dx) = −1 under the same normalisations.
- `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep.epsilon_zero` (degenerate): ε(0, ψ, dx) = 1.
- `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep.epsilon_not_weil_part` (non-example): ε(Sp(2)) ≠ ε(1 ⊕ ω) = 1: the Weil–Deligne correction det(−Φ | V^I/(ker N)^I) cannot be dropped.
- `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep.epsilon_eq_tate` (compatibility): For a ramified character χ, epsilonWeil agrees with AL.1's explicit formula ε(s, χ, ψ) = χ(ϖ^{ν+c})q^{(1/2−s)(ν+c)}𝔤(χ, ψ) at the corresponding s and measure.

**Acceptance.**

- For an unramified character χ with n(ψ) = 0 and ∫_{O_K} dx = 1, ε(χ, ψ, dx) = 1 (Deligne (3.4.3.1)); for the WD representation Sp(2) = (1 ⊕ ω, N), ε(Sp(2), ψ, dx) = ε(1)ε(ω)·det(−r(Φ) | V/ker N) = −1 (Φ acts by 1 on V/ker N).
- Unramified twists: ε(χω, ψ, dx) = ω(π^{n(ψ)+a(χ)})ε(χ, ψ, dx) for ω unramified (Deligne (3.4.3.5)), which must agree with AL.1's ε(s, ω, ψ) = ω(ϖ^ν)q^{(1/2−s)ν} after the change of normalisation.

**Sources.**

- deligne73-constantes, Théorème 4.1, Del-35, printed p. 535 (read on the page image): “Il existe une et une seule fonction ε, vérifiant les conditions (1) à (4) ci-dessous, qui associe un nombre ε(V,ψ,dx) ∈ C* à chaque classe d'isomorphie de sextuples (K, K̄, ψ, dx, V, ρ)” — Existence and uniqueness of local constants of complex representations of the Weil group.
- deligne73-constantes, Théorème 4.1 (3), Del-35, printed p. 535 (read on the page image): “(3) Si L est une extension séparable finie de K dans K̄ et que V_K est la représentation virtuelle de W(K̄/K) induite par une représentation virtuelle de dimension zéro V_L de W(K̄/L), on a” — Inductivity in degree zero: ε(V_K, ψ) = ε(V_L, ψ ∘ Tr_{L/K}).

- deligne73-constantes, Lemme 4.12, Del-44, printed p. 544 (text layer): “Soit K'/K une extension galoisienne de corps globaux.” — The existence proof is global: it passes through Galois extensions of global fields and the global constants of 3.12.
- deligne73-constantes, 3.12 (A)-(C), Del-33, printed p. 533 (read on the page image): “(A) et (B) se démontrent par réduction au cas où dim V = 1, via le théorème de Brauer.” — The global functional equation of Artin L-functions used in §4 comes from Brauer induction and Hecke's functional equation.
- fsy22, §5.3.1, arXiv v5 p. 54 (text layer): “the local ε-factor of the Weil-Deligne representation (ρ, N) defined in [10, above Rem. 5.2.1] is equal to the product” — ε((ρ,N),s) = ε_0(ρ,s)·det(−p^{−s}F_p | V^{ρ(I_p)}/ker(N)^{ρ(I_p)}) (5.33); FSY's ε_0 is Deligne's ε of the Weil representation (Th. 4.1), not Deligne's ε_0 of (3.4.3.3).
- deligne73-constantes, 2.3, Del-23, printed p. 523 (read on the page image): “de telle sorte que les Frobenius géométriques correspondent aux uniformisantes.” — Deligne normalises local class field theory so that uniformisers go to GEOMETRIC Frobenius elements; the Tau Ceti artinMap normalisation must be converted.

#### Required examples: the cyclotomic character, an unramified character, and the Tate curve

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/weil-deligne-required-examples`. Kind: application. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/WeilDeligne/Examples`). Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2`.

Let K/Q_p be finite with residue cardinality q, ℓ ≠ p, Φ an arithmetic and F = Φ^{-1} a geometric Frobenius lift. (1) Cyclotomic: WD(Q_ℓ(1)) = (ω, 0) with ω(Φ) = q; P(χ_ℓ, X) = X − q, L(Q_ℓ(1), X) = 1 − q^{-1}X, pure of weight −2; for K = Q_p and p ≠ ℓ this is the place-p component of χ_ℓ of G_Q. (2) Unramified character: for α ∈ O_E^×, WD(λ(α)) = (λ_W(α), 0), L(λ(α), X) = 1 − α^{-1}X, and λ^{geom}(γ) = λ(γ^{-1}). (3) Tate curve: for q_E ∈ K^× with v(q_E) > 0 and E = E_{q_E} the Tate curve, V_ℓE sits in 0 → Q_ℓ(1) → V_ℓE → Q_ℓ → 0, ρ(I_K) is infinite, and WD(V_ℓE) ≅ Sp(2) = (1 ⊕ ω, N) with N ≠ 0 mapping the quotient onto ker N = Q_ℓ(1) (N is v(q_E) times a generator, up to the scaling of Lemme 8.4.3); it is Frobenius-semisimple, not semisimple; its Frobenius semisimplification is itself and its semisimplification is (1 ⊕ ω, 0); L(V_ℓE, X) = 1 − q^{-1}X, L(V_ℓE^∨, X) = 1 − X; it is pure of weight −1 (V_ℓE^∨ = H^1 of weight 1); the non-split twist by the unramified quadratic character η gives Sp(2) ⊗ η with L(V^∨, X) = 1 + X. (4) For ℓ | v(q_E) the residual E[ℓ] is unramified while V_ℓE is not.

**Hypotheses.**

- the Tate curve and its Tate module are owned by Tau Ceti EllipticCurves layer 4 and R01.6; this node computes their Weil–Deligne data
- ℓ ≠ p

**Construction and proof.**

1. (1): cyclotomic-and-dirichlet-characters (b) and grothendieck-monodromy-and-the-weil-deligne-functor (unramified case).
2. (2): unramified-character-lambda and the unramified case of the functor.

(3): the Tate parametrisation K̄^×/q_E^Z ≅ E(K̄) (EllipticCurves layer 4) gives E[ℓ^n] as an extension of Z/ℓ^n by μ_{ℓ^n} whose extension class is the Kummer class of q_E; σ ∈ I_K acts by e_2 ↦ e_2 + v(q_E)t_ℓ(σ)e_1 (Kummer theory with t_ℓ), so ρ(σ) = exp(t_ℓ(σ)N) with N e_2 = v(q_E)e_1; Frobenius acts by q on e_1 and by 1 on the quotient; then local-euler-factor, purity-of-weil-deligne-representations, frobenius-semisimplification.
