#### Complex conjugations and odd rank-two representations

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/odd-representation`. Kind: definition. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.GaloisRep` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/ResidualImage/Oddness.lean`). Planet: **Odd representation**. Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4`.

Let F be a number field, F̄ an algebraic closure and G_F = Field.absoluteGaloisGroup F with its Krull topology. (1) Complex conjugations. For a real infinite place v of F (NumberField.InfinitePlace.IsReal) and a field embedding ι : F̄ → ℂ whose restriction to F is a real embedding inducing v, the image ι(F̄) is stable under complex conjugation conj = Complex.conjAe, and c_ι := ι⁻¹ ∘ conj ∘ ι ∈ G_F. Then c_ι² = 1, c_ι ≠ 1, and for two such embeddings ι, ι′ above the same v the elements c_ι, c_ι′ are conjugate in G_F; write c_v for this conjugacy class. (2) Totally odd characters. A continuous character μ : G_F → A^× with values in a topological commutative ring A is totally odd if μ(c_v) = −1 for every real place v of F (the condition does not depend on the choice of c_v in its class). (3) Odd representations. Let A be a topological commutative ring and ρ ∈ ContinuousRep G_F A M with M finite projective of rank 2 over A (R01.1/continuous-representation). ρ is odd at the real place v if det_A ρ(c_v) = −1 in A, and odd (totally odd) if it is odd at every real place of F, i.e. if det ρ is totally odd. For F = ℚ there is exactly one real place and c is any complex conjugation. When F has no real place every ρ is odd. Pinned conventions: (a) oddness depends only on the character det ρ; (b) if A is a field of characteristic ≠ 2, ρ is odd at v iff Tr ρ(c_v) = 0 iff ρ(c_v) is conjugate to diag(1, −1); (c) if 2 = 0 in A (for instance A = k a finite field of characteristic 2) then det ρ(c_v) = ±1 = 1 = −1 and every rank-two ρ is odd; the condition ‘ρ(c_v) ≠ 1’ used in characteristic two is a separate condition, named non-trivial at v, and is never part of oddness.

**Hypotheses.**

- F is a number field; G_F carries the Krull topology
- A is a topological commutative ring and M a finite projective A-module of rank 2 (free of rank 2 in framed coordinates)
- c_v is well defined only up to conjugacy in G_F; every statement is conjugation invariant
- in characteristic two oddness is automatic; ρ(c) ≠ 1 is a separate hypothesis

**Construction and proof.**

1. Since ι|_F lands in ℝ, conj fixes ι(F) and preserves the algebraic closure ι(F̄) of ι(F) in ℂ, so c_ι is an F-automorphism of F̄; c_ι² = 1 because conj² = 1, and c_ι ≠ 1 because F̄ is not contained in ℝ (it contains √−1).
2. Two embeddings above v differ by an element g ∈ G_F (ι′ = ι ∘ g after composing with conj if necessary, using that the real embedding is fixed by conj), so c_ι′ = g⁻¹ c_ι g.
3. det ρ is a continuous character G_F → A^× (determinant of a finite projective module of rank 2), so det ρ(c_v) is well defined on the class c_v; oddness of ρ is total oddness of det ρ.
4. If A is a field with char A ≠ 2, ρ(c_v)² = 1 forces ρ(c_v) to be diagonalisable with eigenvalues in {±1}; the determinant is −1 exactly when the eigenvalues are 1 and −1, exactly when the trace is 0 (traces of ±1 are ±2 ≠ 0).
5. Serre 1987, 1.3 fixes the convention det ρ(c) = −1 for G_ℚ; Khare–Wintenberger I §1 define S-type with ‘det ρ̄(c) = −1 for c a complex conjugation’.

**Prerequisites.** `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/continuous-representation`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/coefficient-extension`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/restriction-dual-tensor-twist`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/integral-model`; `mathlib:Field.absoluteGaloisGroup`; `mathlib:NumberField.InfinitePlace`; `mathlib:NumberField.InfinitePlace.IsReal`; `mathlib:NumberField.ComplexEmbedding.IsReal`; `mathlib:Complex.conjAe`; `mathlib:Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.det`; `mathlib:LinearMap.det`; `mathlib:cyclotomicCharacter`.

**Uses.**

- Khare–Wintenberger I, §1 (S-type representations): S-type = continuous, absolutely irreducible, odd ρ̄ : G_ℚ → GL_2(F)
- Serre 1987, 3.3: det ρ = χ makes det ρ(c) = −1, which upgrades irreducibility to absolute irreducibility for p ≠ 2
- SmallRamificationAndAbelianVarietyBaseCases:R25.2/level-one-residual-representation: condition (b): det ρ̄(c) = −1 for a complex conjugation
- GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer:R17.5/octahedral-mod-three-application: odd ρ̄ : G_ℚ → GL_2(F_3) with det ρ̄(c) = −1 lifted through GL_2(ℤ[√−2])
- PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:R24.6/residual-members: residual members of an odd compatible system are odd (det reduces)
- Allen et al. 2023, §1.2: totally odd characters of G_K for K totally real
- GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer:R17.6/wiese-odd-lift: oddness is vacuous in characteristic two; the lift is required to be odd in characteristic 0

**API.**

- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.complexConjugation` (constructor): For a real place v and an embedding ι : F̄ → ℂ above v, the element c_ι = ι⁻¹ ∘ conj ∘ ι of G_F.
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.complexConjugation_sq` (simp): c_ι² = 1 and c_ι ≠ 1; its order is 2.
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.isConj_complexConjugation` (characterisation): Two complex conjugations above the same real place are conjugate in G_F.
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.IsTotallyOddChar` (data): A continuous character μ : G_F → A^× is totally odd iff μ(c_v) = −1 for every real place v.
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.IsOddAt` (data): ρ is odd at v iff det ρ(c_v) = −1; IsOdd ρ iff IsOddAt ρ v for all real v, iff IsTotallyOddChar (det ρ).
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.isOdd_tensor_character` (compatibility): ρ ⊗ ψ is odd iff ρ is odd, for any continuous character ψ (det(ρ ⊗ ψ)(c) = det ρ(c) ψ(c)² and ψ(c)² = 1).
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.isOdd_baseChange` (functoriality): If ρ is odd then ρ ⊗_A B is odd for every continuous ring map A → B; the converse holds when 2 ≠ 0 in B and A → B is injective on {±1}.
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.isOdd_restrict` (functoriality): For F′/F finite, every complex conjugation of F′ at a real place w is a complex conjugation of F at w|_F, so ρ odd ⇒ ρ|_{G_{F′}} odd.
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.IsNontrivialAt` (other): ρ is non-trivial at v iff ρ(c_v) ≠ 1; in characteristic 2 this is the separate condition used instead of oddness.
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.isOdd_iff_conj_diag` (characterisation): Over a field of characteristic ≠ 2, ρ is odd at v iff ρ(c_v) is conjugate to diag(1, −1).

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.isOdd_cyclotomic_sum_one` (computation): For an odd prime p, the representation χ̄_p ⊕ 1 : G_ℚ → GL_2(F_p) is odd: det(c) = χ̄_p(c) = −1.
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.not_isOdd_of_scalar_minus_one` (non-example): Over F_5 the representation χ_{−3} ⊕ χ_{−4} of G_ℚ has ρ(c) = −1 ≠ 1 and det ρ(c) = 1, so it is not odd; the tempting definition ‘ρ(c) ≠ 1’ accepts it.
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.isOdd_of_charTwo` (degenerate): If 2 = 0 in A then every rank-two ρ is odd; in particular the trivial representation of G_ℚ on F_2² is odd although ρ(c) = 1.
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.isOdd_iff_trace_eq_zero` (characterisation): For a field A of characteristic ≠ 2, ρ is odd at v iff Tr ρ(c_v) = 0.
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.isOdd_reduction_iff` (compatibility): For a Γ-stable O_E-lattice with residue characteristic p ≠ 2, ρ is odd iff its reduction ρ̄ is odd (±1 reduce injectively); for p = 2 only ρ odd ⇒ ρ̄ odd holds, and ρ̄ is always odd.

**Acceptance.**

- For p odd and χ̄_p : G_ℚ → F_p^× the mod-p cyclotomic character, χ̄_p ⊕ 1 is odd since c acts on μ_p by inversion; any ρ̄ with det ρ̄ = χ̄_p is odd (the case of E[p], R01.6/determinant-and-oddness).
- Over F_5, ρ = χ_{−3} ⊕ χ_{−4} (quadratic characters of ℚ(√−3), ℚ(i)) has ρ(c) = −1 ≠ 1 but det ρ(c) = 1, so it is not odd: ‘ρ(c) ≠ 1’ is not oddness.
- In characteristic two the trivial representation of G_ℚ on F_2² is odd but not non-trivial at c; the representation of G_ℚ on E[2] for E : y² = x³ − 2 is odd and non-trivial at c (c is a transposition of the three roots of x³ − 2).

#### Odd irreducible residual representations are absolutely irreducible (odd p), and the characteristic-two case

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/odd-irreducible-implies-absolutely-irreducible`. Kind: theorem. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.GaloisRep` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/ResidualImage/AbsolutelyIrreducible.lean`). Planet: **Oddness and absolute irreducibility**. Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4`.

(a) Rationality lemma. Let k be a field, Γ a group and ρ : Γ → GL_2(k). Suppose ρ(Γ) contains a non-scalar element g whose characteristic polynomial splits over k. Then every ρ(Γ)-stable line of k′² (k′/k any field extension) is k-rational; hence ρ is irreducible iff ρ ⊗_k k′ is irreducible, and ρ is irreducible iff it is absolutely irreducible (R01.1/absolutely-irreducible). (b) Odd p. Let F be a number field with a real place v, k a field of characteristic ≠ 2 (for example a finite field of odd characteristic p), and ρ̄ : G_F → GL_2(k) continuous and odd at v. If ρ̄ is irreducible over k then it is absolutely irreducible. In particular for p odd an odd ρ̄ : G_ℚ → GL_2(F_p) irreducible over F_p is absolutely irreducible. (c) Characteristic two. Let k have characteristic 2 and ρ̄ : G_F → GL_2(k) continuous. If ρ̄(c_v) ≠ 1 for some real place v, irreducible implies absolutely irreducible (ρ̄(c_v) is a transvection with a unique, k-rational, invariant line). Without that hypothesis the implication fails: for a cyclic cubic field L/ℚ (for instance the real subfield of ℚ(ζ_7)) and a generator σ of Gal(L/ℚ), the representation G_ℚ → Gal(L/ℚ) → GL_2(F_2), σ ↦ [[0, 1], [1, 1]] (companion matrix of x² + x + 1), is odd (characteristic 2), has image of order 3, is irreducible over F_2 and becomes reducible over F_4 = F_2(ω), where it is ω^a ⊕ ω^{2a}.

**Hypotheses.**

- (a) needs only one non-scalar element with split characteristic polynomial; no finiteness or continuity
- (b) needs char k ≠ 2: then ρ̄(c_v) has the distinct eigenvalues 1 and −1 in k
- (c) needs ρ̄(c_v) ≠ 1; oddness itself carries no information in characteristic 2

**Construction and proof.**

1. (a) If g is non-scalar with split characteristic polynomial, either g has two distinct eigenvalues in k (exactly two invariant lines over k′, both k-rational) or one eigenvalue λ ∈ k with g − λ nilpotent of rank 1 (exactly one invariant line ker(g − λ), k-rational). A ρ(Γ)-stable line of k′² is g-stable, hence one of these, hence k-rational and already ρ(Γ)-stable over k.
2. (b) det ρ̄(c_v) = −1 and ρ̄(c_v)² = 1 give eigenvalues 1 and −1, distinct since char k ≠ 2, so g = ρ̄(c_v) satisfies (a). This is Serre 1987, 3.3 (b′); Serre's sentence treats only a decomposition over F̄_p into a direct sum of two lines, while (a) also covers a reducible but indecomposable ρ̄ ⊗ F̄_p (its unique stable line is ρ̄(c)-stable, hence an eigenline of ρ̄(c), hence F_p-rational); see sourceIssues.
3. (c) In characteristic 2, ρ̄(c_v)² = 1 and ρ̄(c_v) ≠ 1 force ρ̄(c_v) = 1 + n with n² = 0, n ≠ 0, a transvection; (a) applies. In the counterexample the image is generated by an element of order 3 with irreducible characteristic polynomial x² + x + 1 over F_2; over F_4 its eigenlines are stable, and complex conjugation acts trivially because L is totally real.
4. The reduction of finite images: a continuous ρ̄ with discrete finite coefficients has finite image (R01.1/finite-coefficients-and-finite-quotients), so ρ̄(c_v) is a genuine element of a finite group.

**Prerequisites.** `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/odd-representation`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/absolutely-irreducible`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/finite-coefficients-and-finite-quotients`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/coefficient-extension`; `tauceti:TauCeti.GL2Borel.exists_det_sub_algebraMap_eq_zero`; `mathlib:Representation.IsIrreducible`.

**Acceptance.**

- Instance (Serre 1987, 3.3): for p odd, ρ : G_ℚ → GL_2(F_p) with det ρ = χ̄_p (the mod-p cyclotomic character) is odd, so irreducible over F_p implies absolutely irreducible; this is the input of EllipticCurveModularity:R29.1 for E[p].
- Non-example in characteristic 2 (statement (c)): the cyclic-cubic representation over F_2 with image of order 3 is odd, irreducible over F_2 and not absolutely irreducible.
- Positive characteristic-two instance: E[2] for E : y² = x³ − 2 has image GL_2(F_2) ≅ S_3 with ρ̄(c) a transvection; it is irreducible and absolutely irreducible.
- Oddness is needed in odd characteristic too: over F_5 the cyclic-cubic representation σ ↦ [[0, −1], [1, −1]] (characteristic polynomial x² + x + 1, irreducible over F_5) has image of order 3, is irreducible over F_5, splits over F_25, and is even (ρ̄(c) = 1).

**Sources.**

En effet, (a) entraine que det rho est impair, donc que les valeurs propres de rho(c) sont +1 et -1; du fait que p != 2, ces valeurs propres sont distinctes.” — The statement (b) of this node for G_ℚ and det ρ = χ (reused verified excerpt).

#### Dickson's classification of finite subgroups of PGL_2(F̄_p), with the coefficient field visible, its consequences and the p = 2 refinement

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/dickson-classification-and-the-dyadic-refinement`. Kind: theorem. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.GL2Subgroup` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/ResidualImage/Dickson.lean`). Planet: **Dickson's classification**. Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4`.

Let p be a prime, k̄ an algebraic closure of F_p (discrete), π : GL_2(k̄) → PGL_2(k̄) = Matrix.ProjGenLinGroup (Fin 2) k̄ the projection, and F_q ⊂ k̄ the subfield with q elements. (a) [Dickson] Every finite subgroup H ⊂ PGL_2(k̄) satisfies one of: (i) H fixes a point of P¹(k̄), i.e. is conjugate into the image of the upper-triangular Borel; (ii) H is conjugate to PSL_2(F_q) or PGL_2(F_q) for some power q of p; (iii) H is isomorphic to A_4, S_4, A_5, or to the dihedral group of order 2n (Mathlib DihedralGroup n) for some n ≥ 2 with p ∤ n. For q ≥ 4 all subgroups of PGL_2(k̄) isomorphic to PSL_2(F_q) are conjugate, and likewise for PGL_2(F_q). Elements of A_4, S_4, A_5 have order 1, 2, 3, 4 or 5; PSL_2(F_q) is simple for q ≥ 4. (b) [GL_2 form, coefficient field visible] Let k ⊂ k̄ be a finite field and G ⊂ GL_2(k) a subgroup acting absolutely irreducibly on k̄². Then π(G) is not cyclic and fixes no point of P¹(k̄), and either π(G) is dihedral of order 2n (n ≥ 2, p ∤ n), or π(G) ≅ A_4, S_4 or A_5, or π(G) is conjugate in PGL_2(k̄) to PSL_2(F_0) or PGL_2(F_0) where F_0 ⊂ k is the subfield generated by the values Tr(g)²/det(g), g ∈ G. (c) [linear form] If π(G) is conjugate to PSL_2(F_0) or PGL_2(F_0) with |F_0| ≥ 4, then after conjugation in GL_2(k̄) the commutator subgroup [G, G] equals SL_2(F_0) and G ⊂ k̄^× · GL_2(F_0); the abelianisation of π(G) has order 1 (PSL_2) or gcd(2, |F_0| − 1) (PGL_2). Conversely if G ⊃ SL_2(F_1) for a subfield F_1 with |F_1| ≥ 4, then π(G) is conjugate to PSL_2(F_0) or PGL_2(F_0) for a field F_0 ⊃ F_1; in particular for p ≥ 5 and G ⊃ SL_2(F_p) the projective image is PSL_2(F_{p^s}) or PGL_2(F_{p^s}) and its abelianisation has order ≤ 2. (d) [p = 2, Khare–Wintenberger I Lemma 6.1] If p = 2 and G ⊂ GL_2(F̄_2) is finite, irreducible and solvable, then π(G) is dihedral of order 2n with n odd ≥ 3 (S_4 does not occur; A_4 occurs only as the Borel subgroup of PGL_2(F_4) and is reducible). If G is irreducible and not solvable, π(G) is conjugate to PGL_2(F_0) = PSL_2(F_0) ≅ SL_2(F_0) with |F_0| = 2^r, r ≥ 2. (e) [order criteria] If G is irreducible and π(G) contains an element of order > 5, then π(G) is not exceptional; if moreover G is solvable, π(G) is dihedral; if G is irreducible, π(G) contains an element of order > 5 and π(G) normalises no Cartan (equivalently G is not contained in the normaliser of a torus), then G contains a conjugate of SL_2(F_p) (Clozel–Thorne Lemma 7.5).

**Hypotheses.**

- k̄ = F̄_p with the discrete topology; all groups finite
- (b)–(e) concern subgroups of GL_2 over finite fields of characteristic p; absolute irreducibility means irreducibility on k̄²
- the simplicity of PSL_2(F_0) and perfectness of SL_2(F_0) need |F_0| ≥ 4
- (a) is Dickson's theorem, quoted from Dickson 1901 §§255–260 through Darmon–Diamond–Taylor Theorem 2.47(b); its proof is sketched, not decomposed

**Construction and proof.**

1. (a) Dickson 1901 §260 lists the subgroups of LF(2, s) = PSL_2(F_s) and §261 proves simplicity for s > 3; DDT Theorem 2.47(b) states the PGL_2(F̄_ℓ) form used by the consumers. Sketch: a finite H lies in PGL_2(F_s) ⊂ PSL_2(F_{s²}). If p ∤ |H|, lift H to characteristic 0 (Serre 1972 Prop. 16, method 2) and use the finite subgroups of SO_3(ℝ): cyclic, dihedral, A_4, S_4, A_5. If p | |H|, the p-elements are unipotent with unique fixed points (R01.4/p-subgroups-and-borel-subgroups); one Sylow p-subgroup gives (i), two with distinct fixed points generate PSL_2 of the field generated by the products of their parameters (Serre 1972 Prop. 15 over F_p, Dickson §§249–255 in general), and its normaliser is PGL_2 of that field.
2. (b) A cyclic π(G) makes G abelian (a central extension of a cyclic group), so G has a common eigenvector over k̄ (tauceti:TauCeti.exists_unitHom_jointEigenvector_of_pairwise_commute_of_isAlgClosed), contradicting absolute irreducibility; a fixed point of π(G) is a G-stable line. The function g ↦ Tr(g)²/det(g) is a class function on PGL_2, so its values on π(G) ⊂ PGL_2(k) lie in k; on PSL_2(F_0) it takes every square of F_0 (companion matrices), and the squares of F_0 generate F_0, so F_0 ⊂ k.
3. (c) Scalars are central, so [λA, μB] = [A, B] and [G, G] ⊂ [GL_2(F_0), GL_2(F_0)] = SL_2(F_0); [G, G] maps onto [π(G), π(G)] ⊇ PSL_2(F_0) (perfect, mathlib:SL2Simple.PSL_commutator_eq_top), so [G,G]·{±1} = SL_2(F_0), and perfectness of SL_2(F_0) (mathlib:Matrix.SL2.commutator_eq_top) gives [G,G] = SL_2(F_0). Conversely PSL_2(F_1) ⊂ π(G) is non-solvable (mathlib:Group.IsPerfect.not_isSolvable), so π(G) is not Borel, dihedral, A_4, S_4; if π(G) ≅ A_5 then π(G) = PSL_2(F_1) with |F_1| ∈ {4, 5}; otherwise (a)(ii), and F_0 ⊃ F_1 by the trace-field argument of (b). PGL_2(F_0)^{ab} = F_0^×/F_0^{×2} via det.
4. (d) As in Khare–Wintenberger I Lemma 6.1: a 2-element of GL_2(F̄_2) is unipotent of order ≤ 2, so S_4 (elements of order 4) is excluded; the normal Klein subgroup of A_4 lies in a unipotent Sylow 2-subgroup (R01.4/p-subgroups-and-borel-subgroups), whose unique fixed line is G-stable. Dihedral of even n contains a central involution, i.e. a normal 2-subgroup, again fixing a line; so n is odd. Non-solvable: (a) leaves PSL_2(F_0) = PGL_2(F_0) (char 2) with |F_0| ≥ 4; PGL_2(F̄_2) ≅ SL_2(F̄_2) via mathlib:Matrix.ProjectiveSpecialLinearGroup.isoPSLOfAlgClosed and SL_2 = PSL_2 in characteristic 2.
5. (e) A_4, S_4, A_5 have no element of order > 5 (Serre 1972 Prop. 16); solvable irreducible images not exceptional are dihedral by (a); in the last case (a) leaves PSL_2/PGL_2(F_{p^a}) and (c) gives SL_2(F_{p^a}) ⊃ SL_2(F_p).

**Prerequisites.** `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/p-subgroups-and-borel-subgroups`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/subgroups-of-gl2-over-a-prime-field`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/absolutely-irreducible`; `mathlib:Matrix.ProjGenLinGroup`; `mathlib:Matrix.ProjectiveSpecialLinearGroup`; `mathlib:Matrix.ProjectiveSpecialLinearGroup.toPGL`; `mathlib:Matrix.ProjectiveSpecialLinearGroup.isoPSLOfAlgClosed`; `mathlib:Matrix.ProjectiveSpecialLinearGroup.rank_two_simple`; `mathlib:Matrix.SL2.commutator_eq_top`; `mathlib:SL2Simple.PSL_commutator_eq_top`; `mathlib:Group.IsPerfect.not_isSolvable`; `mathlib:DihedralGroup`; `mathlib:alternatingGroup`; `mathlib:Equiv.Perm`; `mathlib:Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.center_eq_range_scalar`; `tauceti:TauCeti.exists_unitHom_jointEigenvector_of_pairwise_commute_of_isAlgClosed`; `tauceti:TauCeti.Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.not_isSolvable_fin_two`.

**Acceptance.**

- Check the exclusion of A_4 in characteristic 2 by exhibiting the normal Klein subgroup inside the unipotent radical of the Borel of SL_2(F_4) ≅ A_5, and check that over F̄_3 the irreducible group SL_2(F_3) has projective image PSL_2(F_3) ≅ A_4, so the dyadic refinement is genuinely characteristic 2.
- Projective images in practice: S_3 ≅ GL_2(F_2) = PGL_2(F_2) (dihedral of order 6, from E[2] of y² = x³ − 2); A_4 ≅ PSL_2(F_3) and S_4 ≅ PGL_2(F_3) (from SL_2(F_3) ⊂ GL_2(F_3) = image of E[3] for a non-CM E with surjective mod-3 image); A_5 ≅ PSL_2(F_5) ≅ SL_2(F_4) (from SL_2(F_5) ⊂ GL_2(F_5)).
- For G = GL_2(F_9) ⊂ GL_2(F̄_3): F_0 = F_9 by (b); G = μ_8 · SL_2(F_9) has [G, G] = SL_2(F_9) by (c).
- A_5 ⊂ PGL_2(F_p) for p ≠ 2, 5 occurs only for p ≡ ±1 mod 5 (Serre 1972 2.6(iii)); for p = 7 the projective image of a subgroup of GL_2(F_7) is never A_5.

#### Subgroups of GL_2(F_ℓ): Serre's Propositions 15–18

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/subgroups-of-gl2-over-a-prime-field`. Kind: theorem. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.GL2Subgroup` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/ResidualImage/PrimeField.lean`). Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4`.

Let ℓ be a prime, V a two-dimensional F_ℓ-vector space and G ⊂ GL(V) ≅ GL_2(F_ℓ) a subgroup. (a) [Serre 1972 Prop. 15] If ℓ divides |G| then G contains SL(V) or G is contained in a Borel subgroup. (b) [Prop. 16 and 2.6] If ℓ ∤ |G|, let H = π(G) ⊂ PGL(V). Then H is cyclic and G lies in a Cartan subgroup, or H is dihedral and G lies in the normaliser of a Cartan subgroup (and not in the Cartan subgroup when H is non-cyclic), or H ≅ A_4, S_4 or A_5, the last only if ℓ ≡ ±1 mod 5; for ℓ = 2, 3 only the first two occur. Every finite subgroup of PGL_2(K) of order prime to char K, K any field, is cyclic, dihedral, A_4, S_4 or A_5. (c) Hence (the form used by Deligne–Serre 7.2): if G acts semisimply on V, then G contains SL(V), or lies in a Cartan subgroup, or lies in the normaliser of a Cartan subgroup but not in it, or π(G) ≅ A_4, S_4, A_5; the reducible semisimple case is the split-Cartan case. (d) [Prop. 17] If G contains a Cartan subgroup C (resp. a split half-Cartan C′) and ℓ ≠ 5 when C is split, then G = GL(V), or G lies in a Borel subgroup, or G lies in the normaliser of a Cartan subgroup. (e) [Prop. 18] If ℓ ≠ 2, G contains a Cartan subgroup or a split half-Cartan, and G is normal in GL(V), then G = GL(V).

**Hypotheses.**

- ℓ prime and G ⊂ GL_2(F_ℓ) (the prime field); Cartan subgroups as in R01.4/cartan-subgroups-and-normalisers
- (d) excludes ℓ = 5 for split C (Serre's remark: S_4 occurs); (e) excludes ℓ = 2

**Construction and proof.**

1. (a) Serre's proof: an element of order ℓ is a transvection fixing a unique line; if all these lines coincide, G stabilises it (Borel); otherwise G contains [[1, a], [0, 1]] and [[1, 0], [b, 1]] with ab ≠ 0, and these generate SL_2(F_ℓ) (Bourbaki A III p. 104 prop. 17, or the transvection generation mathlib:Matrix.SL2.transvection_induction).
2. (b) Prop. 16 for K = F_ℓ: by lifting to characteristic 0 and the finite rotation groups; a cyclic H lies in a unique Cartan of PGL(V) when nontrivial; a dihedral H normalises the Cartan containing its index-2 cyclic subgroup; A_5 needs elements of order 5 in PGL_2(F_ℓ), i.e. 5 | ℓ(ℓ² − 1).
3. (c) combines (a) and (b): a semisimple G with ℓ | |G| cannot lie in a Borel unless reducible-semisimple, which forces ℓ ∤ |G|; so ℓ | |G| gives SL(V) ⊂ G.
4. (d) If ℓ | |G| use (a) and det(C) = F_ℓ^×; otherwise C has image of order ℓ ± 1 ≥ 6 in PGL(V) and A_4, S_4, A_5 have no element of order ≥ 6.
5. (e) Normal subgroups of GL_2(F_ℓ), ℓ ≥ 5, are central or contain SL_2 (R01.4/normal-subgroups-and-automorphisms-of-psl2-pgl2); ℓ = 3 by PGL_2(F_3) ≅ S_4.

**Prerequisites.** `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/cartan-subgroups-and-normalisers`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/p-subgroups-and-borel-subgroups`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/normal-subgroups-and-automorphisms-of-psl2-pgl2`; `tauceti:TauCeti.GL2Borel.mem_iff`; `tauceti:TauCeti.GL2Borel.card_eq`; `mathlib:Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup`; `mathlib:Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup`; `mathlib:Matrix.SL2.transvection_induction`; `mathlib:IsPGroup`; `mathlib:Sylow`.

**Acceptance.**

- Instance: the image of the mod-ℓ representation of a non-CM elliptic curve with a rational ℓ-isogeny lies in a Borel subgroup; the mod-ℓ image of a CM curve over ℚ with ℓ inert in the CM field is the normaliser of a non-split Cartan, case (b)/(c).
- Serre's remark after Prop. 17: for ℓ = 5 and split C, π(G) ≅ S_4 occurs, so the hypothesis ℓ ≠ 5 cannot be dropped.
- For ℓ = 3: GL_2(F_3) has PGL_2(F_3) ≅ S_4 and the subgroup SL_2(F_3) of order 24 is not in a Borel and contains SL(V), consistent with (a).

**Sources.**

- serre72-proprietes, §2.4, Proposition 15, printed p. 280 (transcribed from the GDZ page image): “Proposition 15. Soit G un sous-groupe de GL(V) d'ordre divisible par p. Alors, ou bien G contient SL(V), ou bien G est contenu dans un sous-groupe de Borel de GL(V).” — Statement (a) (Serre writes p for ℓ).
- serre72-proprietes, §2.5, Proposition 16, printed p. 281 (transcribed from the page image): “Soit H un sous-groupe fini de PGL2(k) d'ordre premier à la caractéristique car.k de k. On suppose que H n'est ni cyclique ni diédral. Alors H est isomorphe à l'un des groupes 𝔄4, 𝔖4 et 𝔄5.” — Statement (b), general field form.
- serre72-proprietes, §2.6 (iii), printed p. 282 (transcribed from the page image): “ce dernier cas n'étant d'ailleurs possible que si p≡±1 (mod. 5)” — The congruence condition for A_5 in (b).
- serre72-proprietes, §2.7, Proposition 17, printed p. 282 (transcribed from the page image): “ou bien G est contenu dans le normalisateur d'un sous-groupe de Cartan.” — Statement (d), last alternative.

#### Cartan subgroups of GL_2 over a finite field and their normalisers

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/cartan-subgroups-and-normalisers`. Kind: definition. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.GL2Cartan` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/ResidualImage/Cartan.lean`). Planet: **Cartan subgroups and their normalisers**. Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4`.

Let k be a finite field with q elements, V a two-dimensional k-vector space and GL(V) ≅ GL_2(k). (1) Split Cartan: for two distinct lines D_1 ≠ D_2 of V, C_s(D_1, D_2) := {s ∈ GL(V) : sD_1 = D_1, sD_2 = D_2} ≅ (k^×)², the diagonal torus in a basis adapted to D_1 ⊕ D_2. (2) Non-split Cartan: for a subalgebra k′ ⊂ End_k(V) which is a field with q² elements, C_ns(k′) := k′^× ⊂ GL(V), cyclic of order q² − 1; in coordinates it is TauCeti.GL2NonSplitTorus k k′ (left multiplication on k′ ≅ k² in a chosen basis); for q odd and ε ∈ k^× a non-square it is conjugate to {[[a, εb], [b, a]] : (a, b) ≠ (0, 0)}. (3) Normalisers: N(C) := normaliser of C in GL(V). For a split Cartan, N(C) is the stabiliser of the pair {D_1, D_2}; for a non-split Cartan, N(C) is the group of k′-semilinear automorphisms s(ax) = a^q s(x). If C is non-split, or split with q ≥ 3, then [N(C) : C] = 2, every element of N(C) ∖ C has trace 0 and square scalar, and the images C̄ ⊂ N̄ in PGL(V) are cyclic of order q ∓ 1 (− split, + non-split) and dihedral of order 2(q ∓ 1). (4) Borel: B(D) := stabiliser of a line D, of order q(q − 1)², TauCeti.GL2Borel k for D = ⟨e_1⟩. Half-Cartan (Serre): the subgroup of C_s(D_1, D_2) acting trivially on D_2.

**Hypotheses.**

- k finite with q = |k| elements; q ≥ 3 for statements about split normalisers (for q = 2 the split Cartan is trivial)
- Cartan subgroups are defined basis-free; matrix models are API
- over F̄_p (consumers using algebraically closed coefficients) the image of a finite subgroup of a Cartan of GL_2(k) is diagonalisable over k̄

**Construction and proof.**

1. k′ = k[C] is a commutative semisimple k-algebra of rank 2 with C = k′^× (split: k × k; non-split: F_{q²}); an element of N(C) induces a k-algebra automorphism of k′, trivial exactly on C, and Aut_k(k′) has order 2 (swap, resp. Frobenius), so [N(C) : C] = 2 (Serre 1972 §2.2).
2. For s ∈ N(C) ∖ C, s² ∈ C commutes with s and is fixed by the swap/Frobenius, so s² ∈ k^× (scalar) and the characteristic polynomial is X² − s², trace 0 (split: s is antidiagonal; non-split: s(x) = λ x^q, s² = N(λ)).
3. The union of the Cartan subgroups is the set of semisimple (order prime to p) elements; for p ≠ 2 an element with Tr² − 4 det ≠ 0 lies in exactly one Cartan, split iff Tr² − 4det is a square (Serre 1972 §2.1).
4. Tau Ceti provides the non-split torus with its order q² − 1, its index, its non-conjugacy into the Borel, and the conjugacy classification of non-scalar elements by trace and determinant; the diagonal torus and its Weyl element normaliser are TauCeti.diagGL and TauCeti.gl2WeylElement_mem_normalizer_diagonalTorus.

**Prerequisites.** `tauceti:TauCeti.GL2NonSplitTorus`; `tauceti:TauCeti.GL2NonSplitTorus.natCard_eq`; `tauceti:TauCeti.GL2NonSplitTorus.conj_notMem_gl2Borel`; `tauceti:TauCeti.GL2NonSplitTorus.centralizer_gl2NonSplitTorusHom`; `tauceti:TauCeti.GL2Borel.index_eq`; `tauceti:TauCeti.GL2Borel.card_eq`; `tauceti:TauCeti.isConj_iff_of_notMem_range_scalar`; `tauceti:TauCeti.conjClassesGLFinTwoEquiv`; `tauceti:TauCeti.diagGL`; `tauceti:TauCeti.gl2WeylElement_mem_normalizer_diagonalTorus`; `mathlib:Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup`.

**Uses.**

- Serre 1972 §2.2 and Propositions 14, 17: images of Galois on E[ℓ] are classified through Cartan subgroups and their normalisers
- Caraiani–Newton Lemma 7.1.1: C_s^+(3), C_ns(3), C_ns^+(5) as the possible images with cyclotomically reducible restriction
- EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.5/proper-image-nonsplit: proper images for p > 37 lie in a non-split Cartan normaliser
- EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.5/nonsplit-potential-multiplicative: elements of N_ns ∖ C_ns have trace 0; eigenvalues of C_ns are conjugate over F_{p²}
- Dieulefait–Pacetti Lemma 1.13 proof: abelian normal subgroups of the normaliser of a split Cartan
- AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations:R19.1/bounded-semisimple-subgroups-of-gl2: Deligne–Serre 7.2 case split: Cartan, normaliser, exceptional

**API.**

- `TauCeti.GL2Cartan.split` (constructor): C_s(D_1, D_2) for distinct lines D_1, D_2.
- `TauCeti.GL2Cartan.nonsplit` (constructor): C_ns(k′) = k′^× for a quadratic subfield k′ ⊂ End_k(V).
- `TauCeti.GL2Cartan.normalizer_index` (structure): [N(C) : C] = 2 for C non-split, or split with q ≥ 3.
- `TauCeti.GL2Cartan.mem_normalizer_split_iff` (characterisation): s ∈ N(C_s(D_1, D_2)) iff s{D_1, D_2} = {D_1, D_2}.
- `TauCeti.GL2Cartan.image_PGL` (projection): π(C) is cyclic of order q ∓ 1 and π(N(C)) is dihedral of order 2(q ∓ 1).
- `TauCeti.GL2Cartan.conj` (functoriality): g C(D_1, D_2) g⁻¹ = C(gD_1, gD_2) and g C_ns(k′) g⁻¹ = C_ns(g k′ g⁻¹); N commutes with conjugation.
- `TauCeti.GL2Cartan.exists_unique_of_disc_ne_zero` (relation): For p ≠ 2 and Tr(s)² − 4det(s) ≠ 0, s lies in a unique Cartan, split iff the discriminant is a square in k.
- `TauCeti.GL2Cartan.diagonal_model` (equivalence): C_s(⟨e_1⟩, ⟨e_2⟩) is the range of TauCeti.diagGL and its normaliser is generated with TauCeti.gl2WeylElement.

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.GL2Cartan.card_nonsplit` (computation): |C_ns| = q² − 1 and |N(C_ns)| = 2(q² − 1); for q = 3 these are 8 and 16.
- `TauCeti.GL2Cartan.split_trivial_q_two` (degenerate): For q = 2 the split Cartan is trivial and its normaliser is all of GL_2(F_2) ≅ S_3, so [N : C] = 2 fails; the index statement needs q ≥ 3.
- `TauCeti.GL2Cartan.trace_eq_zero_of_mem_normalizer_not_mem` (characterisation): Every s ∈ N(C) ∖ C has Tr s = 0 and s² scalar.
- `TauCeti.GL2Cartan.nonsplit_eq_GL2NonSplitTorus` (compatibility): In the basis of TauCeti.nonSplitTorusBasis the non-split Cartan k′^× equals TauCeti.GL2NonSplitTorus k k′.
- `TauCeti.GL2Cartan.split_ne_nonsplit` (non-example): A non-split Cartan is not conjugate to the diagonal torus (no non-scalar element has an eigenvalue in k), so the definition ‘any maximal abelian subgroup of order prime to p’ must keep the two types apart by conjugacy.

**Acceptance.**

- |C_s| = (q − 1)², |C_ns| = q² − 1, |N(C_s)| = 2(q − 1)², |N(C_ns)| = 2(q² − 1); for q = 3, N(C_s) is dihedral of order 8 and N(C_ns) is the semidihedral Sylow 2-subgroup of GL_2(F_3) of order 16.
- CM instance: for E/ℚ with CM by an order in K and ℓ ∤ disc(K) inert in K, the image of G_ℚ on E[ℓ] is the normaliser of the non-split Cartan (O_K/ℓ)^× and the image of G_K is the Cartan itself; for ℓ split in K it is N(C_s).

**Sources.**

- serre72-proprietes, §2.1 b), printed p. 279 (transcribed from the GDZ page image): “Un tel sous-groupe de GL(V) (resp. de PGL(V)) est appelé un sous-groupe de Cartan non déployé.” — Definition (2), Serre's normalisation over F_p.
- serre72-proprietes, §2.2, printed p. 279 (transcribed from the page image): “On en conclut que (N:C)=2.” — Index of the normaliser, (3).
- cn23, Lemma 7.1.1, p. 92 of arXiv v3: “ρ(GF ) is a subgroup of the normalizer of a Cartan subgroup.” — Use of normalisers C_s^+(3), C_ns^+(5) by Caraiani–Newton.

#### p-subgroups of GL_2 in characteristic p fix a unique line

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/p-subgroups-and-borel-subgroups`. Kind: lemma. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.GL2Subgroup` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/ResidualImage/Borel.lean`). Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4`.

Let k be a field of characteristic p > 0 (finite or algebraically closed) and P ⊂ GL_2(k) a nontrivial finite p-subgroup. Then every element of P is unipotent, P is elementary abelian of exponent p, conjugate into the upper unitriangular group {[[1, b], [0, 1]]} ≅ (k, +), and P fixes exactly one line D = V^P of k̄² (which is k-rational); the normaliser of P in GL_2(k) lies in the Borel subgroup B(D). Consequently: (i) a subgroup G ⊂ GL_2(k) with a nontrivial normal p-subgroup is reducible, with G-stable line V^{O_p(G)}; (ii) the Sylow p-subgroups of GL_2(F_q) are the unipotent radicals of the q + 1 Borel subgroups, of order q; (iii) for G ⊂ GL_2(k) reducible over k̄ with p | |G|, the Sylow p-subgroup of G is normal and fixes the unique G-stable line; (iv) a finite subgroup of PGL_2(k̄) with a nontrivial normal p-subgroup fixes a point of P¹(k̄).

**Hypotheses.**

- char k = p > 0
- P finite (for k finite automatic)

**Construction and proof.**

1. An element u of p-power order satisfies (u − 1)^{p^a} = u^{p^a} − 1 = 0, so u is unipotent; in dimension 2, (u − 1)² = 0, hence u^p = 1.
2. For u ≠ 1 unipotent, ker(u − 1) is the unique u-invariant line. A nontrivial p-group fixes a nonzero vector of k̄² (orbit counting on the finite F_p-span, or mathlib:IsPGroup.card_modEq_card_fixedPoints on the line set over a finite field); all its non-identity elements then share that line, so P is upper unitriangular in an adapted basis, isomorphic to a subgroup of (k, +).
3. If g normalises P then g permutes the P-fixed lines, of which there is one; so g ∈ B(D). (i) and (iv) follow since O_p(G) is characteristic in G (Mathlib IsPGroup, Sylow).
4. (ii) |GL_2(F_q)| = q(q − 1)²(q + 1) and the unipotent radical of the Borel has order q (tauceti:TauCeti.GL2Borel.card_eq).

**Prerequisites.** `mathlib:IsPGroup`; `mathlib:IsPGroup.card_modEq_card_fixedPoints`; `mathlib:Sylow`; `tauceti:TauCeti.GL2Borel.mem_iff`; `tauceti:TauCeti.GL2Borel.card_eq`; `tauceti:TauCeti.GL2Borel.index_eq`.

**Acceptance.**

- For q = 4: the Sylow 2-subgroups of SL_2(F_4) ≅ A_5 are the five Klein four-groups, the unipotent radicals of the five Borels; this is the exclusion of A_4 in characteristic 2.
- Over F_3 the group SL_2(F_3) has Sylow 3-subgroups of order 3 that are not normal (four of them), so SL_2(F_3) is irreducible; consistent with (iii).
- For a finite Galois extension E/ℚ_p with wild inertia P ≠ 1 embedded in GL_2(F) (char F = p), the image of the decomposition group lies in a Borel and P maps into its unipotent radical (SmallRamificationAndAbelianVarietyBaseCases:R25.1/wild-image-borel-normal-form).

**Sources.**

- kw-serre-modularity-I, Lemma 6.1, proof, p. 11 of the preprint: “a Sylow 2-subgroup of GL2 (F) for F a finite field of characteristic 2 is given by the unipotent matrices.” — The characteristic-2 case of (ii).
- serre72-proprietes, §2.3, printed p. 280 (transcribed from the GDZ page image): “Un tel sous-groupe est appelé un sous-groupe de Borel de GL(V); la droite D correspondante est l'unique droite de V stable par B.” — Borel subgroups and their unique stable line.
- serre72-proprietes, §2.4, proof of Proposition 15, printed p. 280 (transcribed from the page image): “donc laisse fixe une droite D_x et une seule.” — An element of order p fixes a unique line.

#### Dihedral projective image if and only if induced from an index-two subgroup

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/dihedral-projective-image-iff-induced`. Kind: theorem. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.GaloisRep` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/ResidualImage/Dihedral.lean`). Planet: **Dihedral images are induced**. Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4`.

Let Γ be a profinite group, k an algebraically closed field (any characteristic) and ρ : Γ → GL_2(k) a homomorphism whose projectivisation π∘ρ has open kernel and finite image (automatic for k = F̄_p discrete and ρ continuous). (a) The following are equivalent: (1) ρ is irreducible and π(ρ(Γ)) is dihedral of order 2n for some n ≥ 2; (2) ρ ≅ Ind_Δ^Γ χ (R01.1/continuous-induction) for an open subgroup Δ of index 2 and a continuous character χ : Δ → k^× with χ ≠ χ^σ, where χ^σ(δ) = χ(σ δ σ⁻¹) for any σ ∈ Γ ∖ Δ. (b) In (2), ρ|_Δ ≅ χ ⊕ χ^σ, π(ρ(Δ)) is cyclic of order n = order of χ/χ^σ (so char k ∤ n), elements of ρ(Γ ∖ Δ) have trace 0, and det ρ = (χ|_{Ver}) · ε_Δ (R01.1/determinant-of-induced-representation, ε_Δ the quadratic character with kernel Δ). For n ≥ 3, Δ is unique: it is the preimage of the cyclic subgroup of order n; for n = 2 (Klein image) there are exactly three such Δ. (c) If char k ≠ 2 and ρ is irreducible, ρ ≅ Ind_Δ^Γ χ for some χ iff ρ ⊗ ε_Δ ≅ ρ. (d) If ρ|_{Γ′} is reducible for an open normal subgroup Γ′ with Γ/Γ′ abelian and ρ is irreducible, then ρ(Γ′) is diagonalisable (char k ∤ |ρ(Γ′)|) and either π(ρ(Γ′)) = 1 (π(ρ(Γ)) cyclic, impossible for irreducible ρ) or ρ is induced from the stabiliser of one eigenline of ρ(Γ′), an index-2 subgroup containing Γ′. (e) In characteristic 2, an irreducible ρ with dihedral projective image has n odd ≥ 3, and det ρ has odd order on ρ(Δ).

**Hypotheses.**

- k algebraically closed; when k = ℚ̄_ℓ or ℂ the dihedral image is finite by hypothesis
- Δ open of index 2; χ continuous for the topology in which ρ is continuous
- (c) needs char k ≠ 2 (ε_Δ is trivial modulo 2)

**Construction and proof.**

1. (2) ⇒ (1): in a basis {e, σe} of Ind χ, ρ(δ) = diag(χ(δ), χ^σ(δ)) and ρ(σ) is antidiagonal. Since χ ≠ χ^σ the only Δ-stable lines are the two eigenlines, swapped by σ, so ρ is irreducible (characteristic-free; in characteristic 0 this is also tauceti:TauCeti.simple_indFDRep_ofLinearCharacter_iff). The projective image of Δ is the cyclic group generated by the values of χ/χ^σ, order n ≥ 2 prime to char k; an antidiagonal element is an involution in PGL_2 inverting it, so the image is dihedral of order 2n.
2. (1) ⇒ (2): let C ⊂ π(ρ(Γ)) be a cyclic subgroup of index 2 and Δ its preimage, open of index 2. ρ(Δ) is a central extension of a cyclic group, hence abelian, and has a common eigenvector over k (tauceti:TauCeti.exists_unitHom_jointEigenvector_of_pairwise_commute_of_isAlgClosed) with character χ. Frobenius reciprocity (R01.1/continuous-induction) gives a nonzero Γ-map ρ → Ind χ, an isomorphism since ρ is irreducible and both have dimension 2; χ = χ^σ would make Ind χ ≅ χ̃ ⊗ k[Γ/Δ] reducible, χ̃ an extension of χ (which exists as H²(ℤ/2, k^×) = k^×/k^{×2} = 1).
3. (b) The cyclic subgroup of order n ≥ 3 is characteristic in the dihedral group; the Klein group has three subgroups of order 2. The trace of an antidiagonal matrix is 0. The determinant formula is R01.1/determinant-of-induced-representation with rank 1.
4. (c) Ind χ ⊗ ε_Δ ≅ Ind(χ ⊗ ε_Δ|_Δ) = Ind χ; conversely an isomorphism A : ρ ≅ ρ ⊗ ε_Δ has A² scalar by Schur, A non-scalar (ε_Δ ≠ 1 and char ≠ 2), and its two eigenspaces are Δ-stable lines, so ρ|_Δ is reducible and (1) ⇒ (2) applies with this Δ.
5. (d) By R01.4/p-subgroups-and-borel-subgroups a reducible normal ρ(Γ′) with char k | |ρ(Γ′)| has a normal unipotent subgroup whose line is Γ-stable; so ρ(Γ′) is diagonalisable (Clifford: tauceti:TauCeti.Representation.isSemisimpleRepresentation_comp_subtype) and Γ permutes its isotypic lines.
6. (e) In characteristic 2 the image of Δ is diagonalisable, so its projective image has odd order n; n = 2 is excluded since the Klein group would be a 2-group fixing a line.

**Prerequisites.** `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/continuous-induction`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/determinant-of-induced-representation`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/absolutely-irreducible`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/p-subgroups-and-borel-subgroups`; `tauceti:TauCeti.exists_unitHom_jointEigenvector_of_pairwise_commute_of_isAlgClosed`; `tauceti:TauCeti.simple_indFDRep_ofLinearCharacter_iff`; `tauceti:TauCeti.Representation.isSemisimpleRepresentation_comp_subtype`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/InductionRestriction#layer-5-clifford-theory-over-a-normal-subgroup`; `mathlib:DihedralGroup`.

**Acceptance.**

- Instance (Swinnerton-Dyer's mod-23 representation): for L the splitting field of x³ − x − 1 (Galois group S_3, quadratic subfield ℚ(√−23)), the standard two-dimensional representation of S_3 over F̄_23 composed with G_ℚ → S_3 is Ind_{G_{ℚ(√−23)}}^{G_ℚ} χ with χ of order 3; projective image S_3, dihedral of order 6.
- Klein case: for a biquadratic field ℚ(√a, √b), the representation of Gal ≅ (ℤ/2)² lifted to Q_8 ⊂ SL_2(ℂ) is irreducible with projective image V_4 and is induced from each of the three quadratic subfields.
- Characteristic-2 instance: E[2] for E : y² = x³ − 2 is Ind from ℚ(√−3) of a character of order 3 (n = 3 odd).

**Sources.**

- serre72-proprietes, §2.6 (ii), printed p. 282 (transcribed from the GDZ page image): “H est diédral, donc contient un sous-groupe cyclique C' non trivial d'indice 2.” — The index-2 cyclic subgroup used in (1) ⇒ (2).
- dieulefait-pacetti, proof of Lemma 1.14, p. 9 of arXiv v2: “The fact that the representation has irreducible image together with the projective” — Dihedral projective image corresponds to the image lying in the normaliser of a Cartan.
- bcg25-gln, proof of Theorem 3.1, published p. 516 (free offprint): “contains a cyclic subgroup of order p + 1 > 5, so ρf does not” — BCG25 rule out exceptional images by element orders and dihedral images by induction from ℚ(√p*) and twist invariance, statement (c).

#### Bad dihedral representations

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/bad-dihedral-representation`. Kind: definition. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.GaloisRep` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/ResidualImage/BadDihedral.lean`). Planet: **Bad dihedral representation**. Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4`.

Let p be an odd prime and p* := (−1)^{(p−1)/2} p. For a number field F let K_F := F(ζ_p) and let F′ ⊂ K_F be the fixed field of the subgroup of squares of the cyclic group Gal(K_F/F) (so F′ = F if [K_F : F] is odd, and F′ is the quadratic subextension of K_F/F otherwise). For F = ℚ, F′ = ℚ(√p*), the quadratic subfield of ℚ(ζ_p), equal to ℚ(g) for the quadratic Gauss sum g with g² = p* (mathlib:gaussSum_sq). Let k be a finite field of characteristic p (or k = F̄_p) and ρ̄ : G_F → GL_2(k) continuous. ρ̄ is bad dihedral if ρ̄ is absolutely irreducible and ρ̄|_{G_{F′}} is not absolutely irreducible. For F = ℚ this is Dieulefait–Pacetti Definition 1.12: ρ̄ irreducible (over F̄_p) and ρ̄|_{G_{ℚ(√p*)}} reducible. Equivalently (R01.4/bad-dihedral-representations-and-the-oddness-criterion) ρ̄ is absolutely irreducible and ρ̄|_{G_{F(ζ_p)}} is not; ‘not bad dihedral and absolutely irreducible’ is Wiles's condition ‘ρ̄|_{G_{ℚ(√p*)}} absolutely irreducible’.

**Hypotheses.**

- p odd
- coefficients finite of characteristic p or F̄_p; ‘reducible’ means not absolutely irreducible
- F′ is defined by the squares of Gal(F(ζ_p)/F), not by adjoining √p* (for F ∋ √p*, F′ = F(ζ_p)^{Gal²} is different)

**Construction and proof.**

1. Gal(ℚ(ζ_p)/ℚ) ≅ (ℤ/p)^× (mathlib:IsCyclotomicExtension.autEquivPow) is cyclic of even order p − 1, its squares form the unique index-2 subgroup, and its fixed field is ℚ(g) with g² = χ(−1)p = p* for the Legendre character χ (mathlib:gaussSum_sq).
2. Absolute irreducibility is invariant under extension of k (R01.1/absolutely-irreducible), so the definition does not depend on k.

**Prerequisites.** `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/absolutely-irreducible`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/restriction-dual-tensor-twist`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/cyclotomic-and-dirichlet-characters`; `mathlib:IsCyclotomicExtension.autEquivPow`; `mathlib:gaussSum_sq`; `mathlib:IsGalois.intermediateFieldEquivSubgroup`; `mathlib:Field.absoluteGaloisGroup`.

**Uses.**

- Dieulefait–Pacetti, Definition 1.12 and Theorem 1.4: the residual hypothesis ‘ρ̄|_{ℚ(√p*)} absolutely irreducible’ of modularity lifting
- Darmon–Diamond–Taylor Theorem 2.49: Taylor–Wiles primes exist when ρ̄|_{G_L} is absolutely irreducible, L = ℚ(√p*)
- AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights:R15.4/bad-dihedral-normalized-weight-application: bad dihedral ρ̄ have p = 2k − 1 or p = 2k − 3
- ClassicalSerreModularity:R33.1/fontaine-laffaille-member-not-bad-dihedral: members in the Fontaine–Laffaille range are not bad dihedral
- ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.6/sigma-criterion: hypothesis ρ̄|_{G_L} absolutely irreducible for L = ℚ(√ℓ*)
- GL2ModularityLifting:R32.1/quadratic-cyclotomic-irreducibility: identification of the two residual hypotheses
- Khare–Wintenberger II §7.6.2: ρ̄|_{G_{F(μ_p)}} absolutely irreducible over a totally real F

**API.**

- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.cyclotomicSquareSubfield` (constructor): F′ ⊂ F(ζ_p): the fixed field of the squares of Gal(F(ζ_p)/F).
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.cyclotomicSquareSubfield_rat` (simp): For F = ℚ, F′ = ℚ(√p*) = ℚ(g), g the quadratic Gauss sum.
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.IsBadDihedral` (data): ρ̄ absolutely irreducible and ρ̄|_{G_{F′}} not absolutely irreducible.
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.isBadDihedral_iff_cyclotomic` (characterisation): IsBadDihedral ρ̄ iff ρ̄ absolutely irreducible and ρ̄|_{G_{F(ζ_p)}} not absolutely irreducible.
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.isBadDihedral_tensor_character` (compatibility): IsBadDihedral (ρ̄ ⊗ ψ) iff IsBadDihedral ρ̄ for every continuous character ψ.
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.isBadDihedral_baseChange` (functoriality): IsBadDihedral is invariant under extension of the finite coefficient field.
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.IsBadDihedral.projInertia_card_le_two` (relation): For F = ℚ, a bad dihedral ρ̄ has π(ρ̄(I_p)) of order ≤ 2.
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.IsBadDihedral.isInduced` (relation): A bad dihedral ρ̄ is induced from G_{F′} and has image of order prime to p.

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.isBadDihedral_x3_minus_x_minus_1` (computation): The standard representation of S_3 over F_23 through the splitting field of x³ − x − 1 is bad dihedral at p = 23.
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.isBadDihedral_requires_absolute` (non-example): In the previous example ρ̄|_{G_{ℚ(√−23)}} is irreducible over F_23; a definition using irreducibility over the coefficient field instead of absolute irreducibility would wrongly declare it not bad dihedral.
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.not_isBadDihedral_of_SL2_le` (non-example): If p ≥ 5 and SL_2(F_p) ⊆ ρ̄(G_ℚ) then ρ̄ is not bad dihedral.
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.badDihedral_p_three` (degenerate): For p = 3, ℚ(√−3) = ℚ(ζ_3), and bad dihedral means absolutely irreducible with ρ̄|_{G_{ℚ(ζ_3)}} not absolutely irreducible.
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.isBadDihedral_iff_induced` (characterisation): ρ̄ is bad dihedral iff ρ̄ ⊗ F̄_p ≅ Ind_{G_{F′}}^{G_F} χ with χ ≠ χ^σ.

**Acceptance.**

- Instance: the mod-23 representation attached to x³ − x − 1 (standard representation of S_3 over F_23 through G_ℚ → Gal(L/ℚ)) is absolutely irreducible and odd, and its restriction to G_{ℚ(√−23)} has image of order 3 with eigenvalues primitive cube roots of unity not in F_23: irreducible over F_23 but not absolutely irreducible. So it is bad dihedral (p = 23, p* = −23).
- If p ≥ 5 and ρ̄(G_ℚ) ⊇ SL_2(F_p) then ρ̄ is not bad dihedral (the image of G_{ℚ(√p*)} has index ≤ 2 and contains SL_2(F_p)).

**Sources.**

- dieulefait-pacetti, Definition 1.12, p. 7 of arXiv v2: “becomes reducible while restricted to GalQ(√p⋆ ) is called bad dihedral.” — The source definition (coefficients F̄_p): ρ̄ irreducible over F̄_p but reducible on G_{ℚ(√p*)}.
- ddt-fermat, Theorem 2.49, p. 82: “then ρ̄|GL is absolutely irreducible. Then” — Wiles's hypothesis, the negation of bad dihedral for absolutely irreducible ρ̄ (text layer renders ℓ as `).

#### The quadratic–cyclotomic irreducibility criterion and projective inertia of bad dihedral representations

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/bad-dihedral-representations-and-the-oddness-criterion`. Kind: lemma. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.GaloisRep` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/ResidualImage/BadDihedral.lean`). Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4`.

(a) [cyclic restriction criterion] Let L/F be a finite cyclic Galois extension of fields, F′ ⊂ L the fixed field of the subgroup of squares of Gal(L/F), k an algebraically closed field and ρ : G_F → GL_2(k) a homomorphism with open kernel. Then ρ|_{G_{F′}} is irreducible iff ρ|_{G_L} is irreducible. (b) [Dieulefait–Pacetti Lemma 1.13, strengthened] Let F be a number field, p an odd prime, F′ as in R01.4/bad-dihedral-representation, m ≥ 1 and ρ̄ : G_F → GL_2(k) continuous with k finite of characteristic p. The following are equivalent: (1) ρ̄|_{G_{F′}} absolutely irreducible; (2) ρ̄|_{G_{F(ζ_p)}} absolutely irreducible; (3) ρ̄|_{G_{F(ζ_{p^m})}} absolutely irreducible. No oddness hypothesis is needed (the source assumes ρ̄ odd and F = ℚ). (c) If ρ̄ is bad dihedral then ρ̄ ⊗ F̄_p ≅ Ind_{G_{F′}}^{G_F} χ with χ ≠ χ^σ, the projective image is dihedral of order 2n with p ∤ n, and |ρ̄(G_F)| is prime to p. (d) [Dieulefait–Pacetti Lemma 1.14, inertia part] If F = ℚ and ρ̄ is bad dihedral, then the projective image of ρ̄(I_p) has order ≤ 2. Writing (ρ̄|_{I_p}) ⊗ F̄_p ≅ ψ_1 ⊕ ψ_2 (tame characters, R01.2/tame-semisimple-residual-local-representations), ψ_1/ψ_2 has order ≤ 2: in niveau 1, ψ_1/ψ_2 = ω^a with (p − 1) | 2a; in niveau 2, ψ_1 = ω_2^b, ψ_2 = ω_2^{pb} with (p + 1) | 2b. The translation into Serre weights (p = 2k(ρ̄) − 1 in niveau 1, p = 2k(ρ̄) − 3 in niveau 2, after normalising 2 ≤ k(ρ̄) ≤ p + 1) belongs to AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights:R15.4 and is not stated here.

**Hypotheses.**

- (a) is characteristic-free; k algebraically closed
- (b)–(d): p odd
- (d) uses that ℚ(√p*) is ramified at p and unramified elsewhere; it is stated over ℚ as in the source

**Construction and proof.**

1. (a) ⇐ is clear. ⇒: suppose ρ|_{G_{F′}} irreducible and ρ|_{G_L} reducible. If char k | |ρ(G_L)|, the normal unipotent subgroup O_p(ρ(G_L)) fixes a unique line, which ρ(G_{F′}) stabilises (R01.4/p-subgroups-and-borel-subgroups): contradiction. So ρ(G_L) ≅ ψ_1 ⊕ ψ_2 is diagonalisable. If ψ_1 = ψ_2, ρ(G_L) is scalar, π(ρ(G_{F′})) is cyclic, ρ(G_{F′}) abelian and reducible: contradiction. If ψ_1 ≠ ψ_2, G_F (which normalises G_L) permutes the two eigenlines through G_F/G_L = Gal(L/F) → S_2; every element of Gal(L/F′) is a square in the cyclic group Gal(L/F), so acts trivially, and G_{F′} stabilises both lines: contradiction.
2. (b) Apply (a) to L = F(ζ_p) and L = F(ζ_{p^m}) (cyclic over F since p is odd); [F(ζ_{p^m}) : F(ζ_p)] is a power of p, odd, so both have the same subfield F′. This replaces the case analysis of the source proof (Borel / split Cartan normaliser / A_4, S_4), which is also correct.
3. (c) By the proof of (a) with L replaced by F′ and F′ by F (G_{F′} is normal of index 2 in G_F): ρ̄(G_{F′}) is diagonalisable with two distinct characters, G_F swaps the eigenlines, and R01.4/dihedral-projective-image-iff-induced gives ρ̄ ≅ Ind χ; the image of G_{F′} is diagonal of order prime to p and has index 2, and p is odd.
4. (d) Following the source (after Ribet 1997 Prop. 2.2): the image has no element of order p, so ρ̄|_{I_p} is tame, semisimple, with cyclic projective image. If its order were > 2 it would lie in the unique cyclic subgroup of index 2 of the dihedral projective image, whose fixed field is ℚ(√p*) by (c); that field would then be unramified at p, a contradiction. The niveau computations: ω has order p − 1 and ω_2^{b(1−p)} has order (p + 1)/gcd(p + 1, b).

**Prerequisites.** `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/bad-dihedral-representation`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/p-subgroups-and-borel-subgroups`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/dihedral-projective-image-iff-induced`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/tame-inertia-and-fundamental-characters`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/tame-semisimple-residual-local-representations`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/decomposition-group-at-a-place`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/absolutely-irreducible`; `mathlib:IsCyclotomicExtension.autEquivPow`.

**Acceptance.**

- Check both niveau cases on explicit representations: x³ − x − 1 at p = 23 is niveau 1 with ψ_1/ψ_2 of order 2 = ω^{11}; a dihedral representation induced from ℚ(√p*) with niveau-2 inertia ω_2^b ⊕ ω_2^{pb}, (p + 1)/2 | b, illustrates the second case.
- Check that the oddness hypothesis is not used: the even representation Ind_{ℚ(√5)}^{ℚ} χ (χ ≠ χ^σ of odd order, p = 5) is irreducible and reducible on both G_{ℚ(√5)} and G_{ℚ(ζ_5)}, as (b) predicts.
- Check that at p = 2 the oddness argument of R01.4/odd-irreducible-implies-absolutely-irreducible fails by the F_2-irreducible representation of image order 3 that splits over F_4.

**Sources.**

- dieulefait-pacetti, Lemma 1.13, p. 8 of arXiv v2: “Clearly the second condition implies the first one.” — The source proves (b) for F = ℚ, ρ̄ odd, coefficients F̄_p.
- dieulefait-pacetti, Lemma 1.14 with proof, pp. 8–9 of arXiv v2: “Then either p = 2k(ρ̄) − 3 (niveau 2 case) or p = 2k(ρ̄) − 1 (niveau 1 case).” — The weight conclusion, of which (d) is the inertia part; the weight translation is routed to R15.4.
- dieulefait-pacetti, proof of Lemma 1.14, p. 9 of arXiv v2: “We claim that the projective image of ρ̄(Ip ) has order at most 2.” — Statement (d).
- kw-serre-modularity-I, Lemma 6.2(ii) and proof, p. 11: “As p > 2 the projectivisation ρ̄proj of the representation ρ̄ is tamely” — The earlier version of (d); Dieulefait–Pacetti note that this proof lacks details.

#### The image of a restriction and linear disjointness

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/image-of-restriction-to-a-subfield`. Kind: lemma. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.GaloisRep` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/ResidualImage/Restriction.lean`). Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4`.

Let F be a field, ρ : G_F → GL_n(A) continuous with A discrete (finite image), K = F̄^{ker ρ} its kernel field, so that ρ induces an isomorphism Gal(K/F) ≅ ρ(G_F). Let F′/F be a finite separable extension inside F̄. Then: (a) ρ(G_{F′}) is the image of Gal(K/K ∩ F′) ⊂ Gal(K/F) under this isomorphism; (b) if F′ is linearly disjoint from K over F (equivalently K ∩ F′ = F, as K/F is Galois; equivalently [KF′ : F′] = [K : F]), then ρ(G_{F′}) = ρ(G_F); (c) the same holds for the projective image with K replaced by the projective kernel field M = F̄^{ker π∘ρ} ⊂ K, so linear disjointness from M suffices for the projective image; (d) if F′/F is Galois and linearly disjoint from K(μ_p) (resp. from M(μ_p)), then ρ(G_{F′(ζ_p)}) = ρ(G_{F(ζ_p)}) (resp. for projective images); (e) if H ⊂ ρ(G_F) is a perfect subgroup and F′/F is a soluble tower (each step Galois with solvable group), then H ⊂ ρ(G_{F′}); (f) absolute irreducibility, Dickson type and the non-bad-dihedral condition of ρ depend only on the image and so pass to ρ|_{G_{F′}} in cases (b)–(d).

**Hypotheses.**

- ρ continuous with discrete coefficients (finite image); for ℓ-adic ρ apply the lemma to each finite quotient
- linear disjointness of F′ and K over F means K ⊗_F F′ is a field, equivalently [KF′ : F′] = [K : F] since K/F is Galois

**Construction and proof.**

1. Galois theory for the finite Galois extension K/F: restriction G_{F′} → Gal(K/F) has image Gal(K/K ∩ F′) because K/F is Galois (mathlib:IsGalois.intermediateFieldEquivSubgroup); the image is everything iff K ∩ F′ = F iff [KF′ : F′] = [K : F].
2. (d) The compositum F′(ζ_p) is linearly disjoint from K(ζ_p) over F(ζ_p) when F′ is Galois over F and linearly disjoint from K(ζ_p); apply (b) over F(ζ_p).
3. (e) For each Galois step F_i ⊂ F_{i+1} with solvable group, ρ(G_{F_{i+1}}) is normal in ρ(G_{F_i}) with solvable quotient, so H ∩ ρ(G_{F_{i+1}}) is normal in H with solvable quotient; H perfect has no nontrivial solvable quotient (mathlib:Group.IsPerfect.not_isSolvable), so H ⊂ ρ(G_{F_{i+1}}).
4. (f) follows from (b)–(d) as these properties are properties of the subgroup ρ(G_{F′}) ⊂ GL_n.

**Prerequisites.** `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/finite-coefficients-and-finite-quotients`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/restriction-dual-tensor-twist`; `mathlib:IsGalois.intermediateFieldEquivSubgroup`; `mathlib:IsGalois.fixedField_fixingSubgroup`; `mathlib:Group.IsPerfect`; `mathlib:Group.IsPerfect.not_isSolvable`; `mathlib:Group.IsPerfect.map`.

**Acceptance.**

- Instance: F = ℚ, ρ̄ = ρ̄_{E,p} surjective onto GL_2(F_p), F′ = ℚ(√d) with d not a square times ±p: ℚ(E[p]) ∩ F′ = ℚ when √d ∉ ℚ(E[p]); the image over F′ is again GL_2(F_p).
- Non-example: F′ = ℚ(√p*) ⊂ ℚ(ζ_p) ⊂ ℚ(E[p]) is never linearly disjoint, and ρ̄(G_{F′}) = {g : det g a square} has index 2.

#### Normal subgroups, quotients and automorphisms of SL_2, PSL_2, PGL_2 over finite fields

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/normal-subgroups-and-automorphisms-of-psl2-pgl2`. Kind: theorem. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.GL2Subgroup` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/ResidualImage/PSL2Automorphisms.lean`). Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4`.

Let k = F_q be a finite field of characteristic p. (a) If q ≥ 4: SL_2(k) is perfect, PSL_2(k) is simple, and every normal subgroup of GL_2(k) either contains SL_2(k) or is central (contained in k^×). The only normal subgroups of SL_2(k) are 1, {±1} ∩ SL_2(k), SL_2(k); hence its only nontrivial quotients are PSL_2(k) and SL_2(k). For q odd the only nontrivial proper normal subgroup of PGL_2(k) is PSL_2(k), of index 2; for q even PGL_2(k) = PSL_2(k) ≅ SL_2(k). Abelianisations: GL_2(k)^{ab} ≅ k^× via det (q ≥ 3), PGL_2(k)^{ab} ≅ k^×/k^{×2}. (b) Small fields: GL_2(F_2) ≅ S_3 has normal subgroup A_3 ≅ ℤ/3 (not central, not containing SL_2(F_2) = GL_2(F_2)); GL_2(F_3) has normal subgroups 1, {±1}, Q_8, SL_2(F_3), GL_2(F_3); PGL_2(F_3) ≅ S_4, PSL_2(F_3) ≅ A_4. In particular ‘central or ⊇ SL_2’ fails for q ≤ 3. (c) Automorphisms (Schreier–van der Waerden, Dieudonné): for q ≥ 4, Aut(PSL_2(F_q)) = Aut(PGL_2(F_q)) = PΓL_2(F_q) = PGL_2(F_q) ⋊ Gal(F_q/F_p), acting by conjugation and by the Frobenius on entries; for q = p ≥ 5 every automorphism of PGL_2(F_p) is inner. Consequently every automorphism of PSL_2(F_q) maps the class of an element with eigenvalue ratio α to one with ratio Frob^i(α), so eigenvalues in F_p are preserved up to scalar. (d) Products: if S is non-abelian simple, a subgroup of S^r projecting onto each factor is isomorphic to S^s, s ≤ r, cut out by diagonal identifications through automorphisms (Goursat), and Aut(S^r) = Aut(S)^r ⋊ S_r. (e) For two continuous ρ̄_1, ρ̄_2 : G_F → GL_2(k̄) whose projective images are PSL_2(F_q) or PGL_2(F_q), q ≥ 4, the projective kernel fields M_1, M_2 satisfy M_1 ∩ M_2 ∈ {F, a quadratic extension, M_1 = M_2}; if M_1 = M_2 then the projective representations are conjugate up to a Frobenius automorphism of F_q.

**Hypotheses.**

- q = |k|; q ≥ 4 in (a), (c), (e)
- (c) is quoted from the literature (Dieudonné 1951/1963, Steinberg), not reproved; its proof is sketched

**Construction and proof.**

1. (a) Perfectness and simplicity are in Mathlib (mathlib:Matrix.SL2.commutator_eq_top, mathlib:Matrix.ProjectiveSpecialLinearGroup.rank_two_simple). For N ⊴ GL_2(k): N ∩ SL_2 maps to a normal subgroup of PSL_2, trivial or all. If all, (N ∩ SL_2)·Z = SL_2 and perfectness gives SL_2 = [SL_2, SL_2] ⊂ N. If trivial, [N, GL_2] ⊂ N ∩ SL_2 ⊂ {±1}; for g ∈ N, h ↦ [g, h] is a homomorphism SL_2 → {±1}, trivial by perfectness, so g centralises SL_2(k), whose k-span is M_2(k), so g is scalar (mathlib:Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.center_eq_range_scalar).
2. Quotients of SL_2: a normal subgroup not containing SL_2 is central, i.e. inside {±1}. PGL_2(k)/PSL_2(k) ≅ k^×/k^{×2} via det; a normal subgroup of PGL_2 meets PSL_2 in 1 or PSL_2; in the first case it centralises PSL_2, hence is trivial.
3. (b) by direct computation in groups of order 6 and 48.
4. (c) An automorphism permutes the q + 1 Sylow p-subgroups (unipotent radicals of Borels, R01.4/p-subgroups-and-borel-subgroups), i.e. acts on P¹(F_q), normalising the image of PSL_2(F_q) in Sym(P¹(F_q)); that normaliser is PΓL_2(F_q) (Dieudonné, La géométrie des groupes classiques, Ch. IV §6; Steinberg's theorem on automorphisms of Chevalley groups for the general case, as cited by Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Newton–Thorne Lemma 5.2.3). For q = p, Gal(F_p/F_p) = 1.
5. (d) Goursat's lemma (mathlib:Subgroup.goursat) and simplicity by induction on r; minimal normal subgroups of S^r are the factors.
6. (e) Gal(M_1 ∩ M_2/F) is a common quotient of the two projective images; by (a) their nontrivial quotients are ℤ/2 and the group itself. If M_1 = M_2, the two projective representations differ by an automorphism of the image, which is given by (c).

**Prerequisites.** `mathlib:Matrix.SL2.commutator_eq_top`; `mathlib:Matrix.ProjectiveSpecialLinearGroup.rank_two_simple`; `mathlib:SL2Simple.PSL_commutator_eq_top`; `mathlib:Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.center_eq_range_scalar`; `mathlib:Matrix.ProjGenLinGroup`; `mathlib:Matrix.ProjectiveSpecialLinearGroup.toPGL`; `mathlib:Subgroup.goursat`; `mathlib:IsSimpleGroup`; `mathlib:Group.IsPerfect`; `mathlib:alternatingGroup.isSimpleGroup_five`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/p-subgroups-and-borel-subgroups`.

**Acceptance.**

- PGL_2(F_5) ≅ S_5 and PSL_2(F_5) ≅ A_5: Aut(A_5) = S_5 = PGL_2(F_5), all automorphisms of PGL_2(F_5) inner, consistent with (c) for q = p = 5.
- PSL_2(F_9) ≅ A_6: Aut(A_6) has order 1440 = 2·|PGL_2(F_9)| = |PΓL_2(F_9)|, so the Frobenius of F_9 gives automorphisms not induced by PGL_2(F_9); ‘every automorphism is inner’ needs q = p.
- For q = 3 the claim of Allen et al. Lemma 7.1.8(2) proof that normal subgroups of GL_2(F_l) are central or contain SL_2 fails (Q_8 ⊴ GL_2(F_3)); see PAPER-ALLEN-ETAL-23/E100.

**Sources.**

- accplus-cm-potential-automorphy, §7.1, proof of Lemma 7.1.8(2), printed p. 1092: “But any normal subgroup of GL2 (Fl ) either contains SL2 (Fl ) or” — Statement (a) for q = l ≥ 5 as used by ACC+ (fails for l ≤ 3, (b)).
- cg20, Remark 4.12, published p. 820 (author copy Siegel.pdf): “automorphisms of PGL2 .Fp / are inner, this implies that projective representations of” — Statement (c) for q = p ≥ 5 (text layer renders parentheses as dots and slashes).
- nt26, proof of Lemma 5.7, arXiv v2 p. 41: “are generated by PGL2 (Fta ) and the Frobenius” — Statement (c) for q = t^a, citing Dieudonné Ch. IV §6.
- bcgnt25, Lemma 5.2.3, arXiv v3 p. 51 (published pp. 45–46): “then any automorphism of G preserves” — Eigenvalue preservation in (c).
- dickson-linear-groups, §261, printed p. 286 (transcribed from the page image): “261. Theorem. — If p^n > 3, the linear fractional group G_{M(s)} is simple.” — Simplicity of PSL_2(F_q), q ≥ 4.

#### Residual images under restriction to cyclotomic fields

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/restriction-to-the-cyclotomic-field`. Kind: theorem. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.GaloisRep` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/ResidualImage/Cyclotomic.lean`). Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4`.

Let F be a number field, p a prime, k a finite field of characteristic p and ρ̄ : G_F → GL_2(k) continuous; write G = ρ̄(G_F), H = ρ̄(G_{F(ζ_p)}) ⊴ G with G/H a quotient of Gal(F(ζ_p)/F) ⊂ (ℤ/p)^× (cyclic). (a) [cyclic restriction] For p odd and m ≥ 1, ρ̄|_{G_{F(ζ_{p^m})}} is absolutely irreducible iff ρ̄|_{G_{F(ζ_p)}} is iff ρ̄|_{G_{F′}} is (R01.4/bad-dihedral-representations-and-the-oddness-criterion). (b) [Caraiani–Newton Lemma 7.1.1(1)] If ρ̄ is irreducible and ρ̄|_{G_{F(ζ_p)}} is absolutely reducible, then G lies in the normaliser of a Cartan subgroup of GL_2(k) (in the Cartan itself if ρ̄ is not absolutely irreducible). (c) [CN 7.1.1(2),(3)] If moreover k = F_p and det ρ̄ = χ̄_p: for p = 3, G is conjugate to C_s^+(3) or to a subgroup of C_ns(3); for p = 5 and [F(ζ_5) : F] = 4, G is conjugate to a subgroup of C_ns^+(5). (d) [big-image bookkeeping, BCGNT] If p ≥ 5, SL_2(F_p) ⊂ G ⊂ GL_2(F_p) and det ρ̄ is trivial on G_{F(ζ_p)} (for instance det ρ̄ = χ̄_p^{−m}), then H = SL_2(F_p). More generally if G ⊃ SL_2(F_q), q ≥ 4, then H ⊃ SL_2(F_q), and H's projective image is PSL_2(F_q) or PGL_2(F_q)-type by R01.4/dickson-classification-and-the-dyadic-refinement. (e) [Allen et al. Lemma 7.1.6(1)] If p > 3, F′/F is finite, ρ̄(G_{F̃}) ⊃ SL_2(F_p) for the normal closure F̃ of F, F′ is linearly disjoint from F̄^{ker ρ̄} over F and p is unramified in F′/ℚ, then ζ_p ∉ F̄^{ker ad ρ̄}·F′: the projective image PSL_2(k_0) or PGL_2(k_0) has no cyclic quotient of order p − 1 > 2 while Gal(F′(ζ_p)/F′) ≅ (ℤ/p)^×. (f) [Caraiani–Newton Lemma 6.1.4] If ζ_5 ∉ F and the projective image of ρ̄(G_{F(ζ_5)}) is conjugate to PSL_2(F_5), with ρ̄(G_F) ⊂ GL_2(F_5) and det ρ̄ = χ̄_5, then the field cut out by the projective image of ρ̄(G_F) does not contain ζ_5. (g) [Allen et al. Lemma 7.1.8(2), group part] If l ≥ 3 and Δ ⊴ GL_2(F_l) has det(Δ) = F_l^×, then Δ = GL_2(F_l). (h) For p > 2 and ρ̄|_{G_{F(ζ_p)}} absolutely irreducible: no nonzero X ∈ M_2(k) with Tr X = 0 satisfies ρ̄(σ)Xρ̄(σ)⁻¹ = X for all σ ∈ G_F, and none satisfies ρ̄(σ)Xρ̄(σ)⁻¹ = χ̄_p(σ)X for all σ (the invariants H⁰(G_F, ad⁰ρ̄) and H⁰(G_F, ad⁰ρ̄(1)) vanish once G7/adjoint-representations identifies ad⁰ρ̄ with this module).

**Hypotheses.**

- p prime; in (a), (h) p odd; in (d), (e) p ≥ 5 (perfectness of SL_2(F_p))
- (e) requires p unramified in F′, so that [F′(ζ_p) : F′] = p − 1
- (g) needs l ≥ 3: for l = 2, A_3 ⊴ GL_2(F_2) ≅ S_3 has det(A_3) = F_2^× = {1} but A_3 ≠ GL_2(F_2); Allen et al. print Lemma 7.1.8(2) without l > 2 (PAPER-ALLEN-ETAL-23/E100)

**Construction and proof.**

1. (a) is R01.4/bad-dihedral-representations-and-the-oddness-criterion (b).
2. (b) H is absolutely reducible and normal in G; by R01.4/dihedral-projective-image-iff-induced (d) and R01.4/p-subgroups-and-borel-subgroups, H is diagonalisable over k̄ with eigenlines {D_1, D_2}, a Frobenius-stable pair; G permutes it, so G lies in the normaliser of the split (D_i rational) or non-split (D_i conjugate over F_{q²}) Cartan attached to it; if H is scalar, π(G) is cyclic, G abelian, contained in a Cartan. CN prove (1) with [FLHS15, Lemma 2.2].
3. (c) Case analysis of irreducible subgroups of N(C) ⊂ GL_2(F_3), GL_2(F_5) with surjective determinant, following CN's proof via [FLHS15, Prop. 4.1(b)].
4. (d) det is trivial on G_{F(ζ_p)} so H ⊂ SL_2(F_p) ∩ G; G/H is abelian, so H ⊃ [G, G] ⊃ [SL_2(F_p), SL_2(F_p)] = SL_2(F_p) by mathlib:Matrix.SL2.commutator_eq_top.
5. (e) As in Allen et al.: reduce to m = 1; by R01.4/image-of-restriction-to-a-subfield the projective image over F′ equals that over F, which is PSL_2(k_0) or PGL_2(k_0) (R01.4/dickson-classification-and-the-dyadic-refinement (c)) with abelianisation of order ≤ 2 (R01.4/normal-subgroups-and-automorphisms-of-psl2-pgl2); if ζ_p were in the compositum, (ℤ/p)^× of order p − 1 > 2 would be a quotient.
6. (f) CN: ρ̄(G_{F(ζ_5)}) ⊂ SL_2(F_5) surjects onto PSL_2(F_5), so equals SL_2(F_5); compare [G : H] with [F(ζ_5) : F] according as det ρ̄ has order 2 or 4.
7. (g) By R01.4/normal-subgroups-and-automorphisms-of-psl2-pgl2 (a) for l ≥ 5, Δ is central (det(Δ) ⊂ squares, not all of F_l^×) or contains SL_2(F_l); for l = 3 every proper normal subgroup of GL_2(F_3) lies in SL_2(F_3) (list (b)).
8. (h) An X of the first kind commutes with the absolutely irreducible ρ̄(G_{F(ζ_p)}), so is scalar by Schur, hence 0 as Tr X = 2x and p ≠ 2; an X of the second kind is invariant under G_{F(ζ_p)} (χ̄_p trivial there), hence scalar, and Tr X = 0 forces X = 0.

**Prerequisites.** `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/bad-dihedral-representations-and-the-oddness-criterion`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/cartan-subgroups-and-normalisers`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/dickson-classification-and-the-dyadic-refinement`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/normal-subgroups-and-automorphisms-of-psl2-pgl2`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/image-of-restriction-to-a-subfield`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/dihedral-projective-image-iff-induced`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/p-subgroups-and-borel-subgroups`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/cyclotomic-and-dirichlet-characters`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/absolutely-irreducible`; `mathlib:Matrix.SL2.commutator_eq_top`; `mathlib:IsCyclotomicExtension.autEquivPow`.

**Acceptance.**

- Instance: for E/ℚ with surjective mod-p image, p ≥ 5, the image of G_{ℚ(ζ_p)} on E[p] is SL_2(F_p) by (d).
- Instance (CN): for p = 5 and [F(ζ_5) : F] = 4, an irreducible ρ̄ with cyclotomically reducible restriction has image in C_ns^+(5).
- Non-example for (g) at l = 3 in the source's form: Q_8 ⊴ GL_2(F_3) is neither central nor ⊇ SL_2(F_3).

**Sources.**

- cn23, Lemma 7.1.1, p. 92 of arXiv v3: “Lemma 7.1.1. Let F be a number field and ρ : GF → GL2 (Fp ) an irreducible” — Statements (b), (c).
- cn23, Lemma 6.1.4, p. 88 of arXiv v3: “extension of F cut out by the projective image of r E,5 (GF ) does not contain ζ5 .” — Statement (f).
- bcgnt25, proof of Proposition 6.2.3, arXiv v3 p. 63 (published p. 56): “conditions hold by assumption (13) and Lemma 5.2.4.” — The bookkeeping (d) (maintainer item PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25/139) feeds hypothesis (13) into Lemma 5.2.4.
- accplus-cm-potential-automorphy, §7.1, Lemma 7.1.6, printed p. 1090: “(1) If l is unramified in F 0 /Q, then ζl 6∈ F” — Statement (e) (text layer renders ∉ as 6∈ and F′ as F 0).
