#### Large residual image: persistence under small index and soluble base change, and a tame-inertia criterion

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/large-image-persistence`. Kind: theorem. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.GaloisRep` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/ResidualImage/LargeImage.lean`). Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4`.

Let p ≥ 5 and G ⊂ GL_2(F̄_p) a finite subgroup containing a conjugate of SL_2(F_{p^a}) with p^a ≥ 5. (a) [Newton–Thorne Lemma 2.3(3), group part] If a ≥ 2, every subgroup H ⊂ G of index [G : H] < 2p contains gSL_2(F_{p^a})g⁻¹, the same conjugate that G contains. The bound a ≥ 2 is needed (Newton–Thorne assume a ≥ a_0(p) ≥ 3): for a = 1 the Borel subgroup of SL_2(F_p) has index p + 1 < 2p. (b) [perfect subgroups] If H ⊂ ρ̄(G_F) is perfect (e.g. a conjugate of SL_2(F_{p^a}), p^a ≥ 4), it remains in the image after restriction to any soluble tower F′/F (R01.4/image-of-restriction-to-a-subfield (e)); in particular ‘ρ̄(G_F) contains a conjugate of SL_2(F_{p^a})’ survives soluble base change. (c) [tame-inertia criterion, after Boxer–Calegari–Gee Theorem 3.1] Let ρ̄ : G_ℚ → GL_2(F̄_p) be continuous, unramified outside p, with ρ̄|_{G_{ℚ_p}} absolutely irreducible and ρ̄|_{I_p} ≅ ω_2^{a} ⊕ ω_2^{pa} for an integer a with gcd(a, p + 1) = 1. Then ρ̄(G_ℚ) contains a conjugate of SL_2(F_p). Statements that need automorphic input (Newton–Thorne Proposition 5.4 and Theorem 5.9, large image from tamely dihedral local components) are not stated here; their group-theoretic step is R01.4/dickson-classification-and-the-dyadic-refinement (e).

**Hypotheses.**

- p ≥ 5 in (a), (c)
- (c) uses fundamental characters ω_2 of niveau 2 (R01.2/tame-inertia-and-fundamental-characters)

**Construction and proof.**

1. (a) Put S = gSL_2(F_{p^a})g⁻¹ ⊂ G and q = p^a. Then [S : H ∩ S] ≤ [G : H] < 2p. By Galois's theorem (Dickson §262) a proper subgroup of PSL_2(F_q) has index ≥ q + 1 unless q ∈ {2, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11}; a proper subgroup of SL_2(F_q) maps to a proper subgroup of PSL_2(F_q) (a subgroup surjecting onto PSL_2 is all of the perfect group SL_2, mathlib:Matrix.SL2.commutator_eq_top), so it has index ≥ q + 1 as well. For a ≥ 2, q ≥ 25 and q + 1 > 2p, so H ∩ S = S. Newton–Thorne quote Lemma 2.3 from Thorne 2024 Lemma 7.3; the adequacy parts (1)–(2) belong to ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7.
2. (b) Group.IsPerfect has no nontrivial solvable quotient; apply R01.4/image-of-restriction-to-a-subfield (e).
3. (c) The projective image of I_p is generated by ω_2^{a(1−p)}, of order (p + 1)/gcd(p + 1, a) = p + 1 > 5, so π(ρ̄(G_ℚ)) is not A_4, S_4, A_5 (R01.4/dickson-classification-and-the-dyadic-refinement (e)); it is not in a Borel since ρ̄|_{G_{ℚ_p}} is absolutely irreducible. If it were dihedral, ρ̄ would be induced from the quadratic field cut out by the rotation subgroup (R01.4/dihedral-projective-image-iff-induced), unramified outside p, hence ℚ(√p*); then ρ̄|_{G_{ℚ_p}} is induced from ℚ_p(√p*) and hence ≅ ρ̄|_{G_{ℚ_p}} ⊗ η with η the quadratic character of ℚ_p(√p*)/ℚ_p, η|_{I_p} = ω^{(p−1)/2} = ω_2^{(p²−1)/2}. Comparing {ω_2^{a}, ω_2^{pa}} with {ω_2^{a+(p²−1)/2}, ω_2^{pa+(p²−1)/2}}: the first cannot match itself (ω_2 has order p² − 1), so ω_2^{a+(p²−1)/2} = ω_2^{pa}, i.e. (p − 1)a ≡ (p² − 1)/2 mod p² − 1, i.e. a ≡ (p + 1)/2 mod p + 1, and then gcd(a, p + 1) = (p + 1)/2 > 1, a contradiction (Boxer–Calegari–Gee write this as k ≡ (p + 3)/2 mod p + 1 for a = 1 − k, up to their sign convention, sourceIssue PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-25/E9). The remaining case PSL_2/PGL_2(F_{p^s}) gives SL_2(F_{p^s}) ⊂ ρ̄(G_ℚ) by (c) of the Dickson node.

**Prerequisites.** `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/dickson-classification-and-the-dyadic-refinement`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/image-of-restriction-to-a-subfield`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/dihedral-projective-image-iff-induced`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/normal-subgroups-and-automorphisms-of-psl2-pgl2`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/tame-inertia-and-fundamental-characters`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/decomposition-group-at-a-place`; `mathlib:Group.IsPerfect`; `mathlib:Matrix.SL2.commutator_eq_top`.

**Acceptance.**

- Instance (BCG25): for the weight-26 form ΔE_4²E_6 at p = 107, non-ordinary with gcd(k − 1, p + 1) = 1, the residual image contains SL_2(F_107); its determinant ε̄^{−25} is surjective, so the image is GL_2(F_107) (Swinnerton-Dyer's computation, maintainer item PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-25/sd73-image; the modular-form input is not planned here).
- Sharpness for a = 1: in SL_2(F_5) ≅ 2.A_5 the subgroup SL_2(F_3) ≅ 2.A_4 has index 5 < 10 and the Borel has index 6 < 10; neither contains SL_2(F_5).

**Sources.**

- nt26, Lemma 2.3(3), arXiv v2 p. 10: “If H ≤ G is a subgroup of index [G : H] < 2p, then H contains a conjugate” — Statement (a).
- dickson-linear-groups, §262, printed p. 286 (transcribed from the page image): “The group G_{M(s)} always has subgroups of index s + 1, but has subgroups of lower index only when s = 2, 3, 5, 7, 3², 11.” — Galois's minimal-index theorem used in (a).
- nt26, Theorem 4.1, paragraph after the statement, arXiv v2 p. 26: “H is perfect in condition (6) ensures that this condition will still be satisfied after” — Statement (b).
- bcg25-gln, proof of Theorem 3.1, published p. 516: “contains a cyclic subgroup of order p + 1 > 5, so ρf does not” — Statement (c).

#### Characteristic two: non-solvable residual images and the module M_2(F)

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/characteristic-two-residual-image-facts`. Kind: theorem. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.GL2Subgroup` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/ResidualImage/CharacteristicTwo.lean`). Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4`.

Let F be a finite field of characteristic 2, F_0 ⊂ F a subfield with |F_0| = 2^r, r ≥ 2, and G_0 = SL_2(F_0) ≅ PGL_2(F_0) acting on Ad := M_2(F) by conjugation (through SL_2(F_0) ⊂ GL_2(F)); Z := F·1 ⊂ Ad^0 := {X : Tr X = 0} ⊂ Ad (Z ⊂ Ad^0 since Tr 1 = 2 = 0). Let ρ̄ : G_K → GL_2(F) be continuous and absolutely irreducible with non-solvable image, K a number field. (a) [projective image] π(ρ̄(G_K)) is conjugate to PGL_2(F_0) = PSL_2(F_0) ≅ SL_2(F_0) for some F_0 ⊂ F with |F_0| ≥ 4 (R01.4/dickson-classification-and-the-dyadic-refinement (d)). (b) [Khare–Wintenberger II Lemma 4.3(2)(ii)] H⁰(G_0, Ad) = H⁰(G_0, Ad^0) = Z is one-dimensional, and H⁰(G_0, Ad/Z) = H⁰(G_0, (Ad^0)^*) = 0, where (Ad^0)^* ≅ Ad/Z through the trace pairing. (c) [KW II Lemma 4.3(5)(i), Dickinson Lemma 42] H¹(SL_2(F_0), M_2(F)) = 0. (d) [KW II Lemma 4.3(5)(ii)] The only G_0-submodules of Ad are 0, Z, Ad^0, Ad; the only nonzero irreducible submodule is Z. (e) Every one-dimensional F[G_0]-module is trivial (G_0 perfect), and Ad^0/Z is the Frobenius-twisted natural representation, irreducible of dimension 2.

**Hypotheses.**

- characteristic 2 and |F_0| ≥ 4 (for F_0 = F_2, SL_2(F_2) ≅ S_3 is solvable and (b)–(d) fail)
- (c) is quoted from Dickinson (Duke 2001) through KW II; Dickinson's paper was not read (see gaps)

**Construction and proof.**

1. (b) As in KW II: an element of Ad^G0 commutes with the absolutely irreducible SL_2(F_0), so is scalar (Schur); Ad^0 ∋ 1. For Ad/Z: if l ∈ Ad maps to a nonzero invariant of Ad/Z, take g ∈ G_0 semisimple non-scalar with eigenlines D_1, D_2; Ad(g) acts unipotently on the plane P = ⟨1, l⟩ and 1 is not an eigenvalue on Ad/P, so P is the diagonal subalgebra for D_1 ⊕ D_2; P is G_0-stable, so G_0 stabilises {D_1, D_2} and would be solvable, a contradiction. The trace pairing identifies (Ad^0)^* with Ad/Z.
2. (c) Dickinson Lemma 42, quoted by KW II; equivalently Ext¹_{F[SL_2(F_0)]}(V, V) = 0 for the natural module V = F², since H¹(G, Hom(V, V)) = Ext¹(V, V). The composition factors of Ad are Z ≅ F, Ad^0/Z ≅ V^{(2)} (torus weights λ^{±2}) and Ad/Ad^0 ≅ F (trace), and H¹(SL_2(F_0), F) = 0 (perfect); the vanishing of H¹(G_0, Ad) is not a formal consequence of these factors and is Dickinson's computation.
3. (d) KW II: 1-dimensional submodules are trivial, hence inside H⁰ = Z; a 2-dimensional submodule of Ad^0 would give a trivial quotient Ad^0 → F, a nonzero element of H⁰((Ad^0)^*), contradicting (b); a 2-dimensional V ⊂ Ad meets Ad^0 in Z, and V/Z ⊂ Ad/Z would be a trivial line, contradicting H⁰(Ad/Z) = 0; a 3-dimensional V ≠ Ad^0 meets Ad^0 in dimension ≥ 2, so contains Ad^0 and equals it.
4. (e) mathlib:Matrix.SL2.commutator_eq_top (|F_0| ≥ 4 provides a with a ≠ 0, a² ≠ 1).

**Prerequisites.** `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/dickson-classification-and-the-dyadic-refinement`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/p-subgroups-and-borel-subgroups`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/normal-subgroups-and-automorphisms-of-psl2-pgl2`; `mathlib:Matrix.SL2.commutator_eq_top`; `mathlib:Matrix.ProjectiveSpecialLinearGroup.isoPSLOfAlgClosed`; `mathlib:Representation`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ProfiniteCohomology#layer-10-continuous-cohomology-in-all-degrees`.

**Acceptance.**

- Instance: F_0 = F = F_4, G_0 = SL_2(F_4) ≅ A_5 acting on M_2(F_4): Z ⊂ Ad^0 ⊂ Ad with Ad^0/Z ≅ V^{(2)} of dimension 2, irreducible.
- Degenerate failure: for F_0 = F_2, SL_2(F_2) ≅ S_3 has abelianisation ℤ/2, so H¹(S_3, F_2) ≠ 0 and S_3 is solvable; r ≥ 2 is necessary for (a), (e) and for H¹(G_0, Z) = 0.
- Odd p contrast: for p odd, Ad = Z ⊕ Ad^0 and H¹(SL_2(F_p), ad^0) is owned by ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7 (G7/h1-of-sl2-with-adjoint-coefficients).

**Sources.**

- kw-serre-modularity-II, §4.1.4, Lemma 4.3(2)(ii), p. 40 of proofs.pdf: “Further H 0 (G, Ad) = H 0 (G, Ad0 ) = Z is 1-” — Statement (b).
- kw-serre-modularity-II, §4.1.4, Lemma 4.3(5), p. 40: “(ii) The only G-submodules of Ad are 0, Z, Ad0 , Ad.” — Statement (d).
- kw-serre-modularity-II, proof of Lemma 4.3(5)(i), p. 41: “(i) This is Lemma 42 of [21]: in loc. cit. it is proved that given finite” — Statement (c), quoted from Dickinson [21].
- kw-serre-modularity-II, proof of Lemma 4.3(2)(ii), p. 40: “and Dickson’s theorem the projective image of ρ̄ is PGL2 (F0 ) ≃ SL2 (F0 ) for” — Statement (a).

## R01.5. Recognition by Frobenius polynomials

This layer proves that a continuous semisimple Galois representation is determined by the
characteristic polynomials of its Frobenius elements, and it says exactly when such data, given
over a smaller coefficient field, comes from a representation over that field. It supplies the
arithmetic half of the comparison: density of Frobenius elements, continuity, the finite-image and
Haar-measure forms of Chebotarev, and coefficient descent with its Brauer-class obstruction.

It owns none of the following, and cites them:

- the Chebotarev density theorem for finite Galois extensions, `hasDirichletDensity_frobeniusPrimeSet`
  with value `#C/#G` (Tau Ceti Chebotarev, layer 10; natural density, layer 14), and the density
  predicates `HasDirichletDensity` and its bounds (Tau Ceti Arithmetic Dirichlet Series, layer 7);
- multiplicative polynomial laws, determinants, Cayley–Hamilton algebras and the reconstruction
  theorems (IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.0 and IHG.1; uniqueness of determinants from
  Frobenius density over finite quotients is IHG.4, which may consume the density theorem below);
- the Brauer group, splitting fields and the Wedderburn presentation (Tau Ceti SemisimpleAlgebras,
  layers 1, 2 and 6);
- Brauer–Nesbitt, semisimplification, coefficient extension and the Baire descent to a finite
  coefficient field (R01.1), and decomposition groups, Frobenius lifts and the Frobenius
  characteristic polynomial `P_v(ρ, X) = det(X − ρ(Frob_v))` with arithmetic Frobenius (R01.2);
- closed-point Chebotarev on curves over finite fields (DeligneWeightsAndPurity DWP.3).

### Pinned conventions

Frobenius is arithmetic (`x ↦ x^{q_v}` on the residue field), as in Deligne–Serre, whose
"substitution de Frobenius" follows Artin. A density-one set means Dirichlet density one, the ratio
to the all-prime sum. Coefficient fields are of the standard kinds: finite fields with the discrete
topology, and fields of characteristic zero (finite over `ℚ_ℓ`, `ℚ̄_ℓ`, `ℂ`). A residual and a
characteristic-zero representation are never compared directly; two representations are compared
only after both are extended to a common field.

### The density of Frobenius elements

- **Density of Frobenius elements.** For a number field `K` and a set `Σ` of finite places of
  Dirichlet density one, the arithmetic Frobenius lifts at the places of `K̄` above `Σ` are dense in
  `G_K`. Concretely, every coset `gU` of an open normal subgroup contains a Frobenius lift at
  places of a set of density at least `1/[G_K : U]`. The proof applies layer-10 Chebotarev to the
  finite Galois extension `K̄^U/K`. It then intersects with `Σ`, using that a density-one set meets
  every set of positive density, and lifts a prime of `K̄^U` to a place of `K̄`. The corollary used
  everywhere: if `φ : G_K → H` is continuous, `H` is Hausdorff and `φ` kills inertia at `Σ`, then
  any closed condition satisfied by all `φ(Frob_w)` holds on `φ(G_K)`.
- **Every element of a finite image is a Frobenius.** If `φ : G_K → H` has finite image, then
  each `h ∈ φ(G_K)` equals `φ(Frob_w)` for places `w` over a set of `v` of density
  `#(class of h)/#φ(G_K)`, outside any finite set. This is the step of Deligne–Serre 6.12 that
  puts the characteristic-polynomial coefficients of every image element into `k_f`.
- **Prescribed quadratic symbols.** For nonzero integers `d_1, …, d_r` and signs `ε_i`,
  infinitely many odd primes `p ∤ ∏ d_i` have `(d_i/p) = ε_i` for all `i` exactly when
  `∏_{i∈J} ε_i = 1` for every `J` with `∏_{i∈J} d_i` a square. These primes then have density
  `[ℚ(√d_i : i) : ℚ]^{-1}`. The Frobenius action on the generators is Tau Ceti's
  `exists_isArithFrobAt_multiquadratic`. Two non-squares are always simultaneous nonresidues
  infinitely often, even when `ℚ(√d_1) = ℚ(√d_2)`.

### Chebotarev recognition

- **Recognition.** Let `ρ_1, ρ_2` be continuous `n`-dimensional representations of `G_K`, over
  coefficient fields `E_1, E_2`, unramified outside a finite set `S`. Suppose
  `P_v(ρ_1, X) = P_v(ρ_2, X)` in `E[X]` for all `v` in a density-one set disjoint from `S`, where
  `E` is a common extension. Then `(ρ_1 ⊗ E)^ss ≅ (ρ_2 ⊗ E)^ss`. The proof extends both
  representations to `E`. Density and continuity then give equal characteristic polynomials on all
  of `G_K`, and Brauer–Nesbitt (R01.1) finishes.
  - Traces suffice when `n!` is invertible in `E`.
  - In rank two, trace and determinant together are the characteristic polynomial, in every
    characteristic.
  - The same argument works for any profinite group and any dense subset.
- **Curves over finite fields.** Let `C` be a smooth geometrically connected curve over `F_q` and
  `U ⊂ C` a dense open. Two lisse `E`-sheaves on `C` (`E` of characteristic zero) with equal
  characteristic polynomials at every closed point of `U` have isomorphic semisimplifications. The
  inputs are that `π_1(U) → π_1(C)` is surjective and DWP.3's closed-point Chebotarev. This is
  the step of Kisin–Zhou, Proposition 5.3.5, that controls a point outside `U` by continuity.

### Coefficient descent and its obstruction

- **The Brauer class of an absolutely irreducible representation.** For `ρ : Γ → GL_n(k̄)`
  absolutely irreducible, define the following objects.
  - The trace field `k(ρ)`.
  - The image algebra `B(ρ)`, the `k(ρ)`-span of `ρ(Γ)`. The trace-dual-basis argument of
    BLGGT's Lemma A.1.5 shows it is central simple of dimension `n²` over `k(ρ)`, in every
    characteristic.
  - The class `β(ρ) = [B(ρ)] ∈ Br(k(ρ))`.
  - The Schur index, the index of `β(ρ)`.

  For an absolutely irreducible determinant with `k(ρ) = k`, `B(ρ)` is Chenevier's central simple
  quotient `k[Γ]/ker(D)` (Definition-Proposition 2.18).
- **Descent obstruction.** Let `k` be perfect and `ρ ≅ ⊕ ρ_i^{m_i}` semisimple over `k̄`, with
  every characteristic polynomial in `k[X]`.
  - `Gal(k̄/k)` permutes the constituents and preserves the multiplicities.
  - `ρ` is realizable over `k` exactly when the Schur index of each `ρ_i` divides `m_i`.
  - In determinant language: under Chenevier's Theorem 2.16, `k[Γ]/ker(D) ≅ ∏ S_i` and
    `D = ∏ det_{S_i}^{m_i}`, and `D` comes from a `k`-representation exactly when `ind(S_i)`
    divides `m_i` for every `i`.
  - An absolutely irreducible `ρ` descends to `k` exactly when `β(ρ) = 1`, and to `k'` exactly
    when `k'` splits `B(ρ)`.
- **Finite fields.** Deligne–Serre's Lemme 6.13 follows. A semisimple representation over a finite
  field `k'` is realizable over any subfield `k` that contains the coefficients of all its
  characteristic polynomials. The reason is Deligne–Serre's: the Brauer group of a finite field is
  trivial (`TauCeti.subsingleton_brauerGroup_of_finite`), so no Schur index intervenes. Applied
  to a residual Galois representation, the field generated by the Frobenius polynomials suffices,
  because every image element is a Frobenius.
- **One rational regular element.** BLGGT's Lemma A.1.5 covers characteristic zero. If `r` is
  semisimple with traces in `M` and some `r(γ)` has `n` distinct `M`-rational eigenvalues, then
  `r` is conjugate into `GL_n(M)`. The regular element forces every Schur index and every centre
  degree in the Wedderburn decomposition of the image algebra to be one.

### Compact images, lifts, and two image-theoretic criteria

- **Haar-measure Chebotarev.** Let `ρ : G_K → G` be surjective and continuous onto a profinite
  group, unramified outside `S`, and let `μ` be the normalised Haar measure (unique among
  probability Haar measures in Mathlib).
  - An open and closed conjugation-stable set `C` is hit by Frobenius with density `μ(C)`.
  - A closed `C` is hit with upper density at most `μ(C)`.
  - So a closed null set is hit with density zero, and a set with null boundary with density
    `μ(C)`.
  - On an open subgroup of `GL_n(ℤ_ℓ)` the zero locus of a polynomial that is not identically
    zero is null. For example, trace-zero Frobenius has density zero when the image is open in
    `GL_2(ℤ_ℓ)`.

  This is the "By Chebotarev ... positive measure" step of Calegari–Geraghty, Lemma A.8, and
  Serre's qualitative argument.
- **Carayol's lemma.** Let `R` be complete Noetherian local with finite residue field, and let
  `r, r'` be continuous lifts of the same absolutely irreducible `r̄`. Suppose their
  characteristic polynomials agree on a dense set, for instance on Frobenius elements at a
  density-one set.
  - Then `r' = g r g^{-1}` with `g ≡ 1` modulo `m_R`, unique up to `1 + m_R`.
  - For symplectic similitude representations with a common multiplier, `g` can be taken in the
    kernel of `GSp_{2m}(R) → GSp_{2m}(k)`. The reason is Schur's lemma: the invariant forms with
    a fixed multiplier form a free rank-one module.
  - Lifts over `R/𝔞_j` with prescribed characteristic polynomials can be conjugated into
    compatibility and glued over `R`.

  The algebra over henselian rings is IHG.1, through Chenevier's Theorem 2.22, which needs only a
  split and absolutely irreducible residual determinant.
- **GSp4 semisimplicity criteria.** These are Propositions 4.11.1–4.11.2 of
  Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni. Suppose the full characteristic polynomial of `ρ(Frob_l)`
  annihilates `s(Frob_l)` on a density-one set. Then `s ≅ ρ^{⊕m}` in two cases:
  - the Zariski closure of `ρ` contains `Sp_4`;
  - `ρ` is absolutely irreducible, becomes reducible on an index-two subgroup, and its Zariski
    closure contains `SL_2 × SL_2`.

  The first step in both cases is that the annihilation identity holds on all of `G_ℚ`, by density
  and continuity.
- **Potentially abelian representations.** Let `ρ` be irreducible and continuous in characteristic
  zero, with `ρ(G_L)` abelian for a finite Galois `L/F`.
  - `ρ|_{G_L} = ⊕_{i=1}^{b} χ_i^{⊕a}` over a single Galois orbit of characters.
  - `ρ ≅ Ind_{G_{K_i}}^{G_F} V_i` with `[K_i : F] = b`.
  - `b = 1` exactly when `G_L` acts by scalars.

  The proof is Clifford theory (InductionRestriction, layer 5) through the finite quotient
  `Gal(L/F)`.

### ⚠ Pitfalls and false generalisations

- **Traces are not enough in small characteristic.** Over `F_4`, take a cubic character
  `χ : G_ℚ → Gal(ℚ(ζ_7)^+/ℚ) ≅ F_4^×`. Then `1 ⊕ 1` and `χ ⊕ χ` both have trace `0` everywhere,
  but at `p = 2` their characteristic polynomials are `X² + 1` and `X² + χ(Frob_2)²`. Recognition
  uses characteristic polynomials whenever `0 < char E ≤ n`.
- **Only semisimplifications are recognised.** A nonsplit extension of `1` by `1`, for example
  through the `ℤ_ℓ`-quotient of the cyclotomic character, has the same Frobenius polynomials as
  `1 ⊕ 1`. The same holds for lisse sheaves on curves, using the degree map.
- **A trace-and-determinant system over `k` need not descend to `k`.** The two-dimensional
  representation of `Q_8` has rational characteristic polynomials.
  - It is not realizable over `ℝ`, because `[ℍ] ≠ 1` in `Br(ℝ)` (`TauCeti.Quaternion.mk_ne_one`).
  - Composed with a quaternion extension of `ℚ`, it gives a Galois representation that is not
    realizable over `ℚ` or `ℚ_2`, yet is realizable over `ℚ_ℓ` for every odd `ℓ`.
  - `ρ ⊕ ρ` is realizable over `ℝ`: multiplicities matter.
- **Perfectness matters.** Over `F_p(t)`, `χ^{⊕p}` with `χ(1) = t^{1/p}` has characteristic
  polynomial `X^p − t ∈ k[X]` and does not descend, although no Brauer class is involved. The
  descent theorem is stated for perfect `k`, which covers every coefficient field of this roadmap.
- **Absolute irreducibility in Carayol's lemma is necessary.** With residual representation
  `1 ⊕ 1` over `F_p[ε]`, the lifts `1 ⊕ 1` and `[[1, εc],[0, 1]]` have equal characteristic
  polynomials and are not conjugate.
- **A density-zero set is not an empty set.** A Haar-null class can contain Frobenius elements:
  for the cyclotomic character and `C = {a}`, the prime `a` lies in it. Haar-measure Chebotarev
  gives densities, not finiteness. The effective bounds of Serre's Théorème 15 need the effective
  Chebotarev theorem and are not part of this layer.
- **Chenevier's two definitions of "split" differ.** "The determinant of a `k`-representation" and
  "`R/ker(D)` is a product of matrix algebras over `k`" are not equivalent: `ℝ[Q_8]` acting on `ℍ`
  is a counterexample (source issue E501). Realizability is the first; the second is the stronger
  condition that every Brauer class vanishes.

### Acceptance

- The `F_4` pair above: equal traces, different characteristic polynomials, non-isomorphic.
- Deligne–Serre Lemme 3.2 and Dieulefait–Pacetti's Remark 4 (trace and determinant on a
  density-one set) are special cases of the recognition theorem.
- A semisimple representation over `F_4` with `F_2`-rational characteristic polynomials (a
  `GL_2(F_4)`-conjugate of the standard representation of `S_3 ≅ GL_2(F_2)`) descends to
  `GL_2(F_2)`.
- The quaternion representation: Schur index `2` over `ℚ`, `ℝ` and `ℚ_2`, and `1` over `ℚ_ℓ` for
  odd `ℓ`.
- BLGGT's Lemma A.1.5 is consistent with `Q_8`: no element of `Q_8` has two distinct rational
  eigenvalues.
- Primes at which both `2` and `8` are nonresidues have density `1/2`. No prime makes `2`, `3`
  and `6` all nonresidues.
- For an open image in `GL_2(ℤ_ℓ)`, the trace-zero primes have density zero.
- A scalar residual representation shows Carayol's lemma fails without absolute irreducibility.

*Prerequisites:* R01.1, R01.2; IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.0–IHG.1; Tau Ceti Chebotarev
layers 10 and 14, Arithmetic Dirichlet Series layer 7, Number Field Arithmetic layer 2,
SemisimpleAlgebras layers 1, 2 and 6, InductionRestriction layer 5; DeligneWeightsAndPurity DWP.3;
InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups IG.1.

### Declarations of R01.5

Each entry gives the mathematical statement, hypotheses, proof route, prerequisites, uses, API, unit tests, acceptance checks and sources of one planned declaration.

#### Density of Frobenius elements

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.5/frobenius-density`. Kind: theorem. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.GaloisRep` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/Recognition/FrobeniusDensity.lean`). Planet: **Density of Frobenius elements**. Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.5`.

Let K be a number field, G_K = Field.absoluteGaloisGroup K with its Krull topology, and Σ a set of finite places of K of Dirichlet density 1 (HasDirichletDensity Σ 1; every cofinite set qualifies). Call σ ∈ G_K a Σ-Frobenius if σ is an arithmetic Frobenius lift at some place w of K̄ above some v ∈ Σ, i.e. σ ∈ D_w and σ(x) ≡ x^{q_v} modulo the maximal ideal of w for all integral x (R01.2/decomposition-group-at-a-place). Then: (a) the set Frob(Σ) of Σ-Frobenius elements is dense in G_K; more precisely, for every open normal subgroup U ⊴ G_K and every g ∈ G_K, the set of v ∈ Σ unramified in L = K̄^U for which some w | v has every Frobenius lift at w in gU has Dirichlet density at least 1/[G_K : U] (exactly #C/[G_K:U] for the conjugacy class C of gU in Gal(L/K)). (b) If φ : G_K → H is a continuous homomorphism to a Hausdorff topological group with φ(I_w) = 1 for every w above every v ∈ Σ, then φ(Frob_w) depends only on w, the set {φ(Frob_w) : w | v, v ∈ Σ} is dense in the compact subgroup φ(G_K), and every closed subset of H that contains φ(Frob_w) for all w above v ∈ Σ contains φ(G_K). (c) In particular, for any finite set S of finite places and continuous ρ : G_K → GL_n(A) unramified outside S (A a Hausdorff topological ring), the elements ρ(Frob_w), w | v, v ∉ S ∪ T, are dense in ρ(G_K) for every finite T, and any continuous function on ρ(G_K) (e.g. γ ↦ det(X − γ) coefficientwise) vanishing at all of them vanishes on ρ(G_K).

**Hypotheses.**

- K a number field; finite places only (real places may ramify; no condition at infinity).
- Σ has Dirichlet density 1 in the sense of ArithmeticDirichletSeries layer 7 (ratio to the all-prime sum); a set of natural density 1 also has Dirichlet density 1.
- In (b) and (c) the target is Hausdorff and φ (resp. ρ) kills inertia at every place of Σ (resp. outside S), so that φ(Frob_w) is independent of the Frobenius lift.
- Arithmetic Frobenius (x ↦ x^{q_v}); the statement is unchanged for geometric Frobenius because inversion is a homeomorphism preserving conjugacy classes.

**Construction and proof.**

1. Reduce (a) to a finite quotient: a basic open set of G_K is a coset gU with U open normal; L = K̄^U is finite Galois over K (Krull topology) and only finitely many v ramify in L (NumberFieldArithmetic layer 6 / tauceti:NumberField.Chebotarev.finite_compl_iUnion_frobeniusPrimeSet).
2. Apply the Chebotarev density theorem of tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/Chebotarev layer 10 (hasDirichletDensity_frobeniusPrimeSet) to L/K and the class C of g|_L: frobeniusPrimeSet K L C has Dirichlet density #C/#Gal(L/K) > 0.
3. Intersect with Σ: the complement of Σ has density 0, so Σ ∩ frobeniusPrimeSet K L C has positive upper density and is in particular nonempty and infinite (density API of ArithmeticDirichletSeries layer 7: a set of positive density is not contained in a density-zero set).
4. For v in the intersection, tauceti:NumberField.Chebotarev.mem_frobeniusPrimeSet_mk_iff_exists_isArithFrobAt gives a prime Q of O_L above v with g|_L an arithmetic Frobenius at Q (mathlib:IsArithFrobAt); extend Q to a place w of K̄. Any arithmetic Frobenius lift σ at w restricts to the unique Frobenius of the unramified prime Q (Mathlib uniqueness at unramified primes, NumberFieldArithmetic layer 2.2), so σ|_L = g|_L, i.e. σ ∈ gU.
5. (b): φ(Frob_w) is well defined because two Frobenius lifts at w differ by I_w ⊂ ker φ. For an open V ⊂ H meeting φ(G_K), φ^{-1}(V) is a nonempty open subset of G_K and so contains some gU; (a) gives a Σ-Frobenius in gU, whose image lies in V. φ(G_K) is compact, hence closed in H, which gives the closure statement.
6. (c) is (b) for φ = ρ restricted to Σ = (all finite places) ∖ (S ∪ T), which has density 1 because finite sets have density 0; the vanishing statement is the closure statement applied to the zero set of a continuous function.

**Prerequisites.** `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/decomposition-group-at-a-place`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/unramified-and-ramification-set`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/Chebotarev#layer-10-dirichlet-density-chebotarev`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ArithmeticDirichletSeries#layer-7-dirichlet-density`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/NumberFieldArithmetic#layer-2-frobenius-elements-and-the-artin-symbol`; `mathlib:Field.absoluteGaloisGroup`; `mathlib:IsArithFrobAt`; `mathlib:OpenNormalSubgroup`; `tauceti:NumberField.Chebotarev.frobeniusPrimeSet`; `tauceti:NumberField.Chebotarev.mem_frobeniusPrimeSet_mk_iff_exists_isArithFrobAt`; `tauceti:NumberField.Chebotarev.finite_compl_iUnion_frobeniusPrimeSet`.

**Acceptance.**

- DDT Theorem 2.3 is the special case K = ℚ, Σ = all primes outside S, H = Gal(F/ℚ) for F/ℚ Galois unramified outside S: the union of the Frobenius classes is dense.
- For K = ℚ and U = G_{ℚ(ζ_5)}, every coset of U contains Frobenius lifts at primes p ≡ a mod 5 for each a ∈ (ℤ/5)^× (arithmetic Frobenius maps to p mod 5, Chebotarev acceptance test 4), and these primes have density 1/4 each.
- Non-example: the set of Frobenius lifts at a single fixed place w is the coset Frob_w·I_w, which is not dense in G_ℚ; density needs infinitely many places, and a set Σ of density 1/2 such as the primes p ≡ 1 mod 4 (split completely in ℚ(i)) gives Frobenius lifts lying in the closed subgroup G_{ℚ(i)}, again not dense: density one is used to meet every Chebotarev set.

**Sources.**

- ddt-fermat, Theorem 2.3, printed p. 52: “side a finite set S of primes then p6∈S [Frob p ] is dense in Gal (F/Q).” — The density of Frobenius classes in the Galois group of an extension unramified outside S (the text layer renders the union symbol and ∉ as shown); here generalised to any number field and any density-one set of places.
- deligne-serre74, 6.12, printed p. 523: “Le groupe (p (G) est fini; d'après le théorème de Cebotarev,” — The Chebotarev step applied to a finite image (φ rendered as '(p' by the text layer).
- serre81-chebotarev, §2.1, Théorème 1, printed p. 131: “Théorème 1. — L'ensemble Sç est de densité [ G | / | G | dans S^.” — Chebotarev for a finite Galois extension, with density #C/#G; the finite-level input of step 2 (Serre uses natural density; Tau Ceti layer 10 supplies the Dirichlet-density form used here).

#### Every element of a finite image is a Frobenius at a set of primes of positive density

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.5/every-element-of-a-finite-image-is-a-frobenius`. Kind: lemma. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.GaloisRep` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/Recognition/FiniteImage.lean`). Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.5`.

Let K be a number field, H a finite group with the discrete topology and φ : G_K → H a continuous homomorphism (for instance ρ : G_K → GL_n(k) continuous with k finite, or with finite image in GL_n(ℂ), R01.1/finite-coefficients-and-finite-quotients). Let S be the finite set of finite places at which φ is ramified and T any finite set of finite places. Then for every h ∈ φ(G_K) the set of v ∉ S ∪ T such that h = φ(Frob_w) for some place w | v has Dirichlet density #(conjugacy class of h in φ(G_K))/#φ(G_K) > 0, and in particular is infinite. Consequently every polynomial identity in the entries of φ(Frob_v) (resp. every statement about det(X − ρ(Frob_v))) that holds for all v outside a finite set holds for every element of the image.

**Hypotheses.**

- H finite discrete, so ker φ is open and L = K̄^{ker φ} is a finite Galois extension with Gal(L/K) ≅ φ(G_K).
- Only places v outside the ramification set S of φ (equivalently, unramified in L) are used; T is arbitrary finite.
- The class of h is taken in the image φ(G_K), not in H.

**Construction and proof.**

1. φ factors through Gal(L/K) ≅ φ(G_K) with L = K̄^{ker φ} finite Galois (R01.1/finite-coefficients-and-finite-quotients); v is unramified in L iff φ is unramified at v (R01.2/unramified-and-ramification-set).
2. Apply hasDirichletDensity_frobeniusPrimeSet (Chebotarev layer 10) to the class C of the element of Gal(L/K) corresponding to h; removing the finite set S ∪ T does not change the density (hasDirichletDensity_of_symmDiff_finite, ArithmeticDirichletSeries layer 7).
3. For v in the set, tauceti:NumberField.Chebotarev.mem_frobeniusPrimeSet_mk_iff_exists_isArithFrobAt gives a prime of L above v at which the chosen representative is an arithmetic Frobenius; extend it to w | v in K̄, so h = φ(Frob_w).
4. The consequence: the identity holds at h because h is φ(Frob_w) for some v outside the given finite exceptional set.

**Prerequisites.** `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/finite-coefficients-and-finite-quotients`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/unramified-and-ramification-set`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/decomposition-group-at-a-place`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/Chebotarev#layer-10-dirichlet-density-chebotarev`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ArithmeticDirichletSeries#layer-7-dirichlet-density`; `tauceti:NumberField.Chebotarev.frobeniusPrimeSet`; `tauceti:NumberField.Chebotarev.mem_frobeniusPrimeSet_mk_iff_exists_isArithFrobAt`; `mathlib:ConjClasses`.

**Acceptance.**

- Deligne–Serre 6.12: for the semisimplified reduction φ of a mod-λ eigenform representation, every s ∈ φ(G) is F_p for some p ∤ Nl, so the coefficients of det(1 − sT) lie in k_f (6.12.1).
- For φ : G_ℚ → Gal(ℚ(ζ_7)^+/ℚ) ≅ ℤ/3, the nontrivial elements are Frob_p exactly for p ≡ ±2, ±3 mod 7, a set of density 2/3; p = 2 is one of them.
- EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons EC.3: if the mod-2 representation of an elliptic curve over ℚ has image containing an element of order 3, there is a good odd prime q with Frob_q of order 3 on E[2], hence 1 − Frob_q invertible on E[2] and #E(F_q) odd.

**Sources.**

- deligne-serre74, 6.12, printed p. 523: “Le groupe (p (G) est fini; d'après le théorème de Cebotarev,” — Exactly this lemma for G = Gal(Q̄/Q) and a finite image; the continuation (garbled in the text layer) states that every element of φ(G) is F_p with p ∤ Nl.
- serre81-chebotarev, §2.1, Théorème 1, printed p. 131: “Théorème 1. — L'ensemble Sç est de densité [ G | / | G | dans S^.” — The density #C/#G of each Frobenius class.

#### Primes with prescribed quadratic residue symbols, possibly coincident quadratic fields

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.5/prescribed-quadratic-residue-symbols`. Kind: lemma. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.GaloisRep` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/Recognition/QuadraticSymbols.lean`). Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.5`.

Let d_1, …, d_r be nonzero integers and ε_1, …, ε_r ∈ {±1}. The following are equivalent: (i) there are infinitely many odd primes p ∤ d_1⋯d_r with legendreSym p d_i = ε_i for all i; (ii) the set of such primes has Dirichlet density 2^{-m} > 0, where 2^m = [ℚ(√d_1, …, √d_r) : ℚ]; (iii) for every subset J ⊆ {1, …, r} with ∏_{i∈J} d_i a square in ℚ, ∏_{i∈J} ε_i = 1. In particular, for two non-squares d_1, d_2 (the fields ℚ(√d_1), ℚ(√d_2) may coincide, i.e. d_1d_2 may be a square) there are infinitely many primes at which both are quadratic nonresidues; for three non-squares with d_1d_2d_3 a square there are none.

**Hypotheses.**

- d_i ∈ ℤ ∖ {0}; primes p = 2 and p | d_i are excluded.
- Legendre symbols, Mathlib legendreSym; arithmetic Frobenius.

**Construction and proof.**

1. Let M = ℚ(√d_1, …, √d_r) ⊂ ℚ̄, a multiquadratic Galois extension; Kummer theory identifies Gal(M/ℚ) with the dual of the subgroup Δ of ℚ^×/ℚ^{×2} generated by the d_i, σ ↦ (d ↦ σ(√d)/√d) (Tau Ceti Multiquadratic layer 0).
2. For an odd prime p ∤ ∏ d_i, every arithmetic Frobenius σ at a prime above p satisfies σ(√d_i) = legendreSym p d_i · √d_i (tauceti:NumberField.exists_isArithFrobAt_multiquadratic).
3. Hence the primes in question are those whose Frobenius is the element ε ∈ Gal(M/ℚ) with ε(√d_i) = ε_i√d_i, which exists iff the assignment d_i ↦ ε_i is a well-defined character of Δ, i.e. iff (iii) holds.
4. If ε exists, Chebotarev layer 10 (Gal(M/ℚ) abelian, so the class is a singleton) gives Dirichlet density 1/#Gal(M/ℚ) = 2^{-m}; R01.5/every-element-of-a-finite-image-is-a-frobenius packages this. If it does not exist, the set is empty.

**Prerequisites.** `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.5/every-element-of-a-finite-image-is-a-frobenius`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/Chebotarev#layer-10-dirichlet-density-chebotarev`; `tauceti:NumberField.exists_isArithFrobAt_multiquadratic`; `mathlib:legendreSym`.

**Acceptance.**

- d_1 = 2, d_2 = 8 (coincident fields ℚ(√2)): both are nonresidues exactly at p ≡ ±3 mod 8, density 1/2.
- d_1 = 2, d_2 = 3, d_3 = 6: no prime has all three symbols −1, since (2/p)(3/p) = (6/p); condition (iii) fails for J = {1,2,3}.
- EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons EC.3/four-count-square-classes: for C: y² = x(x² + ax + b) with neither b nor a² − 4b a square, there are infinitely many good odd q at which both are nonresidues.

**Sources.**

- ddt-fermat, Theorem 2.3, printed p. 52, and the remark after Theorem 2.4: “side a finite set S of primes then p6∈S [Frob p ] is dense in Gal (F/Q).” — Chebotarev for the finite multiquadratic extension; the residue-symbol translation is the Tau Ceti Multiquadratic Frobenius theorem, which the library supplies.

#### Chebotarev recognition by Frobenius characteristic polynomials

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.5/recognition-by-characteristic-polynomials-and-coefficient-descent`. Kind: theorem. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.GaloisRep` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/Recognition/Recognition.lean`). Planet: **Chebotarev recognition**. Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.5`.

Let K be a number field, S a finite set of finite places, and Σ a set of finite places of K of Dirichlet density 1 disjoint from S. Let E_1, E_2 be coefficient fields of the standard kinds (finite fields with the discrete topology, or fields of characteristic 0 such as finite extensions of ℚ_ℓ, ℚ̄_ℓ or ℂ with their topologies; residual and characteristic-zero representations are compared only through a common field), and let E be a common extension: either a field containing both, or, for ℓ-adic and residual coefficients, a finite extension of ℚ_ℓ (resp. F_ℓ) inside a fixed ℚ̄_ℓ (resp. F̄_ℓ) containing both. Let ρ_i : G_K → GL(V_i), V_i an n-dimensional E_i-vector space, be continuous (R01.1/continuous-representation) and unramified outside S. Suppose that for every v ∈ Σ the Frobenius characteristic polynomials agree in E[X]: P_v(ρ_1, X) = P_v(ρ_2, X) (R01.2/frobenius-characteristic-polynomial, arithmetic Frobenius). Then (V_1 ⊗ E)^ss ≅ (V_2 ⊗ E)^ss as E[G_K]-modules; if each ρ_i ⊗ E is semisimple (automatic for semisimple ρ_i when E/E_i is separable, in particular for finite and characteristic-zero fields), ρ_1 ⊗ E ≅ ρ_2 ⊗ E. Variants: (a) when char E = 0 or char E > n, equality of the traces tr ρ_1(Frob_v) = tr ρ_2(Frob_v) for v ∈ Σ suffices; (b) for n = 2, equality of trace and determinant at v ∈ Σ is equality of P_v and suffices in every characteristic; (c) the same conclusions hold for any profinite Γ and a dense subset D ⊂ Γ in place of the Frobenius elements, with det(X − ρ_1(γ)) = det(X − ρ_2(γ)) for γ ∈ D. Trace equality alone does NOT suffice when 0 < char E ≤ n.

**Hypotheses.**

- Both representations continuous, of the same dimension n, unramified outside the finite set S; the comparison set Σ has Dirichlet density 1 and avoids S (the representations need only be unramified on Σ).
- Characteristic polynomials are compared after the fixed embeddings E_i → E; for ℓ-adic and residual members the common field is reached by R01.1/coefficient-extension (and R01.1/baire-descent-to-a-finite-coefficient-field for ℚ̄_ℓ-valued members).
- The conclusion concerns semisimplifications: no splitting of extensions is inferred (a nonsplit extension and its semisimplification have the same characteristic polynomials).
- Traces suffice only when n! is invertible in E (characteristic 0 or > n).

**Construction and proof.**

1. Extend coefficients to E (R01.1/coefficient-extension); characteristic polynomials and semisimplifications are compatible with the extension (R01.1/semisimplification).
2. The functions γ ↦ det(X − ρ_i(γ)) ∈ E[X]_{≤n}, i = 1, 2, are continuous and class functions on G_K and factor through G_K → GL_n(E_1) × GL_n(E_2) (ρ_1, ρ_2), which is unramified outside S; they agree at every Frobenius element at a place above Σ.
3. R01.5/frobenius-density (c) applied to (ρ_1, ρ_2): the Frobenius elements are dense in the image, so the characteristic polynomials agree on all of G_K (Hausdorff target).
4. R01.1/brauer-nesbitt (semisimple representations over any field with equal characteristic polynomials on all group elements are isomorphic; supplied through IHG.1 reconstruction and descent) gives (V_1 ⊗ E)^ss ≅ (V_2 ⊗ E)^ss. Equivalently, the determinants det ∘ ρ_i agree as continuous determinants on G_K (IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants:IHG.0/continuous-determinant-dense, via IHG.0/determinant-of-matrix-representation); the representation-level statement is the one exported here.
5. (a): if n! ∈ E^×, Newton's identities recover det(X − g) from tr(g^k), k ≤ n, and traces agree on all of G_K by step 3 applied to the trace function. (b): for n = 2, P_v = X² − tr·X + det. (c): step 3 with D in place of the Frobenius set.
6. Counterexample to traces in characteristic p ≤ n: see acceptance.

**Prerequisites.** `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.5/frobenius-density`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/continuous-representation`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/brauer-nesbitt`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/semisimplification`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/coefficient-extension`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/baire-descent-to-a-finite-coefficient-field`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/frobenius-characteristic-polynomial`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/unramified-and-ramification-set`; `IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants:IHG.0/continuous-determinant-dense`; `IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants:IHG.0/determinant-of-matrix-representation`; `mathlib:LinearMap.charpoly`; `mathlib:IsSemisimpleModule`.

**Acceptance.**

- Characteristic two, traces insufficient: let χ : G_ℚ → Gal(ℚ(ζ_7)^+/ℚ) ≅ ℤ/3 ≅ F_4^× be a cubic character. Then 1 ⊕ 1 and χ ⊕ χ : G_ℚ → GL_2(F_4) are semisimple, unramified outside 7, and both have trace 0 everywhere, but at p = 2 (whose class in (ℤ/7)^×/{±1} is nontrivial) P_2(1⊕1) = X² + 1 while P_2(χ⊕χ) = X² + χ(Frob_2)² ≠ X² + 1; they are not isomorphic.
- Semisimplicity is needed: for ℓ odd let c : G_ℚ → ℤ_ℓ be the composite of the cyclotomic character χ_ℓ with ℤ_ℓ^× → 1 + ℓℤ_ℓ ≅ ℤ_ℓ (a nonzero continuous homomorphism unramified outside ℓ). Then g ↦ [[1, c(g)],[0, 1]] is a nonsplit extension of 1 by 1 with P_p = (X − 1)² for every p ≠ ℓ; it is not isomorphic to 1 ⊕ 1, only its semisimplification is.
- Deligne–Serre Lemme 3.2 is the case K = ℚ, coefficients ℂ, a finite field, or a finite extension of ℚ_ℓ, with the trace version in characteristic 0; Dieulefait–Pacetti Remark 4 is the rank-two trace-and-determinant case (b).
- Rank two, any characteristic: two odd semisimple ρ̄, ρ̄' : G_ℚ → GL_2(F̄_2) with the same tr and det at all p ∉ S are isomorphic, by (b).

**Sources.**

- deligne-serre74, Lemme 3.2 with its proof, printed p. 513: “LEMME 3.2. — Soit X un ensemble de nombres premiers de densité 1 et soient p et p'” — The recognition lemma for semisimple representations of G_Q (ρ, ρ' rendered as p, p' by the text layer), with characteristic polynomials in general and traces in characteristic 0.
- deligne-serre74, footnote (1), printed p. 513: “(1) Nous adoptons ici les conventions d'Artin [1]. Notre « substitution de Frobenius » est donc l'élément” — Deligne–Serre use the arithmetic Frobenius, matching the pinned convention.
- ddt-fermat, Proposition 2.6 with proof, printed pp. 53–54: “the Brauer-Nesbitt theorem ([CR], (30.16))” — Recognition by Chebotarev plus Brauer–Nesbitt; part (b) records that traces suffice for mod-ℓ representations when ℓ > d.
- dieulefait-pacetti, Remark 4, p. 7 of arXiv:2108.07577v2: “representations ρp and ρf,p have the same trace and determinant at the Frobenius” — The rank-two trace-and-determinant use (variant (b)), on a density-one set of primes, concluded by Brauer–Nesbitt.
- chenevier-determinants, Example 2.31, printed p. 38: “subgroup, then a continuous determinant on G is uniquely determined by its restriction” — The determinant-level density statement owned by IHG.0; this node supplies the representation-level comparison.

#### The image algebra, field of definition and Brauer class of an absolutely irreducible representation

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.5/brauer-class-of-an-absolutely-irreducible-representation`. Kind: construction. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.GaloisRep` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/Recognition/BrauerClass.lean`). Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.5`.

Let k be a field with algebraic closure k̄, Γ a group and ρ : Γ → GL_n(k̄) an absolutely irreducible representation (R01.1/absolutely-irreducible). (1) The field of traces k(ρ) := k(tr ρ(γ) : γ ∈ Γ) ⊂ k̄. (2) The image algebra B(ρ) := the k(ρ)-linear span of ρ(Γ) in M_n(k̄); it is a k(ρ)-subalgebra, central simple over k(ρ) of dimension n², and the inclusion induces B(ρ) ⊗_{k(ρ)} k̄ ≅ M_n(k̄). (3) The Brauer class β(ρ) := [B(ρ)] ∈ Br(k(ρ)) (Mathlib BrauerGroup, Tau Ceti group structure), and the Schur index s(ρ) := index of B(ρ) = the degree of the division algebra in B(ρ) ≅ M_a(Δ), n = a·s(ρ). These depend only on the isomorphism class of ρ. For a determinant D on k[Γ] whose base change to k̄ is det ∘ ρ (IHG.0/determinant-of-matrix-representation), B(ρ) ≅ k(ρ)[Γ]/ker(D ⊗ k(ρ)) when k(ρ) = k, which is Chenevier's central simple quotient R/ker(D).

**Hypotheses.**

- ρ absolutely irreducible over k̄ (irreducible suffices since k̄ is algebraically closed).
- No condition on the characteristic: the trace form on M_n(k̄) is nondegenerate in every characteristic, which is what makes B(ρ) central simple of the right dimension.
- Γ arbitrary (no topology needed); for Galois representations take Γ = G_K or a finite quotient.

**Construction and proof.**

1. B(ρ) is closed under multiplication because ρ(Γ) is a group, and tr(B(ρ)) ⊂ k(ρ).
2. Burnside: the k̄-span of ρ(Γ) is M_n(k̄) for absolutely irreducible ρ (SemisimpleAlgebras layer 3 density / layer 1 Schur). Choose e_1, …, e_{n²} ∈ ρ(Γ) forming a k̄-basis of M_n(k̄) and let e'_i be the trace-dual basis; for b ∈ B(ρ), b = Σ tr(b e_i) e'_i with tr(b e_i) ∈ k(ρ), so Σ k(ρ) e_i ⊂ B(ρ) ⊂ Σ k(ρ) e'_i, both of dimension n² (BLGGT Lemma A.1.5, proof).
3. Hence B(ρ) ⊗_{k(ρ)} k̄ → M_n(k̄) is an isomorphism, so B(ρ) is central simple over k(ρ) (central simplicity is detected after extension to k̄; SemisimpleAlgebras layer 4).
4. Isomorphic representations have conjugate image algebras (conjugation by an element of GL_n(k̄) commuting with the k(ρ)-structure is a k(ρ)-algebra isomorphism), so β(ρ) is well defined; the Schur index is the index of the Brauer class (SemisimpleAlgebras layer 6).
5. Comparison with Chenevier Definition-Proposition 2.18(iii): for an absolutely irreducible determinant D on k[Γ] with k(ρ) = k, k[Γ]/ker(D) is central simple of rank n², and the map k[Γ] → M_n(k̄) identifies it with B(ρ).

**Prerequisites.** `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/absolutely-irreducible`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/SemisimpleAlgebras#layer-1-simple-modules-schur-and-isotypic-components`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/SemisimpleAlgebras#layer-2-artin-wedderburn-assembled-with-uniqueness`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/SemisimpleAlgebras#layer-6-the-brauer-group-and-splitting-fields`; `mathlib:BrauerGroup`; `mathlib:IsBrauerEquivalent`; `tauceti:TauCeti.BrauerGroup.mk_eq_one_iff_isSplittingField`; `tauceti:TauCeti.BrauerGroup.mk_mem_ker_baseChange_iff_isSplittingField`; `tauceti:TauCeti.Algebra.IsSplittingField`; `tauceti:TauCeti.subsingleton_brauerGroup_of_finite`; `tauceti:TauCeti.Quaternion.mk_ne_one`; `IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants:IHG.0/determinant-coefficient-subring`.

**Uses.**

- ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.5/descent-obstruction: the realizability criterion is stated through β(ρ_i) and the Schur indices of the constituents
- ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.5/finite-field-realisability: β(ρ) = 1 because the Brauer group of a finite field is trivial (Deligne–Serre 6.13: no Schur index)
- ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.5/rational-eigenvalue-descent: BLGGT Lemma A.1.5's proof: an element with n distinct M-rational eigenvalues forces every Schur index and centre degree to be 1
- PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:R24.5/monodromy-component-field: subrepresentations are defined over M_λ after a finite extension; the obstruction to doing so without extension is this Brauer class
- Chenevier, Definition-Proposition 2.18(iii), p. 32: an absolutely irreducible determinant D has R/ker(D) central simple of rank d²

**API.**

- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.traceField` (data): k(ρ) = k(tr ρ(γ) : γ ∈ Γ) as an intermediate field of k̄/k.
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.imageAlgebra` (constructor): B(ρ), the k(ρ)-subalgebra of M_n(k̄) spanned by ρ(Γ).
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.imageAlgebra_isCentralSimple` (instance): B(ρ) is a finite-dimensional central simple k(ρ)-algebra of dimension n² when ρ is absolutely irreducible.
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.imageAlgebra_baseChange` (characterisation): The multiplication map B(ρ) ⊗_{k(ρ)} k̄ → M_n(k̄) is an isomorphism of k̄-algebras.
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.brauerClass` (data): β(ρ) := BrauerGroup.mk (CSA.of k(ρ) B(ρ)) ∈ Br(k(ρ)).
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.brauerClass_congr` (extensionality): ρ ≅ ρ' implies k(ρ) = k(ρ') and β(ρ) = β(ρ').
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.schurIndex` (projection): s(ρ) = the index of β(ρ), the degree of the central division algebra Brauer-equivalent to B(ρ); s(ρ) divides n.
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.brauerClass_eq_one_iff` (characterisation): β(ρ) = 1 iff B(ρ) ≅ M_n(k(ρ)) iff ρ is conjugate to a representation into GL_n(k(ρ)) (tauceti:TauCeti.BrauerGroup.mk_eq_one_iff_isSplittingField).
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.brauerClass_baseChange` (functoriality): For a field extension k' of k(ρ) inside k̄, β(ρ) maps to the class of B(ρ) ⊗ k' under Br(k(ρ)) → Br(k'), and ρ is realizable over k' iff k' splits B(ρ) (tauceti:TauCeti.BrauerGroup.mk_mem_ker_baseChange_iff_isSplittingField).
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.brauerClass_finite` (simp): If k(ρ) is finite, β(ρ) = 1 (tauceti:TauCeti.subsingleton_brauerGroup_of_finite).
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.imageAlgebra_eq_quotient_ker` (compatibility): If k(ρ) = k and D is the determinant of ρ descended to k (IHG.0/determinant-coefficient-subring), B(ρ) ≅ k[Γ]/ker(D).

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.brauerClass_quaternion_real` (computation): For ρ : Q_8 → GL_2(ℂ) the 2-dimensional irreducible representation and k = ℝ: k(ρ) = ℝ, B(ρ) ≅ ℍ[ℝ] and β(ρ) ≠ 1.
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.brauerClass_one_dim` (degenerate): For n = 1 (a character), B(ρ) = k(ρ) and β(ρ) = 1.
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.brauerClass_finite_field` (compatibility): For k = F_q and any absolutely irreducible ρ over F̄_q, β(ρ) = 1, agreeing with tauceti:TauCeti.subsingleton_brauerGroup_of_finite.
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.imageAlgebra_not_field_span` (non-example): The k-span of ρ(Γ) is the wrong object when k(ρ) ≠ k: for χ : ℤ/3 → ℚ̄^× faithful and k = ℚ, the ℚ-span of χ(ℤ/3) is ℚ(ζ_3), of ℚ-dimension 2 ≠ n² = 1 and not central simple over ℚ; the k(ρ)-span with k(ρ) = ℚ(ζ_3) is ℚ(ζ_3), central simple of dimension 1 over k(ρ).
- `TauCeti.GaloisRep.schurIndex_quaternion_rational` (characterisation): For ρ : Q_8 → GL_2(ℚ̄), s(ρ) = 2 over ℚ and over ℚ_2, and s(ρ) = 1 over ℚ_ℓ for odd ℓ (the quaternion algebra (−1,−1) splits exactly away from 2 and ∞).

**Acceptance.**

- Quaternion group: ρ : Q_8 → ℍ^× ⊂ GL_2(ℂ) has k(ρ) = ℚ (traces 2, −2, 0) and B(ρ) = the rational quaternions (−1, −1)_ℚ; over k = ℝ, B = ℍ and β(ρ) = [ℍ] ≠ 1 (tauceti:TauCeti.Quaternion.mk_ne_one), s(ρ) = 2.
- For Γ = GL_2(F_q), ρ the standard representation over k = F_q: B(ρ) = M_2(F_q), β = 1.

**Sources.**

- chenevier-determinants, Definition-Proposition 2.18(iii), printed p. 32: “R/ ker(D) is a central simple k-algebra of rank d2” — The image algebra of an absolutely irreducible determinant is central simple of rank d².
