#### Coefficient descent and its Brauer-class obstruction

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.5/descent-obstruction`. Kind: theorem. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.GaloisRep` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/Recognition/Descent.lean`). Planet: **Brauer-class descent obstruction**. Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.5`.

Let k be a PERFECT field (finite fields and fields of characteristic 0), k̄ an algebraic closure, Γ a group, and ρ : Γ → GL_n(k̄) semisimple with det(X − ρ(γ)) ∈ k[X] for every γ ∈ Γ (equivalently, the determinant det ∘ ρ descends to a k-valued determinant on k[Γ], IHG.0/determinant-coefficient-subring). Write ρ ≅ ⊕_{i=1}^{t} ρ_i^{⊕ m_i} with ρ_i pairwise non-isomorphic irreducible. Then: (1) Gal(k̄/k) permutes the classes [ρ_i] preserving multiplicities, σ(ρ) ≅ ρ for all σ; k(ρ_i) (R01.5/brauer-class-of-an-absolutely-irreducible-representation) is the fixed field of the stabiliser of [ρ_i] and is finite over k. (2) ρ is realizable over k, i.e. ρ ≅ V ⊗_k k̄ for a k[Γ]-module V of dimension n, if and only if the Schur index s(ρ_i) divides m_i for every i. (3) In particular: if every β(ρ_i) ∈ Br(k(ρ_i)) is trivial (e.g. k finite), ρ is realizable over k; if ρ is absolutely irreducible (t = 1, m_1 = 1, so k(ρ) = k), ρ is realizable over k iff β(ρ) = 1 in Br(k), and over a finite extension k' ⊂ k̄ iff k' splits B(ρ). (4) Equivalently in determinant language (Chenevier Theorem 2.16): for the descended determinant D, k[Γ]/ker(D) ≅ ∏ S_i with S_i central simple over k_i = k(ρ_i), D = ∏ det_{S_i}^{m_i}, and D is the determinant of a representation Γ → GL_n(k) iff ind(S_i) | m_i for all i. A trace-and-determinant (or characteristic-polynomial) system defined over k does NOT in general descend: the obstruction is the family of classes β(ρ_i) weighted by the multiplicities.

**Hypotheses.**

- k perfect: over an imperfect field a semisimple representation with k-rational characteristic polynomials can fail to descend for a reason other than the Brauer class (inseparability; see acceptance).
- ρ semisimple over k̄ (for a Galois representation, pass to the semisimplification first).
- Characteristic polynomials (not traces) in k[X]; in characteristic p ≤ n traces in k do not imply characteristic polynomials in k.

**Construction and proof.**

1. For σ ∈ Gal(k̄/k), σ(ρ) is semisimple with the same characteristic polynomials, so σ(ρ) ≅ ρ by R01.1/brauer-nesbitt; hence Gal(k̄/k) permutes the isotypic constituents preserving m_i. Absolutely irreducible representations are determined by their traces (Burnside density makes the traces of non-isomorphic absolutely irreducible representations linearly independent), so the stabiliser of [ρ_i] is Gal(k̄/k(ρ_i)); k perfect makes k(ρ_i)/k separable and finite.
2. For each Galois orbit, B(ρ_i) is central simple over k(ρ_i) (R01.5/brauer-class-of-an-absolutely-irreducible-representation). The simple k[Γ]-module W_i attached to the orbit is the simple module of B(ρ_i) viewed over k; W_i ⊗_k k̄ ≅ ⊕_{τ : k(ρ_i) → k̄} τ(ρ_i)^{⊕ s(ρ_i)} (Chenevier Theorem 2.16 with q_i = 1, and the Wedderburn decomposition of SemisimpleAlgebras layer 2).
3. Every k-form V of ρ is semisimple (k perfect) and so a sum of the W_i; comparing multiplicities of ρ_i gives ρ realizable iff s(ρ_i) | m_i for all i, which is (2). (3) follows: β(ρ_i) = 1 means s(ρ_i) = 1; finite k(ρ_i) has trivial Brauer group (tauceti:TauCeti.subsingleton_brauerGroup_of_finite); in the absolutely irreducible case B(ρ) ⊗ k' splits iff k' splits it (tauceti:TauCeti.BrauerGroup.mk_mem_ker_baseChange_iff_isSplittingField).
4. (4) is the same computation in Chenevier's language: det_{S_i} restricted to the simple module of S_i is det_{S_i}^{s_i}, so a k-representation with determinant ∏ det_{S_i}^{m_i} exists iff s_i | m_i.
5. Do not use the second characterisation in Chenevier's Definition 2.19 ('R/ker(D) a product of matrix algebras') for realizability: it is strictly stronger (source issue ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations/E501).

**Prerequisites.** `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.5/brauer-class-of-an-absolutely-irreducible-representation`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/brauer-nesbitt`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/semisimplification`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/absolutely-irreducible`; `IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants:IHG.0/determinant-coefficient-subring`; `IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants:IHG.1`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/SemisimpleAlgebras#layer-2-artin-wedderburn-assembled-with-uniqueness`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/SemisimpleAlgebras#layer-6-the-brauer-group-and-splitting-fields`; `tauceti:TauCeti.subsingleton_brauerGroup_of_finite`; `tauceti:TauCeti.BrauerGroup.mk_mem_ker_baseChange_iff_isSplittingField`; `tauceti:TauCeti.Quaternion.mk_ne_one`; `mathlib:Quaternion`.

**Acceptance.**

- Quaternion obstruction over ℝ: ρ : Q_8 → GL_2(ℂ) has characteristic polynomials (X ∓ 1)² and X² + 1 in ℝ[X] and is absolutely irreducible, but B(ρ) = ℍ and [ℍ] ≠ 1 in Br(ℝ) (tauceti:TauCeti.Quaternion.mk_ne_one), so ρ is not conjugate into GL_2(ℝ); ρ ⊕ ρ is realizable over ℝ (ℍ with left multiplication), matching s = 2 | m = 2.
- Quaternion obstruction over ℚ and ℚ_2: composing G_ℚ → Gal(K/ℚ) ≅ Q_8 (K a quaternion extension of ℚ, e.g. Dedekind's field ℚ(√((2+√2)(3+√6)))) with ρ gives a continuous representation with Frobenius polynomials in ℚ[X] that is not realizable over ℚ or over ℚ_2, but is realizable over ℚ_ℓ for every odd ℓ, because (−1,−1) splits exactly away from 2 and ∞.
- Finite fields: a semisimple φ over F_4 with F_2-rational characteristic polynomials descends to GL_n(F_2) (R01.5/finite-field-realisability).
- Imperfect field: over k = F_p(t), the character χ : ℤ → k̄^×, 1 ↦ t^{1/p}, gives χ^{⊕p} with characteristic polynomial X^p − t ∈ k[X], but χ^{⊕p} is not realizable over k (a k-form would make the scalar t^{1/p} conjugate to a matrix over k); this is why k is assumed perfect.

**Sources.**

- chenevier-determinants, Theorem 2.16, printed p. 31: “where Si is a simple k-algebra which is of finite dimension n2i over its center ki , and” — The structure of k[Γ]/ker(D) for a determinant over an arbitrary field, with D = ∏ det_{S_i}^{m_i}; realizability is read off from it.
- deligne-serre74, Lemme 6.13, proof, printed p. 523: “cela provient de ce que le groupe de Brauer d'un” — The obstruction is a Schur index / Brauer class, absent over finite fields.
- blggt14, Lemma A.1.5, proof, printed p. 85 (arXiv v4): “for some non-negative integers nj,τ . Since tr (B) ⊂ M , we see that nj,τ = nj is” — Galois-invariance of multiplicities from rationality of traces, and the Wedderburn decomposition B ≅ ⊕ M_{m_j}(D_j) used to read off Schur indices.
- chenevier-determinants, Definition 2.19, printed p. 33: “We say that D is split if it is the determinant of a representation R −→ Md (k).” — Chenevier's 'split'; see source issue E501 for the non-equivalent second characterisation.

#### Realizability over the field of characteristic-polynomial coefficients (finite fields)

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.5/finite-field-realisability`. Kind: theorem. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.GaloisRep` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/Recognition/Descent.lean`). Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.5`.

Deligne–Serre Lemme 6.13. Let Φ be a group, k' a finite field and φ : Φ → GL_n(k') a semisimple representation. Let k ⊂ k' be a subfield containing the coefficients of det(1 − φ(s)T) for all s ∈ Φ. Then φ is realizable over k: there is a representation φ_0 : Φ → GL_n(k) with φ_0 ⊗_k k' ≅ φ. If Φ is a profinite group and φ is continuous (discrete topology), φ_0 can be taken continuous with the same kernel; for Φ = G_K, φ_0 is unramified wherever φ is, with the same Frobenius characteristic polynomials. In particular, for a continuous semisimple ρ̄ : G_K → GL_n(F̄_p) (finite image, R01.1/residual-descent-to-a-finite-field), ρ̄ is realizable over the finite field generated by the coefficients of its Frobenius characteristic polynomials P_v(ρ̄, X), v outside the ramification set.

**Hypotheses.**

- k' finite (so every finite extension of k has trivial Brauer group); φ semisimple.
- Characteristic polynomials, not traces, are required to have coefficients in k.

**Construction and proof.**

1. Deligne–Serre's proof: it suffices that φ ≅ σ(φ) for every k-automorphism σ of k', because the Brauer group of a finite field is trivial (tauceti:TauCeti.subsingleton_brauerGroup_of_finite), so there is no Schur index; φ and σ(φ) are semisimple with the same characteristic polynomials, hence isomorphic (R01.1/brauer-nesbitt, Curtis–Reiner 30.16). Formally: R01.5/descent-obstruction (3) with k finite (perfect), over k̄ = F̄_p ⊃ k'.
2. Continuity and kernel: φ_0 ⊗ k' ≅ φ forces ker φ_0 = ker φ, open when φ is continuous (R01.1/finite-coefficients-and-finite-quotients); Frobenius characteristic polynomials are unchanged by the isomorphism.
3. For the Galois corollary, the coefficients of det(1 − ρ̄(s)T) for s in the (finite) image lie in the field generated by the P_v-coefficients because every element of the image is a Frobenius (R01.5/every-element-of-a-finite-image-is-a-frobenius), exactly as in Deligne–Serre 6.12.

**Prerequisites.** `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.5/descent-obstruction`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.5/every-element-of-a-finite-image-is-a-frobenius`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/brauer-nesbitt`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/residual-descent-to-a-finite-field`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/finite-coefficients-and-finite-quotients`; `tauceti:TauCeti.subsingleton_brauerGroup_of_finite`.

**Acceptance.**

- For S_3 ≅ GL_2(F_2) with its standard representation std and A ∈ GL_2(F_4) not in F_4^×·GL_2(F_2), φ = A·std·A^{-1} has entries outside F_2 but F_2-rational characteristic polynomials (X² + 1 and X² + X + 1 for the non-identity classes), and is conjugate into GL_2(F_2), as the theorem predicts.
- Deligne–Serre 6.12: the residual representation of a mod-λ eigenform is realised over k_f, the field generated by the a_p and ε(p).
- The hypothesis cannot be weakened to traces: 1 ⊕ 1 and χ ⊕ χ over F_4 (χ cubic) have F_2-rational traces, and χ ⊕ χ is not realizable over F_2 because its characteristic polynomials X² + χ(s)² are not F_2-rational.

**Sources.**

- deligne-serre74, Lemme 6.13, printed p. 523: “Soit k un sous-corps de k ' contenant les coefficients des polynômes” — The statement (k' finite, φ semisimple, k containing the characteristic-polynomial coefficients).
- deligne-serre74, Lemme 6.13, proof, printed p. 523: “cela provient de ce que le groupe de Brauer d'un” — The reason: trivial Brauer group of a finite field, so no Schur index.

#### Descent from traces and one element with distinct rational eigenvalues (BLGGT Lemma A.1.5)

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.5/rational-eigenvalue-descent`. Kind: theorem. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.GaloisRep` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/Recognition/Descent.lean`). Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.5`.

Let Γ be a group, M a field of characteristic 0 and M̄ an algebraic closure. Let r : Γ → GL_n(M̄) be semisimple. Suppose tr r(γ) ∈ M for all γ ∈ Γ and that for some γ_0 ∈ Γ the characteristic polynomial of r(γ_0) has n distinct roots, all in M. Then r is conjugate to a representation into GL_n(M). If moreover Γ is profinite, r is continuous and M is a finite extension of ℚ_ℓ, the M-model can be taken continuous and preserves an O_M-lattice (R01.1/compact-subgroups-stabilise-lattices).

**Hypotheses.**

- Characteristic 0 (traces determine semisimple representations and the trace pairing argument uses tr(B) ⊂ M).
- One element with n DISTINCT eigenvalues in M; traces in M alone do not suffice (quaternion example).
- r semisimple.

**Construction and proof.**

1. Let B be the M-span of r(Γ) in M_n(M̄). The trace-dual-basis argument shows B ⊗_M M̄ ≅ B_{M̄} ⊂ M_n(M̄), so B is a finite-dimensional semisimple M-algebra and M̄^n a faithful B ⊗ M̄-module (BLGGT proof; R01.5/brauer-class-of-an-absolutely-irreducible-representation step 2 in the absolutely irreducible case).
2. Wedderburn: B ≅ ⊕_j M_{m_j}(D_j) with D_j central division over Z(D_j) ⊃ M, r_j² = dim_{Z(D_j)} D_j (SemisimpleAlgebras layer 2). As a B ⊗ M̄-module, M̄^n ≅ ⊕_{j,τ} (M̄^{m_j r_j})^{n_{j,τ}}, and tr(B) ⊂ M forces n_{j,τ} = n_j independent of the embedding τ.
3. An element of B with n distinct M-rational eigenvalues forces r_j = n_j = [Z(D_j) : M] = 1 for all j, so B ≅ ⊕ M_{m_j}(M) and M^n with this action is an M-form of r (R01.5/descent-obstruction (2) with all Schur indices 1).
4. Continuity and lattices: the M-form is conjugate to r by an element of GL_n(M̄) and so continuous; a compact image preserves a lattice.

**Prerequisites.** `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.5/descent-obstruction`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.5/brauer-class-of-an-absolutely-irreducible-representation`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/SemisimpleAlgebras#layer-2-artin-wedderburn-assembled-with-uniqueness`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/compact-subgroups-stabilise-lattices`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/semisimplification`.

**Acceptance.**

- Q_8 → GL_2(ℚ̄) has traces in ℚ and is not realizable over ℚ; the hypothesis fails because every element has eigenvalues in {±1} (central elements, repeated) or {±i} (not in ℚ): consistent with the lemma.
- BLGGT Lemma 5.3.1 (proof, p. 71): after enlarging M so that some r_λ(G_{F¹}) contains an element with n distinct M_λ-rational eigenvalues, every H-subrepresentation of a regular weakly compatible system is defined over O_{M,λ}.
- n = 1: every character with values in M̄ and traces in M has values in M; the distinct-eigenvalue element is automatic.

**Sources.**

- blggt14, Lemma A.1.5, printed p. 85 (arXiv:1010.2561v4): “Then r is conjugate to a representation into GLn (M ).” — The conclusion; the statement and proof were read on the rendered page (r : Γ → GL_n(M̄), tr r(γ) ∈ M, one γ with distinct M-rational eigenvalues).
- blggt14, Lemma 5.3.1, proof, printed p. 71: “follows from Lemma A.1.5.” — Its use for subrepresentations of regular weakly compatible systems.

#### Chebotarev density for compact images: Frobenius equidistribution in Haar measure

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.5/haar-measure-chebotarev`. Kind: theorem. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.GaloisRep` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/Recognition/HaarChebotarev.lean`). Planet: **Haar-measure Chebotarev**. Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.5`.

Let K be a number field, G a profinite group (e.g. a closed subgroup of GL_n(O_E), E/ℚ_ℓ finite) with normalised Haar probability measure μ (mathlib:MeasureTheory.Measure.haar, unique by isHaarMeasure_eq_of_isProbabilityMeasure), and ρ : G_K → G a continuous SURJECTIVE homomorphism unramified outside a finite set S of finite places, so that ρ(Frob_v) is a well-defined conjugacy class for v ∉ S. For a conjugation-stable Borel set C ⊂ G let Σ_C = {v ∉ S : ρ(Frob_v) ⊂ C}. (a) If C is open and closed, Σ_C has Dirichlet density μ(C) (and natural density μ(C)). (b) If C is closed, Σ_C has upper Dirichlet density ≤ μ(C); in particular μ(C) = 0 implies Σ_C has Dirichlet density 0. (c) If μ(∂C) = 0, Σ_C has Dirichlet density μ(C). (d) Contrapositive form (CG20 Lemma A.8): if a closed conjugation-stable condition holds at ρ(Frob_v) for v in a set of positive upper density, it holds on a subset of G of positive Haar measure. (e) If G is an open subgroup of GL_n(ℤ_ℓ) (or of GL_n(O_E)) and f is a polynomial function on M_n(E) that does not vanish identically on G, then C = {g ∈ G : f(g) = 0} has μ(C) = 0, so Σ_C has density 0; e.g. for ρ with open image in GL_2(ℤ_ℓ), the primes with tr ρ(Frob_v) = 0 have density 0.

**Hypotheses.**

- ρ surjective onto G (replace G by the closed subgroup ρ(G_K) otherwise; the Haar measure is that of the image).
- Densities are Dirichlet densities (ArithmeticDirichletSeries layer 7); the natural-density form of (a) uses Chebotarev layer 14.
- (e) needs f not identically zero on G; a proper analytic subset with empty interior of a general compact ℓ-adic Lie group is also null (Serre), but that general analytic statement is recorded as a gap.
- Only a density-ZERO conclusion for null sets; no effective error term (Serre's Théorème 15 bounds need the effective Chebotarev theorem and are not planned here).

**Construction and proof.**

1. Open normal subgroups U of G form a basis at 1 (profinite). For C open and closed and conjugation-stable, C is a union of cosets of some open normal U (compactness), C = π^{-1}(C_U) for π : G → G/U, and μ(C) = #C_U/#(G/U) because all cosets of U have equal measure (mathlib:MeasureTheory.Subgroup.index_mul_measure).
2. (a): L = K̄^{ρ^{-1}(U)} is finite Galois with Gal(L/K) ≅ G/U, unramified outside S; v ∈ Σ_C iff Frob_v ∈ C_U; Chebotarev layer 10 (resp. 14) gives density #C_U/#(G/U) = μ(C).
3. (b): μ is outer regular; for ε > 0 choose open W ⊃ C with μ(W) < μ(C) + ε, then (compactness of C, conjugation-stability) an open normal U with CU ⊂ W; CU is open, closed and conjugation-stable, Σ_C ⊂ Σ_{CU}, so the upper density of Σ_C is ≤ μ(CU) < μ(C) + ε.
4. (c): apply (b) to the closure of C and to the closure of the complement and use μ(∂C) = 0; upper and lower bounds coincide (hasDirichletDensity_of_upperBound_of_lowerBound, ArithmeticDirichletSeries layer 7). (d) is the contrapositive of (b).
5. (e): on GL_n(ℤ_ℓ) Haar measure is a multiple of the additive Haar measure of M_n(ℤ_ℓ) (|det| = 1); the zero set of a nonzero polynomial in N variables over ℚ_ℓ is null for the Haar measure of ℤ_ℓ^N (induction on N with Fubini, a nonzero one-variable polynomial having finitely many roots and Haar measure on ℤ_ℓ having no atoms); restrict to the open subgroup G. tr is not identically zero on any open subgroup of GL_2(ℤ_ℓ) (it is 2 at 1).

**Prerequisites.** `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.5/frobenius-density`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/Chebotarev#layer-10-dirichlet-density-chebotarev`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/Chebotarev#layer-14-natural-density-and-consistency-theorems`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ArithmeticDirichletSeries#layer-7-dirichlet-density`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/unramified-and-ramification-set`; `mathlib:MeasureTheory.Measure.haar`; `mathlib:MeasureTheory.Measure.isHaarMeasure_eq_of_isProbabilityMeasure`; `mathlib:MeasureTheory.Subgroup.index_mul_measure`; `mathlib:OpenNormalSubgroup`.

**Acceptance.**

- Serre 1981 introduction: for a non-CM elliptic curve E/ℚ the image of the ℓ-adic representation is open in GL_2(ℤ_ℓ), the trace-zero locus is Haar-null, and so the supersingular-type primes with a_p = 0 have density 0.
- CG20 Lemma A.8 (published p. 890): with ℓ-adic image GSp_4(ℤ_ℓ), a fixed linear relation between 1, p, b_p, a_p, a_p² holding on a set of positive density forces the corresponding identity on a subset of GSp_4(ℤ_ℓ) of positive measure, hence (being polynomial) everywhere, which fails by inspection.
- Finite G recovers Chebotarev: μ(C) = #C/#G.
- Density zero is not emptiness, and an infinite image is needed for null classes: for ρ = χ_ℓ : G_ℚ → ℤ_ℓ^× (surjective, unramified outside ℓ, ρ(Frob_p) = p) and C = {a} with a ≠ ℓ a prime, μ(C) = 0 and Σ_C = {a}, a nonempty set of density 0; for finite G no nonempty conjugation-stable set is null.

**Sources.**

- cg20, Appendix §A.4, proof of Lemma A.8, published p. 890 (author copy Siegel.pdf): “appropriate identity must also hold on a subset of these groups of positive measure.” — The Haar-measure form of Chebotarev used for the ℓ-adic image GSp_4(ℤ_ℓ), cited only as 'By Chebotarev'.
- serre81-chebotarev, Introduction, printed p. 124: “Il est immédiat que G{ est de mesure nulle dans G^, ce qui entraîne” — The trace-zero locus C_ℓ is null in G_ℓ, which gives density zero by qualitative Chebotarev (text layer garbles C_ℓ, G_ℓ).
- serre81-chebotarev, §6.4, proof of Proposition 13, printed p. 168: “analytique d'intérieur vide est de mesure nulle” — Analytic subsets with empty interior are Haar-null (the general form recorded as a gap).
- serre81-chebotarev, §7.2, Théorème 15 and Corollaire 2, printed pp. 173–174: “Nous allons voir que la fonction P^Çx) est « petite » lorsque x-^oo, autrement” — The effective trace-zero bounds, beyond this node: only the density-zero corollary is planned.

#### Carayol's lemma: recognition, conjugacy and gluing of lifts with absolutely irreducible residual representation

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.5/carayol-lifts-recognition`. Kind: theorem. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.GaloisRep` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/Recognition/Carayol.lean`). Planet: **Carayol's lemma**. Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.5`.

Let R be a complete Noetherian local ring with maximal ideal m_R and finite residue field k, Γ a profinite group and r, r' : Γ → GL_d(R) continuous with the same residual representation r̄ = r mod m_R = r' mod m_R, assumed absolutely irreducible. (a) If det(X − r(γ)) = det(X − r'(γ)) for all γ in a dense subset of Γ — for Γ = G_K and r, r' unramified outside a finite S: for all Frobenius elements at places of a density-one set (R01.5/frobenius-density) — then r' = g r g^{-1} for some g ∈ ker(GL_d(R) → GL_d(k)), unique up to multiplication by 1 + m_R. (b) (Symplectic form, CG20) If r, r' take values in GSp_{2m}(R) for a fixed alternating form J with the same multiplier character ν, then g can be chosen in ker(GSp_{2m}(R) → GSp_{2m}(k)). (c) (Gluing) Let (𝔞_j)_{j≥1} be a decreasing sequence of open ideals of R forming a basis of neighbourhoods of 0, D ⊂ Γ dense, and (P_γ)_{γ∈D} ⊂ R[X] monic of degree d. If r_j : Γ → GL_d(R/𝔞_j) are continuous lifts of r̄ with det(X − r_j(γ)) = P_γ mod 𝔞_j for γ ∈ D, then there are g_j ∈ ker(GL_d(R/𝔞_j) → GL_d(k)) such that the g_j r_j g_j^{-1} are compatible, and they glue to a continuous r : Γ → GL_d(R) lifting r̄ with det(X − r(γ)) = P_γ, unique up to ker(GL_d(R) → GL_d(k))-conjugacy (and similarly for GSp_{2m} with fixed multiplier). The algebraic input — reconstruction and uniqueness of a representation over a henselian local ring from a determinant whose residual determinant is split and absolutely irreducible — is IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.1 (Chenevier Theorem 2.22); this node supplies the continuity, Frobenius-density and symplectic refinements.

**Hypotheses.**

- r̄ absolutely irreducible (split: defined over the finite residue field k). Without it the conclusion fails (scalar or reducible residual representation, see acceptance).
- R complete Noetherian local with finite residue field; the m_R-adic topology; r, r' continuous.
- Characteristic polynomials, not traces (traces suffice when d! ∈ R^×, by IHG.0/determinant-trace-injective).
- (b) uses the same J and the same multiplier ν for r and r'.

**Construction and proof.**

1. Continuity and density: the characteristic-polynomial maps γ ↦ det(X − r(γ)), det(X − r'(γ)) ∈ R[X] are continuous and agree on a dense set, hence everywhere (R01.5/frobenius-density; R is Hausdorff). So det ∘ r = det ∘ r' as continuous determinants on R[Γ] (IHG.0/continuous-determinant-dense, IHG.0/determinant-of-matrix-representation).
2. Algebra (IHG.1, Chenevier Theorem 2.22(i)): for the common determinant D, D mod m_R is split and absolutely irreducible, so the Cayley–Hamilton quotient R[Γ]/CH(D) ≅ M_d(R) with D = det. Both r and r' factor through it (matrix representations are Cayley–Hamilton, IHG.1/cayley-hamilton) and induce surjective, hence bijective, R-algebra endomorphisms of M_d(R) (residually surjective by Burnside, then Nakayama); an R-algebra automorphism of M_d(R) over a local ring is inner (Skolem–Noether over local rings, requested from IHG.1), so r' = g r g^{-1} with g ∈ GL_d(R).
3. Normalising g: ḡ commutes with r̄(Γ), so ḡ = c ∈ k^× by Schur's lemma for the absolutely irreducible r̄; replacing g by [c]^{-1}g ([c] ∈ R^× a lift) gives g ∈ 1 + M_d(m_R). Uniqueness: End_{R[Γ]}(r) = R (Nakayama plus residual Schur), so g is unique up to (1 + m_R).
4. (b): g^T J g is an r-invariant alternating form with multiplier ν: r(γ)^T(g^T J g)r(γ) = g^T r'(γ)^T J r'(γ) g = ν(γ) g^T J g. Such forms are Hom_{R[Γ]}(r, r^∨ ⊗ ν), free of rank one over R generated by J (step 3 applied to r^∨ ⊗ ν ≅ r via J), so g^T J g = cJ with c ∈ R^×, c ≡ 1 mod m_R; thus g ∈ GSp_{2m}(R) with multiplier c and ḡ = 1.
5. (c): by (a) applied over R/𝔞_j, r_{j+1} mod 𝔞_j and r_j are conjugate by an element of ker(GL_d(R/𝔞_j) → GL_d(k)); lift it to ker(GL_d(R/𝔞_{j+1}) → GL_d(k)) (1 + M_d(m) surjects) and conjugate r_{j+1}; inductively the system is compatible, and r = lim r_j is continuous for the inverse-limit topology, which is the m_R-adic topology because the 𝔞_j form a neighbourhood basis. The characteristic polynomials are the limits P_γ. Uniqueness follows from (a).

**Prerequisites.** `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.5/frobenius-density`; `IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants:IHG.1`; `IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants:IHG.1/cayley-hamilton`; `IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants:IHG.0/continuous-determinant-dense`; `IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants:IHG.0/determinant-of-matrix-representation`; `IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants:IHG.0/determinant-trace-injective`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/continuous-representation`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/absolutely-irreducible`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/framed-representation`.

**Acceptance.**

- Scalar residual representation (absolute irreducibility is necessary): r̄ = 1 ⊕ 1 over F_p, R = F_p[ε]/(ε²), r = 1 ⊕ 1 and r'(γ) = [[1, ε c(γ)],[0, 1]] for a nonzero continuous homomorphism c : Γ → F_p; both have characteristic polynomial (X − 1)² everywhere, but r' is not conjugate to r (r is central, r' is not).
- Reducible non-scalar residual: r̄ = 1 ⊕ ε̄ with a nonsplit extension lift and the split lift 1 ⊕ ε over the same R have the same characteristic polynomials and are not conjugate.
- CG20 Theorem 6.13 (published p. 842): it suffices to construct for each m a GSp_4-valued representation over T/I_m with the prescribed characteristic polynomials; (b) and (c) glue them over T.
- d = 1: two continuous characters with equal values on a dense set are equal; g ∈ 1 + m_R arbitrary.

**Sources.**

- chenevier-determinants, Theorem 2.22(i), printed p. 34: “(i) If D is split and absolutely irreducible, then there is an A-algebra isomorphism” — The algebraic reconstruction over a henselian local ring, without requiring an algebraically closed residue field (only split and absolutely irreducible); owned by IHG.1.
- chenevier-determinants, Theorem B, introduction, printed p. 4: “tation attached to D ⊗A k by Theorem A. If ρ is irreducible, then there exists a unique” — Existence and uniqueness of the lift (stated there with algebraically closed residue field; Theorem 2.22 removes this via 'split').
- cg20, §6.3, proof of Theorem 6.13, published p. 842 (Siegel.pdf): “it suffices to construct, for each” — The gluing use: Galois representations over T/I_m glued over T, compatibility up to conjugation being Carayol's lemma (uncited in the paper).

#### Semisimplicity criteria from Frobenius annihilation for GSp4-valued ρ (BCGP25 §4.11)

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.5/gsp4-semisimplicity-criteria`. Kind: theorem. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.GaloisRep` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/Recognition/GSp4Semisimplicity.lean`). Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.5`.

Let p be a prime, ρ : G_ℚ → GSp_4(Q̄_p) and s : G_ℚ → GL_n(Q̄_p) continuous (n ≥ 1), unramified outside a finite set (so that they take values in GL over a finite extension E/ℚ_p, R01.1/baire-descent-to-a-finite-coefficient-field). For g ∈ G_ℚ write char_ρ(g)(X) = det(X − ρ(g)). Suppose that for a set of primes l of Dirichlet density 1 at which both are unramified, char_ρ(Frob_l)(s(Frob_l)) = 0 in M_n(Q̄_p). (a) (BCGP25 Proposition 4.11.1, a case of Nekovář's Proposition 3.10) If the Zariski closure of ρ(G_ℚ) contains Sp_4, then s ≅ ρ^{⊕m} for some m ≥ 1. (b) (Proposition 4.11.2) If the Zariski closure of ρ(G_ℚ) contains SL_2 × SL_2, ρ is absolutely irreducible but becomes reducible on an index-two subgroup G_E, then s ≅ ρ^{⊕m} for some m ≥ 1. In both cases the first step is: char_ρ(g)(s(g)) = 0 for EVERY g ∈ G_ℚ (Chebotarev and continuity), hence on the Zariski closure of the image of (ρ, s).

**Hypotheses.**

- Annihilation by the full characteristic polynomial of ρ(Frob_l), on a density-one set — not merely equality of traces.
- The image hypotheses on the Zariski closure (Sp_4 in (a); SL_2 × SL_2 with absolute irreducibility and reducibility on an index-two subgroup in (b)) are essential.
- The conclusion includes semisimplicity of s: s is a direct sum of copies of ρ, not merely an iterated extension.

**Construction and proof.**

1. Density step: g ↦ char_ρ(g)(s(g)) is a continuous M_n(E)-valued function on G_ℚ vanishing at the Frobenius elements of a density-one set, hence identically (R01.5/frobenius-density (c)); being polynomial in the matrix entries of (ρ(g), s(g)), it vanishes on the Zariski closure of (ρ, s)(G_ℚ).
2. (a): with Σ the Frobenius set, hypothesis (C') of Nekovář Proposition 3.10 holds; the Lie algebra of ρ(G_ℚ) is sp_4 or gsp_4 acting through the standard (minuscule) representation, so Nekovář's case (3) gives s ≅ ρ^{⊕m} (BCGP25 proof). Nekovář's proposition is not freely available and was not read; recorded as a gap.
3. (b): restrict to G_E, ρ|_{G_E} = ϱ ⊕ ϱ^c. For an irreducible subquotient t of s|_{G_E}, Goursat's lemma on the Zariski closure of t ⊕ ϱ ⊕ ϱ^c and the annihilation identity show that the kernel of the projection to the closure of t is unipotent, hence trivial; so t is a quotient of the SL_2 × SL_2 representation and t ∈ {ϱ, ϱ^c}.
4. No self-extensions of ϱ (or ϱ^c) occur in s|_{G_E}: a generic element of ϱ^c acts invertibly on ϱ, and the GL_2 version of Nekovář's criterion (Blasius–Rogawski) applies.
5. Remaining case 0 → ρ → W → ρ → 0 nonsplit: Shapiro's lemma splits Ext¹_{G_E}(ϱ, ϱ^c) into H¹(ℚ, A) ⊕ H¹(ℚ, A ⊗ χ), A = s(ϱ) ⊗ η^{-1} the Asai representation twisted by the inverse similitude; a nonsplit extension U of ℚ_p by A cannot have a dense set of semisimple elements, because elements of G_ℚ ∖ G_E act on A with eigenvalues 1, −1, λ, λ^{-1} (corrected from the printed 1, −1, λ, −λ: source issue E502), contradicting the annihilation identity and the minimal-polynomial argument.

**Prerequisites.** `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.5/frobenius-density`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.5/recognition-by-characteristic-polynomials-and-coefficient-descent`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/baire-descent-to-a-finite-coefficient-field`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/restriction-dual-tensor-twist`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/continuous-induction`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/semisimplicity-under-restriction-and-induction`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/unramified-and-ramification-set`.

**Acceptance.**

- BCGP25 §4.11 application: for ρ the GSp_4 representation of a non-CM abelian surface with big Zariski closure and s an Eichler–Shimura subquotient of étale cohomology annihilated by Frobenius characteristic polynomials, s ≅ ρ^{⊕m}.
- Nonexample showing the role of annihilation: s = ρ ⊗ [[1, c],[0, 1]] with c : G_ℚ → ℤ_p ⊂ Q̄_p the composite of χ_p with ℤ_p^× → 1 + pℤ_p ≅ ℤ_p (p odd; c(Frob_l) ≠ 0 for every l ≠ p), a nonsplit self-extension of ρ, has char_ρ(Frob_l)(s(Frob_l)) ≠ 0 at Frobenius elements with ρ(Frob_l) regular semisimple, because s(Frob_l) is not semisimple there; it is excluded by the hypothesis.
- Consistency and twists: s = ρ ⊕ ρ satisfies the hypothesis by Cayley–Hamilton and m = 2; s = ρ ⊗ χ with χ a nontrivial quadratic character fails it at every Frob_l with χ(Frob_l) = −1 for which the eigenvalue multiset of ρ(Frob_l) is not stable under negation, a set of positive density by R01.5/haar-measure-chebotarev, so twists are excluded.

**Sources.**

- bcgp25, Proposition 4.11.1, printed p. 109 (arXiv:2502.20645v1): “(2) for a density one set of primes l, we have charρ(Frobl ) s(Frobl ) = 0.” — The annihilation hypothesis on a density-one set.
- bcgp25, Proposition 4.11.1, printed p. 109: “Then we have s ∼= ρ⊕m for some integer m ≥ 1.” — The conclusion.
- bcgp25, §4.11, printed p. 109: “special case of a result of Nekovář, [Nek18]. If r is a ﬁnite-dimensional representation” — Proposition 4.11.1 rests on Nekovář [Nek18, Prop. 3.10] (Ann. Sci. ÉNS 2018), not read.
- bcgp25, Proposition 4.11.2, proof, printed p. 111: “(the eigenvalues in either case take the form 1, −1, λ, −λ for some λ)” — The printed eigenvalue list, corrected to 1, −1, λ, λ^{-1} (E502).

#### Potentially abelian representations are induced from a character orbit (Clifford part of BCGP25 Lemma 10.2.3)

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.5/potentially-abelian-representations`. Kind: theorem. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.GaloisRep` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/Recognition/PotentiallyAbelian.lean`). Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.5`.

Let F be a field (in the applications a number field), E an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0 (e.g. Q̄_p with its topology), and ρ : G_F → GL_n(E) a continuous irreducible representation. Suppose L/F is a finite Galois extension with ρ(G_L) abelian. Then: (1) ρ|_{G_L} ≅ ⊕_{i=1}^{b} χ_i^{⊕a} with ab = n and χ_1, …, χ_b : G_L → E^× pairwise distinct continuous characters; (2) Gal(L/F) acts on {χ_i} by χ_i^σ(g) = χ_i(σ̃ g σ̃^{-1}) (σ̃ any lift of σ), transitively; (3) with K_i the fixed field of the stabiliser Gal(L/K_i) of χ_i, [K_i : F] = b and there is an irreducible continuous representation V_i of G_{K_i} with V_i|_{G_L} ≅ χ_i^{⊕a} and ρ ≅ Ind_{G_{K_i}}^{G_F} V_i (R01.1/continuous-induction); (4) b = 1 iff ρ(G_L) consists of scalars, and then the projective image of ρ is finite (a quotient of Gal(L/F)); conversely, if the projective image is finite, b = 1 for L the fixed field of the kernel of the projective representation. The de Rham / algebraic Hecke character conclusions of BCGP25 Lemma 10.2.3 (non-parallel weight, b > 1 and CM subfields when ρ is not finite up to twist) are NOT part of this node.

**Hypotheses.**

- ρ irreducible and continuous; characteristic 0 coefficients, algebraically closed (so the abelian semisimple restriction diagonalises).
- L/F finite Galois (G_L open normal in G_F).
- No p-adic Hodge theory: de Rham hypotheses and algebraic Hecke characters are routed to the owners named in the notes.

**Construction and proof.**

1. ρ|_{G_L} is semisimple (restriction of an irreducible characteristic-zero representation to an open normal subgroup, R01.1/semisimplicity-under-restriction-and-induction, Clifford); its image is abelian and E algebraically closed, so it is a sum of characters.
2. For σ ∈ G_F, ρ(σ) maps the χ-eigenspace of G_L to the χ^σ-eigenspace; the sum of eigenspaces over one Gal(L/F)-orbit is G_F-stable, so irreducibility forces a single orbit, and the multiplicities a are constant on it (Clifford's theorem, tauceti InductionRestriction layer 5, applied to the finite quotient through which the permutation action factors).
3. The χ_i-eigenspace V_i is stable under G_{K_i}; orbit–stabiliser gives [K_i : F] = b; Frobenius reciprocity gives a nonzero map ρ → Ind_{G_{K_i}}^{G_F} V_i, an isomorphism by irreducibility and dimension count (n = b·a), and then V_i is irreducible.
4. (4): b = 1 means G_L acts by a single character, i.e. by scalars, so the projective image is a quotient of Gal(L/F); conversely, if the projective image is finite, its kernel is an open normal subgroup G_{L'} acting by scalars, and for L' the decomposition has b = 1.

**Prerequisites.** `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/semisimplicity-under-restriction-and-induction`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/continuous-induction`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/restriction-dual-tensor-twist`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/absolutely-irreducible`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/InductionRestriction#layer-5-clifford-theory-over-a-normal-subgroup`.

**Acceptance.**

- Dihedral case n = 2: ρ = Ind_{G_K}^{G_F} ψ with K/F quadratic and ψ ≠ ψ^c restricts to ψ ⊕ ψ^c on G_K: b = 2, a = 1, K_i = K.
- Finite image: ρ with finite image, L the fixed field of ker ρ ∩ (centre preimage): if ρ(G_L) is scalar, b = 1 and the projective image is finite.
- a > 1 occurs: for K/ℚ a quaternion extension and ρ : G_ℚ → Gal(K/ℚ) ≅ Q_8 ⊂ GL_2(ℂ) the 2-dimensional irreducible representation, take L the biquadratic subfield fixed by the centre {±1}; ρ(G_L) = {±1} is scalar, so b = 1, a = 2, and the projective image Q_8/{±1} ≅ (ℤ/2)² is finite.

**Sources.**

- bcgp25, Lemma 10.2.3, printed p. 212 (arXiv:2502.20645v1): “The action of Gal(L/F ) on the characters χi via χσi (g) = χi (σgσ −1 ) induces a map” — The character orbit and the transitive Galois action.
- bcgp25, Lemma 10.2.3, proof, printed p. 212: “By the orbit–stabilizer theorem, [Ki : F ] = b. By Frobenius reciprocity, there is a” — The induction step.
- bcgp25, Lemma 10.2.3, proof, printed p. 213: “it follows P ρ lifts to a genuine representation” — The finite-projective-image step uses H²(F, Q̄_p^×) = 0 (Tate) and projective lifting, owned by ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.4 and G7/lifting-projective-representations, not by this node.

#### Recognition of lisse sheaves on a curve over a finite field from a dense open subset

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.5/curve-recognition-from-an-open-subset`. Kind: application. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.GaloisRep` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/Recognition/Curves.lean`). Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.5`.

Let F_q be a finite field of characteristic p, C a smooth geometrically connected curve over F_q, U ⊂ C a nonempty (hence dense) open subscheme, ℓ ≠ p, and E a field of characteristic 0 that is a finite extension of ℚ_ℓ (or Q̄_ℓ). Let V_1, V_2 be lisse E-sheaves of rank n on C, i.e. continuous representations of π_1(C, c̄) on n-dimensional E-vector spaces. If det(1 − Frob_x t | V_{1,x̄}) = det(1 − Frob_x t | V_{2,x̄}) in E[t] for every closed point x ∈ |U| (geometric or arithmetic Frobenius, the same for both), then V_1^ss ≅ V_2^ss as representations of π_1(C); if V_1, V_2 are semisimple, V_1 ≅ V_2. This is the step 'by the Chebotarev density Theorem, the semisimplifications … are isomorphic' in the proof of Kisin–Zhou Proposition 5.3.5.

**Hypotheses.**

- C normal and connected (smooth geometrically connected), U dense open; equality at every closed point of U.
- Common coefficient field E of characteristic 0 (for different ℓ the comparison is of polynomials with coefficients in a number field, after which a single ℓ is used).
- Conclusion only for semisimplifications.

**Construction and proof.**

1. π_1(U) → π_1(C) is surjective for a dense open U of a normal connected scheme (IG.1 owner of the arithmetic fundamental group sequence and Frobenius at closed points).
2. Closed-point Chebotarev on curves over finite fields (DeligneWeightsAndPurity DWP.3, which owns the function-field closed-point density statement with the constant-field degree congruences): the Frobenius elements Frob_x, x ∈ |U|, together with their conjugates, are dense in π_1(U); hence their images are dense in π_1(C).
3. The characteristic-polynomial maps π_1(C) → E[t] of V_1, V_2 are continuous class functions agreeing on a dense set, hence everywhere (as in R01.5/recognition-by-characteristic-polynomials-and-coefficient-descent (c)); det(1 − g t) and det(1 − g^{-1} t) determine each other, so the Frobenius convention is irrelevant.
4. R01.1/brauer-nesbitt gives V_1^ss ≅ V_2^ss; semisimple sheaves are equal to their semisimplifications.

**Prerequisites.** `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.5/recognition-by-characteristic-polynomials-and-coefficient-descent`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/brauer-nesbitt`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/semisimplification`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/baire-descent-to-a-finite-coefficient-field`; `DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.3`; `InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.1`.

**Acceptance.**

- Semisimplicity is required: on C = P¹ ∖ {0, ∞} over F_q, the representation g ↦ [[1, deg(g)],[0, 1]] (deg : π_1(C) → Ẑ → ℤ_ℓ the degree map) is a nonsplit extension of the trivial sheaf by itself with det(1 − Frob_x t) = (1 − t)² at every closed point, the same as the trivial rank-two sheaf.
- Kisin–Zhou Proposition 5.3.5: K^C_{ℓ'} and L^C_{ℓ'} agree on closed points of a dense open U ⊂ C, so their semisimplifications agree on C and the conjugacy classes ϑ(γ_{y,ℓ}) and ϑ(γ_{y,ℓ'}) coincide at the point y ∈ C(F_q) outside U.
- U = C recovers recognition at every closed point; the content is that points of C ∖ U are controlled by continuity.

**Sources.**

- kz25, Proof of Proposition 5.3.5, p. 54 (arXiv:2103.09945v2): “Therefore, by the Chebotarev density Theorem, the semisimplifications of KℓC′ and” — The curve recognition step, from equality on closed points of a dense open U ⊂ C.
- kz25, Proof of Proposition 5.3.5, p. 54: “We first show that if the proposition holds for the image under ψ of a Zariski open” — The reduction to a dense open subset of the curve.

## R01.6. Tate modules of elliptic curves and abelian varieties

**Purpose and boundary.** This layer turns the torsion of an abelian variety into a continuous Galois representation in the sense of R01.1, and proves the facts every consumer reads off it: rank and continuity, the residual representation, functoriality in homomorphisms and isogenies, the Weil pairing with its similitude character, the determinant and oddness, the Frobenius polynomial at a place of good reduction, and the local Euler factor. It owns the arithmetic Frobenius convention for Tate modules. It does not own the torsion group schemes and pairings themselves (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A3 constructs `[n]`, isogenies, duals and the scheme-theoretic Weil and polarization pairings), nor the elliptic-curve layers of Tau Ceti EllipticCurves (Layer 2: `E[N] ≃+ (ZMod N)²`, the Weil pairing, `T_ℓE` with `det = χ_ℓ`; Layer 3: `frobeniusTrace`, the Frobenius isogeny, `deg(1 − π_q) = #E(𝔽_q)`, Hasse; Layer 4: reduction, Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich for elliptic curves, the Tate curve). Those are imported, and this layer proves that its constructions agree with them. The conductor and Ogg's formula are ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.3, which imports this layer; the converse of Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich and ℓ-independence at bad places are NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties R11.5; the Weil estimate is DeligneWeightsAndPurity DWP.1; Faltings' semisimplicity and Tate conjecture are FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems R28.4. All four consume this layer and are never cited here. The finite-flat and crystalline properties of `T_pA` at places above `p` are outputs of R07 and R06, not consequences of the definition.

**Conventions.** `K` is a field, `K̄ = AlgebraicClosure K`, `K^sep ⊆ K̄`, and `G_K = Field.absoluteGaloisGroup K` with its Krull topology. An abelian variety is Tau Ceti's `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety` (a proper geometrically integral group scheme over `Spec K`) of dimension `g`. Throughout `ℓ` is a prime different from `char K`. An automorphism `σ` acts on a point by acting on its coordinates; for a Weierstrass curve this is Mathlib's `WeierstrassCurve.Affine.Point.map` along `σ`. The arithmetic Frobenius raises residues to the `q`-th power; the geometric Frobenius is its inverse. On a Tate module the arithmetic Frobenius acts as the Frobenius endomorphism `π` of the reduction. The first cohomology is `H¹_ℓ(A) := V_ℓA^∨`, and Euler factors are taken there with the geometric Frobenius: `det(1 − T·Φ | H¹) = det(1 − T·π | V_ℓA)`.

**The Tate module.** For `n ≥ 0`, `A[ℓ^n] = ker[ℓ^n]` is finite étale of order `ℓ^{2gn}` (A3), so `A[ℓ^n](K^sep) = A[ℓ^n](K̄)` is free of rank `2g` over `ℤ/ℓ^n`. The transition maps `[ℓ]` are surjective, and
`T_ℓA := lim_n A[ℓ^n](K^sep)`, `V_ℓA := T_ℓA ⊗ ℚ_ℓ`.
`T_ℓA` is free of rank `2g` over `ℤ_ℓ`, its inverse-limit topology is the module topology, and `T_ℓA/ℓ^n ≅ A[ℓ^n](K^sep)` `G_K`-equivariantly. The action is jointly continuous because each level factors through the finite group `Gal(K(A[ℓ^n])/K)`. So `(T_ℓA, ρ_{A,ℓ})` is a `ContinuousRep G_K ℤ_ℓ` of R01.1, and `V_ℓA` is its coefficient extension. The adelic module `T̂A = ∏_{ℓ ≠ char K} T_ℓA` serves the genericity definitions. Over the base `Spec K`, AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A4's étale Tate local system, evaluated at `Spec K^sep`, is this module: the two constructions are compared once and not duplicated. ⚠ Torsion is taken over `K^sep`, never over `K`: `lim E[ℓ^n](ℚ) = 0` for every elliptic curve over `ℚ`. ⚠ For `ℓ = char K` the construction is not made: a supersingular curve over `𝔽̄_p` has no `p`-torsion.

**Residual representation and isogenies.** Reduction mod `ℓ` recovers the pointwise action on `A[ℓ](K^sep)`. Every stable lattice in `V_ℓA` has the same residual semisimplification (R01.1). For an elliptic curve, the `G_K`-stable lines in `E[ℓ]` are exactly the kernels of cyclic `K`-rational `ℓ`-isogenies. ⚠ On such a line `G_K` acts by a character `ψ` that need not be trivial: the twist of 11a3 by `−1` has a rational 5-isogeny but no rational point of order 5 on that line. A homomorphism `α` induces `T_ℓα`, functorially and additively. Products go to direct sums. For an isogeny `φ` of degree `d`, `T_ℓφ` is injective with cokernel `(ker φ)(K^sep)[ℓ^∞]` of order the `ℓ`-part of `d`. Hence `V_ℓφ` is an isomorphism, and `T_ℓφ` is one when `ℓ ∤ d`. ⚠ Isogenous varieties have isomorphic rational Tate modules, but their integral Tate modules need not be isomorphic.

**Weil pairing.** From A3's compatible perfect pairings `e_{ℓ^n} : A[ℓ^n] × A^∨[ℓ^n] → μ_{ℓ^n}` one obtains `e_ℓ : T_ℓA × T_ℓA^∨ → ℤ_ℓ(1)`, a perfect pairing with `e_ℓ(σx, σy) = χ_ℓ(σ)·e_ℓ(x, y)`. Equivalently `T_ℓA^∨ ≅ (T_ℓA)^∨(1)`. A polarization `λ` gives the alternating form `e^λ_ℓ(x, y) = e_ℓ(x, T_ℓλ·y)`. It is nondegenerate over `ℚ_ℓ`, and perfect over `ℤ_ℓ` exactly when `ℓ ∤ deg λ`. It satisfies the Rosati adjunction, and it is an orthogonal sum on products. So `ρ_{A,ℓ}(G_K) ⊆ GSp(V_ℓA, e^λ)` with multiplier `χ_ℓ`. ⚠ The target keeps its Tate twist: complex conjugation negates `e_ℓ`.

**Determinant and oddness.** A symplectic similitude of multiplier `μ` has determinant `μ^g`, so `det V_ℓA = χ_ℓ^g`. For elliptic curves `∧²T_ℓE ≅ ℤ_ℓ(1)`, `det ρ_{E,ℓ} = χ_ℓ` and `det ρ̄_{E,ℓ} = χ̄_ℓ`. Let `c` be a complex conjugation at a real place. Then `χ_ℓ(c) = −1`, so each of the `±1`-eigenspaces of `c` is isotropic for `e^λ_ℓ`. Hence both are Lagrangian of dimension `g`, `tr ρ(c) = 0` and `det ρ(c) = (−1)^g`. For elliptic curves over `ℚ`, `det ρ_{E,ℓ}(c) = −1` for every `ℓ`, including `ℓ = 2`. ⚠ The residual statement `ρ̄(c) ≠ 1` is separate. For `y² = x³ − x` all 2-torsion is real, so `ρ̄_{E,2}(c) = 1`. ⚠ In dimension `2g` the right oddness statement is `tr ρ(c) = 0`, not `det ρ(c) = −1`: for a product of two elliptic curves the determinant at `c` is `+1`.

**Good reduction and the Frobenius polynomial.** Let `F` be a number field and `v ∤ ℓ` a place where `A` extends to an abelian scheme over `O_v`. The torsion `𝒜[ℓ^n]` is finite étale over `O_v`, so `V_ℓA` is unramified at `v`, and reduction gives a `D_w`-equivariant isomorphism `T_ℓA ≅ T_ℓA_v`. The arithmetic Frobenius acts as the Frobenius endomorphism `π_v` of `A_v`. Hence `P_v(X) := det(X − Frob_v | V_ℓA) = det(X − π_v | V_ℓA_v)`. It has constant term `q_v^g` and satisfies `X^{2g}P_v(q_v/X) = q_v^g P_v(X)`. For elliptic curves, `P_v(X) = X² − a_vX + q_v`, where `a_v` is Tau Ceti's `frobeniusTrace` of the reduction. The proof combines `det(V_ℓβ) = deg β`, which comes from the Weil pairing, with `deg(1 − π) = pointCount`. So `a_v ∈ ℤ` is independent of `ℓ` with no further input. For `g > 1`, integrality and `ℓ`-independence are Milne's Proposition 10.20. Its plan is the node `AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A6/characteristic-polynomial-on-tate-module`, which does not depend on this layer. But the A6 stage currently requires R01.6 through one node, on the Weil restriction, so the input is recorded as a gap, together with a restructuring proposal that removes that single edge. ⚠ For `ℓ = p` the representation is ramified in general even with good reduction.

**Local Euler factors.** For `A` over a local field with residue field `𝔽_q` and `ℓ ≠ p`, put `L_v(A, T) := det(1 − T·Φ_v | H¹_ℓ(A)^{I_v})`. This is R01.2's Euler factor of `H¹`, equivalently `det(1 − T·Frob_v | (V_ℓA)_{I_v})` on coinvariants. It is isogeny-invariant and multiplicative, has degree at most `2g`, and at good places equals `det(1 − T·π_v)`. ⚠ `det(1 − T·Φ_v | V_ℓA)` is not the Euler factor: for `y² = x³ − x` at `5` it is `1 + (2/5)T + (1/5)T²`, while the Euler factor is `1 + 2T + 5T²`. For elliptic curves this layer proves `L_v = WeierstrassCurve.localPolynomial` at good places, and at split and nonsplit multiplicative places, through the Tate curve and the unramified quadratic twist. At additive places Mathlib's polynomial is `1`. The matching vanishing of inertia invariants rests on the Néron model and belongs to R11.5, as does ℓ-independence of `L_v` at bad places.

**Endomorphism coefficients.** Let `E ⊆ End⁰_K(A)` be a number field of endomorphisms defined over `K`. Then `V_ℓA` is an `E ⊗ ℚ_ℓ[G_K]`-module and splits as `⊕_{λ|ℓ} V_λA`. Each `V_λA` is an `E_λ`-linear continuous representation, two-dimensional for `GL₂`-type and one-dimensional for CM type. The dimensions use the freeness of `V_ℓA` over `E ⊗ ℚ_ℓ` (Milne 10.23, again A6, so a gap). When `O_E ⊆ End_K(A)`, the λ-torsion `A[λ]` is the residual λ-adic representation. Suppose `E` is totally real and the Rosati involution of a polarization fixes `E`. Then the Weil pairing is `E`-balanced, the components are mutually orthogonal, `det_{E_λ} ρ_λ = χ_ℓ` for `GL₂`-type, and every component is odd. ⚠ If the endomorphisms are defined only over an extension `L`, Galois acts semilinearly. For `y² = x³ − x` over `ℚ`, complex conjugation anticommutes with `[i]`, so the image lies in the normaliser of the Cartan subgroup `(ℤ[i] ⊗ ℤ_ℓ)^×`, not in the Cartan itself.

**Genericity, Serre and Noot.** Following Masser–Zannier, a principally polarized `A` over a number field is `p`-Galois generic if its image is open in `GSp(T_pA, e^λ) ≅ GSp_{2g}(ℤ_p)`. It is Galois generic if the adelic image is open in `GSp_{2g}(ℤ̂)`. ⚠ The definition must use `GSp`: the multiplier `χ_p` has infinite image. Isogeny invariance, Cadoret's implication and Serre's open image theorem need Faltings and stay with AbelianVarietiesIsogenousToNoJacobian G0. Serre's theorem, as Richard–Yafaev use it, says that after a finite extension the adelic image is a product of its ℓ-adic components, each Zariski connected, and contained in `M(ℤ̂)` for the Mumford–Tate group `M`. Containment rests on Deligne's absolute Hodge theorem (AutomorphicBundles B1, ShimuraData D1). The original proofs of independence and connectedness were not read, and a recorded gap and restructuring proposal move those parts downstream if they need Faltings' semisimplicity or semistable reduction. Noot's specialisation identifies `T_ℓX_η` with `T_ℓX_σ` along a closed point of a family, `D_σ`-equivariantly. By ℓ-adic Hilbert irreducibility (requested from IG.2) some closed point keeps the full ℓ-adic image. ⚠ Noot's equality of endomorphism rings uses Faltings over fields of finite type and is not part of this layer.

**Dependencies.** Inside the roadmap: R01.1 (the carrier, coefficient extension, framing, finite quotients, the Tate twist, duals and twists, lattice independence, induction) and R01.2 (decomposition groups, local restriction, unramified representations, Frobenius polynomials, cyclotomic characters, quasi-unipotence, Euler factors and the Weil–Deligne functor). Other roadmaps: AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A3 and A4; Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layers 2–5, JacobianChallenge layer E, NumberFieldArithmetic Layer 5, LocalFieldsRamification Layer 2, Chebotarev Layer 10, and ModularCurves 0E (spreading out); ShimuraData D1; AutomorphicBundles B1; InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups IG.2.

**Acceptance tests.**
- `χ_p`: `T_p(μ_{p^∞}) = ℤ_p(1)` and `det T_pE = χ_p`.
- Split Tate curve: `0 → ℤ_ℓ(1) → T_ℓE_q → ℤ_ℓ → 0`, with unipotent inertia and Euler factor `1 − T`. For 11a3 at 11, Tau Ceti's `frobeniusTrace` is `1`.
- Supersingular good reduction: `y² = x³ + 1` has `a_p = 0` for `p = 5, 11, 17, 23`.
- CM over `ℚ`: `y² = x³ − x` has image in a Cartan normaliser, `V_ℓE ⊗ ℚ̄_ℓ` is induced from a character of `G_{ℚ(i)}`, and `a_p = 0` for `p ≡ 3 mod 4`.
- Frobenius conventions over `𝔽_5` for `y² = x³ − x`:
  - arithmetic Frobenius on `V_ℓ`: `X² + 2X + 5`;
  - geometric Frobenius on `V_ℓ`: `X² + (2/5)X + 1/5`;
  - geometric Frobenius on `H¹`: `X² + 2X + 5`;
  - Euler factor: `1 + 2T + 5T²`.

### Declarations of R01.6

Each entry gives the mathematical statement, hypotheses, proof route, prerequisites, uses, API, unit tests, acceptance checks and sources of one planned declaration.

#### The ℓ-adic Tate module of an abelian variety as a continuous Galois representation

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6/tate-module-of-an-abelian-variety`. Kind: construction. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/TateModule/AbelianVariety`). Planet: **ℓ-adic Tate module**. Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6`.

Throughout: K is a field, K̄ = AlgebraicClosure K with separable closure K^sep ⊆ K̄, and G_K = Field.absoluteGaloisGroup K = Aut(K̄/K) with its Krull topology (restriction identifies it with Gal(K^sep/K)); σ ∈ G_K acts on a point x ∈ A(K̄) by acting on its coordinates (for a Weierstrass curve this is Mathlib's WeierstrassCurve.Affine.Point.map along σ). A is an abelian variety over K in Tau Ceti's sense (TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety: proper geometrically integral group scheme over Spec K) of dimension g, and ℓ is a prime number with ℓ ≠ char K. For n ≥ 0 put A[ℓ^n] := ker([ℓ^n] : A → A), a finite étale K-group scheme of order ℓ^{2gn} (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A3), and A[ℓ^n](K^sep) = A[ℓ^n](K̄) its group of geometric points, with the transition maps [ℓ] : A[ℓ^{n+1}](K^sep) → A[ℓ^n](K^sep). Define T_ℓA := lim_n A[ℓ^n](K^sep), with the inverse-limit topology of the discrete finite groups, V_ℓA := T_ℓA ⊗_{Z_ℓ} Q_ℓ, and the prime-to-char K adelic module T̂A := lim_N A[N](K^sep) (N invertible in K) = ∏_{ℓ ≠ char K} T_ℓA. Then: (a) each A[ℓ^n](K^sep) is a free Z/ℓ^n-module of rank 2g, the transition maps are surjective, and T_ℓA is a free Z_ℓ-module of rank 2g whose inverse-limit topology is the ℓ-adic topology (equivalently Mathlib's module topology, IsModuleTopology Z_ℓ); (b) the projection induces a canonical G_K-equivariant isomorphism T_ℓA/ℓ^n T_ℓA ≅ A[ℓ^n](K^sep); (c) G_K acts Z_ℓ-linearly on T_ℓA through its coordinatewise action on A[ℓ^n](K̄), the action map G_K × T_ℓA → T_ℓA is jointly continuous, and so (T_ℓA, ρ_{A,ℓ}) is an object of ContinuousRep G_K Z_ℓ (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/continuous-representation) of rank 2g, with V_ℓA its coefficient extension to Q_ℓ; (d) the kernel of G_K → Aut(A[ℓ^n](K^sep)) is the open subgroup G_{K(A[ℓ^n])} fixing the finite Galois extension K(A[ℓ^n]) generated by the coordinates of the ℓ^n-torsion points, and ρ_{A,ℓ} factors through Gal(K(A[ℓ^∞])/K); (e) a different choice of algebraic closure changes (T_ℓA, ρ_{A,ℓ}) by a canonical isomorphism, and conjugating the embedding K^sep ⊆ K̄ by τ ∈ G_K changes it by the isomorphism x ↦ τx. A choice of Z_ℓ-basis gives the framed form ρ_{A,ℓ} : G_K → GL_{2g}(Z_ℓ) (R01.1/framed-representation), well defined up to GL_{2g}(Z_ℓ)-conjugacy. The Tate module is covariant in A. It is not defined for ℓ = char K (there A[ℓ](K^sep) has order at most ℓ^g).

**Hypotheses.**

- K any field; ℓ a prime different from char K (for ℓ = char K the construction is not made: A[ℓ](K^sep) has order ≤ ℓ^g)
- A an abelian variety over K of dimension g in Tau Ceti's sense (TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety)
- torsion points are taken over K^sep (equivalently K̄), never over K
- G_K = Field.absoluteGaloisGroup K (automorphisms of AlgebraicClosure K) with the Krull topology

**Construction and proof.**

1. Order and étaleness: AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A3 proves [n] finite locally free of rank n^{2g} and étale when n is invertible on the base; over K with ℓ ≠ char K, A[ℓ^n] is finite étale of order ℓ^{2gn}, so #A[ℓ^n](K^sep) = ℓ^{2gn} and the K^sep- and K̄-points agree (Milne AV, Remark 7.3, p. 34).
2. Structure: applying the count to every m | ℓ^n and the structure theorem for finite abelian groups gives A[ℓ^n](K^sep) ≅ (Z/ℓ^n)^{2g} (Milne AV, Remark 7.3, p. 34).
3. Surjective transitions: [ℓ] : A → A is a finite étale surjective isogeny (A3), so every K^sep-point of A[ℓ^n] lifts to a K^sep-point of A[ℓ^{n+1}]; the inverse limit of free Z/ℓ^n-modules of rank 2g along surjections reducing compatibly is free of rank 2g over Z_ℓ with T_ℓA/ℓ^n ≅ A[ℓ^n](K^sep) (Milne AV, Proposition 10.5, p. 45).
4. Galois action: σ ∈ G_K acts on A(K̄) through the functoriality of points along the K-automorphism σ (coordinates); it commutes with [ℓ^n], so preserves A[ℓ^n](K̄) and commutes with the transition maps; hence it acts Z_ℓ-linearly on T_ℓA.
5. Continuity: each A[ℓ^n](K^sep) is finite and pointwise defined over the finite Galois extension K(A[ℓ^n]), so the action on it factors through the finite quotient Gal(K(A[ℓ^n])/K) and is continuous for the discrete topology (R01.1/finite-coefficients-and-finite-quotients); joint continuity on the inverse limit follows level by level, and the module topology on the finite free Z_ℓ-module T_ℓA is its inverse-limit topology.
6. Independence of choices: an isomorphism of algebraic closures over K transports torsion points and Galois actions compatibly; this is the transport-of-structure argument of R01.1/restriction-dual-tensor-twist applied to the isomorphism of profinite groups it induces.

**Prerequisites.** `AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A3`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/continuous-representation`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/coefficient-extension`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/framed-representation`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/finite-coefficients-and-finite-quotients`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/restriction-dual-tensor-twist`; `tauceti:TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety`; `tauceti:TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.mulBy`; `tauceti:TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.baseChange`; `mathlib:Field.absoluteGaloisGroup`; `mathlib:PadicInt`; `mathlib:IsModuleTopology`; `mathlib:ContRepresentation`; `mathlib:Submodule.torsionBy`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/JacobianChallenge#layer-e-abelian-varieties`.

**Uses.**

- AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A6/tate-module-of-a-weil-restriction: T_ℓ(Res_{L/K}A) ≅ Ind_{G_L}^{G_K} T_ℓA needs T_ℓA as a continuous G_L-module over a field
- FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems:R28.4/semisimplicity-and-the-tate-homomorphism-comparison: Faltings' Satz 3 and 4 are statements about the continuous Gal(K̄/K)-module T_ℓA and V_ℓA
- EllipticCurveModularity:R29.4/tate-module-comparison: V_r(E) as a Q_r[G_Q]-module compared with V_r(F) of a newform

- NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties:R11.3/toric-finite-filtration: saturated G_K-stable submodules T_t ⊂ T_f ⊂ T_ℓ(A) of the actual inverse-limit Tate module
