**API.**

- `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.torsionPoints` (data): A[N](K^sep) for N invertible in K, the N-torsion of the K^sep-points, as a finite Z/N-module with its G_K-action.
- `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.tateModule` (constructor): T_ℓA := lim_n A[ℓ^n](K^sep) along [ℓ], as a Z_ℓ-module with the inverse-limit topology.
- `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.tateModule.toTorsion` (projection): The projection T_ℓA → A[ℓ^n](K^sep), G_K-equivariant and Z_ℓ-linear (Z_ℓ acting through Z/ℓ^n).
- `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.tateModule_free` (structure): T_ℓA is a free Z_ℓ-module of rank 2g; Module.finrank Z_ℓ T_ℓA = 2·dim A.
- `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.tateModule.modPowEquiv` (equivalence): T_ℓA/ℓ^n T_ℓA ≃ A[ℓ^n](K^sep), G_K-equivariant.
- `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.tateModule.ext` (extensionality): Two elements of T_ℓA are equal iff their images in A[ℓ^n](K^sep) agree for every n.
- `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.tateModuleRep` (instance): (T_ℓA, ρ_{A,ℓ}) as a ContinuousRep G_K Z_ℓ (R01.1/continuous-representation); its underlying Mathlib ContRepresentation is obtained by forgetting joint continuity.
- `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.rationalTateModule` (constructor): V_ℓA := T_ℓA ⊗_{Z_ℓ} Q_ℓ as the coefficient extension of tateModuleRep to Q_ℓ (R01.1/coefficient-extension).
- `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.tateModule.map` (functoriality): A homomorphism α : A → B over K induces T_ℓα : T_ℓA → T_ℓB, (x_n) ↦ (α(x_n)), with map_id, map_comp, and map_add for the group structure of Hom(A, B).
- `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.tateModule.baseChange` (compatibility): For a field extension L/K with L ⊆ K̄, T_ℓ(A_L) = T_ℓA as Z_ℓ-modules and ρ_{A_L,ℓ} is the restriction of ρ_{A,ℓ} to G_L (Tau Ceti AbelianVariety.baseChange).
- `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.tateModule.kernel_mod_pow` (characterisation): ker(ρ_{A,ℓ} mod ℓ^n) = G_{K(A[ℓ^n])}, an open normal subgroup of finite index.
- `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.tateModule_compare_etaleLocalSystem` (compatibility): Over the base Spec K, the étale Tate local system of AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A4, evaluated at the geometric point Spec K^sep, is T_ℓA with the same G_K-action.
- `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.adelicTateModule` (constructor): T̂A := lim_N A[N](K^sep) over N invertible in K, canonically ∏_{ℓ ≠ char K} T_ℓA, with the product action of G_K.

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.tateModule_rank_eq` (computation): For E : y² = x³ − x over Q (g = 1) and ℓ = 5, T_5E is free of rank 2 over Z_5 and T_5E/5T_5E has exactly 25 elements.
- `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.tateModule_of_dim_zero` (degenerate): If A is the zero abelian variety Spec K (g = 0), then T_ℓA = 0 and ρ_{A,ℓ} is the zero representation, for every ℓ ≠ char K.
- `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.tateModule_ne_limit_rational_torsion` (non-example): The tempting definition lim_n A[ℓ^n](K) using K-rational points is wrong: for E : y² = x³ − x over Q, E(Q)[ℓ^∞] is finite for every ℓ, so lim_n E[ℓ^n](Q) = 0, whereas T_ℓE ≅ Z_ℓ².
- `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.tateModule_char_p_excluded` (non-example): For a supersingular elliptic curve E over F̄_p (e.g. y² = x³ + 1 over F̄_5) one has E[p^n](F̄_p) = 0, so the formula lim E[p^n] would give 0 at ℓ = p = char K; the construction requires ℓ ≠ char K.
- `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.tateModule_mod_pow_equiv_galois` (characterisation): For every n, the reduction map T_ℓA/ℓ^n T_ℓA → A[ℓ^n](K^sep) is a G_K-equivariant isomorphism; for n = 1 it identifies ρ_{A,ℓ} mod ℓ with the pointwise Galois action on A[ℓ](K^sep).

**Acceptance.**

- For an elliptic curve (g = 1) the construction recovers Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 2's T_ℓE, free of rank 2 (node elliptic-tate-module-comparison).
- For E : y² = x³ − x over Q, E[2](Q̄) = {O, (0,0), (1,0), (−1,0)} consists of rational points, so T_2E/2T_2E ≅ (Z/2)² with trivial G_Q-action, while ρ_{E,2} itself is nontrivial (its determinant is χ_2, node determinant-and-oddness).
- The analogous construction for the multiplicative group, lim μ_{ℓ^n}(K^sep), is the Tate twist Z_ℓ(1) of R01.1/tate-twist, with G_K acting through the cyclotomic character χ_ℓ (Mathlib cyclotomicCharacter): this is the χ_ℓ example of the roadmap.

**Sources.**

- milne-av, Ch. I, Remark 7.3, p. 34: “free Z` -module of rank 2g. It is called the Tate module of A.” — T_ℓA = lim A_{ℓ^n}(k) is free of rank 2g; the same remark defines it over k^sep for non-closed k.
- milne-av, Ch. I, Proposition 10.5, p. 45: “P ROPOSITION 10.5. For ` ¤ char.k/, T` A is a free Z` -module of rank 2g.” — Rank 2g for ℓ ≠ char k (the text layer renders ≠ as ¤).
- milne-ec, Ch. V, §8, pp. 223–224: “on T` E, i.e., a continuous homomorphism (also referred to as a representation)” — The Galois action on the Tate module of an elliptic curve over Q is a continuous representation into Aut(T_ℓE) ≅ GL_2(Z_ℓ).

#### Finite torsion, the residual representation and rational cyclic isogenies

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6/torsion-and-residual-representation`. Kind: theorem. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/TateModule/Theorems`). Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6`.

Throughout: K is a field, K̄ = AlgebraicClosure K with separable closure K^sep ⊆ K̄, and G_K = Field.absoluteGaloisGroup K = Aut(K̄/K) with its Krull topology (restriction identifies it with Gal(K^sep/K)); σ ∈ G_K acts on a point x ∈ A(K̄) by acting on its coordinates (for a Weierstrass curve this is Mathlib's WeierstrassCurve.Affine.Point.map along σ). A is an abelian variety over K in Tau Ceti's sense (TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety: proper geometrically integral group scheme over Spec K) of dimension g, and ℓ is a prime number with ℓ ≠ char K. (a) For every n ≥ 1 the G_K-module T_ℓA/ℓ^nT_ℓA is canonically isomorphic to A[ℓ^n](K^sep) with its pointwise action; in particular the residual representation ρ̄_{A,ℓ} := T_ℓA ⊗_{Z_ℓ} F_ℓ (R01.1/reduction-and-residual-semisimplification) is the G_K-module A[ℓ](K^sep) of dimension 2g over F_ℓ. (b) For every G_K-stable Z_ℓ-lattice Λ ⊂ V_ℓA, (Λ/ℓΛ)^ss ≅ A[ℓ](K^sep)^ss as F_ℓ[G_K]-modules (R01.1/continuity-descent-and-lattice-independence). (c) Let E be an elliptic curve over K (Weierstrass, IsElliptic). The G_K-stable F_ℓ-lines L ⊂ E[ℓ](K^sep) are exactly the K-rational cyclic subgroups of order ℓ, i.e. the kernels of the cyclic K-rational isogenies of degree ℓ out of E (the quotient E → E/L of AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A3); so ρ̄_{E,ℓ} is reducible over F_ℓ iff E admits a K-rational isogeny of degree ℓ. On such a line G_K acts through a character ψ : G_K → F_ℓ^×, and on the quotient E[ℓ]/L through χ̄_ℓ ψ^{−1} (node determinant-and-oddness); ψ need not be trivial, so reducibility of ρ̄_{E,ℓ} does not imply that E has a K-rational point of order ℓ.

**Hypotheses.**

- ℓ ≠ char K
- in (c), the line L is a subgroup of the K^sep-points; its K-rationality means stability under G_K, not pointwise rationality

**Construction and proof.**

1. (a) is part (b) of node tate-module-of-an-abelian-variety, restated for consumers; n = 1 is the comparison of the residual representation with the existing pointwise action requested by the stage.
2. (b) Λ and T_ℓA are both G_K-stable lattices in V_ℓA; R01.1/continuity-descent-and-lattice-independence gives (Λ/ℓΛ)^ss ≅ (T_ℓA/ℓT_ℓA)^ss, and (a) identifies the latter.
3. (c) A G_K-stable line L is a finite subgroup of E(K^sep) stable under G_K, hence the K^sep-points of a finite étale K-subgroup scheme (Galois descent for finite étale schemes); the quotient isogeny E → E/L of A3 is defined over K with kernel L. Conversely the kernel of a K-rational isogeny of degree ℓ (ℓ ≠ char K, so the kernel is étale of order ℓ) is a G_K-stable line. The character ψ is the action on L ≅ F_ℓ; the quotient character follows from det ρ̄_{E,ℓ} = χ̄_ℓ (node determinant-and-oddness).
4. Non-triviality of ψ: E and its quadratic twist E^d (Tau Ceti WeierstrassCurve.quadraticTwistOf) have the same stable lines with ψ replaced by ψ·ε_d for the quadratic character ε_d, so a rational point of order ℓ on E (ψ = 1) gives ψ = ε_d ≠ 1 on E^d for d not a square.

**Prerequisites.** `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6/tate-module-of-an-abelian-variety`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/reduction-and-residual-semisimplification`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/continuity-descent-and-lattice-independence`; `AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A3`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6/determinant-and-oddness`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/EllipticCurves#layer-2-torsion-the-weil-pairing-and-the-tate-module-aec-iii68`; `tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.quadraticTwistOf`.

**Acceptance.**

- The curve 11a3, y² + y = x³ − x², has a rational point (0, 0) of order 5, so ρ̄_{E,5} has a stable line with trivial character ψ = 1 and quotient character χ̄_5 (Δ = −11).
- Its quadratic twist by d = −1 still has a G_Q-stable line in E[5] (the twist of the same line) but its character is the nontrivial character ε_{−1} of Q(i)/Q, so the twisted curve has a rational 5-isogeny but no rational point of order 5 in that line.
- For E : y² = x³ − x over Q, ρ̄_{E,2} is trivial (all of E[2] is rational) and every line in E[2] is G_Q-stable: three rational 2-isogenies.

**Sources.**

- milne-av, Ch. I, Remark 7.3, p. 34: “module of rank 2g (easy exercise using the structure theorem for finite abelian groups).” — A_n(k) is free of rank 2g over Z/n; T_ℓA mod ℓ^n is the ℓ^n-torsion.
- ddt-fermat, §2.2, p. 55: “Note that ρ̄E,`n ∼” — ρ̄_{E,ℓ^n} ≅ ρ_{E,ℓ} mod ℓ^n: the residual representation is the action on E[ℓ^n].
- ddt-fermat, §2.2, Theorem 2.9 and the sentence before it, p. 55: “a semi-stable curve with a rational subgroup of order ` is necessarily isogenous” — A rational subgroup of order ℓ (a stable line) is distinguished from a rational point of order ℓ.

#### Comparison with the Tate module of a Weierstrass curve (Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 2)

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6/elliptic-tate-module-comparison`. Kind: comparison. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/TateModule/Theorems`). Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6`.

Let K be a field, W a Weierstrass curve over K with [W.IsElliptic], E_W the elliptic curve it defines (the projective closure of W.toAffine, an abelian variety of dimension 1 whose L-points are W⁄L.Point functorially in the field L/K), and ℓ a prime ≠ char K. Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 2 constructs E[N] = Submodule.torsionBy ℤ (W⁄K^sep).Point N ≃+ (ZMod N)², the Weil pairing e_N valued in rootsOfUnity N K^sep, the Tate module T_ℓW := lim E[ℓ^n] with its continuous G_K-representation into Module.Aut Z_ℓ (T_ℓW) and det = χ_ℓ. Then the identification E_W(K^sep) = (W⁄K^sep).Point induces, for every n, a G_K-equivariant group isomorphism E_W[ℓ^n](K^sep) ≅ Submodule.torsionBy ℤ (W⁄K^sep).Point ℓ^n compatible with the transition maps, hence an isomorphism T_ℓ(E_W) ≅ T_ℓW of continuous Z_ℓ[G_K]-modules, under which: (i) Tau Ceti's isogeny map TauCeti.Isogeny.toPointHom of φ : W₁ → W₂ corresponds to T_ℓ of the induced homomorphism E_{W₁} → E_{W₂}; (ii) Tau Ceti's e_{ℓ^n} corresponds to the polarization pairing e^λ_{ℓ^n} of node weil-pairing-on-tate-modules for the canonical principal polarization λ : E → E^∨, P ↦ class of (P) − (O), up to the inversion e ↦ e^{−1} fixed once by a named comparison lemma; (iii) the determinant theorem of Layer 2 and node determinant-and-oddness give the same character χ_ℓ. Consequently every statement of this layer about T_ℓA for abelian varieties applies to Tau Ceti's T_ℓW, and every Layer-2 statement about T_ℓW applies to T_ℓ(E_W).

**Hypotheses.**

- W elliptic over a field K; ℓ ≠ char K
- the identification of E_W with an abelian variety of dimension 1 together with E_W(L) = W⁄L.Point is an input recorded as a gap (no owner located)

**Construction and proof.**

1. Both inverse systems are built from the same groups: E_W(K^sep)[ℓ^n] and the ℓ^n-torsion submodule of (W⁄K^sep).Point coincide under the point identification, and multiplication by ℓ corresponds because the group laws coincide.
2. Galois equivariance: σ acts on both sides by acting on coordinates (Mathlib WeierstrassCurve.Affine.Point.map along σ), so the identification is G_K-equivariant at each level and hence on the limits; continuity is level-wise on both sides.
3. Isogenies: a Tau Ceti isogeny is a coordinate-ring pullback; on points it induces the same map as the morphism of abelian varieties it defines (Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 0 place dictionary and Layer 1 toPointHom).
4. Weil pairing: both pairings are characterised by compatibility with isogenies and duals (e_N(φP, Q) = e_N(P, φ̂Q), Milne AV Proposition 13.2(a)) and agree up to the universal sign/inversion convention, which is fixed by evaluating both on a single curve.
5. Determinant: both equal χ_ℓ since both pairings are perfect alternating and Galois-equivariant into Z_ℓ(1).

**Prerequisites.** `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6/tate-module-of-an-abelian-variety`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6/weil-pairing-on-tate-modules`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/EllipticCurves#layer-2-torsion-the-weil-pairing-and-the-tate-module-aec-iii68`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/JacobianChallenge#layer-e-abelian-varieties`; `mathlib:WeierstrassCurve.Affine.Point`; `mathlib:WeierstrassCurve.Affine.Point.map`; `mathlib:WeierstrassCurve.IsElliptic`; `mathlib:Submodule.torsionBy`; `tauceti:TauCeti.Isogeny`.

**Acceptance.**

- For W : y² = x³ − x over Q, both constructions give the same mod-2 reduction: the four rational points O, (0,0), (±1,0), with trivial G_Q-action.
- For the Tate curve E_q over a p-adic field with ℓ ≠ p, both constructions give the extension 0 → Z_ℓ(1) → T_ℓE_q → Z_ℓ → 0 from Tau Ceti Layer 4's uniformisation K̄^×/q^Z ≅ E_q(K̄) (node required-examples).

**Sources.**

- milne-ec, Ch. III, before Proposition 3.22, pp. 99–100: “The Tate module T` E of E is defined to be” — The Tate module of an elliptic curve as lim E(k)_{ℓ^n}, free of rank 2.
- milne-av, Ch. I, §13, p. 57: “For an elliptic curve A over a field k, and an integer m not divisible by the characteristic of” — The elliptic Weil pairing as the special case of the abelian-variety pairing combined with a polarization.

#### Functoriality: homomorphisms, products, isogenies and base change

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6/functoriality-products-and-isogenies`. Kind: theorem. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/TateModule/Theorems`). Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6`.

Throughout: K is a field, K̄ = AlgebraicClosure K with separable closure K^sep ⊆ K̄, and G_K = Field.absoluteGaloisGroup K = Aut(K̄/K) with its Krull topology (restriction identifies it with Gal(K^sep/K)); σ ∈ G_K acts on a point x ∈ A(K̄) by acting on its coordinates (for a Weierstrass curve this is Mathlib's WeierstrassCurve.Affine.Point.map along σ). A is an abelian variety over K in Tau Ceti's sense (TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety: proper geometrically integral group scheme over Spec K) of dimension g, and ℓ is a prime number with ℓ ≠ char K. (a) Every homomorphism α : A → B of abelian varieties over K induces a Z_ℓ-linear G_K-equivariant map T_ℓα : T_ℓA → T_ℓB, (x_n) ↦ (α(x_n)); T_ℓ(id) = id, T_ℓ(βα) = T_ℓβ ∘ T_ℓα, T_ℓ(α + α′) = T_ℓα + T_ℓα′, so Hom_K(A, B) → Hom_{Z_ℓ[G_K]}(T_ℓA, T_ℓB) is a group homomorphism and End_K(A) → End_{Z_ℓ[G_K]}(T_ℓA) a ring homomorphism, which extends Z_ℓ-linearly to Hom_K(A, B) ⊗ Z_ℓ. (b) For the product A × B (Tau Ceti AbelianVariety.prod), (T_ℓpr_1, T_ℓpr_2) : T_ℓ(A × B) → T_ℓA ⊕ T_ℓB is an isomorphism of continuous representations. (c) Let φ : A → B be an isogeny (finite surjective, Tau Ceti IsIsogeny) of degree d. Then T_ℓφ is injective and there is a canonical G_K-equivariant isomorphism coker(T_ℓφ) ≅ (ker φ)(K^sep)[ℓ^∞]; in particular #coker(T_ℓφ) = d_ℓ, the ℓ-part of d, and V_ℓφ : V_ℓA → V_ℓB is an isomorphism of Q_ℓ[G_K]-modules. If ℓ ∤ d, T_ℓφ is an isomorphism and φ induces G_K-isomorphisms A[ℓ^n](K^sep) ≅ B[ℓ^n](K^sep) for all n. If ψ : B → A satisfies ψφ = [m], then T_ℓψ ∘ T_ℓφ = m. (d) For a field extension L ⊆ K̄ of K, T_ℓ(A_L) = T_ℓA|_{G_L} (Tau Ceti AbelianVariety.baseChange). (e) For a field isomorphism τ : K → K′ extended to τ̄ : K̄ → K̄′, transport of structure gives a Z_ℓ-isomorphism T_ℓA ≅ T_ℓ(A^τ) intertwining ρ_{A,ℓ}(σ) with ρ_{A^τ,ℓ}(τ̄στ̄^{−1}).

**Hypotheses.**

- ℓ ≠ char K
- in (c) the degree d is the rank of the finite group scheme ker φ (its p-primary part may be infinitesimal in characteristic p; only its ℓ-primary part, which is étale, enters coker T_ℓφ)

**Construction and proof.**

1. (a) α commutes with [ℓ^n] and with the Galois action on coordinates; additivity holds level-wise because the group law on Hom(A, B) is pointwise (Milne AV, §10, p. 45).
2. (b) A × B represents the product functor on points, so (A × B)[ℓ^n](K^sep) = A[ℓ^n](K^sep) × B[ℓ^n](K^sep) compatibly with transitions and Galois.
3. (c) Put G = ker φ, a finite K-group scheme of order d (A3). On K^sep-points, 0 → G(K^sep)[ℓ^∞] → A[ℓ^∞](K^sep) → B[ℓ^∞](K^sep) → 0 is exact (φ is surjective on K^sep-points and A[ℓ^∞] is divisible). Applying the snake lemma to multiplication by ℓ^n and passing to the limit (Hom(Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ, −) is left exact and G(K^sep)[ℓ^∞] is finite, so T_ℓG = 0) gives 0 → T_ℓA → T_ℓB → G(K^sep)[ℓ^∞] → 0. The ℓ-primary part of G is étale since ℓ is invertible, so its order is d_ℓ (Milne AV, proof of Proposition 10.20, p. 52, uses exactly #Coker(T_ℓβ) = #Ker(β)(ℓ)).
4. The quasi-inverse: the kernel of φ is killed by m = exponent, so φ factors [m] through A/G ≅ B and ψ exists with ψφ = [m] (A3, isogenies and quotients); then T_ℓψ T_ℓφ = T_ℓ[m] = m; hence V_ℓφ is invertible (Milne AV Ch. IV, Corollary 3.6, p. 142).
5. (d) and (e) are transport of structure, using R01.1/restriction-dual-tensor-twist for the restricted and conjugated representations.

**Prerequisites.** `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6/tate-module-of-an-abelian-variety`; `AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A3`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/restriction-dual-tensor-twist`; `tauceti:TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.prod`; `tauceti:TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.IsIsogeny`; `tauceti:TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.End`; `tauceti:TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.baseChange`.

**Acceptance.**

- For the 5-isogeny φ : E = 11a3 → E′ with kernel the rational subgroup ⟨(0,0)⟩, T_5φ is injective with cokernel Z/5 and V_5φ is an isomorphism; for ℓ ≠ 5, T_ℓφ is an isomorphism and E[ℓ] ≅ E′[ℓ] as G_Q-modules.
- For [m] : A → A, coker T_ℓ[m] = T_ℓA/m T_ℓA ≅ A[m](K^sep)[ℓ^∞] has order m_ℓ^{2g} = (ℓ-part of deg [m] = m^{2g}).
- For A = E_1 × E_2 a product of elliptic curves, T_ℓA = T_ℓE_1 ⊕ T_ℓE_2 has rank 4 and det = χ_ℓ² (node determinant-and-oddness).

**Sources.**

- milne-av, Ch. I, §10, after Proposition 10.5, p. 45: “Therefore T` is a functor from abelian varieties to Z` -modules.” — T_ℓα for a homomorphism α and functoriality.
- milne-av, Ch. I, proof of Proposition 10.20, p. 52: “P ROOF. We now prove (10.20). Clearly we may assume k D ks . For any ˇ 2 End.A/,” — The proof records |deg β|_ℓ = #(Ker β)(ℓ)^{-1} = #(Coker T_ℓβ)^{-1}: the cokernel of T_ℓ of an isogeny has order the ℓ-part of its degree.
- milne-av, Ch. IV, Corollary 3.6, p. 142: “P ROOF. The isogeny defines an isomorphism V` A ! V` B commuting with the actions of” — An isogeny induces a Galois-equivariant isomorphism of rational Tate modules.

#### The Weil pairing on Tate modules, polarization pairings and the similitude character

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6/weil-pairing-on-tate-modules`. Kind: construction. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/TateModule/WeilPairing`). Planet: **Weil pairing on Tate modules**. Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6`.

Throughout: K is a field, K̄ = AlgebraicClosure K with separable closure K^sep ⊆ K̄, and G_K = Field.absoluteGaloisGroup K = Aut(K̄/K) with its Krull topology (restriction identifies it with Gal(K^sep/K)); σ ∈ G_K acts on a point x ∈ A(K̄) by acting on its coordinates (for a Weierstrass curve this is Mathlib's WeierstrassCurve.Affine.Point.map along σ). A is an abelian variety over K in Tau Ceti's sense (TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety: proper geometrically integral group scheme over Spec K) of dimension g, and ℓ is a prime number with ℓ ≠ char K. Let A^∨ be the dual abelian variety and Z_ℓ(1) = lim μ_{ℓ^n}(K^sep) the Tate twist (R01.1/tate-twist), on which G_K acts through χ_ℓ = cyclotomicCharacter K̄ ℓ. From A3's perfect Weil pairings e_{ℓ^n} : A[ℓ^n] × A^∨[ℓ^n] → μ_{ℓ^n}, which satisfy e_{ℓ^{n+1}}(a, a′)^ℓ = e_{ℓ^n}(ℓa, ℓa′), define e_ℓ : T_ℓA × T_ℓA^∨ → Z_ℓ(1), e_ℓ((a_n), (a′_n)) := (e_{ℓ^n}(a_n, a′_n))_n. Then e_ℓ is Z_ℓ-bilinear, perfect (it induces an isomorphism T_ℓA^∨ ≅ Hom_{Z_ℓ}(T_ℓA, Z_ℓ(1)) = (T_ℓA)^∨(1) of continuous representations, R01.1/restriction-dual-tensor-twist) and Galois-equivariant: e_ℓ(σx, σy) = χ_ℓ(σ)·e_ℓ(x, y) for σ ∈ G_K, writing Z_ℓ(1) additively. For a homomorphism λ : A → A^∨ put e^λ_ℓ(x, y) := e_ℓ(x, T_ℓλ(y)). Properties: (i) adjunction e_ℓ(x, T_ℓα^∨(y)) = e_ℓ(T_ℓα(x), y) for α : A → B, x ∈ T_ℓA, y ∈ T_ℓB^∨; (ii) if λ = φ_L for a line bundle L (in particular if λ is a polarization), e^λ_ℓ is alternating; (iii) for a polarization λ of degree d, e^λ_ℓ ⊗ Q_ℓ is nondegenerate, and e^λ_ℓ is perfect over Z_ℓ iff ℓ ∤ d (always when λ is principal); (iv) for α ∈ End(A) ⊗ Q and the Rosati involution α ↦ α^† of λ, e^λ_ℓ(αx, y) = e^λ_ℓ(x, α^†y); (v) for polarizations λ, μ of A, B, e^{λ×μ}_ℓ is the orthogonal sum on T_ℓA ⊕ T_ℓB; (vi) consequently ρ_{A,ℓ}(G_K) ⊂ GSp(V_ℓA, e^λ) with similitude character (multiplier) χ_ℓ, and for principal λ, ρ_{A,ℓ}(G_K) ⊂ GSp(T_ℓA, e^λ) ≅ GSp_{2g}(Z_ℓ) after a symplectic basis. Reducing mod ℓ^n recovers A3's pairings e_{ℓ^n} and e^λ_{ℓ^n}.

**Hypotheses.**

- ℓ ≠ char K
- polarizations and the dual abelian variety are imported (A3 for the pairings; Tau Ceti JacobianChallenge layer E and AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A2 for A^∨ and φ_L)
- the target keeps the Tate twist Z_ℓ(1); it is never identified with Z_ℓ without a chosen compatible system of roots of unity

**Construction and proof.**

1. Compatibility of levels: e_{ℓ^{n+1}}(a, a′)^ℓ = e_{ℓ^n}(ℓa, ℓa′) (Milne AV Lemma 13.1, p. 57; A3 for the scheme-theoretic pairing), so the sequence (e_{ℓ^n}(a_n, a′_n)) is an element of lim μ_{ℓ^n} = Z_ℓ(1).
2. Perfectness: each e_{ℓ^n} is perfect (A3, Cartier duality A^∨[n] = A[n]^D), and a compatible system of perfect pairings of free Z/ℓ^n-modules of rank 2g gives a perfect pairing of the limits.
3. Galois equivariance: A3's pairing is a morphism of K-group schemes, so e_{ℓ^n}(σa, σa′) = σ(e_{ℓ^n}(a, a′)) = e_{ℓ^n}(a, a′)^{χ_ℓ(σ) mod ℓ^n} by Mathlib cyclotomicCharacter.spec.
4. (i), (ii), (iv): Milne AV Proposition 13.2 (a)–(d), p. 58; (iv) follows from (i) and the definition α^† = λ^{−1}α^∨λ.
5. (iii): ker(T_ℓλ ⊗ Q_ℓ) = 0 because λ is an isogeny (node functoriality-products-and-isogenies (c)); over Z_ℓ the discriminant of e^λ_ℓ is #coker T_ℓλ = d_ℓ.
6. (vi): from equivariance, e^λ_ℓ(σx, σy) = χ_ℓ(σ) e^λ_ℓ(x, y), which is the definition of a similitude with multiplier χ_ℓ(σ).

**Prerequisites.** `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6/tate-module-of-an-abelian-variety`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6/functoriality-products-and-isogenies`; `AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A3`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/tate-twist`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/restriction-dual-tensor-twist`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/JacobianChallenge#layer-e-abelian-varieties`; `mathlib:cyclotomicCharacter`; `mathlib:cyclotomicCharacter.spec`; `mathlib:rootsOfUnity`.

- AbelianVarietiesIsogenousToNoJacobian:G0/universal-open-monodromy: openness in Sp_{2g}(Z_p) plus the similitude character gives openness in GSp_{2g}(Z_p)
- PadicHodgeTheory:R06.5/weil-pairing-duality: V_p(A^∨) ≅ V_p(A)^∨(1) from the perfect Galois-equivariant Weil pairing
- MordellLawrenceVenkatesh:LV.1/abelian-variety-cohomology-properties: (d) a polarization induces a perfect alternating pairing ρ_A × ρ_A → Q_p(−1) on H¹ = V_p(A)^∨

**API.**

- `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.weilPairing` (constructor): e_ℓ : T_ℓA →ₗ[Z_ℓ] T_ℓA^∨ →ₗ[Z_ℓ] Z_ℓ(1), the limit of A3's e_{ℓ^n}.
- `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.weilPairing_mod_pow` (compatibility): e_ℓ reduces mod ℓ^n to A3's e_{ℓ^n} on A[ℓ^n](K^sep) × A^∨[ℓ^n](K^sep).
- `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.weilPairing_perfect` (equivalence): T_ℓA^∨ ≅ (T_ℓA)^∨(1) as continuous Z_ℓ[G_K]-modules via y ↦ e_ℓ(·, y).
- `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.weilPairing_galois` (relation): e_ℓ(σx, σy) = χ_ℓ(σ)·e_ℓ(x, y).
- `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.weilPairing_map_dual` (relation): e_ℓ(x, T_ℓα^∨ y) = e_ℓ(T_ℓα x, y) for α : A → B.
- `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.polarizationPairing` (constructor): e^λ_ℓ(x, y) := e_ℓ(x, T_ℓλ y) for λ : A → A^∨.
- `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.polarizationPairing_alternating` (relation): e^{φ_L}_ℓ(x, x) = 0 for every line bundle L; hence e^λ_ℓ is alternating for a polarization λ.
- `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.polarizationPairing_perfect_iff` (characterisation): For a polarization λ of degree d, e^λ_ℓ is perfect over Z_ℓ iff ℓ ∤ d; it is nondegenerate over Q_ℓ always.
- `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.polarizationPairing_rosati` (relation): e^λ_ℓ(αx, y) = e^λ_ℓ(x, α^† y) for α ∈ End(A) ⊗ Q (when the right side is integral) and the Rosati involution †.
- `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.polarizationPairing_prod` (compatibility): e^{λ×μ}_ℓ on T_ℓ(A × B) = T_ℓA ⊕ T_ℓB is e^λ_ℓ ⊥ e^μ_ℓ.
- `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.image_le_GSp` (structure): ρ_{A,ℓ}(G_K) ⊆ GSp(V_ℓA, e^λ_ℓ) with multiplier χ_ℓ; for principal λ, ⊆ GSp(T_ℓA, e^λ_ℓ).
- `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.weilPairing_compare_elliptic` (compatibility): For an elliptic Weierstrass curve, e^{λ_E}_{ℓ^n} agrees with Tau Ceti's e_{ℓ^n} up to inversion (node elliptic-tate-module-comparison).

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.weilPairing_galois` (characterisation): For σ ∈ G_K, x ∈ T_ℓA, y ∈ T_ℓA^∨: e_ℓ(σx, σy) = χ_ℓ(σ)·e_ℓ(x, y) in Z_ℓ(1).
- `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.polarizationPairing_elliptic_det` (computation): For an elliptic curve E with its canonical principal polarization and any basis (P, Q) of T_ℓE, e_ℓ(P, Q) generates Z_ℓ(1) and det ρ_{E,ℓ}(σ) = χ_ℓ(σ) for all σ ∈ G_K.
- `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.polarizationPairing_zero_dim` (degenerate): For A = 0 the pairings are the zero pairing on the zero module (perfect).
- `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.polarizationPairing_not_perfect` (non-example): For E an elliptic curve and λ = [ℓ]∘λ_E, e^λ_ℓ = ℓ·e_ℓ is not perfect over Z_ℓ; a definition demanding perfectness for every polarization is wrong.
- `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.weilPairing_target_twist` (non-example): The pairing is not Galois-invariant with values in Z_ℓ: for complex conjugation c on Q̄ ⊂ C, e_ℓ(cx, cy) = −e_ℓ(x, y) ≠ e_ℓ(x, y) whenever e_ℓ(x, y) ≠ 0, because χ_ℓ(c) = −1.

**Acceptance.**

- χ_ℓ example: for an elliptic curve, the polarization pairing e_ℓ : T_ℓE × T_ℓE → Z_ℓ(1) is perfect alternating, so ∧²T_ℓE ≅ Z_ℓ(1) and det ρ_{E,ℓ} = χ_ℓ (Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 2's determinant theorem).
- For E : y² = x³ − x over Q and ℓ = 2, the mod-2 pairing on E[2] = {O, P_1, P_2, P_3} takes the value −1 on every pair of distinct nonzero points and 1 on the diagonal: it is alternating and nondegenerate on (Z/2)².
- For a polarization λ = [ℓ]∘λ_0 (λ_0 principal), e^λ_ℓ = ℓ·e^{λ_0}_ℓ is nondegenerate over Q_ℓ but not perfect over Z_ℓ (discriminant divisible by ℓ^{2g}).

**Sources.**

- milne-av, Ch. I, §13, p. 57: “Again, it is nondegenerate, and it commutes with the action of” — e_m : A_m × A^∨_m → μ_m is nondegenerate and Galois-equivariant.
- milne-av, Ch. I, §13, Lemma 13.1 and the definition of e_ℓ, pp. 57–58: “T` A_ ! Z` .1/ by the rule17” — The ℓ-adic pairing into Z_ℓ(1) from the compatible finite pairings.
- milne-av, Ch. I, Proposition 13.2(d), p. 58: “skew-symmetric.” — e^L_ℓ is skew-symmetric (alternating), and L ↦ e^L_ℓ is a homomorphism to Hom(∧²T_ℓA, Z_ℓ(1)).
- ddt-fermat, §2.2, proof of Proposition 2.8, p. 55: “Part (a) follows from the existence of the non-degenerate alternating” — det ρ_{E,ℓ} = ε from the alternating Galois-equivariant Weil pairing T_ℓE × T_ℓE → Z_ℓ(1).

#### Determinant of the Tate module and oddness over real places

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6/determinant-and-oddness`. Kind: theorem. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/TateModule/Theorems`). Planet: **Oddness of Tate modules**. Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6`.

Throughout: K is a field, K̄ = AlgebraicClosure K with separable closure K^sep ⊆ K̄, and G_K = Field.absoluteGaloisGroup K = Aut(K̄/K) with its Krull topology (restriction identifies it with Gal(K^sep/K)); σ ∈ G_K acts on a point x ∈ A(K̄) by acting on its coordinates (for a Weierstrass curve this is Mathlib's WeierstrassCurve.Affine.Point.map along σ). A is an abelian variety over K in Tau Ceti's sense (TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety: proper geometrically integral group scheme over Spec K) of dimension g, and ℓ is a prime number with ℓ ≠ char K. Let λ be a polarization of A (abelian varieties over a field are projective, so one exists). (a) det_{Q_ℓ} ρ_{V_ℓA} = χ_ℓ^g, and if ℓ ∤ deg λ (e.g. λ principal) ∧^{2g}_{Z_ℓ} T_ℓA ≅ Z_ℓ(g), i.e. det_{Z_ℓ} ρ_{A,ℓ} = χ_ℓ^g. (b) For an elliptic curve E: ∧²T_ℓE ≅ Z_ℓ(1), det ρ_{E,ℓ} = χ_ℓ, and det ρ̄_{E,ℓ} = χ̄_ℓ = modularCyclotomicCharacter (the mod-ℓ cyclotomic character) on E[ℓ](K^sep). (c) Oddness: suppose ι : K → R is a real place, extend ι to K̄ → C, and let c ∈ G_K be the induced complex conjugation (c² = 1, χ_ℓ(c) = −1). Then for every prime ℓ (including ℓ = 2) the ±1-eigenspaces V^± of ρ_{V_ℓA}(c) are Lagrangian for e^λ_ℓ ⊗ Q_ℓ, both of dimension g; hence tr ρ_{V_ℓA}(c) = 0 and det ρ_{V_ℓA}(c) = (−1)^g. For an elliptic curve, det ρ_{E,ℓ}(c) = −1, i.e. ρ_{E,ℓ} is odd in the roadmap's convention (det ρ(c) = −1 at every real place; the definition is stated in stage R01.4, which may cite this node as its instance), and for ℓ odd ρ̄_{E,ℓ}(c) is conjugate to diag(1, −1). For ℓ = 2, det ρ̄_{E,2}(c) = 1 = −1 holds automatically and ρ̄_{E,2}(c) may be trivial. (d) Over a number field K, det ρ_{E,ℓ}(Frob_v) = q_v for every place v ∤ ℓ at which ρ_{E,ℓ} is unramified (R01.2/cyclotomic-and-dirichlet-characters: χ_ℓ(arithmetic Frob_v) = q_v).

**Hypotheses.**

- ℓ ≠ char K
- in (c), K has a real place and c is a complex conjugation attached to it; oddness is a statement about every such c
- in (a) the integral statement needs ℓ ∤ deg λ; the rational one holds for every polarization

**Construction and proof.**

1. (a) By node weil-pairing-on-tate-modules (vi), ρ(σ) is a similitude of the nondegenerate alternating form e^λ_ℓ with multiplier χ_ℓ(σ); for a symplectic similitude h of multiplier μ on a 2g-dimensional space, det h = μ^g (det h² = μ^{2g} from h^t J h = μJ, and the sign is fixed by the Pfaffian: Pf(h^t J h) = det h · Pf J). Integrally, when e^λ_ℓ is perfect, the Pfaffian of a symplectic basis identifies ∧^{2g}T_ℓA with Z_ℓ(g).
2. (b) is (a) for g = 1 with the canonical principal polarization; reduction mod ℓ gives det ρ̄ = χ̄_ℓ (Mathlib cyclotomicCharacter.toZModPow relates χ_ℓ mod ℓ to modularCyclotomicCharacter). Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 2 states the same determinant theorem for its T_ℓW (node elliptic-tate-module-comparison).
3. (c) c acts on roots of unity by inversion, so χ_ℓ(c) = −1 (Mathlib cyclotomicCharacter.spec). For x, y ∈ V^+: e(x, y) = e(cx, cy) = χ_ℓ(c)e(x, y) = −e(x, y), so 2e(x, y) = 0 and e(x, y) = 0 since Q_ℓ(1) is torsion-free; likewise for V^−. Since c² = 1 and char Q_ℓ = 0, V = V^+ ⊕ V^−; two isotropic subspaces of a 2g-dimensional nondegenerate alternating space have dimension ≤ g, so both are Lagrangian of dimension g. Hence tr = g − g = 0 and det = (−1)^g. For ℓ odd the same argument works on E[ℓ] over F_ℓ (2 is invertible), giving eigenvalues 1, −1.
4. ℓ = 2 caveat: over F_2, −1 = 1 and the argument shows nothing; for y² = x³ − x every 2-torsion point is real, so ρ̄_{E,2}(c) = 1.
5. (d) is (b) evaluated at a Frobenius element, using R01.2/frobenius-characteristic-polynomial (well defined at unramified places).

**Prerequisites.** `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6/weil-pairing-on-tate-modules`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6/tate-module-of-an-abelian-variety`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/tate-twist`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/cyclotomic-and-dirichlet-characters`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/frobenius-characteristic-polynomial`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/EllipticCurves#layer-2-torsion-the-weil-pairing-and-the-tate-module-aec-iii68`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/JacobianChallenge#layer-e-abelian-varieties`; `mathlib:cyclotomicCharacter`; `mathlib:cyclotomicCharacter.spec`; `mathlib:modularCyclotomicCharacter`; `mathlib:LinearMap.det`.

**Acceptance.**

- E/Q any elliptic curve: Milne EC, p. 224, the Weil pairing gives ∧²E_ℓ ≅ μ_ℓ and the representation on E_ℓ is odd (det ρ̄(c) = −1).
- For E : y² = x³ − x and ℓ = 2, ρ̄_{E,2}(c) = 1 although det ρ_{E,2}(c) = −1 in Z_2^×: oddness of ρ_{E,2} is a statement in characteristic 0, and the residual condition ρ̄(c) ≠ 1 is a separate hypothesis.
- For A = E_1 × E_2 over Q, det ρ_{V_ℓA}(c) = (−1)² = 1 and tr ρ_{V_ℓA}(c) = 0: the correct dimension-general oddness statement is tr(c) = 0 (eigenvalues ±1 each with multiplicity g), not det(c) = −1.
- Serre 1972, §5.2, p. 304: φ_ℓ(G) contains the element c with eigenvalues {1, −1} given by complex conjugation, so for ℓ ≠ 2 the image is never contained in a non-split Cartan subgroup.

**Sources.**

- milne-ec, Ch. V, §8, p. 224: “shows that the representation of GS on E` is odd.” — Oddness of E[ℓ] over Q from the Weil pairing ∧²E_ℓ ≅ μ_ℓ and c acting by inversion on μ_ℓ.
- ddt-fermat, §2.2, Proposition 2.8(a), p. 55: “Part (a) follows from the existence of the non-degenerate alternating” — det ρ_{E,ℓ} = ε_ℓ (the cyclotomic character) from the Weil pairing.
- serre72-proprietes, §5.2, remark (on complex conjugation), printed p. 304 (GDZ OCR page 00000312): “celui fourni par la conjugaison complexe” — The image of G_Q in Aut(E_ℓ) contains the element c with eigenvalues {1, −1} given by complex conjugation.

#### Unramifiedness and the Frobenius polynomial at a place of good reduction

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6/good-reduction-frobenius-polynomial`. Kind: theorem. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/TateModule/Theorems`). Planet: **Good-reduction Frobenius polynomial**. Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6`.

Let F be a number field, v a finite place of F with completion F_v (Tau Ceti NumberFieldArithmetic Layer 5), valuation ring O_v, residue field k_v = F_{q_v} of characteristic p, and fix a decomposition group D_w ⊆ G_F and inertia I_w at a place w | v of F̄ (R01.2/decomposition-group-at-a-place). Let A be an abelian variety of dimension g over F with good reduction at v: A_{F_v} is the generic fibre of an abelian scheme 𝒜 over O_v, with special fibre A_v := 𝒜 ⊗ k_v. Let π_v ∈ End(A_v) be the q_v-Frobenius endomorphism (raising coordinates to the q_v-th power) and ℓ ≠ p. Then: (a) V_ℓA is unramified at v (R01.2/unramified-and-ramification-set): I_w acts trivially on T_ℓA. (b) Reduction 𝒜[ℓ^n](O_v^{sh}) gives a D_w-equivariant isomorphism r : T_ℓA ≅ T_ℓA_v, where D_w acts on the right through D_w → Gal(k̄_v/k_v). (c) Every arithmetic Frobenius Frob_w ∈ D_w (lifting x ↦ x^{q_v}) acts on T_ℓA as r^{−1} ∘ T_ℓ(π_v) ∘ r; a geometric Frobenius acts as the inverse. (d) Hence the Frobenius characteristic polynomial P_v(V_ℓA, X) := det(X − ρ_{A,ℓ}(Frob_w) | V_ℓA) of R01.2/frobenius-characteristic-polynomial equals det(X − V_ℓπ_v | V_ℓA_v), depends only on v (not on w or the Frobenius lift), and has constant term q_v^g and the functional equation X^{2g}P_v(q_v/X) = q_v^g P_v(X) (from the Weil pairing). (e) For elliptic curves (g = 1, A = E_W for a Weierstrass W whose minimal model over O_v has Mathlib WeierstrassCurve.HasGoodReduction): P_v(X) = X² − a_v X + q_v with a_v = WeierstrassCurve.frobeniusTrace of the reduction = q_v + 1 − #Ẽ(k_v) ∈ Z, independent of ℓ ≠ p. (f) For general g, P_v(X) is the characteristic polynomial P_{π_v} of the endomorphism π_v in the sense of AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A6: monic of degree 2g in Z[X] and independent of ℓ ≠ p — this integrality and ℓ-independence is imported (gap: owner A6 is currently downstream of this stage). Convention: with H¹ := V_ℓA^∨, det(1 − T·Φ_w | H¹) = det(1 − T·Frob_w | V_ℓA) = T^{2g}P_v(1/T) for a geometric Frobenius Φ_w (the roadmap's convention), whereas det(1 − T·Φ_w | V_ℓA) = Q_v(T/q_v) with Q_v(T) := T^{2g}P_v(1/T) (by the functional equation in (d)); the latter is not the Euler factor.

**Hypotheses.**

- ℓ ≠ p = char k_v (for ℓ = p the representation is in general ramified even with good reduction: PadicHodgeTheory R06.6 treats it)
- good reduction means existence of an abelian scheme model over O_v; for elliptic curves this is Mathlib's HasGoodReduction of the minimal model
- the conductor comparison (Ogg) is not stated here: it is ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.3, which imports this stage
- the converse (unramified ⇒ good reduction, Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich) is NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties R11.5, which consumes this stage, and Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 4 for elliptic curves

**Construction and proof.**

1. (a),(b): by A3 applied over the base O_v, 𝒜[ℓ^n] is finite étale over O_v (ℓ^n invertible). A finite étale scheme over the henselian O_v^{sh} (strict henselisation, residue field k̄_v) has all its geometric generic points defined over F_v^{ur} and they reduce bijectively to k̄_v-points (Milne AV Ch. IV, proof of Theorem 3.5, p. 141: A(K_v^un)_{ℓ^n} = A_0(k^al)_{ℓ^n} has ℓ^{2n dim A} elements); hence I_w acts trivially and reduction is a D_w-isomorphism, compatible with [ℓ] and so with limits.
2. (c): for x ∈ A_v(k̄_v), the arithmetic Frobenius of Gal(k̄_v/k_v) raises coordinates to the q_v-th power, which is π_v(x) (Milne AV Ch. II, §1, p. 75, the Frobenius map on points; Ch. IV, p. 142: 'Frob_w acts on V_ℓA as π'); transport by r.
3. (d): conjugate Frobenius lifts differ by elements of I_w (trivial action) and conjugation in G_F, so the characteristic polynomial depends only on v (R01.2/frobenius-characteristic-polynomial). The constant term: det ρ(Frob_w) = χ_ℓ(Frob_w)^g = q_v^g (node determinant-and-oddness (a) and R01.2/cyclotomic-and-dirichlet-characters). The functional equation: ρ(Frob_w) is a similitude of multiplier q_v for e^λ_ℓ, so its eigenvalues are stable under α ↦ q_v/α with multiplicities.
4. (e): for g = 1: det(V_ℓπ_v) = q_v by (d). Trace: det(1 − V_ℓπ_v) = deg(1 − π_v) because det(V_ℓβ) = deg β for β ∈ End(E) (Weil pairing: e(βx, βy) = e(x, β̂βy) = deg β · e(x, y), Milne EC Prop. III.3.22, p. 100), and deg(1 − π_v) = pointCount of the reduction (Tau Ceti TauCeti.Isogeny.degree_oneSubFrobeniusIsogeny_eq_pointCount); so 1 − tr + q_v = #Ẽ(k_v) and tr = q_v + 1 − #Ẽ(k_v) = frobeniusTrace (Tau Ceti WeierstrassCurve.frobeniusTrace_eq_card_point; Milne EC Ch. IV, p. 150 and Ch. V Proposition 8.3, p. 224; DDT Proposition 2.11(a), p. 56). Both are integers independent of ℓ.
5. (f): P_{π_v} = det(X − V_ℓπ_v) with integer coefficients independent of ℓ is Milne AV Proposition 10.20 (p. 50), planned as AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A6/characteristic-polynomial-on-tate-module; the stage edge R01.6 → A6 currently forbids citing it (gap and restructure proposal).

**Prerequisites.** `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6/tate-module-of-an-abelian-variety`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6/functoriality-products-and-isogenies`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6/determinant-and-oddness`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6/weil-pairing-on-tate-modules`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6/elliptic-tate-module-comparison`; `AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A3`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/decomposition-group-at-a-place`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/local-restriction`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/unramified-and-ramification-set`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/frobenius-characteristic-polynomial`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/cyclotomic-and-dirichlet-characters`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/NumberFieldArithmetic#layer-5-the-global-local-dictionary-at-finite-places`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/LocalFieldsRamification#layer-2-unramified-extensions-and-frobenius`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/EllipticCurves#layer-3-elliptic-curves-over-finite-fields--the-hasse-bound-aec-v1`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/EllipticCurves#layer-4-elliptic-curves-over-local-fields--reduction-tates-algorithm-the-tate-curve-aec-vii-ataec-ivv`; `tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.frobeniusTrace`; `tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.frobeniusTrace_eq_card_point`; `tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.pointCount`; `tauceti:TauCeti.Isogeny.frobeniusIsogeny`; `tauceti:TauCeti.Isogeny.degree_frobeniusIsogeny`; `tauceti:TauCeti.Isogeny.degree_oneSubFrobeniusIsogeny_eq_pointCount`; `mathlib:WeierstrassCurve.HasGoodReduction`; `mathlib:WeierstrassCurve.reduction`; `mathlib:LinearMap.charpoly`.

**Acceptance.**

- Supersingular good reduction: E : y² = x³ + 1 over Q at p = 5 (p ≡ 2 mod 3, Δ = −432 prime to 5): #Ẽ(F_5) = 6, a_5 = 0, P_5(X) = X² + 5; likewise a_11 = a_17 = a_23 = 0 — a_p = 0 for supersingular good reduction at p ≥ 5 by the Hasse bound |a_p| ≤ 2√p and p | a_p (Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 3).
- E : y² = x³ − x over Q: a_3 = 0, a_5 = −2, a_7 = 0, a_13 = 6, so P_5(X) = X² + 2X + 5 and P_13(X) = X² − 6X + 13, the same for every ℓ ≠ p.
- Milne AV Ch. IV, p. 142: P_v(A, t) is the characteristic polynomial of Frob_w acting on V_ℓA, defined as the Frobenius polynomial of the reduction.

**Sources.**

- milne-av, Ch. IV, Theorem 3.5 and its proof, p. 141: “Then A has good reduction at v if and only if the representation of Gal.K al =K/ on V` A is” — Good reduction at v ∤ ℓ iff V_ℓA unramified; the proof of '⇒' counts A(K_v^un)_{ℓ^n}.
- milne-av, Ch. IV, after Corollary 3.6, p. 142: “, and so Pv .A; t / is the characteristic polynomial of Frobw acting on V` A. If w 0 also lies” — Frob_w acts on V_ℓA as the Frobenius endomorphism of the reduction; P_v(A, t) is its characteristic polynomial and depends only on v.
- milne-ec, Ch. V, Proposition 8.3 and proof, p. 224: “and the reduction map P 7! PN induces an isomorphism T` E ! T` Ep . By” — Reduction identifies T_ℓE with T_ℓE_p and Frobenius with the Frobenius endomorphism; tr = a_p = p + 1 − N_p.
- milne-ec, Ch. III, Proposition 3.22, p. 100: “P ROPOSITION 3.22 Let E and ` be as above. For any nonzero endomorphism” — det(α | T_ℓE) = deg α, the input for the trace computation.
- ddt-fermat, §2.2, Proposition 2.11(a), p. 56: “Proposition 2.11 Suppose E has good reduction at p.” — Unramified at p ≠ ℓ with tr ρ_{E,ℓ}(Frob_p) = p + 1 − #Ē_p(F_p), an integer independent of ℓ.

#### Comparison with Mathlib's WeierstrassCurve.localPolynomial

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6/comparison-with-weierstrass-local-polynomial`. Kind: comparison. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/TateModule/Theorems`). Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6`.

Let F be a number field, W an elliptic Weierstrass curve over F, p a height-one prime of O_F (IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum), R = p.adicCompletionIntegers F, K = p.adicCompletion F, q = #(O_F/p), and ℓ a prime not dividing q. Mathlib defines localPolynomial R (W.baseChange K) ∈ Z[X] from the minimal model W′ = (W.baseChange K).minimal R as 1 − aX + qX² with a = q + 1 − Nat.card (W′.reduction R).toAffine.Point if W′ has good reduction, 1 − X if split multiplicative, 1 + X if nonsplit multiplicative, 1 otherwise. Then: (a) if W′ has good reduction, a equals Tau Ceti's frobeniusTrace of W′.reduction R (since the reduction is elliptic, WeierstrassCurve.pointCount_eq_card_point), and localPolynomial R (W.baseChange K) = det(1 − X·Frob_v | V_ℓE) = det(1 − X·Φ_v | V_ℓE^∨) = L_v(V_ℓE^∨, X), the local Euler factor of R01.2/local-euler-factor of H¹ = V_ℓE^∨ (node local-euler-factor-of-an-abelian-variety), for every ℓ ∤ q; (b) if W′ has split multiplicative reduction, localPolynomial = 1 − X = det(1 − X·Φ_v | (V_ℓE^∨)^{I_v}); if nonsplit multiplicative, localPolynomial = 1 + X = det(1 − X·Φ_v | (V_ℓE^∨)^{I_v}); (c) consequently, for the places of good or multiplicative reduction, Mathlib's WeierstrassCurve.LFunction has the Euler factors of the Galois representation V_ℓE^∨. At additive places localPolynomial = 1, and the equality with det(1 − XΦ_v | (V_ℓE^∨)^{I_v}) needs (V_ℓE)^{I_v} = 0, which rests on the Néron model (connected component of the special fibre unipotent) and is NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties R11.5/local-euler-polynomial, downstream of this stage; it is not asserted here.

**Hypotheses.**

- ℓ ∤ q; the residue field is finite, so Mathlib's Nat.card junk value 0 for infinite residue fields does not occur
- the multiplicative cases use Tate's uniformisation over K (Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 4) and the theorem that an elliptic curve with split multiplicative reduction over K is K-isomorphic to a Tate curve E_q (requested from that layer)
- the variable X of localPolynomial is the variable T of det(1 − T·Φ); substituting q^{−s} gives the Dirichlet-series factor

**Construction and proof.**

1. (a) Good reduction: node good-reduction-frobenius-polynomial (e) gives det(X − Frob_v | V_ℓE) = X² − aX + q with a = frobeniusTrace(W′.reduction R); hence det(1 − X·Frob_v | V_ℓE) = 1 − aX + qX², which is Mathlib's good-reduction branch after pointCount_eq_card_point identifies Mathlib's Nat.card of the affine point type (point at infinity included) with Tau Ceti's pointCount. Transposition: geometric Frobenius on V^∨ is the transpose of arithmetic Frobenius on V, so the two determinants agree; the minimal model is used on both sides (Mathlib's localPolynomial minimises first; good reduction of the curve is HasGoodReduction of the minimal model).
2. (b) Split multiplicative: E_K ≅ E_q (Tate; ATAEC V.5.3), and the uniformisation K̄^×/q^Z ≅ E_q(K̄) gives 0 → Z_ℓ(1) → T_ℓE → Z_ℓ → 0 with inertia acting through a nontrivial unipotent (the Kummer class of q, v(q) > 0, has infinite-order image on inertia); so (V_ℓE)^{I_v} = Q_ℓ(1) and, dually, (V_ℓE^∨)^{I_v} = Q_ℓ (trivial), on which Φ_v acts by 1: the factor is 1 − X (DDT Proposition 2.12(a), p. 56). Nonsplit: E is the quadratic twist of a split curve by the unramified quadratic character δ (Tau Ceti WeierstrassCurve.quadraticTwistOf, EllipticCurves Layer 5), so Φ_v acts by δ(Φ_v) = −1: the factor is 1 + X.
3. (c) Mathlib's LFunction is the Euler product of localEulerFactor over all primes; at good and multiplicative primes the factors agree by (a), (b).

**Prerequisites.** `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6/good-reduction-frobenius-polynomial`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6/local-euler-factor-of-an-abelian-variety`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6/elliptic-tate-module-comparison`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/local-euler-factor`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/unramified-and-ramification-set`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/EllipticCurves#layer-3-elliptic-curves-over-finite-fields--the-hasse-bound-aec-v1`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/EllipticCurves#layer-4-elliptic-curves-over-local-fields--reduction-tates-algorithm-the-tate-curve-aec-vii-ataec-ivv`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/EllipticCurves#layer-5-twists-aec-x2-x5`; `mathlib:WeierstrassCurve.localPolynomial`; `mathlib:WeierstrassCurve.LFunction`; `mathlib:WeierstrassCurve.minimal`; `mathlib:WeierstrassCurve.reduction`; `mathlib:WeierstrassCurve.HasGoodReduction`; `mathlib:WeierstrassCurve.HasMultiplicativeReduction`; `mathlib:WeierstrassCurve.HasSplitMultiplicativeReduction`; `tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.pointCount_eq_card_point`; `tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.frobeniusTrace`; `tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.quadraticTwistOf`.

**Acceptance.**

- E : y² = x³ − x over Q at p = 5: localPolynomial = 1 + 2X + 5X² = det(1 − X·Frob_5 | V_ℓE) for every ℓ ≠ 5 (a_5 = −2).
- E = 11a3 : y² + y = x³ − x² at p = 11 (Δ = −11, c₄ = 16 a unit): split multiplicative with frobeniusTrace = 1 under Tau Ceti's all-points count, and localPolynomial = 1 − X = det(1 − X·Φ_11 | (V_ℓE^∨)^{I_11}).
- Pitfall check: det(1 − X·Φ_5 | V_ℓE) = 1 + (2/5)X + (1/5)X² ≠ localPolynomial for y² = x³ − x at p = 5; the Euler factor uses H¹ = V_ℓE^∨ (equivalently the arithmetic Frobenius on V_ℓE).

**Sources.**

- ddt-fermat, §2.2, Proposition 2.12, p. 56: “Proposition 2.12 Suppose that E has multiplicative reduction at p. Let q =” — ρ_{E,ℓ}|G_p ≅ (ε *; 0 1) ⊗ δ with δ trivial (split) or the unramified quadratic character (nonsplit).
- ddt-fermat, Introduction, §1 (the L-series of E), p. 18: “(1 − ap p−s + p1−2s )−1 = 1 + ap p−s + ap2 p−2s + ap3 p−3s + · · · .” — The good-reduction Euler factor 1 − a_p p^{−s} + p^{1−2s}, i.e. 1 − a_pT + pT² at T = p^{−s}.
- milne-ec, Ch. V, Proposition 8.3, p. 224: “the same action on T` E. Therefore the proposition follows from (7.5).” — tr ρ_ℓ(F_p) = a_p = p + 1 − N_p for p of good reduction.

#### The local Euler factor of an abelian variety at a finite place

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6/local-euler-factor-of-an-abelian-variety`. Kind: construction. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/TateModule/EulerFactor`). Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6`.

Let F_v be a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_{q_v} of characteristic p (or a number field F with a finite place v, through R01.2/local-restriction), A an abelian variety over F_v of dimension g, and ℓ ≠ p. Put H¹_ℓ(A) := V_ℓA^∨ = Hom_{Q_ℓ}(V_ℓA, Q_ℓ) with the dual action (R01.1/restriction-dual-tensor-twist). Define L_v(A, T) := det(1 − T·Φ_v | H¹_ℓ(A)^{I_v}) ∈ Q_ℓ[T], Φ_v a geometric Frobenius (R01.2/local-euler-factor applied to the ℓ-adic representation H¹_ℓ(A), equivalently to its Weil–Deligne representation through R01.2/grothendieck-monodromy-and-the-weil-deligne-functor, where (ker N)^{I_v} = H¹_ℓ(A)^{I_v}). Equivalently L_v(A, T) = det(1 − T·Frob_v | (V_ℓA)_{I_v}) with the arithmetic Frobenius on inertia coinvariants. Properties: (a) well defined: independent of the choice of Φ_v and of the decomposition group; (b) at a place of good reduction (ℓ ≠ p), L_v(A, T) = T^{2g}P_v(1/T) = det(1 − T·π_v | V_ℓA_v) with P_v of node good-reduction-frobenius-polynomial; for elliptic curves it lies in Z[T] and is independent of ℓ, for general g likewise once the A6 input of that node is available; (c) isogeny invariance: if A and B are F_v-isogenous then L_v(A, T) = L_v(B, T); (d) multiplicativity: L_v(A × B, T) = L_v(A, T)L_v(B, T); (e) degree ≤ 2g, with equality iff V_ℓA is unramified. For a number field F, the partial L-function of A outside a finite set S ⊇ {bad places} is the formal Euler product ∏_{v ∉ S} L_v(A, q_v^{−s})^{−1}. Independence of ℓ at places of bad reduction, and integrality there, are not asserted: they are NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties R11.5 (semistable reduction and the Néron model), which consumes this stage.

**Hypotheses.**

- ℓ ≠ p
- the definition is a priori ℓ-dependent at bad places
- Φ_v geometric; the arithmetic version uses coinvariants of V_ℓA

**Construction and proof.**

1. Definition: R01.2/local-euler-factor gives det(1 − T·r(Φ_v) | (ker N)^{I_v}) for a Weil–Deligne representation and, for an ℓ-adic representation with ℓ ≠ p, the Grothendieck monodromy functor identifies (ker N)^{I_v} with the inertia invariants (R01.2/grothendieck-monodromy-and-the-weil-deligne-functor).
2. Coinvariant form: (V^∨)^{I} = ((V)_{I})^∨ and the geometric Frobenius acting on V^∨ by f ↦ f ∘ Φ_v^{−1} is the transpose of the arithmetic Frobenius on V, so the determinants agree.
3. (b): V_ℓA is unramified (node good-reduction-frobenius-polynomial (a)), so the invariants are all of H¹ and det(1 − TΦ_v | V^∨) = det(1 − T Frob_v | V) = T^{2g}P_v(1/T).
4. (c): an isogeny induces an isomorphism V_ℓA ≅ V_ℓB of Q_ℓ[G_{F_v}]-modules (node functoriality-products-and-isogenies (c)); (d): node functoriality (b); (e): dim H¹^{I} ≤ 2g with equality iff I acts trivially on V^∨, i.e. on V.

**Prerequisites.** `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6/tate-module-of-an-abelian-variety`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6/good-reduction-frobenius-polynomial`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6/functoriality-products-and-isogenies`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/restriction-dual-tensor-twist`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/local-euler-factor`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/local-restriction`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/grothendieck-monodromy-and-the-weil-deligne-functor`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/unramified-and-ramification-set`.

**Uses.**

- NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties:R11.5/local-euler-polynomial: full-monodromy local Euler polynomial det(1 − TF | H¹^I) with H¹ = H¹_et(A, Q_ℓ) and geometric Frobenius
- FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems:R28.4/isogeny-criterion-by-rational-tate-modules-and-local-factors: equality of local L-factors at almost all places in Korollar 2
- EllipticCurveModularity:R29.6/newform-from-a-modular-quotient: Euler factors of E compared with those of a newform, at good and bad primes
- AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations:R19.4/conductor-and-local-factors-classical: the local Euler factor det(1 − X Frob | V^{I}) of the λ-adic representation
- MordellLawrenceVenkatesh:LV.1/abelian-variety-cohomology-properties: characteristic polynomial of geometric Frobenius on H¹ = V_p(A)^∨ at good places

**API.**

- `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.firstCohomologyRep` (constructor): H¹_ℓ(A) := V_ℓA^∨ as a continuous Q_ℓ-representation of G_K (dual, R01.1).
- `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.localEulerFactor` (constructor): L_v(A, T) := det(1 − T·Φ_v | H¹_ℓ(A)^{I_v}) ∈ Q_ℓ[T].
- `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.localEulerFactor_eq_coinvariants` (characterisation): L_v(A, T) = det(1 − T·Frob_v | (V_ℓA)_{I_v}) with the arithmetic Frobenius.
- `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.localEulerFactor_of_goodReduction` (simp): At good reduction, L_v(A, T) = T^{2g}P_v(1/T) = det(1 − T·π_v | V_ℓA_v).
- `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.localEulerFactor_isogeny` (relation): Isogenous abelian varieties have the same local Euler factors.
- `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.localEulerFactor_prod` (relation): L_v(A × B, T) = L_v(A, T)·L_v(B, T).
- `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.localEulerFactor_natDegree_le` (other): deg L_v(A, T) ≤ 2g, with equality iff V_ℓA is unramified at v.
- `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.localEulerFactor_eq_weilDeligne` (compatibility): L_v(A, T) equals R01.2's local Euler factor of the Weil–Deligne representation WD(H¹_ℓ(A)).

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.localEulerFactor_goodReduction` (computation): For E : y² = x³ − x over Q and v = 5, localEulerFactor E 5 = 1 + 2T + 5T² for every ℓ ≠ 5.
- `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.localEulerFactor_zero` (degenerate): For A = 0, L_v(A, T) = 1.
- `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.localEulerFactor_compare_localPolynomial` (compatibility): For an elliptic Weierstrass curve W over a number field with good or multiplicative reduction at p, localEulerFactor (E_W) p = WeierstrassCurve.localPolynomial (p.adicCompletionIntegers F) (W.baseChange (p.adicCompletion F)) under Z[T] ⊂ Q_ℓ[T].
- `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.localEulerFactor_not_on_V` (non-example): Using V_ℓA with the geometric Frobenius instead of H¹ = V_ℓA^∨ gives det(1 − TΦ_5 | V_ℓE) = 1 + (2/5)T + (1/5)T² for y² = x³ − x at 5, which is not the Euler factor (not in Z[T]).
- `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.localEulerFactor_tate_curve` (computation): For a Tate curve E_q over Q_p (split multiplicative), L_p(E_q, T) = 1 − T: the inertia invariants of H¹ are one-dimensional with trivial Frobenius.

**Acceptance.**

- Elliptic curves: L_v(E, T) agrees with Mathlib's localPolynomial at good and multiplicative places (node comparison-with-weierstrass-local-polynomial).
- For E : y² = x³ − x over Q, L_5(E, T) = 1 + 2T + 5T² and L_13(E, T) = 1 − 6T + 13T².
- Faltings' L-series (FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems:R28.4/isogeny-criterion-by-rational-tate-modules-and-local-factors) uses det(1 − (Nv)^{−s} F_v | T_l(A)) at good places with F_v the arithmetic Frobenius: this is L_v(A, (Nv)^{−s}) by the coinvariant form.

**Sources.**

- milne-av, Ch. IV, after Corollary 3.6, p. 142: “Pv .A; t/ D P .A.v/; t/:” — The Frobenius polynomial at a good place defined from the reduction, which the Euler factor reverses.
- ddt-fermat, §1.7, the L-series of A_f, p. 45: “L(Af /Fp , s) = det(1 − F p−s )−1 ,” — Local L-factor as det(1 − F p^{−s})^{−1} with F the Frobenius endomorphism acting on the Tate module.

#### Tate modules with endomorphism coefficients and their λ-adic components

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6/tate-module-with-endomorphism-coefficients`. Kind: construction. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/TateModule/Coefficients`). Planet: **λ-adic Tate module**. Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6`.

Throughout: K is a field, K̄ = AlgebraicClosure K with separable closure K^sep ⊆ K̄, and G_K = Field.absoluteGaloisGroup K = Aut(K̄/K) with its Krull topology (restriction identifies it with Gal(K^sep/K)); σ ∈ G_K acts on a point x ∈ A(K̄) by acting on its coordinates (for a Weierstrass curve this is Mathlib's WeierstrassCurve.Affine.Point.map along σ). A is an abelian variety over K in Tau Ceti's sense (TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety: proper geometrically integral group scheme over Spec K) of dimension g, and ℓ is a prime number with ℓ ≠ char K. Let E ⊆ End⁰_K(A) := End_K(A) ⊗ Q be a number field (a Q-subalgebra that is a field, same unit) of degree d, and O := E ∩ End_K(A) its order. (a) O ⊗ Z_ℓ acts on T_ℓA and E ⊗ Q_ℓ on V_ℓA through node functoriality-products-and-isogenies (a), commuting with ρ_{A,ℓ}(G_K) because the endomorphisms are defined over K. (b) E ⊗_Q Q_ℓ = ∏_{λ|ℓ} E_λ via the idempotents e_λ, so V_ℓA = ⊕_{λ|ℓ} V_λA with V_λA := V_ℓA ⊗_{E⊗Q_ℓ} E_λ = e_λV_ℓA, each a continuous E_λ-linear representation ρ_{A,λ} : G_K → Aut_{E_λ}(V_λA) (R01.1/continuous-representation over the coefficient field E_λ). (c) If V_ℓA is free over E ⊗ Q_ℓ (true with rank 2g/d: Milne AV Prop. 10.23, planned as AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A6/trace-and-degree-on-a-subfield — imported, gap), each V_λA has E_λ-dimension 2g/d; GL₂-type (d = g): dim 2; CM type (d = 2g): dim 1. (d) If O_E ⊆ End_K(A), T_λA := T_ℓA ⊗_{O_E⊗Z_ℓ} O_{E,λ} is a G_K-stable O_{E,λ}-lattice in V_λA and its reduction T_λA/λT_λA is the λ-torsion A[λ](K^sep) := {x ∈ A[ℓ](K^sep) : αx = 0 for all α ∈ λ}, a G_K-module over O_E/λ (the residual λ-adic representation); freeness of T_ℓA over O_E ⊗ Z_ℓ is not asserted in general (it holds for ℓ prime to the index of the endomorphism order, e.g. Serre–Tate). (e) Determinant and oddness of λ-components: if E is totally real and the Rosati involution of a polarization λ_0 is the identity on E, then e^{λ_0}_ℓ is E-balanced (e(αx, y) = e(x, αy)), V_λA ⊥ V_λ′A for λ ≠ λ′, each V_λA carries a nondegenerate E_λ-bilinear alternating form with similitude character χ_ℓ, so for GL₂-type det_{E_λ}ρ_{A,λ} = χ_ℓ, and at a real place each V_λA is odd: det_{E_λ}ρ_{A,λ}(c) = −1. For a CM field E the determinant is εχ_ℓ with ε of finite order (Ribet 1992, Lemma 3.1); that refinement uses Hodge–Tate theory and is not asserted here. (f) Frobenius: at a good place v ∤ ℓ, ρ_{A,λ}(Frob_v) is the E_λ-linear map induced by π_v, which commutes with E acting on A_v; its E_λ-characteristic polynomial is the image of the E-characteristic polynomial of π_v ∈ End⁰(A_v) (imported with (c)). (g) Over a smaller field: if the endomorphisms are defined only over a finite Galois extension L/K, V_ℓA is an E ⊗ Q_ℓ[G_L]-module and G_K acts semilinearly through Gal(L/K) → Aut(E).

**Hypotheses.**

- E ⊆ End⁰_K(A): the endomorphisms are defined over K (otherwise use (g))
- ℓ ≠ char K
- integral statements require O_E ⊆ End_K(A)

**Construction and proof.**

1. (a) Functoriality of T_ℓ in endomorphisms (node functoriality-products-and-isogenies (a)), extended Q_ℓ-linearly; Galois commutation because α ∈ End_K(A) commutes with the coordinate action of G_K.
2. (b) Chinese remainder decomposition E ⊗ Q_ℓ = ∏ E_λ; each summand e_λV_ℓA is G_K-stable because e_λ commutes with ρ.
3. (c) Rank: V_ℓA is free over E ⊗ Q_ℓ of rank 2g/d (Milne AV Prop. 10.23; Ribet 1992, §2 for GL₂-type: 'free of rank two over E ⊗ Q_ℓ').
4. (e) For α ∈ E, α^† = α gives e(αx, y) = e(x, αy) (node weil-pairing-on-tate-modules (iv)); then e(e_λx, e_λ′y) = e(x, e_λe_λ′y) = 0 for λ ≠ λ′. A Q_ℓ-bilinear E-balanced alternating form on V_λ is Tr_{E_λ/Q_ℓ} of a unique E_λ-bilinear alternating form, nondegenerate since e is; the similitude property passes to it; for a 2-dimensional symplectic space det = multiplier. Oddness: the argument of node determinant-and-oddness (c) applied inside each V_λ (c commutes with E) gives V_λ^± isotropic of E_λ-dimension 1.
5. (d) λ-torsion: T_λA/λT_λA = (T_ℓA/ℓT_ℓA) ⊗_{O_E/ℓ} O_E/λ = A[ℓ] ⊗ O_E/λ, which is the λ-torsion by the Chinese remainder theorem for O_E/ℓ.
6. (f) node good-reduction-frobenius-polynomial (c), with π_v commuting with the reductions of the endomorphisms.

Over K = Q(i), V_ℓE is free of rank 1 over Q(i) ⊗ Q_ℓ (Serre 1972 §4.5: T_ℓ free of rank 1 over R_ℓ), so ρ_{E,ℓ}(G_{Q(i)}) ⊆ (Z[i] ⊗ Z_ℓ)^×, an abelian group, the Cartan subgroup. Over Q, complex conjugation c satisfies c·i = −i·c (semilinearity (g)), so ρ_{E,ℓ}(G_Q) lies in the normaliser of that Cartan, with ρ_{E,ℓ}(G_Q) ⊄ Cartan; for ℓ = 5 (split in Q(i)) V_5E = V_λ ⊕ V_λ̄ over Q(i), two characters of G_{Q(i)} swapped by c, so V_5E ≅ Ind_{G_{Q(i)}}^{G_Q} ψ_λ (R01.1/continuous-induction) with ψ_λ the λ-adic avatar of the Hecke character of E (owned by ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocity CM.4).
- Consistency with a_p = 0: for p ≡ 3 mod 4 (inert in Q(i)), Frob_p ∈ G_Q \ G_{Q(i)} acts by an element of the non-identity coset of the Cartan normaliser, which has trace 0 — matching a_3 = a_7 = a_11 = a_19 = a_23 = 0 computed for y² = x³ − x.
- GL₂-type: for A_f attached to a weight-two newform f with trivial character, E = K_f is totally real, the Hecke algebra acts by Rosati-fixed endomorphisms, and each V_λ(A_f) is two-dimensional with determinant χ_ℓ (AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations R19.6 consumes this).
