#### Galois generic and p-Galois generic abelian varieties

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6/galois-generic-abelian-varieties`. Kind: definition. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/TateModule/GaloisGeneric`). Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6`.

Let k be a number field and (A, λ) a principally polarized abelian variety over k of dimension g ≥ 1. For a prime p, ρ_{A,p} : G_k → GSp(T_pA, e^λ_p) (node weil-pairing-on-tate-modules (vi)) is the action on the p-power torsion; a symplectic Z_p-basis identifies GSp(T_pA, e^λ_p) with GSp_{2g}(Z_p), uniquely up to conjugation. A is p-Galois generic if ρ_{A,p}(G_k) is open in GSp(T_pA, e^λ_p)(Z_p) (equivalently, being closed, of finite index). Let ρ̂_A : G_k → ∏_p GSp(T_pA, e^λ_p) = GSp(T̂A, e^λ) ≅ GSp_{2g}(Ẑ) be the action on all torsion (adelic Tate module, node tate-module-of-an-abelian-variety). A is Galois generic if ρ̂_A(G_k) is open in GSp_{2g}(Ẑ). Both notions are independent of the choice of symplectic basis. Galois generic implies p-Galois generic for every p (projection to a factor is open); the converse implication (Cadoret) and isogeny/conjugation invariance are statements of AbelianVarietiesIsogenousToNoJacobian G0, which consumes this definition.

**Hypotheses.**

- k a number field
- λ a principal polarization (for g = 1 the canonical one; then GSp_2 = GL_2)
- g ≥ 1

**Construction and proof.**

1. The images are compact (G_k is profinite and ρ continuous), hence closed; a closed subgroup of a profinite group is open iff of finite index.
2. Basis independence: two symplectic bases differ by an element of GSp_{2g}(Z_p) (resp. GSp_{2g}(Ẑ)), and conjugation preserves openness.
3. Galois generic ⇒ p-Galois generic: the projection GSp_{2g}(Ẑ) → GSp_{2g}(Z_p) is a continuous open surjective homomorphism, and the image of an open subgroup under an open map is open.
4. Base change: for a finite extension k′/k, G_{k′} is open of finite index in G_k, so (p-)Galois genericity over k and over k′ are equivalent.

**Prerequisites.** `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6/weil-pairing-on-tate-modules`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6/tate-module-of-an-abelian-variety`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/framed-representation`.

**Uses.**

- Masser–Zannier, Annals 191 (2020), §5.1, p. 658, Lemma 5.1(c): candidates A_n that are not p-Galois generic are counted and excluded
- AbelianVarietiesIsogenousToNoJacobian:G0/p-generic-isogeny: isogeny and Galois-conjugation invariance of p-genericity
- AbelianVarietiesIsogenousToNoJacobian:G0/p-to-adelic: Cadoret: p-Galois generic implies Galois generic
- AbelianVarietiesIsogenousToNoJacobian:G0/serre-open-image: End = Z and g odd or g ∈ {2, 6} implies p-Galois generic for every p
- AbelianVarietiesIsogenousToNoJacobian:G0/universal-open-monodromy: open in Sp_{2g}(Z_p) and the multiplier χ_p give open in GSp_{2g}(Z_p)

**API.**

- `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.pAdicImage` (data): ρ_{A,p}(G_k) ⊆ GSp(T_pA, e^λ_p)(Z_p), a closed subgroup.
- `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.IsPGaloisGeneric` (constructor): The predicate: ρ_{A,p}(G_k) is open in GSp(T_pA, e^λ_p)(Z_p).
- `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.IsGaloisGeneric` (constructor): The predicate: ρ̂_A(G_k) is open in GSp(T̂A, e^λ)(Ẑ) ≅ GSp_{2g}(Ẑ).
- `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.isPGaloisGeneric_iff_finiteIndex` (characterisation): Open iff of finite index (closed subgroups of profinite groups).
- `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.IsGaloisGeneric.isPGaloisGeneric` (relation): Galois generic ⇒ p-Galois generic for every p.
- `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.isPGaloisGeneric_baseChange_iff` (relation): Invariance under finite extension of k.
- `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.isPGaloisGeneric_iff_framed` (equivalence): For any symplectic basis, A is p-Galois generic iff the framed image is open in GSp_{2g}(Z_p).

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.isPGaloisGeneric_cm` (non-example): For E : y² = x³ − x over Q (g = 1), E is not p-Galois generic for any p: ρ_{E,p}(G_Q) is contained in the normaliser of a Cartan subgroup of GL_2(Z_p), a closed subgroup of infinite index.
- `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.isPGaloisGeneric_iff_finiteIndex` (characterisation): A is p-Galois generic iff ρ_{A,p}(G_k) has finite index in GSp(T_pA, e^λ_p)(Z_p).
- `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.not_open_in_Sp` (non-example): The definition must use GSp and not Sp: ρ_{A,p}(G_k) is never contained in Sp(T_pA, e^λ_p), since its multiplier χ_p has infinite image on G_k; a definition 'open in Sp_{2g}(Z_p)' is never satisfied.
- `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.isGaloisGeneric_baseChange` (compatibility): For a finite extension k′/k, A is (p-)Galois generic over k iff A_{k′} is (p-)Galois generic over k′.

**Acceptance.**

- g = 1: GSp_2 = GL_2, and a non-CM elliptic curve over Q is p-Galois generic for every p (Serre's open image theorem; the theorem itself is owned downstream by AbelianVarietiesIsogenousToNoJacobian G0/serre-open-image, since its proof uses Faltings' theorems).
- A CM elliptic curve (e.g. y² = x³ − x over Q) is never p-Galois generic: its image lies in the normaliser of a Cartan subgroup (node tate-module-with-endomorphism-coefficients), which has infinite index in GL_2(Z_p).

**Sources.**

- masser-zannier20, §5.1, p. 658: “It is especially convenient to use the concept of p-Galois generic (see [36,” — Introduces p-Galois genericity, citing Pink [36, p. 275].
- masser-zannier20, §5.1, p. 658: “is open in GSp2g (Zp ). It is known” — p-Galois generic: the Galois group of the p^∞-division field is open in GSp_{2g}(Z_p); this implies Galois generic (Cadoret).
- masser-zannier20, §1, p. 637: “stronger, but conjecturally equivalent) of being “Galois generic” (see also [36]).” — Galois genericity as the adelic property, apparently stronger than Hodge genericity.

#### Serre: independence and connectedness of the ℓ-adic images after a finite extension

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6/serre-independence-and-connectedness`. Kind: theorem. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/TateModule/Theorems`). Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6`.

Let A be an abelian variety over a number field K, ρ̂ : G_K → ∏_ℓ GL(T_ℓA) its adelic representation (node tate-module-of-an-abelian-variety), and for a subgroup U ⊆ ∏_ℓ GL(T_ℓA) let U_ℓ be its image in GL(T_ℓA). Say U satisfies the ℓ-independence property if U = ∏_ℓ U_ℓ (Richard–Yafaev, Def. 2.4), and U_ℓ is Zariski connected if its Zariski closure in GL(V_ℓA) (a Q_ℓ-algebraic group) is connected. Then there is a finite extension L/K such that U := ρ̂(G_L) (1) satisfies the ℓ-independence property and (2) has every U_ℓ Zariski connected; moreover the kernel of G_K → G_ℓ/G_ℓ° (G_ℓ the Zariski closure of ρ_ℓ(G_K)) is independent of ℓ. These are Serre's theorems as Richard–Yafaev Theorem 4.9 cites them. The third clause of that theorem, U ⊆ M(Ẑ) for the Mumford–Tate group M, rests on Deligne's theorem that Hodge cycles on abelian varieties are absolutely Hodge, whose owners (ShimuraData D1, AutomorphicBundles B1) consume this stage; it is not stated here (gap and restructure proposal R01.6-RS3).

**Hypotheses.**

- K a number field
- the proofs of (1) and (2) cited by the source were not read; their inputs that might lie downstream of this stage are recorded as a gap

**Construction and proof.**

1. (2) Serre (Œuvres IV nos. 133, 135; Larsen–Pink 1992, 6.14, as cited by Richard–Yafaev): the component group of the Zariski closure G_ℓ of ρ_ℓ(G_K) defines a finite quotient G_K → G_ℓ/G_ℓ° whose kernel is independent of ℓ; its proof compares Frobenius characteristic polynomials across ℓ (node good-reduction-frobenius-polynomial) through Chebotarev density (Tau Ceti Chebotarev Layer 10). Take L ⊇ the fixed field of that kernel.
2. (1) Serre (Œuvres IV no. 136, Th. 1; Serre 2013, §3.1, as cited): a criterion for a family of ℓ-adic representations to become independent after a finite extension, verified for abelian varieties using bounded ramification (R01.2/grothendieck-quasi-unipotence) and the ℓ-independence of Frobenius polynomials.
3. Placement check: if the cited proofs of (1) or (2) use Faltings' semisimplicity (FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems R28.4) or semistable reduction (NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties R11.3), both downstream of R01.6, the theorem must move to a stage downstream of them (restructure proposal R01.6-RS2).

**Prerequisites.** `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6/tate-module-of-an-abelian-variety`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6/good-reduction-frobenius-polynomial`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6/weil-pairing-on-tate-modules`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/grothendieck-quasi-unipotence`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/Chebotarev#layer-10-dirichlet-density-chebotarev`.

**Acceptance.**

- For a non-CM elliptic curve over Q, U is open in ∏ GL_2(Z_ℓ) (Serre 1972) and every U_ℓ is Zariski dense in GL_2, hence connected with L = Q; ℓ-independence holds only after a finite extension (the Serre curve phenomenon: Q(√Δ) ⊆ Q(ζ_N) entangles the 2-adic and N-adic images).
- For a CM elliptic curve over Q with CM field F, the Zariski closure of U_ℓ for L = Q is the normaliser of a torus, which is disconnected; after L ⊇ F it is the torus Res_{F/Q}G_m ⊗ Q_ℓ, connected — the finite extension in (2) is needed.

**Sources.**

- richard-yafaev25, Theorem 4.9, arXiv v4 p. 17 (published pp. 263–264): “Theorem 4.9 (Serre). In the same situation, assume moreover that K” — Statement of the three properties after a finite extension L/K, with references.
- richard-yafaev25, Theorem 4.9(2), arXiv v4 p. 17: “(2) and such that the Up are Zariski connected,” — Zariski connectedness of the ℓ-adic images, citing Serre Œuvres IV 133, 135 and Larsen–Pink 6.14.
- richard-yafaev25, Definition 2.4, arXiv v4 p. 8: “independence property if it is of the form” — ℓ-independence: U = ∏_p U_p with U_p ≤ M(Q_p).

#### Specialization of Tate modules and Galois images in a family (Noot, after Serre)

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6/noot-specialization`. Kind: theorem. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/TateModule/Theorems`). Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6`.

Let F be a field of finite type over Q, S a normal absolutely irreducible F-variety with function field K = F(S), η : Spec K → S the generic point, X/S an abelian scheme of relative dimension g. For every closed point σ of S, with a point σ̄ of the normalisation S̄ of S in K̄ over it and decomposition group D_σ ⊆ G_K, the specialisation maps s_n : X_η[n](K̄) ≅ X[n](S̄) ≅ X_σ[n](F̄) are group isomorphisms (X[n] is finite étale over S, AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A3), compatible in n and D_σ-equivariant, where D_σ acts on the right through D_σ ↠ Gal(F̄/F(σ)); their limit is a D_σ-equivariant isomorphism T_ℓX_η ≅ T_ℓX_σ for every ℓ (and on adelic Tate modules), so ρ_{X_η,ℓ}(D_σ) = ρ_{X_σ,ℓ}(Gal(F̄/F(σ))) ⊆ ρ_{X_η,ℓ}(G_K). This is Noot §1.2 and the diagram Richard–Yafaev use in the proof of Proposition 4.8. Serre's complement (Noot Prop. 1.3: for each ℓ some closed point σ gives equality of images) needs Hilbert irreducibility for compact ℓ-adic Lie quotients, owned by InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups IG.2, which lies downstream of this stage; it is not stated here (restructure proposal R01.6-RS4). The consequence End_K̄(X_η) = End_F̄(X_σ) (Noot Cor. 1.5) uses Faltings' theorem over fields of finite type and belongs to FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems.

**Hypotheses.**

- F of finite type over Q (characteristic 0, so all X[n] are finite étale over S)
- X/S an abelian scheme; an abelian variety over K is first spread out to such an X over a dense open of a model (Tau Ceti ModularCurves 0E, spreading out)

**Construction and proof.**

1. X[n] → S is finite étale (A3, n invertible since char F = 0); a point of X_η[n](K̄) extends uniquely to an S̄-point (finiteness), and specialising at σ̄ is a bijection onto X_σ[n](F̄) (étaleness) (Noot §1.2, p. 163). Compatibility with D_σ: D_σ preserves σ̄ and acts on the residue field through Gal(F̄/F(σ)). Pass to limits as in node tate-module-of-an-abelian-variety.
2. Richard–Yafaev's use (proof of Prop. 4.8): F := Q in Noot's notation, a number field F′ ⊆ K̄ and A_{F′} with T_A ≅ T_{A_{F′}}, the commutative diagram giving ρ(D_{F′}) = ρ′(Gal(F̄′/F′)) — which is (a) — and the endomorphism identity (10), which is Noot Cor. 1.5 and depends on Faltings ([FW, VI, 3]).

**Prerequisites.** `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6/tate-module-of-an-abelian-variety`; `AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A3`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularCurves#0e-effective-descent-and-spreading-out`.

**Acceptance.**

- Legendre family X : y² = x(x − 1)(x − t) over S = A¹ \ {0, 1} over Q: specialising at t = −1 gives y² = x³ − x, whose ℓ-adic image is contained in a Cartan normaliser, a proper subgroup of the generic image (open in GL_2(Z_ℓ) after Igusa); so (a) gives only an inclusion ρ_σ(G_{Q}) ⊆ ρ_η(G_K); the equality of images of Serre's complement fails at such CM points.
- Noot §1.2: the identification T_lX_η ≅ T_lX_σ and the diagram with D_σ ↠ Gal(F̄/F(σ)) is exactly (a) (read on the page image, p. 163).

**Sources.**

- noot95, §1.2, p. 163: “Let X/S be an abelian scheme. We intend to show that we can find a” — Specialisation of torsion and Tate modules along a closed point, D_σ-equivariantly.
- noot95, Proposition 1.3, pp. 163–164: “1.3 PROPOSITION (Serre). Suppose F is a field, of finite type over Q, that” — Existence of a closed point with the same ℓ-adic Galois image.
- noot95, Proof 1.6 of Corollary 1.5, p. 165 (read on the page image): “By [FW, VI, 3] we have” — The endomorphism equality uses Faltings' theorem [FW, VI, 3]; hence it is routed downstream.
- richard-yafaev25, Proof of Proposition 4.8, arXiv v4 p. 17: “§1.2 and Cor. 1.5]6, there exists a number field F ≤ K, and an abelian” — Richard–Yafaev's use of Noot's specialisation.

#### Required examples: χ_p, the split Tate curve, supersingular good reduction, a CM curve over Q, Frobenius conventions

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6/required-examples`. Kind: application. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/TateModule/Theorems`). Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6`.

(1) χ_p: the Tate module of μ_{p^∞} is Z_p(1) with G_Q acting through χ_p, χ_p(Frob_ℓ) = ℓ for ℓ ≠ p, χ_p(c) = −1, HT(χ_p) = +1; it is det T_pE for every elliptic curve E/Q (node determinant-and-oddness). (2) Split Tate curve: for a p-adic field K, q ∈ K^× with |q| < 1 and ℓ ≠ p, Tau Ceti's uniformisation K̄^×/q^Z ≅ E_q(K̄) gives 0 → Z_ℓ(1) → T_ℓE_q → Z_ℓ → 0, the extension class being the Kummer class of q; inertia acts through a nontrivial unipotent (so V_ℓE_q is ramified, with (V_ℓE_q)^{I} = Q_ℓ(1)), the Frobenius polynomial on V_ℓ^{I} is X − q_K and L(E_q, T) = 1 − T; example 11a3 at 11. (3) Supersingular good reduction: y² = x³ + 1 over Q at p ∈ {5, 11, 17, 23} has a_p = 0 and P_p(X) = X² + p; in general good supersingular reduction at p ≥ 5 forces a_p = 0 (p | a_p and |a_p| ≤ 2√p < p). (4) CM curve over Q: y² = x³ − x (CM by Z[i]): ρ_{E,ℓ}(G_Q) lies in the normaliser of the Cartan subgroup (Z[i] ⊗ Z_ℓ)^×, ρ_{E,ℓ}|_{G_{Q(i)}} is abelian (the λ-adic Hecke character), V_ℓE ⊗ Q̄_ℓ ≅ Ind_{G_{Q(i)}}^{G_Q} ψ, and a_p = 0 for p ≡ 3 mod 4. (5) Frobenius conventions on a finite field: for E/F_q with a = q + 1 − #E(F_q), the arithmetic Frobenius φ : x ↦ x^q acts on T_ℓE as π (characteristic polynomial X² − aX + q), the geometric Frobenius φ^{−1} as π^{−1} (X² − (a/q)X + 1/q), and on H¹ = V_ℓE^∨ the geometric Frobenius has characteristic polynomial X² − aX + q, so det(1 − TΦ | H¹) = 1 − aT + qT² is the local factor; for y² = x³ − x over F_5: X² + 2X + 5, X² + (2/5)X + 1/5, X² + 2X + 5 and 1 + 2T + 5T².

**Hypotheses.**

- ℓ ≠ p in (2)–(5)
- the CM and Hecke-character statements of (4) are owned by ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocity CM.4; this node only computes them on the Tate module

**Construction and proof.**

1. (1): R01.1/tate-twist and R01.2/cyclotomic-and-dirichlet-characters; det by node determinant-and-oddness (b).
2. (2): Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 4 (Tate curve, uniformisation, Galois equivariance); the ℓ^n-torsion of K̄^×/q^Z is generated by μ_{ℓ^n} and an ℓ^n-th root of q; Kummer theory shows inertia acts unipotently and nontrivially since v(q) > 0 (DDT Prop. 2.12); the local factor by node comparison-with-weierstrass-local-polynomial (b).
3. (3): node good-reduction-frobenius-polynomial (e) and the point counts; Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 3 (supersingular iff p | a_p over F_p, Hasse bound).
4. (4): node tate-module-with-endomorphism-coefficients (acceptance), Serre 1972 §4.5; induction by R01.1/continuous-induction; a_p = 0 for inert p since Frob_p lies in the non-identity coset of the normaliser, of trace 0.
5. (5): node good-reduction-frobenius-polynomial (c) over the finite field itself (A = E over F_q, good reduction trivially), node local-euler-factor-of-an-abelian-variety for the transpose.

## G7. Dimension-general arithmetic API

### Purpose and boundary

This half of the layer builds the representation-level operations that every rank-n argument downstream uses: tensor, symmetric and exterior powers, tensor induction and restriction of scalars of the coefficients; the adjoint representation with its trace kernel and its quotient by scalars; polarizations with an actual pairing, multiplier and sign, the group scheme 𝒢_n of Clozel–Harris–Taylor and the similitude groups GSp and GO; oddness at real places; GSp₄-valued representations with symplectic induction; Zariski closures and monodromy groups, strong irreducibility, and two theorems that consume them (Newton–Thorne's unequal-weight irreducibility and the Tate–Conrad–Patrikis lifting of projective representations). The image conditions (adequacy, enormous, vast and tidy images, Taylor–Wiles image lemmas) form the other half of G7.

The carrier is R01.1's `ContinuousRep Γ A M`: M finite projective over a topological commutative ring A with the module topology and a jointly continuous action. Framed coordinates appear only where a basis is chosen. Induction, restriction, duals, tensor products and twists of R01.1 are used, not rebuilt. The algebraic symmetric and exterior power representations are already in Tau Ceti (`Representation.symmetricPower`, `Representation.exteriorPower`, from the ClassicalGroups roadmap, layer 1); G7 adds finite projectivity, continuity and the characteristic-polynomial identities on top of them. Determinants (polynomial laws) become representations only through IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.1 and its hypotheses. Hodge–Tate and Hodge–Tate–Sen weights, and Sen operators, are PadicHodgeTheory's (R06.2); Tate's vanishing of H²(G_F, ℚ/ℤ) is ArithmeticGaloisDuality's (R02.4). The rank-two oddness and image facts remain R01.4.

### Operations

For (M, ρ) of rank n, the d-th tensor, symmetric and exterior powers are again continuous representations: M^{⊗d}, Sym[A]^d M (Mathlib's quotient symmetric power) and ⋀[A]^d M are finite projective of ranks n^d, binom(n+d−1, d) and binom(n, d), with the module topology. If ρ(g) has characteristic roots α_i, then Sym^d ρ(g) and ∧^d ρ(g) have roots the d-fold products with and without repetition, so at an unramified place P_v(Sym^d ρ, X) and P_v(∧^d ρ, X) come from P_v(ρ, X) (arithmetic Frobenius, as fixed in R01.2). The top exterior power is det ρ, ∧^d vanishes for d > n, and ρ^{⊗2} ≅ Sym² ρ ⊕ ∧² ρ when 2 is invertible.

Tensor induction from an open subgroup H of index m is V^{⊗m} with Γ acting through the monomial homomorphism Γ → H^m ⋊ S_m of a transversal. This is the homomorphism that ProfiniteCohomology's layer 13 builds for the Evens norm, requested here for arbitrary coefficients. The result is independent of the transversal up to canonical isomorphism, multiplicative, transitive, and has the cycle-product trace formula. Its index-two case is the Asai representation As(ρ), with As(ρ)|_H ≅ ρ ⊗ ρ^σ. Restriction of scalars along a finite projective map of coefficient rings A → B regards a B-representation as an A-representation; its characteristic polynomial is the norm of the B-characteristic polynomial. Base-field Weil restriction is a different operation and corresponds to induction (R01.1), as AbelianSchemes A6 uses it.

### Adjoint representations

ad ρ is End_A(M) with the conjugation action (Mathlib's `Representation.linHom ρ ρ`), canonically ρ ⊗ ρ^∨. Three modules are kept distinct:

- the trace kernel ad⁰ ρ;
- the scalars A·1 ⊂ ad ρ;
- the quotient ad ρ/A·1.

The trace pairing on ad ρ is perfect over every A (Tau Ceti's `traceBilinForm_nondegenerate`), and it identifies ad⁰ ρ with the dual of ad ρ/A·1. Only when n ∈ A^× does ad split as A ⊕ ad⁰ with ad⁰ ≅ ad/A·1 self-dual. When char A = p divides n, the scalars lie in ad⁰, the trace pairing on ad⁰ has radical A·1, and H⁰(H, ad⁰) ≠ 0 for every subgroup H; this is why ACC+'s enormous-image condition can never hold when p | n. In rank two with 2 invertible, ad⁰ ρ ≅ Sym² ρ ⊗ det^{−1}, the Galois counterpart of the Gelbart–Jacquet lift that GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer R17.4 uses; the adjoint of a Weil–Deligne parameter is (ad r, [N, −]).

### Polarizations

Let F be CM or totally real, with maximal totally real subfield F⁺. A polarized representation is (ρ, μ, ⟨ , ⟩) at a real place v of F⁺, with these pieces:

- ρ is a continuous representation of G_F;
- μ is a continuous character of G_{F⁺};
- ⟨ , ⟩ is a perfect pairing with ⟨ρ(σ)x, ρ(c_vσc_v)y⟩ = μ(σ)⟨x, y⟩ and ⟨x, y⟩ = ε_v⟨y, x⟩;
- for F imaginary, ε_v = −μ(c_v).

This is BLGGT §2.1. Over any coefficient ring it is equivalent to Clozel–Harris–Taylor's triples (ρ, μ, ⟨ , ⟩) at any γ₀ ∈ G_{F⁺} ∖ G_F, and hence (CHT Lemma 2.1.1) to homomorphisms G_{F⁺} → 𝒢_n(A) with G_F as preimage of 𝒢_n⁰. Here 𝒢_n = (GL_n × GL_1) ⋊ {1, j}, with j(g, μ)j^{−1} = (μ ᵗg^{−1}, μ), ν(j) = −1 and ad(j)x = −ᵗx. A polarization is data: essential conjugate self-duality alone loses the sign, and in rank one over an imaginary CM field a character with μ(c) = +1 is essentially conjugate self-dual but not polarized.

The sign theorem records four facts. The sign transforms under change of place by ε_{v′} = μ(c_vc_{v′})ε_v. Determinants satisfy det ρ(cσc)·det ρ(σ) = μ(σ)^n. An alternating perfect form forces even rank. For absolutely irreducible ρ the pairing is unique up to scalars and the sign is intrinsic (BLGGT's sgn(r, μ)), and extensions to 𝒢_n are a torsor under k^×/(k^×)² (CHT Lemma 2.1.4). The operations carry the quadratic character δ = δ_{F/F⁺}, which is trivial on G_F and is required at c_v:

| Operation | Multiplier | Sign |
|---|---|---|
| dual | μ^{−1} | ε |
| twist by χ | μ·(χ ∘ Ver) | ε |
| tensor product | μμ′δ | εε′ |
| ∧^k, Sym^k (k ≥ 1) | μ^kδ^{k−1} | ε^k |

Here (χ ∘ Ver) is the transfer: it restricts to χχ^c on G_F and has value 1 at c_v. The Sym^k operation needs k! invertible. The similitude groups GSp(M, B) and GO(M, B) of a perfect form are the targets in the totally real case and for BCG25's G_n: GSp_n for n even with A_n = J_n, GO_n for n odd with A_n = 1_n. Their multiplier ν satisfies det = ν^{n/2} on GSp_n, and gsp = sp ⊕ scalars when 2 is invertible. BCG25's injection G_n × {±1} → 𝒢_n, which a numerical check in this job confirms is a homomorphism with ν(r(g, s)) = ν(g)s^n, gives ψ ↦ r_ψ.

On a rank-two symplectic representation with 2 and d! invertible, the normalised symmetrisation B_d of the form is perfect on Sym^d. It has antidiagonal Gram entries (−1)^i/binom(d, i), sign (−1)^d and multiplier μ^d, so Sym^{n−1} lands in G_n. Over a finite field of odd characteristic, the odd-dimensional symmetric form is identified with 1_n up to a scalar; over a general field that identification is an extra hypothesis. The test cases are d = p − 2 and d = p − 1 (alternating of rank p − 1, symmetric of rank p), and d = p fails: over F₇ the SL₂(F₇)-invariant forms on Sym⁷ form a line of rank 6.

### Oddness

Oddness in dimension n is a sign condition at each real place, not the rank-two determinant test:

- a polarized (ρ, μ) is totally odd when every ε_v = 1, equivalently μ(c_v) = −1 for F imaginary;
- a 𝒢_n- or GSp-valued representation is odd when ν(c_v) = −1, a GO-valued one when ν(c_v) = +1;
- a character of a totally real field is totally odd when μ(c_v) = −1 (ACC+).

Calegari–Geraghty's unpolarized GL_n notion is that the ±1-eigenspaces of c_v have dimensions differing by at most one. Their gloss "Trace(c_v) ∈ {−1, 0, 1}" is equivalent to it only in characteristic 0 or in characteristic ℓ > n + 1 (n even), ℓ > n (n odd) (sourceIssue E702). In rank two all of these reduce to det ρ(c_v) = −1, which is R01.4's condition. The cohomological content is CHT Lemma 2.1.3: dim gl_n^{c=η} = n(n + ην(c))/2.

### GSp₄

GSp₄-valued representations come with two normalisations of J, BCGP21's and CG20's, related by an explicit permutation. Oddness means ν(r(c)) = −1. Then r(c) has Lagrangian ±1-eigenspaces and dim H⁰(⟨c⟩, sp₄) = 4. For p > 2, ad r = sp₄ ⊕ (trivial line) and asp⁰ = Lie PGSp₄ = sp₄; CG20 prints "⊕ ν" (sourceIssue E701). Symplectic induction from an index-two subgroup carries two forms, with similitudes χ and χη_{K/F}. In BCGP21's J, the pairs (A, B) with det A = det B embed in a block pattern. ad⁰ of an induction is As(ρ)χ^{−1} ⊕ Ind ad⁰ρ, up to the quadratic twist of As. Semisimple GSp₄-valued representations over an algebraically closed field are determined by the GL₄ × GL₁ data only in characteristic ≠ 2 (BCGP21 Lemma 2.1.3, corrected, sourceIssue E703). The similitude character of an irreducible symplectic ρ is unique unless ρ becomes reducible over a quadratic field (Lemma 8.3.1).

### Monodromy groups

The Zariski closure of a subgroup Σ of G(K), for G affine of finite type over a field K, is the closed subgroup scheme cut out by the vanishing Hopf ideal. Tau Ceti classifies closed subgroups by Hopf ideals; no library or atlas layer owns closures of abstract subgroups, so G7 plans them. For a representation, the monodromy group G_ρ, its geometric identity component G_ρ⁰, the open finite-index Γ⁰ = ρ^{−1}(G_ρ⁰) and the component field F_ρ⁰ follow. Borel's facts are planned with them:

- closures commute with homomorphisms;
- the closure of a commutator subgroup is the derived group;
- in characteristic 0, G_ρ⁰ is reductive for semisimple ρ;
- connected irreducible subgroups of GL₂ are SL₂ or GL₂;
- Goursat holds for PGL₂ × PGL₂.

Strong irreducibility, irreducibility on every open subgroup, is equivalent in characteristic 0 to irreducibility of G_ρ⁰. Newton–Thorne's Lemma 2.2 follows. Take two strongly irreducible ρ, ρ′ : G_F → GL₂(Q̄_p) with HT_τ(ρ) = {a, b} and HT_τ(ρ′) = {a′, b′} at one τ, and with a − b ≠ ±(a′ − b′). Then the projective monodromy of the pair is PGL₂ × PGL₂, and Sym^m ρ ⊗ Sym^{m′} ρ′ is strongly irreducible on G_{F(ζ_{p^∞})}. Finally, projective representations of G_F lift to GL_n(Q̄_ℓ), using Tate's H²(G_F, ℚ/ℤ) = 0 and Conrad's lifting through central tori. Lifts are unramified almost everywhere and differ by characters. In rank two, Patrikis's Lemma 2.7.4 gives lifts with Hodge–Tate–Sen weights in ½ℤ, which is how BCGP21 lifts Proj s_l to a weight-(0, 1) representation in Proposition 9.2.1.

### Pitfalls

- ⚠ Sym^d is a quotient. Its dual is the divided power Γ^d, and the invariant pairing on Sym^d degenerates once d ≥ char A.
- ⚠ ad, ad⁰ and ad/scalars are three different modules when char A divides n. Do not define ad⁰ as a complement of the scalars.
- ⚠ The δ_{F/F⁺} correction in tensor and power operations is invisible on G_F, but without it the CM sign condition fails at every c_v.
- ⚠ Oddness is a sign; the trace test fails in small characteristic, and the rank-two determinant test does not generalise.
- ⚠ Base-field Weil restriction is induction, not restriction of scalars of the coefficients.
- ⚠ A residually reducible determinant does not determine a representation over A.

### Acceptance tests

- Over F₇, B₅ on Sym⁵ is alternating of rank 6.
- Over F₇, B₆ on Sym⁶ is symmetric of rank 7 with all d!-scaled antidiagonal entries −1.
- Over F₇, Sym⁷ has no nondegenerate invariant form.
- Over F₂, the identity lies in ad⁰ for n = 2.
- In rank one over an imaginary CM field, polarized characters are totally odd.
- Over F₃ with n = 2, the trivial representation passes the trace test but is not odd.
- For odd GSp₄-valued r, ad r ≇ ad⁰ r ⊕ ν∘r.
- (2.1.2) is a homomorphism with ν(r(g, s)) = ν(g)s^n.
- An induced character from a quadratic field is irreducible but not strongly irreducible.

### Residual-image criteria for Taylor–Wiles primes

This half of the layer fixes the group-theoretic hypotheses that automorphy lifting theorems place on a residual representation, states each as an explicit cohomological and eigenvalue condition on a finite subgroup of `GL_n(k)` or `GSp_4(k)`, and proves the verification lemmas that the sources use to check them. The conditions are properties of subgroups; a representation enters only through the image of a specified subgroup of `G_F`, almost always `G_{F(ζ_p)}` or `G_{F(ζ_{p^N})}`. Rank-two finite group theory (Dickson's classification, normal subgroups and automorphisms of `PSL_2` and `PGL_2`, the behaviour of images under restriction to cyclotomic fields) belongs to R01.4 and is cited. Decomposed genericity is outside the layer: it is defined at AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII:AG2.7, which itself requires G7. The lemmas that produce it are therefore routed to PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure:PA.5. These are Allen et al. Lemmas 7.1.5, 7.1.6(3)–(5) and 7.1.7, Caraiani–Newton Lemma 6.2.2, and the first clause of Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Newton–Thorne Definition 5.2.1.

**Conventions.** `k` is a field of characteristic `p`. Unless stated otherwise it is finite, or an algebraic extension of `F_p`. `ad = M_n(k)` carries the conjugation action, which is the adjoint representation of G7's operations half. Inside it, `ad⁰` is the trace-zero submodule and `ad₀ = ad/k·1` is the quotient by the scalars. These two modules are isomorphic exactly when `p ∤ n`, and the layer never identifies them. Group cohomology of a finite group is Mathlib's `groupCohomology`. For `g` in a finite group, *semisimple* means of order prime to `p`, equivalently diagonalisable over `k̄`. An element of `GL_n(k)` is *regular semisimple* when its characteristic polynomial is separable, that is, has `n` distinct roots in `k̄`. Finally, `e_{g,α}` is the `g`-equivariant projection onto the generalised `α`-eigenspace.

**Adequacy.** A finite subgroup `H ⊆ GL_n(k)` is *adequate* in Thorne's sense (2012, Definition 2.3) when three conditions hold:
- `H¹(H, k) = 0`;
- `H⁰(H, ad⁰) = H¹(H, ad⁰) = 0`;
- every simple `k̄[H]`-submodule `W` of `ad⁰ ⊗ k̄` meets some `e_{g,α}` with nonzero trace.

It is *GHT-adequate* (Guralnick–Herzig–Tiep; Thorne 2017, Definition 2.20) when `H¹(H, k) = 0`, `H¹(H, ad₀) = 0`, and the trace condition holds for semisimple `g` on simple submodules of `ad ⊗ k̄`. It is *weakly adequate* when its semisimple elements span `M_n(k)`. By the GHTT appendix (Lemma 1), the trace condition is the spanning condition for irreducible `H`. With Burnside's theorem, every one of these notions forces absolute irreducibility. Thorne's notion forces `p ∤ n`, and for `p ∤ n` the two cohomological forms agree. All three notions are invariant under extension of `k` and under multiplying `H` by scalars, so they depend only on the projective image.

The verification theorem collects the criteria the sources use:
- the Guralnick–Herzig–Taylor–Thorne theorem: an irreducible `H` is adequate when `p ≥ 2(d+1)`, where `d` bounds the irreducible constituents of the subgroup generated by `p`-elements; in particular `p ≥ 2(n+1)` suffices for absolutely irreducible `H`;
- prime-to-`p` order;
- normal subgroups of index prime to `p`, and reduction to the subgroup generated by `p`-elements;
- tensor products (BLGG13 Lemma A.3.1);
- the rank-two classification;
- Guralnick–Herzig–Tiep's list of the non-adequate representations of `SL_2(F_{p^r})`.

In rank two, an irreducible `G ⊆ GL_2(F̄_p)` with `p` odd is adequate except when its projective image is `PSL_2(F_3)` (`p = 3`) or `PSL_2(F_5)` (`p = 5`). This layer records that the published proof in BLGG13 also excludes `PGL_2(F_5)`, wrongly: `H¹(GL_2(F_5), ad⁰) = 0` (sourceIssue E754).

**Enormous image.** Following Allen et al. (Definition 6.2.29 of the Annals version, numbered 6.2.28 in arXiv v2), an absolutely irreducible `H ⊆ GL_n(k)` is *enormous* when three conditions hold:
- `H` has no nontrivial quotient of `p`-power order;
- `H⁰(H, ad⁰) = H¹(H, ad⁰) = 0`;
- every simple `k[H]`-submodule `W ⊆ ad⁰` has `W^h ≠ 0` for some regular semisimple `h ∈ H`.

The notion depends only on the image in `PGL_n(k)`, and no subgroup is enormous when `p | n`. Lemma 6.2.30 (v2: 6.2.29) proves invariance under algebraic extension of `k`, by Galois descent of the submodule spanned by the conjugates of a counterexample. When `k` contains all eigenvalues, the definition agrees with Khare–Thorne's Definition 4.10, and enormous implies adequate (Gee–Newton Remark 3.2.2). In rank two the two notions coincide for odd `p`.

A separate definition records Newton–Thorne's characteristic-zero notion (2023, Definition 2.23) for subgroups of `GL_n(O)`. It has no cohomological conditions and tests the whole of `M_n(E)`. Its criterion (Lemma 2.28) is the one Newton–Thorne 2026 use in Lemma 4.7: the identity component of the Zariski closure must contain regular semisimple elements and act absolutely irreducibly. Comparing the two definitions shows they are different notions, and neither is deduced from the other.

**Symmetric powers and the bound `p > 2n + 1`.** If `p > 2n + 1` and `k^× Sym^{n−1} GL_2(k') ⊇ H ⊇ Sym^{n−1} SL_2(k')`, then `H` is enormous (Gee–Newton Lemma 3.2.5, after Clozel–Harris–Taylor Corollary 2.5.4). Hence the following are enormous:
- `Sym^{n−1}H ⊆ GL_n(F̄_l)` for every finite `H ⊇ SL_2(F_l)` with `l > 2n + 1` (Allen et al. Lemma 7.1.4, whose codomain is printed as `GL_2`: sourceIssue E751);
- `(Sym^m r̄)(G_{F'(ζ_l)})` under the linear-disjointness hypotheses of Allen et al. Lemma 7.1.6(2) and Qian Lemma 2.6(1).

The cohomological input is `H¹(SL_2(F), Sym^{2i}) = 0` for `2i < p − 3`. The vanishing fails exactly at `Sym^{p−3}`. For `p = 5` this is the classical exception of Darmon–Diamond–Taylor Lemma 2.48: `H¹(SL_2(F), ad⁰) = 0` for `#F ≠ 5`, while `H¹(SL_2(F_5), ad⁰)` is one-dimensional. The bound `l > 2n − 1` printed by Clozel–Harris–Taylor is therefore too weak (E756).

The mod `p` Clebsch–Gordan theorem supplies the module decompositions:
- `V ⊗ Sym^{r−1}V ≅ Sym^r V ⊕ det ⊗ Sym^{r−2}V` whenever `r` is invertible in `k`, a genuine isomorphism;
- for `0 < r < p`, the two-constituent congruence `(Sym^{p+r−1}V)^ss ≅ (det^r ⊗ Sym^{p−r−1}V)^ss ⊕ (Frob V ⊗ Sym^{r−1}V)^ss`, with Frobenius acting on coefficients. Clozel–Thorne's (1.1) is the case `r = 2`;
- `End(Sym^{n−1}V)^ss ≅ ⊕_i (Sym^{2i}V ⊗ det^{−i})^ss`.

The semisimplified identities follow from Brauer–Nesbitt (R01.1) by comparing characteristic polynomials. Adequacy of symmetric powers follows from these and the criteria above:
- Boxer–Calegari–Gee Lemma 2.2: `p − 2 ≤ n ≤ p`, in the GHT sense, because `n = p` is divisible by `p`;
- Newton–Thorne Lemma 2.3, with one threshold `a₀(p)` for the symmetric powers, the Frobenius-twisted tensors, and the subgroups of small index.

**GSp₄.** Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni define enormous and weakly enormous subgroups of `GSp_4(k)` using `𝔰𝔭_4` (dimension 10, not `𝔰𝔩_4`). Their definition has no `p`-power-quotient condition, which admits the `p = 3` images of Wiles's original setting. On top of this they define *vast* representations, through the images over `F(ζ_{p^N})` for large `N`, and *tidy* subgroups, which contain an element with `ν(h) ≠ 1` and no eigenvalue ratio equal to `ν(h)`. The verification theorem collects:
- the Galois-cohomology vanishing of Lemma 7.5.9;
- `Sp_4(F_p)` is enormous and `GSp_4(F_p)` is tidy for `p ≥ 3`;
- the decomposition `ad⁰(Ind V) = Ind ad⁰(V) ⊕ As(V)` for representations induced from index two;
- the wreath products `SL_2(k) ≀ Z/2`;
- the `p = 3` enumeration;
- inductions from quadratic fields.

It carries the four recorded mistakes (E761–E764). It adds a fifth: contrary to Remark 7.5.23, the Sylow 2-subgroup of `Sp_4(F_3)` is enormous (E765).

Calegari–Geraghty's big image assumption (H1)–(H3) is stated with `ad(r̄) = ad⁰(r̄) ⊕ k`, the trivial character, where the source prints the similitude character (E759). Together with absolute irreducibility over every `Q(ζ_{p^N})`, it implies vastness. Its examples are surjective `GSp_4(F_p)` images and inductions from imaginary quadratic fields. For the inductions, the proof must use an element of `r̄(G_{Q(ζ_{p^m})})` (E757); and only the eigenvalue 1, not −1, is automatic on `Ind ad⁰` (E758).

**Taylor–Wiles image conditions.** A continuous `s̄ : G_F → GL_n(F̄_p)` satisfies the Taylor–Wiles image conditions when `s̄(G_{F(ζ_p)})` is adequate and some `σ ∈ G_F ∖ G_{F(ζ_p)}` has `s̄(σ)` scalar. The second condition is equivalent to `ζ_p ∉ F̄^{ker ad s̄}`. The enormous variant is hypotheses (3)–(4) of Allen et al. Theorems 6.1.1–6.1.2. The verification lemmas are the image-theoretic parts of Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Newton–Thorne Lemmas 5.2.2–5.2.6, with two corrections:
- in Lemma 5.2.6, absolute irreducibility of `r̄_B|G_{F(ζ_p)}` is required (E766);
- for `m = 2` in Lemma 5.2.4, the Galois closures must be linearly disjoint (E767).

The scalar-element half of Allen et al. Lemma 7.1.6(1) also belongs here.

**Dependencies.** Inside the roadmap, this half uses:
- R01.1: absolute irreducibility, coefficient extension, semisimplification, Brauer–Nesbitt, coefficient Frobenius twist, induction, residual descent;
- R01.2: the cyclotomic character;
- R01.4: Dickson, automorphisms of `PSL_2`, restriction to cyclotomic fields, persistence of large image;
- the operations half of G7: adjoint representations, symmetric powers, tensor induction, `GSp_4` and symplectic induction, Zariski closures, polarizations.

Across roadmaps it uses:
- Tau Ceti ProfiniteCohomology layer 6, for corestriction and `cor ∘ res`;
- Tau Ceti Chebotarev layer 10;
- Tau Ceti RepresentationTheory/InductionRestriction layer 4, for Mackey's criterion.

Recorded gaps:
- the classification-dependent input and Guralnick's Ext¹ theorem behind the GHTT adequacy theorem;
- the `SL_2(F_q)` extension computations behind GHT17 Corollary 9.4;
- the exact statement of Cline–Parshall–Scott Lemma 2.7(c);
- the Magma computations of Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni §7.5;
- Thorne 2024 Lemma 7.3.

**⚠ Pitfalls.**
- Adequate, big, enormous (Allen et al.), enormous (Newton–Thorne, characteristic zero) and enormous (Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, `GSp_4`) are five different conditions. The image of `Q₈ × Q₈` on `F̄_p^2 ⊗ F̄_p^2` (`p` odd) is adequate but not enormous, because it has no regular semisimple element.
- `ad⁰` and `ad₀` differ when `p | n`. Thorne's adequacy and Allen et al.'s enormity are then impossible, while GHT-adequacy is not.
- `SL_2(F_5)` is neither adequate nor enormous, but `GL_2(F_5)` is both: a subgroup of an enormous group need not be enormous.
- `SL_2(F_3)` has vanishing `H⁰` and `H¹` with `ad⁰` coefficients, yet it is not enormous, because it has a quotient of order 3.
- The conditions concern `ρ̄(G_{F(ζ_p)})`, not `ρ̄(G_F)`. The condition `ζ_p ∉ F̄^{ker ad ρ̄}` depends on more than the image group.

**Acceptance.**
- `SL_2(F_p) ⊆ GL_2(F_p)` is adequate and enormous for `p ≥ 7`. It fails at `p = 5` (`H¹ ≠ 0`), at `p = 3` (quotient of order 3), and at `p = 2` (`p | n`).
- No subgroup of `GL_p(k)` is enormous.
- Computation recorded with the layer: `dim H¹(SL_2(F_p), ad⁰) = 0, 1, 0, 0, 0` for `p = 3, 5, 7, 11, 13`, and `H¹(GL_2(F_5), ad⁰) = 0`.
- Computation recorded with the layer: `H¹(SL_2(F_p), Sym^a) ≠ 0` only for `a = p − 3`, checked for `p ≤ 11`.
- `Sp_4(F_p)` is enormous and `GSp_4(F_p)` is tidy for `p ≥ 3`. For `p = 3`, `H¹(Sp_4(F_3), 𝔰𝔭_4) = 0` is a finite computation.
- A non-CM elliptic curve over `Q` with surjective mod-`l` image, `l ≥ 7`, satisfies both forms of the Taylor–Wiles image conditions.

### Declarations of G7

Each entry gives the mathematical statement, hypotheses, proof route, prerequisites, uses, API, unit tests, acceptance checks and sources of one planned declaration.

#### Tensor, symmetric and exterior powers of continuous representations

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/symmetric-and-exterior-powers`. Kind: construction. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.ContinuousRep` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/Operations/Powers`). Planet: **Symmetric and exterior powers**. Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7`.

Let Γ be a profinite group, A a topological commutative ring and (M, ρ) ∈ ContinuousRep Γ A M (R01.1: M finite projective of constant rank n with its module topology, jointly continuous action). For d ≥ 0 define (i) T^d ρ on M^{⊗d} = ⨂_{i∈Fin d} M (g ↦ ρ(g)^{⊗d}); (ii) Sym^d ρ on Sym[A]^d M (the quotient of M^{⊗d} by the permutation relation, Mathlib SymmetricPower) by the Tau Ceti action Representation.symmetricPower ρ d; (iii) ∧^d ρ on ⋀[A]^d M (Mathlib exteriorPower) by the Tau Ceti action Representation.exteriorPower ρ d. Each is again an object of ContinuousRep Γ A: the module is finite projective of rank n^d, binom(n+d−1, d) and binom(n, d) respectively, it carries its module topology, and the action is jointly continuous. These constructions are functorial in Γ-equivariant A-linear maps, commute with coefficient extension along continuous A → B and with restriction along continuous group homomorphisms. Characteristic-polynomial identities: if ρ(g) has characteristic polynomial ∏_{i=1}^n (X − α_i) over some A-algebra B in which it splits, then det(X − Sym^d ρ(g)) = ∏_{i_1≤…≤i_d}(X − α_{i_1}⋯α_{i_d}) and det(X − ∧^d ρ(g)) = ∏_{i_1<…<i_d}(X − α_{i_1}⋯α_{i_d}); in general the coefficients of these polynomials are universal integer polynomials in the coefficients of det(X − ρ(g)). ∧^n ρ ≅ det ρ (a rank-one ContinuousRep), ∧^d ρ = 0 for d > n, and when 2 ∈ A^× the symmetriser and antisymmetriser give ρ^{⊗2} ≅ Sym^2 ρ ⊕ ∧^2 ρ.

**Hypotheses.**

- M finite projective over A (a framed M = A^n is the special case where a basis is chosen); for the rank formulas A ≠ 0 and M of constant rank n
- No invertibility of d! is assumed for the construction; Sym^d is the quotient (coinvariant) symmetric power, not the invariant symmetric tensors or the divided power Γ^d, which differ from it when d! ∉ A^×
- The characteristic polynomial identities are statements about Γ acting through ρ; at an unramified place v they give P_v(Sym^d ρ, X) and P_v(∧^d ρ, X) from P_v(ρ, X) with the arithmetic-Frobenius convention of R01.2/frobenius-characteristic-polynomial

**Construction and proof.**

1. Underlying abstract representations: use Representation.symmetricPower and Representation.exteriorPower (Tau Ceti, RepresentationTheory/SymmetricPower.lean and ExteriorPower.lean), which give the action through SymmetricPower.map and exteriorPower.map; tensor powers through iterated Representation.tprod (Mathlib).
2. Finite projectivity and rank: for M free with basis b, Module.Basis.symmetricPower and Module.Basis.exteriorPower give bases indexed by multisets Sym κ d and d-element subsets, so SymmetricPower.finrank_eq and exteriorPower.finrank_eq give the ranks; for projective M localise at primes (or write M as a direct summand of A^N and use functoriality of the three constructions in split idempotents) and use compatibility with base change.
3. Continuity: M^{⊗d}, Sym^d M and ∧^d M are finite A-modules and carry the module topology (IsModuleTopology); every A-linear map between finite modules with the module topology is continuous, and the action map Γ × M^{⊗d} → M^{⊗d} is jointly continuous because in a basis of a free module containing M as a summand its matrix entries are polynomials in the entries of ρ(g), which are continuous by R01.1/continuous-representation; Sym^d and ∧^d are continuous quotients of M^{⊗d}.
4. Characteristic polynomials: for a split endomorphism choose (after a faithfully flat or splitting extension, e.g. A → A[α_1,…,α_n] universal splitting algebra) a triangular basis; SymmetricPower.map_basis_symmetricPower_of_apply_basis and the exterior analogue show the induced map is triangular with diagonal entries the monomials α_{i_1}⋯α_{i_d}; descend coefficients since the universal splitting algebra is free over A. SymmetricPower.trace_map_of_apply_basis gives the trace case.
5. ∧^n ρ ≅ det ρ: exteriorPower.finrank_eq gives rank one, and ∧^n f acts by det f on the top exterior power; ∧^d M = 0 for d > n by the basis count. Tensor-square decomposition when 2 is invertible: the idempotents (1 ± swap)/2 on M^{⊗2} commute with ρ(g)^{⊗2}; compare with TauCeti.tensorSquareFDRepIso over ℂ (Tau Ceti ClassicalGroups layer 1), whose proof is the same.

**Prerequisites.** `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/continuous-representation`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/restriction-dual-tensor-twist`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/coefficient-extension`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/frobenius-characteristic-polynomial`; `tauceti:Representation.symmetricPower`; `tauceti:Representation.exteriorPower`; `mathlib:Representation.tprod`; `mathlib:SymmetricPower`; `mathlib:ExteriorAlgebra.exteriorPower`; `tauceti:Module.Basis.symmetricPower`; `tauceti:SymmetricPower.finrank_eq`; `mathlib:exteriorPower.finrank_eq`; `tauceti:SymmetricPower.trace_map_of_apply_basis`; `mathlib:IsModuleTopology`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/ClassicalGroups#layer-1-functorial-constructions-and-tensor-powers`.

**Uses.**

- PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:R24.5/linear-algebra-operations-on-systems: member-by-member Sym^k, ∧^k, ⊗ and their Frobenius-root rules
- Boxer–Calegari–Gee, Cuspidal cohomology classes for GL_n(Z), proof of Theorem 2.1: ρ = Sym^{n−1}(ρ_f ⊗ ε^{(k−2)/2}) is the residual representation deformed
- Newton–Thorne, Symmetric power functoriality for Hilbert modular forms, Lemma 2.2: Sym^m ρ ⊗ Sym^{m′} ρ′ restricted to G_{F(ζ_{p^∞})}
- ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/symmetric-power-polarization: the form B_d lives on the existing Sym^d
- ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/enormous-symmetric-powers: G7b: image conditions for Sym^{n−1} ρ̄ (ACC+ Lemma 7.1.4)
- ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/adjoint-representations: ad ρ ≅ ρ ⊗ ρ^∨ and, in rank two with 2 invertible, ad⁰ ρ ≅ Sym^2 ρ ⊗ det^{−1}

**API.**

- `TauCeti.ContinuousRep.symPower` (constructor): Sym^d ρ ∈ ContinuousRep Γ A (Sym[A]^d M).
- `TauCeti.ContinuousRep.extPower` (constructor): ∧^d ρ ∈ ContinuousRep Γ A (⋀[A]^d M).
- `TauCeti.ContinuousRep.tensorPower` (constructor): T^d ρ ∈ ContinuousRep Γ A (⨂^d M), and ρ ⊗ ρ′ for two representations (R01.1).
- `TauCeti.ContinuousRep.symPower_rank` (structure): Sym^d M is finite projective of rank binom(n+d−1, d); ∧^d M of rank binom(n, d).
- `TauCeti.ContinuousRep.symPower_map` (functoriality): A Γ-map f : M → N gives Sym^d f and ∧^d f, with map_id and map_comp.
- `TauCeti.ContinuousRep.symPower_baseChange` (compatibility): Sym^d(ρ ⊗_A B) ≅ (Sym^d ρ) ⊗_A B and ∧^d(ρ ⊗_A B) ≅ (∧^d ρ) ⊗_A B for continuous A → B.
- `TauCeti.ContinuousRep.charpoly_symPower` (characterisation): The characteristic polynomial of Sym^d ρ(g) (resp. ∧^d ρ(g)) is the universal polynomial of the characteristic polynomial of ρ(g) with roots the d-fold products with repetition (resp. without).
- `TauCeti.ContinuousRep.extPowerTopEquivDet` (equivalence): ∧^n ρ ≅ det ρ as rank-one continuous representations.
- `TauCeti.ContinuousRep.tensorSquareEquiv` (equivalence): When 2 ∈ A^×, ρ ⊗ ρ ≅ Sym^2 ρ ⊕ ∧^2 ρ.
- `TauCeti.ContinuousRep.extPowerPairing` (relation): The wedge pairing ∧^d M × ∧^{n−d} M → ∧^n M is perfect and Γ-equivariant, so ∧^d ρ ≅ (∧^{n−d} ρ)^∨ ⊗ det ρ.

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.ContinuousRep.symPower_zero` (degenerate): Sym^0 ρ and ∧^0 ρ are the trivial rank-one representation A, and Sym^1 ρ ≅ ∧^1 ρ ≅ ρ.
- `TauCeti.ContinuousRep.extPower_top` (computation): For ρ of rank 3, ∧^3 ρ is the character det ρ and ∧^4 ρ = 0.
- `TauCeti.ContinuousRep.charpoly_symPower_two` (computation): If det(X − ρ(g)) = (X − α)(X − β) then det(X − Sym^2 ρ(g)) = (X − α^2)(X − αβ)(X − β^2).
- `TauCeti.ContinuousRep.symPower_toRepresentation` (compatibility): The underlying abstract representation of Sym^d ρ is Representation.symmetricPower ρ d and that of ∧^d ρ is Representation.exteriorPower ρ d.
- `TauCeti.ContinuousRep.symPower_not_dual_char_p` (non-example): Over F_2, Sym^2 of the standard representation of GL_2(F_2) is not isomorphic to (Sym^2 of the dual) ⊗ det^2: the line spanned by the squares x^2, y^2 is a subrepresentation on one side and not on the other; a definition of Sym^d as symmetric invariant tensors fails this test.

**Acceptance.**

- Computation: for ρ = 1 ⊕ χ (χ a character) Sym^d ρ ≅ ⊕_{i=0}^d χ^i and ∧^2 ρ ≅ χ; for ρ the p-adic Tate module of an elliptic curve (R01.6), ∧^2 ρ ≅ Z_p(1) (Weil pairing).
- At an unramified place, P_v(Sym^2 ρ, X) for ρ of rank two with P_v(ρ, X) = X^2 − aX + b is X^3 − (a^2 − b)X^2 + b(a^2 − b)X − b^3.
- Non-example in characteristic p: for k = F_p, the GL_2(k)-module Sym^p k^2 is not isomorphic to its dual twisted by det^p (it contains the Frobenius twist k^{2,(1)} spanned by x^p, y^p as a submodule but not as a quotient); the dual of Sym^d is the divided power Γ^d.

**Sources.**

- bcg25-gln, Proof of Theorem 2.1, p. 513 (published offprint): “Since ρf is symplectic with multiplier ε1−k , the twist ρf ⊗ ε 2 is symplectic with” — Sym^{n−1} of a twisted residual rank-two representation is the representation BCG feed into the polarized deformation argument (with its multiplier read off from the power).
- nt26, Lemma 2.2, arXiv v2 p. 10: “Lemma 2.2. Let F be a number field. Let ρ, ρ′ : GF → GL2 (Qp ) be continuous” — Tensor products of symmetric powers Sym^m ρ ⊗ Sym^{m′} ρ′ of continuous p-adic representations, the operations this node supplies.
- blggt14, §1.1, p. 12 (arXiv v4): “of r ⊗ r′ differs from the product of the multipliers of r and r′ by the non-trivial” — Tensor products of representations are used together with their polarizations; the tensor operation itself is this node, its polarization is G7/operations-on-polarized-representations.

#### Tensor induction from an open subgroup (Asai representation in index two)

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/tensor-induction`. Kind: construction. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.ContinuousRep` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/Operations/TensorInduction`). Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7`.

Let Γ be profinite, H ≤ Γ an open subgroup of index m, A a topological commutative ring and (V, ρ) ∈ ContinuousRep H A V of rank n. Choose a left transversal t_1,…,t_m of Γ/H and let Φ_t : Γ → H^m ⋊ S_m be the monomial homomorphism, g t_i = t_{π_g(i)} h_i(g) with h_i(g) ∈ H (ProfiniteCohomology layer 13, milestones 1–2). The tensor induction ⊗-Ind_H^Γ ρ is V^{⊗m} = ⨂_{i=1}^m V with g acting by g·(v_1 ⊗ … ⊗ v_m) = ⊗_i ρ(h_i(g)) v_{i} placed in slot π_g(i). It is an object of ContinuousRep Γ A of rank n^m; a different transversal gives a canonically isomorphic representation; it is functorial, multiplicative (⊗-Ind(ρ ⊗ ρ′) ≅ ⊗-Ind ρ ⊗ ⊗-Ind ρ′), compatible with coefficient extension and transitive in towers. If H is normal, its restriction to H is ⊗_{i} ρ^{t_i} (with ρ^{t}(h) = ρ(t^{-1} h t)). Trace formula: for g ∈ Γ with cycles C_1,…,C_r of π_g on Γ/H, of lengths ℓ_j and starting coset t_{i_j}H, tr(⊗-Ind ρ)(g) = ∏_j tr ρ(t_{i_j}^{−1} g^{ℓ_j} t_{i_j}). For m = 2, H = G_K ⊂ G_F = Γ (K/F quadratic), As(ρ) := ⊗-Ind_{G_K}^{G_F} ρ is the Asai representation: As(ρ)|_{G_K} ≅ ρ ⊗ ρ^σ, and As(ρ) ⊗ η_{K/F} is the other extension of ρ ⊗ ρ^σ to G_F.

**Hypotheses.**

- H open (so of finite index); no invertibility hypothesis on A
- the isomorphism class is independent of the transversal, the representation on a fixed model is not
- As(ρ) and As(ρ) ⊗ η_{K/F} are different extensions of ρ ⊗ ρ^σ; sources that do not distinguish them must say so

**Construction and proof.**

1. Monomial homomorphism Φ_t : Γ → H^m ⋊ S_m and its continuity for open H: ProfiniteCohomology layer 13 milestones 1–2 (requested); the action of the permutation wreath product H^m ⋊ S_m on V^{⊗m} (factors permuted, H^m acting factorwise) is a group action because the place-permutation action of S_m on PiTensorProduct commutes appropriately with ⊗_i ρ(h_i).
2. Change of transversal t′_i = t_i u_i (u_i ∈ H): the map ⊗_i ρ(u_i)^{−1} intertwines the two actions; canonicity follows from the cocycle identity of Φ under change of transversal.
3. Continuity: the matrix entries of ⊗-Ind ρ(g) are products of entries of ρ(h_i(g)), and g ↦ (h_i(g), π_g) is locally constant in π and continuous in h because H is open.
4. Restriction to normal H and the trace formula: compute Φ_t on H (π_h = id, h_i(h) = t_i^{−1} h t_i) and, for general g, the trace of a permuted tensor product is the product over cycles of traces of the cycle products (standard; CG20 and BCGP21 use only m = 2).
5. Asai case m = 2: As(ρ)|_{G_K} = ρ ⊗ ρ^σ by the restriction formula; the action of a lift of σ is the swap composed with ρ(σ^2) in one factor, as in CG20's explicit realisation.

**Prerequisites.** `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/continuous-representation`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/continuous-induction`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/restriction-dual-tensor-twist`; `mathlib:PiTensorProduct`; `mathlib:MonoidHom.transfer`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ProfiniteCohomology#layer-13-the-evens-norm`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/symmetric-and-exterior-powers`.

**Uses.**

- Calegari–Geraghty 2020, Example 4.11: ad⁰(Ind_K^Q ρ̄) ≅ As(ρ̄)ε^{k−1} ⊕ Ind ad⁰ ρ̄ (G7b big-image verification)
- Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni 2021, §7.5.16 and Lemma 7.5.17: decomposition of W ⊗ W, ad⁰(W) and ∧^2 W for W induced from index two, used for condition (E3)
- ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/gsp4-and-symplectic-induction: ad⁰ of a symplectic induction from an index-two subgroup
- PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:R24.5/system-operations: tensor induction of compatible systems, when used, is applied member by member

**API.**

- `TauCeti.ContinuousRep.tensorInd` (constructor): ⊗-Ind_H^Γ ρ for open H and a chosen transversal.
- `TauCeti.ContinuousRep.tensorIndEquivOfTransversal` (equivalence): Canonical isomorphism between the tensor inductions for two transversals, compatible with composition of changes.
- `TauCeti.ContinuousRep.tensorInd_rank` (structure): ⊗-Ind_H^Γ V is finite projective of rank (rank V)^{[Γ:H]}.
- `TauCeti.ContinuousRep.tensorInd_tprod` (compatibility): ⊗-Ind(ρ ⊗ ρ′) ≅ ⊗-Ind ρ ⊗ ⊗-Ind ρ′.
- `TauCeti.ContinuousRep.tensorInd_restrict_normal` (relation): For H normal, (⊗-Ind_H^Γ ρ)|_H ≅ ⊗_{i} ρ^{t_i}.
- `TauCeti.ContinuousRep.trace_tensorInd` (characterisation): The cycle-product trace formula for tr(⊗-Ind ρ)(g).
- `TauCeti.ContinuousRep.tensorInd_trans` (functoriality): Transitivity ⊗-Ind_K^Γ ⊗-Ind_H^K ≅ ⊗-Ind_H^Γ, and functoriality in Γ-maps.
- `TauCeti.ContinuousRep.asai` (constructor): As(ρ) := ⊗-Ind_{G_K}^{G_F} ρ for a quadratic extension K/F, with As(ρ) ⊗ η_{K/F} the other extension of ρ ⊗ ρ^σ.

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.ContinuousRep.tensorInd_index_one` (degenerate): For H = Γ, ⊗-Ind_Γ^Γ ρ ≅ ρ.
- `TauCeti.ContinuousRep.tensorInd_character` (characterisation): For a continuous character ψ : H → A^×, ⊗-Ind_H^Γ ψ = ψ ∘ Ver_{Γ→H}, the composition with Mathlib MonoidHom.transfer.
- `TauCeti.ContinuousRep.asai_restrict` (computation): For [Γ : H] = 2 and σ ∈ Γ ∖ H, As(ρ)|_H ≅ ρ ⊗ ρ^σ, rank n^2.
- `TauCeti.ContinuousRep.tensorInd_ne_ind` (non-example): For Γ = Z/2, H = 1 and V = A^2, ⊗-Ind V has rank 4 and the generator acts by the swap (trace 2), whereas Ind V has rank 4 with trace 0: tensor induction is not induction.

**Acceptance.**

- CG20, proof of Example 4.11: for K/Q imaginary quadratic and ρ: G_K → GL_2(F_p) with det ρ = ε^{1−k}, ad⁰(Ind_K^Q ρ) ≅ As(ρ) ⊗ ε^{k−1} ⊕ Ind_K^Q ad⁰(ρ) up to replacing As by its quadratic twist; the element c·(g, h) with g = diag(x, x^{−1}), h = diag(y, y^{−1}) acts on As with eigenvalues xy, (xy)^{−1}, ±1.
- BCGP21 §7.5.16: for W = Ind_H^G V with V two-dimensional, ∧^2 W ≅ k ⊕ k(χ) ⊕ As(V) ⊗ χ (characteristic ≠ 2).
- Degenerate: for m = 1, ⊗-Ind_Γ^Γ ρ = ρ; for V = A the trivial rank-one representation, ⊗-Ind V is trivial; for a character ψ of H, ⊗-Ind ψ = ψ ∘ Ver_{Γ→H} (the transfer).

**Sources.**

- cg20, §4, proof of Example 4.11, arXiv v1 p. 14: “where As is the Asai representation. Over Q(ζpm ) for any m, the character ǫk−1 is trivial,” — The Asai representation, the index-two tensor induction, appears in ad⁰ of an induced symplectic representation.
- bcgp21, §7.5.16, arXiv v3 p. 202: “Here As(V ) is the Asai representation, which satisﬁes As(V )|H = V ⊗ V σ . These” — The restriction formula As(V)|_H = V ⊗ V^σ that the construction must satisfy.

#### Restriction of scalars of the coefficients

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/restriction-of-scalars`. Kind: construction. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.ContinuousRep` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/Operations/RestrictionOfScalars`). Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7`.

Let A → B be a continuous homomorphism of topological commutative rings making B a finite projective A-module of constant rank r with the module topology (B's topology is the A-module topology), and let (M, ρ) ∈ ContinuousRep Γ B M of rank n. The restriction of scalars Res_{B/A} ρ is M regarded as an A-module with the same action; it is an object of ContinuousRep Γ A M of rank rn. Characteristic polynomials: det_A(X − ρ(g) | M) = N_{B[X]/A[X]}(det_B(X − ρ(g) | M)). If B is étale over A and A → A′ splits B (B ⊗_A A′ ≅ ∏_{σ ∈ Hom_A(B, A′)} A′), then (Res_{B/A} ρ) ⊗_A A′ ≅ ⊕_σ ρ ⊗_{B,σ} A′. For finite extensions E′/E of coefficient fields finite over Q_ℓ, Res_{E′/E} is the forgetful functor from E′-linear to E-linear continuous representations. Restriction of scalars along the base field (an abelian variety Res_{L/K} A) is not this construction: on Galois representations it is induction (R01.1/continuous-induction).

**Hypotheses.**

- B finite projective over A with the A-module topology (true for finite extensions of complete DVRs and of finite fields)
- the norm formula uses B[X] finite projective over A[X]
- the splitting statement needs B étale over A

**Construction and proof.**

1. The A-module M is finite projective since B is finite projective over A; the module topology over A agrees with that over B (transitivity of module topologies for finite modules), so joint continuity is unchanged.
2. Norm formula: for M free over B use the block matrix of ρ(g) over A obtained from an A-basis of B; det of the A-linear map equals N_{B/A} of the B-determinant (Mathlib Algebra.norm transitivity, det of restriction of scalars); for projective M localise.
3. Splitting: B ⊗_A A′ ≅ ∏_σ A′ gives M ⊗_A A′ ≅ M ⊗_B (B ⊗_A A′) ≅ ⊕_σ M ⊗_{B,σ} A′, Γ-equivariantly.

**Prerequisites.** `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/continuous-representation`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/coefficient-extension`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/frobenius-characteristic-polynomial`; `mathlib:IsModuleTopology`; `mathlib:LinearMap.charpoly`.

**Uses.**

- PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:R24.5/system-operations: changing the coefficient field of a compatible system: an E′-valued member viewed over E
- AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A6/tate-module-of-a-weil-restriction: contrast: base-field Weil restriction corresponds to induction, supplied by R01.1/continuous-induction
- ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/transfer-of-determinants-to-representations: determinants over A of B-representations are norms of B-determinants

**API.**

- `TauCeti.ContinuousRep.resScalars` (constructor): Res_{B/A} ρ for B finite projective over A.
- `TauCeti.ContinuousRep.resScalars_rank` (structure): rank_A Res_{B/A} M = rank_A B · rank_B M.
- `TauCeti.ContinuousRep.charpoly_resScalars` (characterisation): det_A(X − ρ(g)) = N_{B[X]/A[X]} det_B(X − ρ(g)).
- `TauCeti.ContinuousRep.resScalars_map` (functoriality): B-linear Γ-maps are A-linear Γ-maps; map_id, map_comp.
- `TauCeti.ContinuousRep.resScalarsBaseChangeEquiv` (equivalence): (Res_{B/A} ρ) ⊗_A A′ ≅ ⊕_σ ρ ⊗_{B,σ} A′ when A′ splits the étale A-algebra B.
- `TauCeti.ContinuousRep.resScalars_trans` (compatibility): Res_{C/A} = Res_{B/A} ∘ Res_{C/B}.

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.ContinuousRep.resScalars_self` (degenerate): Res_{A/A} ρ = ρ.
- `TauCeti.ContinuousRep.charpoly_resScalars` (computation): For B = A[√d] free with d ∈ A^× and a character ψ, det_A(X − ψ(g)) = X^2 − (ψ(g) + ψ(g)^σ)X + ψ(g)ψ(g)^σ.
- `TauCeti.ContinuousRep.resScalars_baseChange_split` (characterisation): If B ⊗_A A′ ≅ A′ × A′ then (Res_{B/A} ρ) ⊗_A A′ ≅ ρ ⊗_{σ_1} A′ ⊕ ρ ⊗_{σ_2} A′.
- `TauCeti.ContinuousRep.resScalars_ne_ind` (non-example): Res_{B/A} does not change Γ: it never coincides with induction Ind_{G_L}^{G_K}, which changes the group; for B = A it is the identity while Ind_{G_L}^{G_K} multiplies rank by [L:K].

**Acceptance.**

- For E′ = Q_ℓ(√u) unramified quadratic over E = Q_ℓ and a character ψ : Γ → E′^×, Res_{E′/E} ψ is two-dimensional with characteristic polynomial X^2 − Tr(ψ(g))X + N(ψ(g)), and after extending scalars to E′ it is ψ ⊕ ψ^{Frob}.
- For A = B the construction is the identity; for B = A^r (r copies) Res is the direct sum of the r components.

**Sources.**

- bcgp21, §2.2, arXiv v3 p. 18: “and the corresponding symplectic structure on this representation coincides with” — The Weil-restriction case is induction (the Tate module of Res_{K/F} E is the induction), which this node distinguishes from coefficient restriction.

#### The adjoint representation, the trace kernel and the quotient by scalars

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/adjoint-representations`. Kind: construction. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.ContinuousRep` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/Adjoint`). Planet: **Adjoint representations ad and ad⁰**. Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7`.

Let (M, ρ) ∈ ContinuousRep Γ A M of rank n ≥ 1. (i) ad ρ is End_A(M) with g·X = ρ(g) X ρ(g)^{−1} (Mathlib Representation.linHom ρ ρ), an object of ContinuousRep Γ A of rank n^2, canonically ≅ ρ ⊗ ρ^∨. (ii) The scalars A·1 ⊂ ad ρ form a trivial subrepresentation; the quotient ad ρ / A·1 (the pgl-module) is a ContinuousRep of rank n^2 − 1. (iii) The trace tr : ad ρ → A is Γ-equivariant onto the trivial representation; ad⁰ ρ := ker tr (the sl-module) is a ContinuousRep of rank n^2 − 1. (iv) The trace pairing (X, Y) ↦ tr(XY) on ad ρ is perfect and Γ-invariant, and induces a Γ-isomorphism ad⁰ ρ ≅ (ad ρ / A·1)^∨ for every A. (v) If n ∈ A^×, then ad ρ = A·1 ⊕ ad⁰ ρ, the composite ad⁰ ρ → ad ρ → ad ρ/A·1 is an isomorphism, and the trace pairing restricts to a perfect pairing on ad⁰ ρ, so ad⁰ ρ is self-dual. (vi) If A is a field of characteristic p with p | n, then A·1 ⊂ ad⁰ ρ, so ad⁰ ρ contains the trivial representation, ad⁰ ρ → ad ρ/A·1 has kernel and cokernel of rank one, and the trace pairing on ad⁰ ρ is degenerate with radical A·1. The three modules ad ρ, ad⁰ ρ and ad ρ/A·1 are kept distinct throughout. (vii) Lie-algebra form: when M = A^n these are gl_n, sl_n and pgl_n := gl_n/scalars with the adjoint action of GL_n(A) through ρ. (viii) For a Weil–Deligne representation (r, N) on V (R01.2), ad(r, N) := (ad r, [N, −]) on End(V), a Weil–Deligne representation.

**Hypotheses.**

- M finite projective of constant rank n ≥ 1
- no hypothesis on n for (i)–(iv); n ∈ A^× for (v)
- in (viii) the Weil–Deligne relation for ad follows from that of (r, N)

**Construction and proof.**

1. Use Representation.linHom ρ ρ (Mathlib) for the action; continuity of the action map as for ρ ⊗ ρ^∨ (G7/symmetric-and-exterior-powers and R01.1/restriction-dual-tensor-twist); over a normed field ContRepresentation.linHom (Tau Ceti) is the continuous counterpart and agrees in finite dimension.
2. Equivariance of the trace: tr(ρ(g) X ρ(g)^{−1}) = tr X. The trace form is nondegenerate on matrices over any commutative ring (TauCeti.traceBilinForm_nondegenerate); for finite projective M localise to the free case, so the trace pairing on End_A(M) is perfect.
3. Duality (iv): the annihilator of A·1 under the trace pairing is ker tr = ad⁰, so the perfect pairing on ad induces ad⁰ ≅ (ad/A·1)^∨.
4. Splitting (v): X ↦ (tr X / n)·1 is an equivariant projection onto A·1 with kernel ad⁰; nondegeneracy on ad⁰ follows from (iv) and ad⁰ ≅ ad/A·1.
5. (vi): tr(1) = n = 0 in A, so 1 ∈ ad⁰ and tr(1·Y) = tr Y = 0 for Y ∈ ad⁰.
6. (viii): if r(w) N r(w)^{−1} = q^{v′(w)} N (R01.2 normalisation) then r(w)[N, X]r(w)^{−1} = q^{v′(w)}[N, r(w)Xr(w)^{−1}], and [N, −] is nilpotent.

**Prerequisites.** `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/continuous-representation`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/restriction-dual-tensor-twist`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/weil-deligne-representation`; `mathlib:Representation.linHom`; `tauceti:ContRepresentation.linHom`; `tauceti:TauCeti.traceBilinForm`; `tauceti:TauCeti.traceBilinForm_nondegenerate`; `mathlib:LinearMap.trace`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/symmetric-and-exterior-powers`.

**Uses.**

- GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer:R17.4/adjoint-lift: the canonical adjoint representation, its scalar-quotient/traceless comparison in characteristic zero, and the adjoint of a Weil–Deligne parameter
- GlobalGaloisDeformations:G7/enormous-taylor-wiles-primes: ad ρ̄(1) and ad⁰ in the Taylor–Wiles dual Selmer groups
- ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/enormous-image-and-its-coefficient-extension-invariance: H^0(H, ad⁰) = H^1(H, ad⁰) = 0 and the p | n failure (G7b)
- Calegari–Geraghty 2018, §8.4: dim H^0(F_v, ad⁰ V) at real places (G7/oddness-at-real-places)
- Boxer–Calegari–Gee 2025, proof of Theorem 2.1: H^0(Q, (g⁰_n)^*(1)) = 0 via gl_n^{ss} ≅ ⊕ Sym^{2i} ρ̄_f ⊗ det^{−i}

**API.**

- `TauCeti.ContinuousRep.ad` (constructor): ad ρ on End_A(M) by conjugation.
- `TauCeti.ContinuousRep.adZero` (constructor): ad⁰ ρ := ker(tr : ad ρ → A).
- `TauCeti.ContinuousRep.adQuot` (constructor): ad ρ / A·1, the quotient by scalars.
- `TauCeti.ContinuousRep.adEquivTensorDual` (equivalence): ad ρ ≅ ρ ⊗ ρ^∨.
- `TauCeti.ContinuousRep.tracePairing_perfect` (relation): The trace pairing on ad ρ is perfect and Γ-invariant; it induces ad⁰ ρ ≅ (ad ρ/A·1)^∨.
- `TauCeti.ContinuousRep.adDecomp_of_invertible` (equivalence): If n ∈ A^×, ad ρ ≅ A ⊕ ad⁰ ρ and ad⁰ ρ ≅ ad ρ/A·1, and ad⁰ ρ is self-dual via the trace pairing.
- `TauCeti.ContinuousRep.one_mem_adZero_iff` (characterisation): 1 ∈ ad⁰ ρ iff n = 0 in A.
- `TauCeti.ContinuousRep.ad_baseChange` (compatibility): ad, ad⁰ and ad/A·1 commute with coefficient extension and with restriction to subgroups; ad(ρ ⊗ χ) = ad ρ for a character χ.
- `TauCeti.WeilDeligneRep.ad` (constructor): ad(r, N) = (ad r, [N, −]) for a Weil–Deligne representation (r, N).

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.ContinuousRep.ad_rank_one` (degenerate): For n = 1, ad ρ is the trivial rank-one representation, ad⁰ ρ = 0 and ad ρ/A·1 = 0.
- `TauCeti.ContinuousRep.adZero_equiv_symSq` (computation): For n = 2 with 2 ∈ A^×, ad⁰ ρ ≅ Sym^2 ρ ⊗ (det ρ)^{−1}.
- `TauCeti.ContinuousRep.adZero_dual_adQuot` (characterisation): For every A, the trace pairing identifies ad⁰ ρ with the dual of ad ρ/A·1.
- `TauCeti.ContinuousRep.ad_eq_linHom` (compatibility): The underlying representation of ad ρ is Representation.linHom ρ ρ (Mathlib).
- `TauCeti.ContinuousRep.scalar_mem_adZero_char_two` (non-example): Over k = F_2 with n = 2, the identity lies in ad⁰ ρ and ad⁰ ρ ↛ ad ρ/k·1 is not injective; a definition of ad⁰ as the complement of the scalars, or as ad/scalars, fails here.

**Acceptance.**

- For n = p = char k (e.g. n = 2, k = F_2), the identity matrix lies in sl_2(k), so H^0(H, ad⁰) ≠ 0 for every subgroup H; this is why ACC+ note that no subgroup of GL_n(k) is enormous when p | n.
- CHT08 §2.1: for 𝒢_n-valued r, ad extends to 𝒢_n on gl_n with ad(j)(x) = −ᵗx, and over Z[1/2] the 𝒢_n-invariants of gl_n vanish (G7/clozel-harris-taylor-group).

**Sources.**
