#### Verification criteria for adequacy: large characteristic, prime-to-p order, normal subgroups, tensor products, rank two and SL₂(p^r)

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/adequacy-criteria`. Kind: theorem. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.ResidualImage` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/ImageConditions/AdequacyCriteria`). Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7`.

Let p be a prime, k a field of characteristic p and H ⊆ GL_n(k) a finite subgroup; 'adequate' and 'GHT-adequate' are as in G7/adequate-subgroup. (1) (Guralnick–Herzig–Taylor–Thorne, appendix to Thorne 2012, Theorem 9, cited as Theorem A.9) Suppose H acts irreducibly on k̄^n, let H⁺ be the subgroup generated by the elements of p-power order (then k̄^n is a semisimple H⁺-module) and let d be the largest dimension of an irreducible H⁺-submodule of k̄^n. If p ≥ 2(d+1), then H⁰(H, ad⁰) = H¹(H, ad⁰) = H¹(H, k) = 0 and the semisimple elements of H span ad; hence H is adequate. In particular every absolutely irreducible H ⊆ GL_n(k) is adequate if p ≥ 2(n+1) (Thorne 2012, Lemma 2.4(ii); Newton–Thorne 2026, §2: p > 2n+2). (2) If p ∤ #H and H acts absolutely irreducibly, H is adequate (BLGG13 Remark A.1.2; GHTT Lemma 2(i)). (3) If N ⊴ H is adequate and p ∤ [H : N], then H is adequate (BLGG13 Lemma A.1.3); and if H acts irreducibly and some subgroup of H containing a Sylow p-subgroup of H is GHT-adequate on k^n, in particular if H⁺ is, then H is GHT-adequate (GHT17 Remark 6.1). (4) (BLGG13 Lemma A.3.1, Taylor) For a group Γ and representations r_i : Γ → GL_{n_i}(k̄), i = 1, 2, with r₁(Γ) adequate, r₂|_{ker r₁} irreducible and p ∤ #r₂(Γ), the image (r₁ ⊗ r₂)(Γ) is adequate; the same proof shows: if r₁(Γ) satisfies H¹(r₁(Γ), k̄) = 0, H¹(r₁(Γ), ad) = 0 and the spanning condition, so does (r₁ ⊗ r₂)(Γ) (Boxer–Calegari–Gee 2025, proof of Theorem 3.1). (5) (rank two; BLGG13 Proposition A.2.1 as corrected by sourceIssue E754, in agreement with Gee–Newton Lemma 3.2.3) If p > 2 and G ⊆ GL₂(F̄_p) is finite and irreducible on F̄_p², then G is adequate unless p = 3 and the image of G in PGL₂(F̄_3) is conjugate to PSL₂(F_3), or p = 5 and that image is conjugate to PSL₂(F_5). (6) (GHT17 Corollary 9.4) A nontrivial absolutely irreducible representation V of SL₂(F_{p^r}) over a field of characteristic p is GHT-adequate unless (i) r = 1 and 1 < dim V = (p ± 1)/2, (ii) p^r ∈ {2, 3, 4} and dim V = p^r, or (iii) p^r = 9 and dim V ∈ {3, 6, 9}.

**Hypotheses.**

- (1) needs H irreducible and p ≥ 2(d+1) with d computed for H⁺, not for H
- (4) needs p ∤ #r₂(Γ) and r₂ irreducible on ker r₁; tensor products of two adequate groups need not be adequate
- (5) is for p odd; p = 2 and n = 2 is excluded since then p | n
- (6) concerns GHT-adequacy; for p ∤ dim V it is Thorne-adequacy

**Construction and proof.**

1. (1): GHTT Theorem 9. dim V is prime to p (Clifford theory and [CR62, 51.7]); by Proposition 7 (which rests on the classification of finite simple groups) H is r(G(F_p)) for an algebraic group G = G⁰ ⋊ H₀ with G⁰ simply connected semisimple and p ∤ #H₀; H¹(H⁺, Hom(W_i, W_j)) = Ext¹ vanishes by Guralnick 1999, Theorem A, as dim W_i + dim W_j ≤ p − 2; then H¹(H, ad V) = 0 via the index-prime-to-p restriction, and the spanning statement follows from Lemma 3 and Lemma 8 on maximal tori. These two external inputs are recorded as a gap. The 'in particular' is Thorne 2012 Lemma 2.4(ii) with d ≤ n.
2. (2): BLGG13 Remark A.1.2: (A1) is trivial; p ∤ n since n divides #H (lift to characteristic 0); every element is semisimple and spans by Burnside; H¹ vanishes because #H is invertible (restriction to the trivial subgroup composed with corestriction is multiplication by #H: tauceti ProfiniteCohomology layer 6, cor ∘ res).
3. (3): BLGG13 Lemma A.1.3 by the inflation–restriction exact sequence (Mathlib groupCohomology.H1InfRes_exact) for N ⊴ H with ad^N = k·1, and GHT17 Remark 6.1 (spanning passes to overgroups; H¹ injects under restriction to a subgroup containing a Sylow p-subgroup, by cor ∘ res).
4. (4): BLGG13 Lemma A.3.1: with H_i = r_i(Γ), K_i = r_i(ker r_{3−i}) and Z the scalars z with (z, z⁻¹) in the image, H/K₂ ≅ H₁/Z; spanning is checked on A₁ ⊗ A₂ using r₂(ker r₁)-spans; H¹ by Hochschild–Serre: H¹(H/K₂, ad(r₁⊗r₂)^{K₂}) = H¹(H₁, ad r₁) = 0 and H¹(K₂, ·) = 0 as p ∤ #K₂.
5. (5): BLGG13 Proposition A.2.1 case analysis over Dickson's list (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/dickson-classification-and-the-dyadic-refinement): p ≥ 7 by (1) with d ≤ 2; prime-to-p projective images by (2); PSL₂/PGL₂(k) with |k| ≥ p² by reduction to SL₂(k) and G7/h1-of-sl2-with-adjoint-coefficients; p = 3 with PGL₂(F_3) or A₅ adequate; p = 3 with PSL₂(F_3) fails (A1); p = 5 with PSL₂(F_5) fails as H¹(SL₂(F_5), ad⁰) ≠ 0. For p = 5 with image PGL₂(F_5): replace G by k^×G and then by GL₂(F_5) (Lemmas A.1.3, A.1.4); H¹(GL₂(F_5), ad⁰) = 0 (G7/h1-of-sl2-with-adjoint-coefficients (b)), so G is adequate — the opposite of BLGG13's Point 5 (E754).
6. (6): GHT17 Corollary 9.4: r = 1 is [GHT, Cor. 1.4]; for r > 1, Ext¹_G(V,V) = 0 by Andersen–Jørgensen–Landrock [2, Cor. 4.5(a)], H¹(G,k) = 0 as G is perfect and H²(G,k) = 0 unless p^r ∈ {4, 9}; the cases p^r = 4, 9 are computed via tilting modules T(b₀) ⊗ T(b₁)^{(1)}. The AJL Ext computation is not in any library and is recorded as a gap.

#### The 'enormous' condition for Taylor–Wiles data, its failure when p divides n, and its invariance under coefficient extension

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/enormous-image-and-its-coefficient-extension-invariance`. Kind: definition. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.ResidualImage` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/ImageConditions/Enormous`). Planet: **Enormous image**. Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7`.

Let p be a prime, k an algebraic extension of F_p, n ≥ 1, and ad⁰ ⊆ M_n(k) the trace-zero matrices with the conjugation action of GL_n(k) (G7/adjoint-representations). An element h ∈ GL_n(k) is regular semisimple if its characteristic polynomial has n distinct roots in k̄ (equivalently is separable). An absolutely irreducible (R01.1/absolutely-irreducible) subgroup H ⊆ GL_n(k) is enormous over k (Allen et al. 2023, Definition 6.2.29; arXiv v2 Definition 6.2.28) if (1) H has no nontrivial quotient of p-power order; (2) H⁰(H, ad⁰) = H¹(H, ad⁰) = 0; (3) for every simple k[H]-submodule W ⊆ ad⁰ there is a regular semisimple h ∈ H with W^h ≠ 0. The condition depends only on the image of H in PGL_n(k). If p | n, no subgroup of GL_n(k) is enormous, because the scalar matrices lie in ad⁰ and are H-invariant. (Lemma 6.2.30; arXiv v2 Lemma 6.2.29) For an algebraic extension k'/k and H ⊆ GL_n(k), H is enormous over k if and only if it is enormous over k'; hence 'enormous' is used without 'over k'. (Remark 6.2.31) If k contains all eigenvalues of all elements of H, H is enormous iff it satisfies Khare–Thorne 2017, Definition 4.10: (1), (2) and (3') for every simple k[H]-submodule W ⊆ ad⁰ there are h ∈ H with n distinct eigenvalues in k and an eigenvalue α of h with tr(e_{h,α}W) ≠ 0. Relation with adequacy: if k contains all eigenvalues of the elements of a finite enormous H, then H is adequate (Gee–Newton, Remark 3.2.2, via bigness); for n = 2 and p odd, enormous and adequate coincide for irreducible finite H (Gee–Newton, Lemma 3.2.3). Enormous is not a synonym for adequate: for n ≥ 3 adequate groups need not contain any regular semisimple element.

**Hypotheses.**

- H must be absolutely irreducible as part of the definition, not merely irreducible
- condition (3) requires h to be regular semisimple; dropping regularity gives a different condition
- the condition cannot hold when p divides n; the source says so explicitly
- the equivalence with Khare–Thorne Definition 4.10 holds under the hypothesis that k contains all eigenvalues of the elements of H
- in the applications the group is the image of ρ̄ restricted to G_{F(ζ_p)}, not the image of ρ̄ itself
- H need not be finite in the definition, although in applications it is the image of a continuous representation into GL_n of a finite field

**Construction and proof.**

1. Lemma 6.2.30 (Allen et al.): only (3) needs attention, and it is equivalent to: for all nonzero k[H]-submodules W ⊆ ad⁰ there is a regular semisimple h ∈ H with W^h ≠ 0. In that form enormity over k' implies enormity over k.
2. Conversely, the property V^h = 0 is closed under direct sums and quotients (V^h ≠ 0 iff the coinvariants V_h ≠ 0, h acting semisimply). For V ⊆ ad⁰ ⊗_k k', σ h v = h σ v for σ ∈ Gal(k'/k) since H ⊆ GL_n(k), so V^h ≠ 0 iff (σV)^h ≠ 0. If W' is a simple k'[H]-submodule with (W')^h = 0 for every regular semisimple h (corrected reading, sourceIssue E752), the submodule generated by all σW' is stable under H and Gal(k'/k), hence by Galois descent is W ⊗_k k' for a k[H]-submodule W; (3) applied to a simple submodule of W gives a regular semisimple h with W^h ≠ 0, hence (W ⊗ k')^h ≠ 0, a contradiction. Conditions (1) and (2) are insensitive to k'/k because group cohomology commutes with the flat base change k → k' (finite-dimensional coefficients) and absolute irreducibility is invariant (R01.1/absolutely-irreducible).
3. Projective invariance: the conjugation action on ad⁰ factors through the image P of H in PGL_n(k); (1) passes between H and P because the kernel Z = H ∩ k^× consists of elements of order prime to p (k^× has no p-torsion); (2) by inflation–restriction (Mathlib groupCohomology.H1InfRes_exact): Z acts trivially on ad⁰ and is a torsion group without elements of order p, so H¹(Z, ad⁰) = Hom(Z, ad⁰) = 0 (ad⁰ is killed by p) and H^i(P, ad⁰) = H^i(H, ad⁰) for i = 0, 1; (3) is unchanged since regularity and fixed vectors are unchanged by scalars.
4. Remark 6.2.31: with all eigenvalues in k, a regular semisimple h is diagonalisable over k with one-dimensional eigenspaces, and W^h ≠ 0 iff tr(e_{h,α}W) ≠ 0 for some eigenvalue α (the projection to the h-fixed part of ad is X ↦ Σ_α e_{h,α}Xe_{h,α} and the trace pairing identifies W with its dual for ad⁰ when p ∤ n); compare Khare–Thorne Definition 4.10.
5. Enormous ⇒ adequate (k containing eigenvalues): Gee–Newton Remark 3.2.2 — enormous is big in the sense of CHT08 Definition 2.5.1 (a regular semisimple element has multiplicity-one eigenvalues), and big ⇒ adequate (Thorne 2012 Lemma 2.4(i)); (1) gives H¹(H, k) = 0. For n = 2, Gee–Newton Lemma 3.2.3: if tr(e_{h,α}W) ≠ 0 for W ⊆ ad⁰ then h has distinct eigenvalues (else e_{h,α} = 1 and tr W = 0).

**Prerequisites.** `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/adjoint-representations`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/absolutely-irreducible`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/coefficient-extension`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/adequate-subgroup`; `mathlib:groupCohomology.H0`; `mathlib:groupCohomology.H1`; `mathlib:groupCohomology.H1InfRes_exact`; `mathlib:Representation.invariants`; `mathlib:Matrix.charpoly`; `mathlib:Polynomial.Separable`; `mathlib:IsPGroup`; `mathlib:LieAlgebra.SpecialLinear.sl`; `mathlib:Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.center_eq_range_scalar`.

- `TauCeti.ResidualImage.isEnormous_iff_forall_submodule` (characterisation): Given (1) and (2), condition (3) holds iff for all nonzero k[H]-submodules W ⊆ ad⁰ there is a regular semisimple h ∈ H with W^h ≠ 0.

- `TauCeti.ResidualImage.isEnormous_baseChange_iff` (compatibility): For algebraic k'/k and H ≤ GL_n(k): IsEnormous H over k ↔ IsEnormous (H ≤ GL_n(k')) over k' (Lemma 6.2.30).
- `TauCeti.ResidualImage.isEnormous_iff_KT` (equivalence): If k contains all eigenvalues of all h ∈ H: IsEnormous H ↔ Khare–Thorne Definition 4.10 (Remark 6.2.31).
- `TauCeti.ResidualImage.IsEnormous.isAdequate` (relation): If H is finite, k contains all eigenvalues of its elements and IsEnormous H, then IsAdequate H.
- `TauCeti.ResidualImage.isEnormous_iff_isAdequate_of_two` (equivalence): For n = 2, p odd and H finite and irreducible with eigenvalues in k: IsEnormous H ↔ IsAdequate H.
- `TauCeti.ResidualImage.IsEnormous.eq_of_normal_pGroup_quotient` (relation): IsEnormous H → for N ⊴ H with H/N a p-group, N = H; applied to ρ̄(G_{F(ζ_{p^N})}) ⊴ ρ̄(G_{F(ζ_p)}) it gives equality of the images for all N ≥ 1.
- `TauCeti.ResidualImage.IsEnormous.map_conj` (simp): Enormity is invariant under conjugation by GL_n(k̄) and under multiplying H by scalars.

- `TauCeti.ResidualImage.not_isEnormous_SL2_ZMod3` (non-example): SL₂(ZMod 3) is not enormous: it has a quotient of order 3, although H⁰(SL₂(F_3), ad⁰) = H¹(SL₂(F_3), ad⁰) = 0. A definition omitting condition (1) (as in Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni's GSp₄ variant) accepts it.
- `TauCeti.ResidualImage.not_isEnormous_of_dvd` (non-example): If p ∣ n then ¬ IsEnormous H for every H ≤ GL_n(k).
- `TauCeti.ResidualImage.isEnormous_of_rank_one` (degenerate): For n = 1 every subgroup H ≤ GL₁(k) = k^× is enormous: ad⁰ = 0, and H has no p-torsion.
- `TauCeti.ResidualImage.not_isEnormous_Q8_tensor_Q8` (non-example): For p odd the image of Q₈ × Q₈ in GL₄(F̄_p) on the tensor product is adequate but not enormous; an identification of enormous with adequate fails this test.

**Acceptance.**

- SL₂(F_p) ⊆ GL₂(F_p) is enormous for every p ≥ 7: SL₂(F_p) is perfect (Mathlib Matrix.SL2.commutator_eq_top, as F_p has an element a with a² ≠ 1), ad⁰ = Sym² ⊗ det⁻¹ is absolutely irreducible with H⁰ = 0, H¹(SL₂(F_p), ad⁰) = 0 for p ≠ 5 (Darmon–Diamond–Taylor Lemma 2.48; G7/h1-of-sl2-with-adjoint-coefficients), and h = diag(a, a⁻¹) with a² ≠ 1 is regular semisimple and fixes diag(1, −1) ∈ ad⁰.
- SL₂(F_5) is not enormous (H¹(SL₂(F_5), ad⁰) is one-dimensional); SL₂(F_3) is not enormous (quotient of order 3, although H⁰ = H¹ = 0 for ad⁰); SL₂(F_2) is not enormous (2 | 2). GL₂(F_5) is enormous (H¹(GL₂(F_5), ad⁰) = 0, no quotient of order 5), so a subgroup of an enormous group need not be enormous.
- For n = p: the scalar matrix 1 has trace p = 0, so 1 ∈ ad⁰ is H-invariant and (2) fails for every H ⊆ GL_p(k).
- Not merely a synonym for adequacy: for p odd the image H of Q₈ × Q₈ in GL₄(F̄_p) acting on the tensor product of two copies of the two-dimensional representation has order 32, is irreducible and hence adequate (G7/adequacy-criteria (2)), but every element g ⊗ h has repeated eigenvalues (products of {±1} or {±i} with {±1} or {±i}), so H has no regular semisimple element and is not enormous.
- Lemma 6.2.30 check: SL₂(F_7) is enormous over F_7 and over F_49.

#### Enormous subgroups of GL_n(O) in characteristic zero (Newton–Thorne) and the Zariski-closure criterion

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/characteristic-zero-enormous-subgroups`. Kind: definition. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.ResidualImage` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/ImageConditions/EnormousCharZero`). Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7`.

Let E/Q_p be a finite extension with ring of integers O, n ≥ 1, and W_E = M_n(E) = ad ⊗_O E with H acting by conjugation. A subgroup H ⊆ GL_n(O) is enormous in the characteristic-zero sense (Newton–Thorne 2023, Definition 2.23) if for every simple E[H]-submodule V ⊆ W_E there are h ∈ H with n distinct eigenvalues in E and an eigenvalue α ∈ E of h with tr(e_{h,α}V) ≠ 0, where e_{h,α} is the h-equivariant projection onto the α-eigenspace. No vanishing of cohomology and no p-power-quotient condition is imposed, and the whole of W_E (not its trace-zero part) is tested. Facts: (Lemma 2.25) such H acts absolutely irreducibly on E^n, so H⁰(H, W⁰_E) = 0. (Lemma 2.28) Suppose H is compact and every h ∈ H has characteristic polynomial split over E. (1) If a closed subgroup H' ⊆ H is enormous, so is H. (2) If the identity component G° of the Zariski closure G ⊆ GL_n of H (G7/zariski-closure-and-monodromy-groups) contains regular semisimple elements and acts absolutely irreducibly on E^n, then H is enormous. Newton–Thorne 2026 (proof of Lemma 4.7) applies (2) through: if the derived subgroup G¹ of G° contains regular semisimple elements and acts absolutely irreducibly, and G¹ lies in the Zariski closure of H, then H is enormous. This notion is distinct from the residual notion of G7/enormous-image-and-its-coefficient-extension-invariance: it lives over a characteristic-zero field, has no cohomological conditions, and neither notion is deduced from the other.

**Hypotheses.**

- E has characteristic zero; the residual notion is a different definition
- Lemma 2.28 needs the characteristic polynomials of elements of H to split over E (enlarge E if necessary)
- regular semisimple elements of G° (an algebraic group over E), not merely of H, are required in Lemma 2.28(2)

**Construction and proof.**

1. Lemma 2.25: if U = {u ∈ W_E : tr(hu) = 0 for all h ∈ H} is nonzero, a simple submodule V of U violates the definition (tr(e_{h,α}V) = 0 since e_{h,α} is a polynomial in h); so H spans W_E and acts absolutely irreducibly by Burnside's theorem.
2. Lemma 2.28(1) is immediate from the definition. (2): reduce to G = G°; G(E) spans W_E by absolute irreducibility; the regular semisimple locus G^reg is a nonempty Zariski-open subset and H^reg = H ∩ G^reg is Zariski dense in G; if tr(hv) = 0 for all h ∈ H^reg then tr(gv) = 0 for all g ∈ G, so v = 0; projections e_{h,α} are polynomials in h.
3. Newton–Thorne 2026, Lemma 4.7: G¹ ⊆ Zariski closure of ρ(G_{K(ζ_{p^∞})}) (passage to derived subgroups commutes with Zariski closure, Borel Ch. I §2.4) and G° and G¹ have the same invariant subspaces, so Lemma 2.28 applies to ρ(G_{K(ζ_{p^∞})}).

**Prerequisites.** `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/zariski-closure-and-monodromy-groups`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/adjoint-representations`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/absolutely-irreducible`; `mathlib:Module.End.maxGenEigenspace`; `mathlib:Matrix.charpoly`; `mathlib:Polynomial.Separable`.

**Uses.**

- Newton–Thorne (2026), Lemma 4.7: (r ⊗ s)|G_K ⊗ r(G_{K(ζ_{p^∞})}) is enormous via Lemma 2.28 (NT26 item nt23-enormous-criterion)
- Newton–Thorne (2023), Theorems 2.30–2.31 and §4: enormous image of r_{π,ι}(G_{F(ζ_{p^∞})}) gives vanishing of adjoint Bloch–Kato Selmer groups; consumed by AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII and PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems

**API.**

- `TauCeti.ResidualImage.IsEnormousCharZero` (constructor): IsEnormousCharZero H : Prop for H ≤ GL_n(O), with the condition of Newton–Thorne Definition 2.23 on simple E[H]-submodules of M_n(E).
- `TauCeti.ResidualImage.IsEnormousCharZero.absolutelyIrreducible` (relation): Lemma 2.25: an enormous H acts absolutely irreducibly, so H⁰(H, ad⁰ ⊗ E) = 0.
- `TauCeti.ResidualImage.IsEnormousCharZero.mono` (relation): Lemma 2.28(1): H' ≤ H closed and enormous → H enormous (split characteristic polynomials).
- `TauCeti.ResidualImage.isEnormousCharZero_of_zariskiClosure` (characterisation): Lemma 2.28(2): if G° of the Zariski closure contains regular semisimple elements and acts absolutely irreducibly, H is enormous.
- `TauCeti.ResidualImage.isEnormousCharZero_of_derived` (characterisation): Newton–Thorne 2026 Lemma 4.7 form: derived subgroup of G° absolutely irreducible with regular semisimple elements and contained in the Zariski closure of H ⇒ H enormous.

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.ResidualImage.isEnormousCharZero_SL2` (computation): Every compact open subgroup of SL₂(Z_p) ⊆ GL₂(Z_p) is enormous in the characteristic-zero sense (Zariski closure SL₂ contains diag(a, a⁻¹), a² ≠ 1, and acts absolutely irreducibly).

**Acceptance.**

- Newton–Thorne 2023 Example 2.29: for π regular algebraic cuspidal on GL₂ over a totally real or CM field with Sym²π cuspidal, a model of Sym^{n−1} r_{π,ι} has ρ(G_{F(ζ_{p^∞})}) enormous (the Zariski closure contains Sym^{n−1}(SL₂), which has regular semisimple elements and acts irreducibly).
- A finite irreducible subgroup with no element of n distinct eigenvalues (the image of Q₈ × Q₈ on the four-dimensional tensor product, now over a p-adic field containing i) is not enormous in this sense; its Zariski closure is finite and contains no regular semisimple element.

#### Symmetric powers of groups containing SL₂(F_l) are enormous, and the Galois-theoretic consequence after restriction to F'(ζ_l)

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/enormous-symmetric-powers`. Kind: theorem. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.ResidualImage` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/ImageConditions/EnormousSymmetricPowers`). Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7`.

(1) (Gee–Newton, Lemma 3.2.5; Clozel–Harris–Taylor Corollary 2.5.4 with the corrected bound) Let n ≥ 2, p a prime with p > 2n + 1, k an algebraic extension of F_p, k' ⊆ k a finite subfield and H ⊆ GL_n(k) with k^× · Sym^{n−1}GL₂(k') ⊇ H ⊇ Sym^{n−1}SL₂(k'), where Sym^{n−1} : GL₂ → GL_n is the symmetric power of G7/symmetric-and-exterior-powers in the monomial basis. Then H is enormous. (2) (Allen et al. 2023, Lemma 7.1.4, with the codomain corrected to GL_n, sourceIssue E751) If n ≥ 2, l > 2n + 1 and H ⊆ GL₂(F̄_l) is a finite subgroup containing SL₂(F_l), then Sym^{n−1}H ⊆ GL_n(F̄_l) is enormous. (3) (Allen et al. 2023, Lemma 7.1.6(2); Qian 2023, Lemma 2.6(1)) Let F/Q be finite with normal closure F̃, m ≥ 1, l > 2m + 3 a prime, r̄ : G_F → GL₂(F̄_l) continuous with r̄(G_{F̃}) ⊇ SL₂(F_l), and F'/F a finite extension linearly disjoint from F̄^{ker r̄} over F. Then (Sym^m r̄)(G_{F'(ζ_l)}) is enormous. Qian's form (n = m + 1, l > 2n + 5) is the special case with a stronger bound; for n = 1 the image is trivial in GL₁ and enormous. (4) (Gee–Newton, Lemma 3.2.4) If n > 2, p > n, k' ⊆ k is a finite subfield and k^× · GL_n(k') ⊇ H ⊇ SL_n(k'), then H is enormous.

**Hypotheses.**

- the bound is p > 2n + 1 (l > 2m + 3 for Sym^m); Clozel–Harris–Taylor print l > 2n − 1, which fails for n = 2, l = 5 (sourceIssue E756)
- (3) needs SL₂(F_l) ⊆ r̄(G_{F̃}) with F̃ the normal closure, and linear disjointness from the field cut out by r̄ itself, not by ad r̄
- the subgroup in (3) is the image of G_{F'(ζ_l)}, not of G_{F'}

**Construction and proof.**

1. (1), condition (2) of enormity: as SL₂(k')-modules ad Sym^{n−1} ≅ ⊕_{i=0}^{n−1} Sym^{2i} ⊗ det^{−i} (G7/mod-p-clebsch-gordan-decompositions (d), valid as 2n − 2 < p), each Sym^{2i} irreducible (G7/adjoint-invariants-of-symmetric-powers (a)); so H⁰(Sym^{n−1}SL₂(k'), ad⁰) = 0, and H¹(SL₂(k'), Sym^{2i}) = 0 for 1 ≤ i ≤ n − 1 because 2i ≤ 2n − 2 < p − 3 (G7/h1-of-sl2-with-adjoint-coefficients (c)); pass from Sym^{n−1}SL₂(k') to H since the index is prime to p up to scalars (inflation–restriction and cor ∘ res, Mathlib groupCohomology.H1InfRes_exact, tauceti ProfiniteCohomology layer 6). Condition (1): PSL₂(k') is simple and the quotient of H by Sym^{n−1}SL₂(k')·(scalars) has order dividing #k'^× · 2. Condition (3): Clozel–Harris–Taylor Lemma 2.5.2 — the diagonal torus generator t of SL₂(k') has n distinct eigenvalues on Sym^{n−1} (n < p) and each Sym^{2i} meets the t-fixed part D = ⊕ Hom(V_j, V_j) in a line (Gee–Newton: these eigenspaces are one-dimensional, so t is regular semisimple).
2. (2): Dickson (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/dickson-classification-and-the-dyadic-refinement): the image of H in PGL₂(F̄_l) is conjugate to PSL₂(k) or PGL₂(k) for a finite k ⊇ F_l, so F̄_l^× Sym^{n−1}GL₂(k) ⊇ Sym^{n−1}H ⊇ Sym^{n−1}SL₂(k), and (1) applies with k' = k.
3. (3): linear disjointness gives r̄(G_{F'}) = r̄(G_F) ⊇ r̄(G_{F̃}) ⊇ SL₂(F_l); SL₂(F_l) is perfect for l ≥ 5 (Mathlib Matrix.SL2.commutator_eq_top) and Gal(F'(ζ_l)/F') is abelian, so r̄(G_{F'(ζ_l)}) ⊇ SL₂(F_l) (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/restriction-to-the-cyclotomic-field); apply (2) with n = m + 1, l > 2n + 1 = 2m + 3.
4. (4): Gee–Newton Lemma 3.2.4 from the proof of Clozel–Harris–Taylor Lemma 2.5.6 (bigness of groups between SL_n(k') and k^×GL_n(k')), plus a regular semisimple element of SL_n(k'): the companion matrix of X^n + (−1)^n, which has n distinct roots as p > n.

**Prerequisites.** `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/enormous-image-and-its-coefficient-extension-invariance`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/symmetric-and-exterior-powers`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/mod-p-clebsch-gordan-decompositions`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/adjoint-invariants-of-symmetric-powers`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/h1-of-sl2-with-adjoint-coefficients`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/dickson-classification-and-the-dyadic-refinement`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/restriction-to-the-cyclotomic-field`; `mathlib:Matrix.SL2.commutator_eq_top`; `mathlib:Matrix.ProjectiveSpecialLinearGroup.rank_two_simple`; `mathlib:groupCohomology.H1InfRes_exact`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ProfiniteCohomology#layer-6-change-of-groups`.

**Acceptance.**

- n = 2, (2): every finite H ⊆ GL₂(F̄_l) containing SL₂(F_l) is enormous for l ≥ 7; for l = 5 the bound l > 5 fails and indeed SL₂(F_5) is not enormous (H¹(SL₂(F_5), ad⁰) ≠ 0), which shows the printed Clozel–Harris–Taylor bound l > 2n − 1 = 3 is too weak.
- n = 3, l = 11 (> 7): Sym²(SL₂(F_11)) ≅ SO₃-image in GL₃(F_11) is enormous; ad⁰ Sym² = Sym² ⊕ Sym⁴ (twists) and H¹(SL₂(F_11), Sym^{2i}) = 0 for i = 1, 2 since 2, 4 ≠ 11 − 3.
- (3) for an elliptic curve E/Q without CM and l ≥ 7 with r̄_{E,l}(G_Q) = GL₂(F_l), F = F' = Q, m = 1: r̄_{E,l}(G_{Q(ζ_l)}) = SL₂(F_l) is enormous.

#### H¹(SL₂(F), ad⁰) vanishes unless #F = 5, and the symmetric-power vanishing behind the bound p > 2n + 1

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/h1-of-sl2-with-adjoint-coefficients`. Kind: lemma. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.ResidualImage` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/ImageConditions/SL2Cohomology`). Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7`.

Let F be a finite field of odd characteristic p and ad⁰ = End⁰(F²) = sl₂(F) with the conjugation action. (a) (Darmon–Diamond–Taylor, Lemma 2.48) If #F ≠ 5 then H¹(SL₂(F), ad⁰) = 0; also H⁰(SL₂(F), ad⁰) = 0. (b) For F = F_5, H¹(SL₂(F_5), ad⁰) is one-dimensional over F_5, while H¹(GL₂(F_5), ad⁰) = 0 and H¹(GL₂(F_5), ad⁰ ⊗ det²) is one-dimensional; consequently H¹(G, ad⁰) = 0 for every G ⊆ GL₂(F̄_5) whose image in PGL₂(F̄_5) is conjugate to PGL₂(F_5), and H¹(G, ad⁰) ≠ 0 when that image is PSL₂(F_5). (c) (input to Clozel–Harris–Taylor Corollary 2.5.4, with the corrected bound) If n ≥ 2, p > 2n + 1 and F ⊇ F_p is finite, then H¹(SL₂(F), Sym^{2i}(F̄_p²)) = 0 for 1 ≤ i ≤ n − 1. In particular H¹(SL₂(F_p), ad⁰) = 0 for p ≥ 7 is the case n = 2 of (c) and of (a).

**Hypotheses.**

- p odd; for p = 2, ad⁰ contains the scalars
- #F = 5 is a genuine exception in (a), not an artefact of the proof
- (c) needs 2i ≠ p − 3 for all i ≤ n − 1, which p > 2n + 1 guarantees; the module Sym^{p−3} has nonzero H¹ (computed: dim H¹(SL₂(F_p), Sym^a) = 1 for a = p − 3 and 0 for the other 0 ≤ a ≤ p − 1, p = 5, 7, 11)

**Construction and proof.**

1. (a): Darmon–Diamond–Taylor Lemma 2.48: p ∤ [SL₂(F) : B] for the Borel B, so H¹(SL₂(F), ad⁰) → H¹(B, ad⁰) is injective (cor ∘ res, tauceti ProfiniteCohomology layer 6); H¹(B, M) = H¹(U, M)^{B/U} for the unipotent radical U; filter ad⁰ by B-stable lines M₁ ⊆ M₂ ⊆ M₃ and compute with long exact sequences; #F = 3 is done directly with the norm element, and #F = 9 needs the connecting homomorphism H¹(U, M₃/M₂)^{B/U} → H²(U, M₂/M₁) to be injective. H⁰ = 0 because ad⁰ is irreducible and nontrivial for p odd.
2. (b): the p = 5 value is Cline–Parshall–Scott table 4.5 (cited by Darmon–Diamond–Taylor and by BLGG13, Point 5); in this job it was checked by computing cocycles on the Cayley graph of each group over F_5 (a direct linear-algebra computation of the cocycle space): dim H¹ = 0, 1, 0, 0, 0 for SL₂(F_p), p = 3, 5, 7, 11, 13; dim H¹(GL₂(F_p), ad⁰) = 0 for p = 3, 5, 7; dim H¹(GL₂(F_5), ad⁰ ⊗ det^j) = 0, 0, 1, 0 for j = 0, 1, 2, 3; dim H¹({det = ±1} ⊆ GL₂(F_5), ad⁰) = 1. The PGL₂(F_5) statement follows by replacing G with k^×G and then GL₂(F_5) (index prime to 5, inflation–restriction).
3. (c): Clozel–Harris–Taylor, proof of Corollary 2.5.4: restrict to the Borel and its Sylow p-subgroup U, H¹(SL₂(F), Sym^{2i}) ↪ H¹(U, Sym^{2i})^B, which vanishes by Cline–Parshall–Scott Lemma 2.7(c) when 2i ≤ 2n − 2 < p − 3. The printed hypothesis l > n + 1 there is too weak (it would include n = 2, l = 5, contradicting (b)); Cline–Parshall–Scott was not read in this job and the statement is recorded as a gap.

**Prerequisites.** `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/adjoint-representations`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/symmetric-and-exterior-powers`; `mathlib:groupCohomology.H1`; `mathlib:groupCohomology.H1InfRes_exact`; `mathlib:Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ProfiniteCohomology#layer-6-change-of-groups`.

**Acceptance.**

- Computed: dim H¹(SL₂(F_p), ad⁰) = 0, 1, 0, 0, 0 for p = 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, matching (a) and the exception p = 5 that Calegari–Dimitrov–Tang's proof of Lemma 4.5.6 excludes.
- Computed: H¹(GL₂(F_5), ad⁰) = 0 but H¹(GL₂(F_5), ad⁰ ⊗ det²) ≠ 0, so the group GL₂(F_5) is adequate and enormous while SL₂(F_5) is neither.
- For p = 2, SL₂(F_2) ≅ S₃ acting on the trace-zero matrices (which contain the scalars) has H⁰ and H¹ both one-dimensional, so the odd-characteristic hypothesis is needed.
- Computed by this job (direct linear algebra on the cocycle space): for p = 5, 7, 11 and 0 ≤ a ≤ p − 1, H¹(SL₂(F_p), Sym^a(F_p²)) is one-dimensional for a = p − 3 and zero otherwise; so (c) holds for F = F_p, p ≤ 11, and the bound p > 2n + 1 is sharp (n = (p − 1)/2 gives 2(n − 1) = p − 3).

**Sources.**

- ddt-fermat, Lemma 2.48, Current Developments version, PDF p. 82: “Lemma 2.48 Let F be a finite field of odd characteristic `. If #F 6= 5, then” — (a); the text layer renders ℓ as a backquote and ≠ as '6='.
- ddt-fermat, Lemma 2.48: “H 1 (SL2 (F), End 0 (F2 )) = 0.” — The conclusion of (a).

- blgg13-serre-weights, proof of Proposition A.2.1, Point 5, arXiv v1 p. 34: “Point 5. Next we consider the case where l = 5 and Ḡ is PSL2 (F5 ) or PGL2 (F5 ).” — H¹ is one-dimensional for projective image PSL₂(F_5) (CPS table 4.5); the PGL₂(F_5) half of Point 5 is wrong (E754).
- cht08, proof of Corollary 2.5.4, p. 57: “As l > n + 1 it follows from Lemma (2.7) c) of [CPS] that for i = 0, ..., n − 1 we” — (c) with the printed, too weak, bound.

#### Mod p Clebsch–Gordan decompositions: V ⊗ Sym^{r−1}V, the two-constituent congruence for Sym^{p+r−1}V, and End(Sym^{n−1}V)

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/mod-p-clebsch-gordan-decompositions`. Kind: theorem. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.ResidualImage` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/ImageConditions/ClebschGordan`). Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7`.

Let k be a field, Γ a group and V a two-dimensional representation of Γ over k; Sym^a is G7/symmetric-and-exterior-powers, det = ∧²V, and (·)^ss is R01.1/semisimplification. (a) (Newton–Thorne 2026, (1.3)) If r ≥ 2 and r is invertible in k (in characteristic p: p ∤ r, in particular 1 < r < p), then V ⊗ Sym^{r−1}V ≅ Sym^rV ⊕ (det ⊗ Sym^{r−2}V) as representations of Γ; for r = 1, V ⊗ Sym⁰V ≅ V. (b) (Newton–Thorne 2026, (1.1); Clozel–Thorne 2017, (1.1) for p = 7, r = 2, and proof of Theorem 6.2 for r = 2, general l) Let k ⊇ F_p be perfect, 0 < r < p, and let Frob V be the coefficient Frobenius twist of V (R01.1/coefficient-frobenius-twist: matrix entries raised to the p-th power; for a Galois representation, the action of an arithmetic Frobenius lift φ_p on coefficients). Then (Sym^{p+r−1}V)^ss ≅ (det^{⊗r} ⊗ Sym^{p−r−1}V)^ss ⊕ (Frob V ⊗ Sym^{r−1}V)^ss; this is an identity after semisimplification only. (c) (Boxer–Calegari–Gee 2025, proof of Theorem 2.1) For every n ≥ 1, (End(Sym^{n−1}V))^ss ≅ ⊕_{i=0}^{n−1} (Sym^{2i}V ⊗ det^{−i})^ss. (d) (Clozel–Harris–Taylor, proof of Lemma 2.5.2) If char k = p > 2n − 2 and Γ acts through SL₂(F_p) ⊆ SL₂(k), then ad Sym^{n−1}V ≅ ⊕_{i=0}^{n−1} Sym^{2i}V as representations (not only after semisimplification), each summand irreducible.

**Hypotheses.**

- (a) needs r invertible in k; it is a genuine isomorphism
- (b) is only an isomorphism of semisimplifications; Sym^{p+r−1}V is in general a non-split extension
- (b) uses the coefficient Frobenius twist, not restriction to a decomposition group or a Frobenius element of Γ
- (c) holds for all n after semisimplification; (d) needs p > 2n − 2

**Construction and proof.**

1. (a): the comultiplication Δ : Sym^rV → V ⊗ Sym^{r−1}V, F ↦ x ⊗ ∂_xF + y ⊗ ∂_yF (natural in V, hence Γ-equivariant) and multiplication m : V ⊗ Sym^{r−1}V → Sym^rV satisfy m ∘ Δ = r·id (Euler's identity), so r⁻¹Δ splits m; the map det ⊗ Sym^{r−2}V → V ⊗ Sym^{r−1}V, (x∧y) ⊗ G ↦ x ⊗ yG − y ⊗ xG, is Γ-equivariant, injective, lands in ker m, and dimensions match (2r − (r+1) = r − 1).
2. (b): by R01.1/brauer-nesbitt it suffices that both sides have the same characteristic polynomial for each γ ∈ Γ. If γ has eigenvalues a, b on V (in k̄), Sym^{p+r−1}V has eigenvalues a^i b^{p+r−1−i}, 0 ≤ i ≤ p+r−1; det^r ⊗ Sym^{p−r−1}V contributes the exponents r ≤ i ≤ p − 1, and Frob V ⊗ Sym^{r−1}V (eigenvalues a^p, b^p on Frob V) contributes i = p + j and i = j for 0 ≤ j ≤ r − 1; the multisets agree.
3. (c): same method: End(Sym^{n−1}V) = Sym^{n−1}V ⊗ (Sym^{n−1}V)^∨ has eigenvalues (a/b)^m with multiplicity n − |m| for |m| ≤ n − 1, and ⊕_i Sym^{2i}V ⊗ det^{−i} has eigenvalues (a/b)^m, |m| ≤ i, again with multiplicity n − |m|.
4. (d): Clozel–Harris–Taylor: semisimplicity of ad Sym^{n−1} as an SL₂(F_p)-module follows from Serre's semisimplicity theorem for small modules ([Se2] there), and Sym^{2i} is irreducible for 2i ≤ p − 1 (G7/adjoint-invariants-of-symmetric-powers (a)); combine with (c). For the Clozel–Thorne case a = 1 of their discussion: if Γ acts through SL₂(F_p) then Frob V ≅ V and Frob V ⊗ V = Sym²V ⊕ det contains det, so the first constituent of (b) is not irreducible.

**Prerequisites.** `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/symmetric-and-exterior-powers`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/adjoint-representations`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/brauer-nesbitt`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/semisimplification`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/coefficient-frobenius-twist`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/restriction-dual-tensor-twist`.

**Acceptance.**

- Clozel–Thorne (1.1): p = 7, r = 2 gives Sym⁸V ~ (Frob V ⊗ V) ⊕ det² ⊗ Sym⁴V, dimensions 9 = 4 + 5.
- (a) with r = 2: V ⊗ V ≅ Sym²V ⊕ det for p odd; for p = 2 this fails (V ⊗ V is not semisimple for SL₂(F_2) acting on F̄_2², the case r = p excluded by the hypothesis).
- (c) with n = 2: End(V)^ss ≅ 1 ⊕ (Sym²V ⊗ det⁻¹)^ss, i.e. ad = k ⊕ ad⁰ after semisimplification, which is an honest splitting exactly when p ≠ 2.

**Sources.**

- nt26, Introduction, (1.3), arXiv v2 p. 4: “(1.3)         rπ,ι ⊗ Symr−1 r σ,ι ∼” — (a), displayed for Galois representations.
- nt26, Introduction, (1.1), arXiv v2 p. 3: “(where ϕp ∈ GFp is the arithmetic Frobenius, and we are twisting the coefficients;” — (b): the twist is on coefficients.
- nt26, Introduction after (1.1): “the superscript ss indicates that there is in fact only an isomorphism after passage” — (b) holds only after semisimplification.
- ct17, (1.1), accepted manuscript p. 2: “Sym8 r ∼ (ϕ r ⊗ r) ⊕ χ2 Sym4 r.” — The case p = 7, r = 2.
- ct17, after (1.1): “Here χ is the determinant of r, and ϕ is the Frobenius endomorphism acting on the coefficients. Since, as” — Coefficient Frobenius and determinant.
- bcg25-gln, proof of Theorem 2.1, published pp. 513–514: “verify that H 0 (Q, (g0n )∗ (1)) = 0, where g0n is respectively spn or son according to” — (c) is used there after semisimplification.

#### Irreducibility of small symmetric powers of SL₂(F) and the one-dimensional constituents of their adjoints

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/adjoint-invariants-of-symmetric-powers`. Kind: theorem. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.ResidualImage` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/ImageConditions/SymmetricPowerAdjoint`). Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7`.

Let p be a prime and F a finite field of characteristic p, with SL₂(F) acting on F̄_p² by the standard representation. (a) For 0 ≤ a ≤ p − 1, Sym^a(F̄_p²) is an absolutely irreducible representation of SL₂(F); hence if r̄ : Γ → GL₂(F̄_p) has SL₂(F_p) ⊆ r̄(Γ) and 1 ≤ n ≤ p, every twist of Sym^{n−1} r̄ by a character is absolutely irreducible (Boxer–Calegari–Gee 2025, proof of Theorem 2.1). (b) (ibid., p. 514) Let p be odd. For 0 ≤ i ≤ p − 1, the one-dimensional composition factors of Sym^{2i}(F̄_p²) as an SL₂(F)-module occur with multiplicity at most one, and only for i = 0, for 2i = p + 1 (only when F = F_p) and for 2i = 2p − 2. (c) (ibid., pp. 513–514) Let p > 3, 1 ≤ n ≤ p, r̄ : G_Q → GL₂(F̄_p) continuous with SL₂(F_p) ⊆ r̄(G_Q), and ρ̄ = Sym^{n−1} r̄ ⊗ ψ for a character ψ. Then every one-dimensional constituent χ of (ad ρ̄)^ss satisfies χ² = 1, and therefore H⁰(G_Q, M(1)) = 0 for every G_Q-subquotient M of ad ρ̄ or of its dual; in particular H⁰(Q, (𝔤⁰_n)^*(1)) = 0 for the Lie algebra 𝔤⁰_n = 𝔰𝔭_n or 𝔰𝔬_n of the similitude group preserved by ρ̄.

**Hypotheses.**

- (a) fails for a = p: Sym^p contains the Frobenius twist of the standard representation as a proper submodule
- (b) is about composition factors (semisimplification), not submodules
- (c) needs p > 3 so that the mod p cyclotomic character satisfies ε̄^{−2} ≠ 1

**Construction and proof.**

1. (a): Sym^a for a ≤ p − 1 is the restricted simple module L(a) of SL₂ over F̄_p and stays simple on SL₂(F) for every finite F ⊇ F_p (Steinberg restriction; Clozel–Harris–Taylor proof of Lemma 2.5.2 uses the same fact for F = F_l); twisting by a character preserves absolute irreducibility; the image r̄(Γ) contains SL₂(F_p).
2. (b): compute composition factors of Sym^{2i} for 0 ≤ 2i ≤ 2p − 2 via G7/mod-p-clebsch-gordan-decompositions (b) for 2i ≥ p (Sym^{p+r−1} has constituents det^r ⊗ Sym^{p−r−1} and Frob ⊗ Sym^{r−1}); a one-dimensional constituent arises from Sym^{p−r−1} with r = p − 1 (2i = 2p − 2) or from Frob V ⊗ V ⊇ det when F = F_p and r = 2 (2i = p + 1). The Boxer–Calegari–Gee extraction checked this with Brauer characters for p = 7, 11, 13 and F = F_{p²}, p = 5, 7.
3. (c): Boxer–Calegari–Gee: (𝔤⁰_n)^{*,ss} ⊆ (gl_n^*)^ss ≅ gl_n^ss ≅ ⊕_{i=0}^{n−1} (Sym^{2i} r̄)^ss ⊗ det(r̄)^{−i} (G7/mod-p-clebsch-gordan-decompositions (c)); by (b) the one-dimensional constituents are self-dual characters, and ε̄^{−1} is not self-dual for p > 3 (ε̄ has order p − 1 > 2 on G_Q); H⁰ of a subquotient injects into H⁰ of the semisimplification's one-dimensional part.

**Prerequisites.** `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/mod-p-clebsch-gordan-decompositions`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/symmetric-and-exterior-powers`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/adjoint-representations`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/absolutely-irreducible`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/semisimplification`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/cyclotomic-and-dirichlet-characters`; `mathlib:Representation.invariants`.

**Acceptance.**

- p = 7, F = F_7: Sym^0 = 1, Sym^8 (2i = p + 1) contains det-type constituent once, Sym^12 (2i = 2p − 2) contains one, and no other Sym^{2i} with i ≤ 6 has a one-dimensional constituent.
- (c) fails for p = 3: ε̄^{−1} has order 2 and is self-dual, so the vanishing argument does not apply.

**Sources.**

- bcg25-gln, proof of Theorem 2.1, published p. 513: “Since SL2 (Fp ) ⊆ ρf (GQ ), the representation ρ is absolutely irreducible (see also” — (a).
- bcg25-gln, proof of Theorem 2.1, published p. 514: “From the representation theory of SL2 (F), we see that the only characters occur-” — (b).
- bcg25-gln, proof of Theorem 2.1, published p. 514: “acters that arise are in particular self-dual, and so distinct from ε−1 since p > 3.” — (c).
- cht08, proof of Lemma 2.5.2, p. 56: “(That ad Symmn−1 is semi-simple follows for instance from [Se2].) As 2n − 2 ≤ l − 1” — Irreducibility of each Sym^{2i} for 2i ≤ l − 1.

#### Adequacy of symmetric powers and Frobenius-twisted tensor products of large SL₂ images, with one common threshold

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/adequacy-of-symmetric-powers`. Kind: theorem. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.ResidualImage` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/ImageConditions/AdequateSymmetricPowers`). Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7`.

(1) (Boxer–Calegari–Gee 2025, Lemma 2.2) Let p > 5 and r̄ : G_Q → GL₂(F̄_p) continuous with SL₂(F_p) ⊆ r̄(G_Q). For p − 2 ≤ n ≤ p, the group (Sym^{n−1} r̄)(G_{Q(ζ_p)}) is GHT-adequate (Thorne 2017, Definition 2.20); for n = p − 2, p − 1 it is adequate in the sense of Thorne 2012. (2) (Newton–Thorne 2026, Lemma 2.3, quoting Thorne 2024, Lemma 7.3; common threshold) Let p ≥ 5 and φ_p ∈ G_{Q_p} a lift of arithmetic Frobenius. There is an integer a₀ = a₀(p) ≥ 3 such that for every a ≥ a₀ and every finite G ⊆ GL₂(F̄_p) containing a conjugate of SL₂(F_{p^a}): (i) for each 0 < r < p, the image of Sym^{r−1} : G → GL_r(F̄_p) is adequate (Thorne 2012, Definition 2.3); (ii) for each 0 < r < p, the image of φ_p Std ⊗ Sym^{r−1} : G → GL_{2r}(F̄_p) is adequate, φ_p acting on the coefficients of the first factor only; (iii) every subgroup of G of index < 2p contains a conjugate of SL₂(F_{p^a}) and so satisfies (i) and (ii). One a₀(p) is chosen for (i)–(iii) simultaneously; where Newton–Thorne require a > a₀(p), that strict inequality is kept. (3) (from G7/adequacy-criteria (1)) If SL₂(F_p) ⊆ r̄(Γ) and p ≥ 2n + 2, then (Sym^{n−1} r̄)(Γ') is adequate for every Γ' ⊆ Γ with SL₂(F_p) ⊆ r̄(Γ').

**Hypotheses.**

- (1): n = p is divisible by p, so only GHT-adequacy (quotient by scalars) can hold there
- (2)(ii) twists only the first factor by the coefficient Frobenius (R01.1/coefficient-frobenius-twist)
- (2)(iii) is the group-theoretic statement of ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/large-image-persistence, quoted here for the common threshold

**Construction and proof.**

1. (1): Boxer–Calegari–Gee: SL₂(F_p) is perfect, so SL₂(F_p) ⊆ r̄(G_{Q(ζ_p)}); by Dickson (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/dickson-classification-and-the-dyadic-refinement) SL₂(F_q) ⊆ r̄(G_{Q(ζ_p)}) for a power q of p with index prime to p up to scalars; by GHT17 Remark 6.1 (G7/adequacy-criteria (3)) it suffices that V = Sym^{n−1}U is GHT-adequate for SL₂(F_q); V is absolutely irreducible as n ≤ p (G7/adjoint-invariants-of-symmetric-powers (a)) and is not in the exceptional list of GHT17 Corollary 9.4 since n ≥ p − 2 > (p+1)/2 for p > 5 (G7/adequacy-criteria (6)). For n < p, p ∤ n and GHT-adequacy is Thorne-adequacy (G7/adequate-subgroup).
2. (2): Newton–Thorne quote Thorne 2024 Lemma 7.3, which was not read in this job. A proof along the same lines as (1): by Dickson G has projective image PSL₂(F_{p^b}) or PGL₂(F_{p^b}) with b ≥ a, so up to scalars and index prime to p it contains SL₂(F_{p^b}); Sym^{r−1} = L(r−1) and φ_p Std ⊗ Sym^{r−1} = L(1)^{(1)} ⊗ L(r−1) = L(p + r − 1) (Steinberg) are absolutely irreducible of dimensions r and 2r, both prime to p; GHT17 Corollary 9.4 with b ≥ 3 (excluding p^b ∈ {4, 9}) gives adequacy; G7/adequacy-criteria (3) passes to G. (iii) is ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/large-image-persistence; take a₀(p) as the maximum of the thresholds.
3. (3): Sym^{n−1} of SL₂(F_p) is absolutely irreducible for n ≤ p, so G7/adequacy-criteria (1) applies with d ≤ n.

**Prerequisites.** `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/adequate-subgroup`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/adequacy-criteria`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/adjoint-invariants-of-symmetric-powers`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/symmetric-and-exterior-powers`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/dickson-classification-and-the-dyadic-refinement`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/large-image-persistence`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/coefficient-frobenius-twist`; `mathlib:Matrix.SL2.commutator_eq_top`.

**Acceptance.**

- Boxer–Calegari–Gee p = 107, n = 105, 106: (Sym^{n−1} r̄)(G_{Q(ζ_107)}) is adequate for the mod-107 representation of the weight-26 level-one form (whose image contains SL₂(F_107)); this feeds their Theorem 2.4.
- The bound in (1) is sharp in the sense of GHT17 Corollary 9.4(i): for n = (p ± 1)/2 > 1, Sym^{n−1} of SL₂(F_p) is not adequate (Ext¹ ≠ 0); e.g. p = 7, n = 3, 4.

- bcg25-gln, Lemma 2.2: “SL2 (Fp ) ⊆ r(GQ ). Then for p − 2 ≤ n ≤ p, the group (Symn−1 r)(GQ(ζp ) ) is” — (1), range of n.

#### Enormous and weakly enormous subgroups of GSp₄(k); vast and tidy GSp₄-valued representations

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/vast-tidy-and-enormous-gsp4-subgroups`. Kind: definition. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.ResidualImage.GSp4` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/ImageConditions/GSp4BigImage`). Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7`.

Let k be a finite field of characteristic p ≥ 3, GSp₄ the similitude group of the symplectic form of G7/gsp4-and-symplectic-induction with similitude character ν, and ad⁰ = Lie(Sp₄) ⊗ k (dimension 10) with the adjoint action of GSp₄(k). (i) (Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni 2021, Definition 7.5.2) A subgroup H ⊆ GSp₄(k) is enormous if (E1) H¹(H, ad⁰) = 0; (E2) H acts absolutely irreducibly on k⁴ (so H⁰(H, ad⁰) = 0); (E3) for every simple k̄[H]-submodule W ⊆ k̄ ⊗ ad⁰ there is h ∈ H with 4 distinct eigenvalues in GSp₄(k̄) such that 1 is an eigenvalue of h on W. H is weakly enormous if it satisfies (E2) and (E3). No condition on p-power quotients is imposed (Remark 7.5.4), unlike G7/enormous-image-and-its-coefficient-extension-invariance; and ad⁰ is 𝔰𝔭₄, not the 15-dimensional 𝔰𝔩₄. (ii) (Lemma 7.5.3) Each notion depends only on the image of H in PGSp₄(k); a group containing a weakly enormous subgroup is weakly enormous, which fails for enormous. (iii) (Lemma 7.5.5) For a number field F and continuous ρ̄ : G_F → GSp₄(k) there is δ depending only on F (δ = 1 if p is unramified in F) such that ρ̄(G_{F(ζ_{p^N})}) is independent of N for N ≥ 1 + δ (p ≥ 5) or N ≥ 2 + δ (p = 3). (iv) (Definition 7.5.6) ρ̄ is vast if either ρ̄(G_{F(ζ_{p^N})}) is enormous for all sufficiently large N, or ρ̄(G_{F(ζ_{p^N})}) is weakly enormous for all sufficiently large N and the fixed field L of ad⁰ρ̄ does not contain ζ_p. (v) (Definition 7.5.11) H ⊆ GSp₄(k) is tidy if some h ∈ H has ν(h) ≠ 1 and no two eigenvalues of h (counted in k̄, not necessarily distinct) have ratio ν(h); ρ̄ is tidy if ρ̄(G_F) is tidy; a group containing a tidy subgroup is tidy.

**Hypotheses.**

- p ≥ 3; the decomposition 𝔤𝔰𝔭₄ = 𝔰𝔭₄ ⊕ k·1 with trivial action on the centre (not ⊕ ν, sourceIssue E759) needs p > 2
- (E3) is tested on simple submodules of ad⁰ ⊗ k̄, with an element having 4 distinct eigenvalues and eigenvalue 1 on W
- vastness concerns the images over F(ζ_{p^N}) for large N, not over F(ζ_p)

**Construction and proof.**

1. Define ad⁰ as the restriction of G7/adjoint-representations to the symplectic Lie algebra (Mathlib Matrix.symplecticGroup for the form J, transported to the form of G7/gsp4-and-symplectic-induction); 𝔰𝔭₄ ≅ Sym²(k⁴) ⊗ ν⁻¹ for p odd.
2. Lemma 7.5.3: with P the projective image and Z = H ∩ k^×, H⁰(P, ad⁰) = H⁰(H, ad⁰) and 0 → H¹(P, ad⁰) → H¹(H, ad⁰) → H¹(Z, ad⁰)^P = 0 (Mathlib groupCohomology.H1InfRes_exact; #Z prime to p); (E2), (E3) are unchanged by scalars.
3. Lemma 7.5.5: Gal(F(ζ_{p^N})/F) ↪ (Z/p^N)^× contains 1 + p^δ; p-power elements of GSp₄(k) have order dividing p (p ≥ 5) or p² (p = 3) because they are unipotent with (σ − 1)⁴ = 0; this forces the kernel of Gal(M(ζ_{p^{N+1}})/F) → Gal(M(ζ_{p^N})/F) to be nontrivial for N in the stated range.
4. Vast and tidy are defined from (i) and from eigenvalues; the inheritance statements are immediate.

**Prerequisites.** `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/gsp4-and-symplectic-induction`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/adjoint-representations`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/absolutely-irreducible`; `mathlib:Matrix.symplecticGroup`; `mathlib:Matrix.J`; `mathlib:groupCohomology.H1`; `mathlib:groupCohomology.H1InfRes_exact`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/restriction-to-the-cyclotomic-field`.

**Uses.**

- Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni (2021), Hypothesis 7.7.1(1), Lemma 7.6.1 and Lemma 9.2.2: vastness gives Taylor–Wiles primes through Lemma 7.5.9; tidiness gives an auxiliary place v₀ at which all lifts are unramified and the level is neat
- Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni (2025), Modularity theorems for abelian surfaces: tidiness and vastness of residual GSp₄ representations, filed there under GlobalGaloisDeformations; G7 owns the definitions
- Calegari–Geraghty (2020), Assumptions 4.1 and 4.2: the big image and neatness assumptions are the H1–H3 form of vast and the analogue of tidy (G7/cg20-big-image-assumption)
- GlobalGaloisDeformations (GSp₄ Taylor–Wiles systems): the image hypotheses of the GSp₄ patching argument

**API.**

- `TauCeti.ResidualImage.GSp4.IsEnormous` (constructor): IsEnormous H : Prop for H ≤ GSp₄(k): (E1) ∧ (E2) ∧ (E3).
- `TauCeti.ResidualImage.GSp4.IsWeaklyEnormous` (constructor): IsWeaklyEnormous H : Prop := (E2) ∧ (E3).
- `TauCeti.ResidualImage.GSp4.IsTidy` (constructor): IsTidy H : Prop := ∃ h ∈ H, ν h ≠ 1 ∧ ∀ eigenvalues λ, μ of h (in k̄, with multiplicity), λ ≠ ν(h)·μ.
- `TauCeti.ResidualImage.GSp4.IsVast` (constructor): IsVast ρ̄ : Prop for continuous ρ̄ : G_F → GSp₄(k), by Definition 7.5.6.
- `TauCeti.ResidualImage.GSp4.isEnormous_iff_of_projective_eq` (relation): Lemma 7.5.3: same image in PGSp₄(k) ⇒ (IsEnormous H ↔ IsEnormous H') and likewise for weakly enormous.
- `TauCeti.ResidualImage.GSp4.IsWeaklyEnormous.mono` (relation): H' ≤ H and IsWeaklyEnormous H' → IsWeaklyEnormous H; IsTidy is also inherited by overgroups.
- `TauCeti.ResidualImage.GSp4.image_cyclotomic_stabilises` (other): Lemma 7.5.5: ρ̄(G_{F(ζ_{p^N})}) is constant for N ≥ 1 + δ (p ≥ 5), N ≥ 2 + δ (p = 3), δ = 1 when p is unramified in F.
- `TauCeti.ResidualImage.GSp4.isVast_twist_iff` (compatibility): Remark 7.5.8: ρ̄ is vast iff ρ̄ ⊗ χ is vast for any character χ.
- `TauCeti.ResidualImage.GSp4.IsEnormous.toGL4` (compatibility): Relation with GL₄: (E2) is absolute irreducibility in GL₄(k); the GL₄ notion of Allen et al. uses 𝔰𝔩₄ and the p-power condition and is not implied.

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.ResidualImage.GSp4.isEnormous_Sp4_ZMod7` (computation): Sp₄(ZMod 7) ⊆ GSp₄(ZMod 7) is enormous.
- `TauCeti.ResidualImage.GSp4.isWeaklyEnormous_not_isEnormous_wreath_ZMod5` (non-example): SL₂(ZMod 5) ≀ Z/2Z ⊆ Sp₄(ZMod 5) is weakly enormous but not enormous; a definition omitting (E1) or merging the two notions fails.
- `TauCeti.ResidualImage.GSp4.isEnormous_SL2wr_ZMod3` (non-example): SL₂(ZMod 3) ≀ Z/2Z ⊆ Sp₄(ZMod 3) is enormous in the GSp₄ sense although it has a quotient of order 3; the Allen et al. condition (1) would reject it.
- `TauCeti.ResidualImage.GSp4.isTidy_of_center` (characterisation): An absolutely irreducible H ⊆ GSp₄(k) whose centre has order ≥ 3 is tidy (Lemma 7.5.12).
- `TauCeti.ResidualImage.GSp4.not_isTidy_Sp4` (degenerate): No subgroup of Sp₄(k) is tidy, since ν = 1 on Sp₄(k).

**Acceptance.**

- Sp₄(F_p) is enormous and GSp₄(F_p) is tidy for p ≥ 3 (G7/gsp4-big-image-verification (5)); in particular, for p = 3, an element of order 20 with eigenvalues ζ, ζ³, ζ⁹, ζ²⁷ and ν = −1 witnesses tidiness.
- Remark 7.5.4: the image of a surjective ρ̄ : G_Q → GL₂(F_3) with cyclotomic determinant has a quotient of order 3, so it is not enormous in the sense of Allen et al.; the GSp₄ notion omits that condition so that such images (and the p = 3 subgroups of §7.5.20) are allowed.
- SL₂(F_5) ≀ Z/2Z ⊆ Sp₄(F_5) is weakly enormous but not enormous (E1 fails through H¹(SL₂(F_5), Sym²) ≠ 0).

#### Verification of vast and tidy images in GSp₄: Galois cohomology vanishing, Sp₄(F_p), induced representations, wreath products and the p = 3 computations

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/gsp4-big-image-verification`. Kind: theorem. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.ResidualImage.GSp4` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/ImageConditions/GSp4BigImage`). Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7`.

Notation of G7/vast-tidy-and-enormous-gsp4-subgroups; k finite of characteristic p ≥ 3. (1) (Lemma 7.5.9) If ρ̄ : G_F → GSp₄(k) is continuous, N ≥ 1, L is the fixed field of ad⁰ρ̄ and either ζ_p ∉ L or ρ̄(G_{F(ζ_{p^N})}) is enormous, then H¹(Gal(L(ζ_{p^N})/F), ad⁰ρ̄(1)) = 0; so this holds for all large N if ρ̄ is vast. (2) (Lemma 7.5.12) An absolutely irreducible H ⊆ GSp₄(k) with centre of order ≥ 3 is tidy. (3) (Lemma 7.5.13) If p ≥ 5 and Δ = {(A, B) ∈ GL₂(F_p)² : det A = det B} ⊆ H ⊆ GSp₄(F_p), H is tidy. (4) (Lemma 7.5.14) If p ≥ 11 and H ⊆ GSp₄(k) is absolutely irreducible, (E1) and (E2) hold. (5) (Lemma 7.5.15) For p ≥ 3, Sp₄(F_p) is enormous and GSp₄(F_p) is tidy; a surjective ρ̄ : G_F → GSp₄(F_p) with similitude ε̄⁻¹ is vast and tidy. (6) (§7.5.16) If G ⊆ Sp₄(k) is absolutely irreducible and its representation W becomes reducible on an index-two subgroup H, with W|_H = V ⊕ V^σ and χ the quadratic character of G/H, then ad⁰(W) = Sym²(W) ≅ Ind_H^G ad⁰(V) ⊕ As(V), ∧²W ≅ k ⊕ k(χ) ⊕ As(V) ⊗ χ, W ⊗ W ≅ k ⊕ k(χ) ⊕ Ind_H^G ad⁰(V) ⊕ As(V) ⊕ As(V) ⊗ χ, with As(V) the Asai (tensor-induced) representation, As(V)|_H = V ⊗ V^σ (G7/tensor-induction). (7) (Lemma 7.5.17) If As(V) and Ind_H^G ad⁰(V) are absolutely irreducible and G ∖ H contains an element whose order neither divides 4 nor is divisible by p, then G satisfies (E3). (8) (Lemma 7.5.18, corrected proof, E761) SL₂(k) ≀ Z/2Z ⊆ Sp₄(k) is weakly enormous, and enormous if #k ≠ 5. (9) (Lemma 7.5.19) If H/F is quadratic, r̄ : G_H → GL₂(F_5) surjective with det r̄ = ε̄⁻¹, ρ̄ = Ind r̄ : G_F → GSp₄(F_5), ρ̄(G_{F(ζ_5)}) = SL₂(F_5) ≀ Z/2Z and 5 unramified in F, then ρ̄(G_{F(ζ_{5^N})}) is weakly enormous for all N ≥ 1, ζ_5 ∉ fixed field of ad⁰ρ̄, and ρ̄ is vast. (10) (§7.5.20, Lemma 7.5.21; finite computations) Exactly 11 of the 162 conjugacy classes of subgroups of Sp₄(F_3) are enormous (orders 40, 128, 160, 192, 240, 320, 384, 384, 1152, 1920, 51840), and the groups G ⊆ GSp₄(F_3) listed in Lemma 7.5.21 (GSp₄(F_3); a group of order 3840; Γ = Δ ⋊ Z/2Z of order 2304 and its two index-3 subgroups of order 768; Ã₅ ⋊ ⟨σ⟩ of order 480) are tidy with G ∩ Sp₄(F_3) enormous. (11) (Lemma 7.5.22, corrected, E762–E764) Let p ≥ 3, K/F quadratic with K unramified at p, r̄ : G_K → GL₂(k) with r̄(G_{K(ζ_p)}) = SL₂(k), σ ∈ G_F ∖ G_K with Proj r̄^σ ≇ Proj r̄ and det r̄^σ = det r̄ = ε̄⁻¹, ρ̄ = Ind_{G_K}^{G_F} r̄; if p = 3 assume the fixed fields of ker Proj r̄ and ker Proj r̄^σ are linearly disjoint over K(ζ_3). Then ρ̄ is vast and tidy. (12) (Remark 7.5.23, corrected, E765) The Sylow 2-subgroup Q₈ ≀ Z/2Z (order 128) of Sp₄(F_3) is enormous.

**Hypotheses.**

- (4) needs p ≥ 11 (GHTT with d ≤ 4); for p = 3, 5, 7 the vanishing H¹(Sp₄(F_p), ad⁰) = 0 in (5) is a finite computation
- (8) excludes #k = 5 because H¹(SL₂(F_5), Sym²) ≠ 0
- (11) for #k > 3 includes the case Proj r̄^σ ≅ τ ∘ Proj r̄ with τ a field automorphism of order 2, which the printed proof omits

**Construction and proof.**

1. (1): Lemma 7.5.9 by inflation–restriction (Mathlib groupCohomology.H1InfRes_exact): if ζ_p ∉ L, Gal(L(ζ_p)/L) acts trivially on ad⁰ but by nontrivial scalars on ad⁰(1), killing invariants, and p ∤ [L(ζ_p) : L]; if the image H over F(ζ_{p^N}) is enormous, H⁰(H, ad⁰) = H¹(H, ad⁰) = 0 and the splitting field M has p ∤ [M : L].
2. (2), (3): Schur's lemma makes the centre cyclic and scalar; a scalar ζ with ζ² ≠ 1 has ν = ζ² ≠ 1 and all eigenvalue ratios 1. Δ contains scalars of order p − 1 > 2.
3. (4): G7/adequacy-criteria (1) with d ≤ 4 (GHTT Theorem A.9), whose two external inputs are recorded as gaps.
4. (5): 𝔰𝔭₄ is absolutely irreducible for Sp₄(F_p), p ≥ 3; an element with distinct eigenvalues λ, ν/λ, μ, ν/μ has eigenvalue 1 on 𝔰𝔭₄ (from λ·(ν/λ)/ν); H¹(Sp₄(F_p), ad⁰) = 0 by (4) for p ≥ 11 and by computer for p = 3, 5, 7 (the authors' published Magma files; a gap until the computation is certified); tidiness by (2) for p > 3 and, for p = 3, an element of order 20 with ν = −1 and eigenvalues ζ, ζ³, ζ⁹, ζ²⁷; vastness because Sp₄(F_p) has no quotient of order p (PSp₄(F_p) simple).
5. (6): compute over H and use W ≅ W ⊗ χ; As(V) from G7/tensor-induction; induced representations from ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/continuous-induction.
6. (7): g ∈ G ∖ H has eigenvalues (α, α⁻¹, −α, −α⁻¹), distinct when α⁴ ≠ 1; counting in the Grothendieck group of ⟨g⟩: [As(V)] = [−1, 1, α², α⁻²] and [Ind ad⁰(V)] = [1, −1, α², −α², α⁻², −α⁻²], both containing 1.
7. (8): (E1) by inflation–restriction reduces to H¹(SL₂(k), Sym²(k²)) = 0 for #k ≠ 5 (G7/h1-of-sl2-with-adjoint-coefficients (a)); (E2) is clear; (E3) by (7) with g = (a, 1)σ, a ∈ SL₂(k) of order 4 (e.g. [[0,1],[−1,0]]), so g² = (a, a) has order 4 and g has order 8, not dividing 4 and prime to p. The printed proof takes a of order 8, which does not exist when #k ≡ ±3 mod 8 (E761).
8. (9): the abelianisation of SL₂(F_5) ≀ Z/2Z has order prime to 5, so the image over F(ζ_{5^N}) does not depend on N, and is weakly enormous by (8); the image Γ of ρ̄ is the full preimage of G with [Γ : G] = 4, whose projective image has abelianisation (Z/2)², which does not surject onto Gal(F(ζ_5)/F) = Z/4.
9. (10): finite group enumeration (the authors' Magma computation, reproduced as a certified finite computation), except (3a), which is (8). Recorded as a gap.
10. (11): for #k > 3, Goursat (PSL₂(k) simple; Mathlib Matrix.ProjectiveSpecialLinearGroup.rank_two_simple) and Aut(PSL₂(k)) = PΓL₂(k) (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/normal-subgroups-and-automorphisms-of-psl2-pgl2) show that either the image over K(ζ_p) is SL₂(k)², giving SL₂(k) ≀ Z/2Z over F(ζ_{p^N}) and (8), (9); or Proj r̄^σ ≅ τ ∘ Proj r̄ with τ of order 2, where the image over F(ζ_p) is an index-two extension of {(A, ±τ(A))}, still enormous (V ≇ V^τ; H¹(SL₂(k), Sym²) = 0 as #k ≥ 25; H¹(SL₂(k), V ⊗ V^τ) = 0 for p ≥ 5; (E3) via (7) with g = (C, ±C)·swap, C of order q₀ + 1), and tidiness from ρ̄(g) with r̄(g) = diag(a, −a⁻¹), a a generator of k^× (E763). For k = F_3 the image over F(ζ_{3^N}), N ≥ 2, is SL₂(F_3) ≀ Z/2Z or its normal subgroup of index 3, both enormous by (10) (the abelianisation is Z/6Z, not prime to 3: E764); the p = 3 hypothesis is linear disjointness over K(ζ_3) (E762); tidiness for p = 3 from an element of order 8 with ν = −1 and eigenvalues (ζ, −ζ⁻¹, ζ, −ζ⁻¹).
11. (12): |Q₈ ≀ Z/2Z| = 128 is prime to 3, so (E1) holds; the natural representation restricted to Q₈ × Q₈ is V_A ⊕ V_B, non-isomorphic and swapped, so (E2) holds; ad⁰ = Ind(χ₁) ⊕ Ind(χ₂) ⊕ Ind(χ₃) ⊕ As(V) with χ_j the nontrivial characters of Q₈/{±1}, pairwise non-isomorphic irreducibles; g = (a, b)σ with ab of order 4 has the four primitive 8th roots of unity as eigenvalues, acts on Ind(χ_j) with eigenvalues ±√χ_j(ab) (containing 1 when ab ∈ ker χ_j) and on As(V) with eigenvalues 1, −1, i, −i; so (E3) holds.

#### The big image assumption (H1)–(H3) for GSp₄-valued residual representations of G_Q

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/cg20-big-image-assumption`. Kind: definition. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.ResidualImage.GSp4` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/ImageConditions/GSp4BigImage`). Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7`.

Let p > 2, k a finite field of characteristic p, and r̄ : G_Q → GSp₄(k) continuous (G7/gsp4-and-symplectic-induction). Let ad(r̄) be r̄ composed with the 11-dimensional adjoint representation on 𝔤𝔰𝔭₄ and ad⁰(r̄) its composite with 𝔰𝔭₄ (10-dimensional); ad(r̄) = ad⁰(r̄) ⊕ k with the trivial action on the centre k·1 (corrected statement, sourceIssue E759), and ad⁰(r̄)(1) = ad⁰(r̄) ⊗ ε̄. r̄ has big image (Calegari–Geraghty 2020, Assumption 4.1, after Pilloni §5.7) if (H1) the field Q(ad⁰(r̄)) cut out by ad⁰(r̄) does not contain ζ_p; (H2) for every m ≥ 1 there is σ ∈ G_{Q(ζ_{p^m})} such that r̄(σ) has four distinct eigenvalues and σ has 1 as an eigenvalue on each irreducible k̄[G_{Q(ζ_{p^m})}]-constituent of ad⁰(r̄) ⊗ k̄; (H3) neither the image Γ of ad⁰(r̄) nor the image of ad⁰(r̄)(1) has a quotient of order p. (H1) depends on more than the group r̄(G_{Q(ζ_p)}). Relation with Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni: if r̄|G_{Q(ζ_{p^N})} is absolutely irreducible for all N and r̄ has big image, then r̄ is vast (G7/vast-tidy-and-enormous-gsp4-subgroups, Definition 7.5.6(2)), since (H2) for each m gives (E3) for the image over Q(ζ_{p^m}) with a single element for all constituents.

**Hypotheses.**

- p > 2, so that 𝔤𝔰𝔭₄ = 𝔰𝔭₄ ⊕ k·1
- (H2) asks for one σ that works for all irreducible constituents at once, for every m
- (H1) is a condition on the field cut out by ad⁰(r̄), not on the image group

**Construction and proof.**

1. Form ad and ad⁰ from G7/adjoint-representations restricted along GSp₄ ⊆ GL₄; the splitting 𝔤𝔰𝔭₄ = 𝔰𝔭₄ ⊕ k·I₄ holds for p > 2 (if XᵀJ + JX = cJ then X − (c/2)I ∈ 𝔰𝔭₄) and the adjoint action fixes I₄ (E759).
2. Constituents are taken after extending scalars to k̄ (R01.1/semisimplification); eigenvalues of σ on a constituent are those of the induced endomorphism.
3. Relation with vastness: (H2) gives, for W a simple submodule of ad⁰ ⊗ k̄ over G_{Q(ζ_{p^m})}, an element with distinct eigenvalues and eigenvalue 1 on W, i.e. (E3); with absolute irreducibility (E2) the image over Q(ζ_{p^m}) is weakly enormous; with (H1) this is Definition 7.5.6(2).

**Prerequisites.** `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/gsp4-and-symplectic-induction`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/adjoint-representations`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/vast-tidy-and-enormous-gsp4-subgroups`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/semisimplification`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/cyclotomic-and-dirichlet-characters`; `mathlib:Matrix.symplecticGroup`.

**Uses.**

- Calegari–Geraghty (2020), Proposition 4.10 and §6.3: (H1)–(H3) produce Taylor–Wiles primes for the fixed-similitude GSp₄ deformation problem and the vanishing of the dual Selmer group
- Calegari–Geraghty (2020), Theorems 1.1, 1.2 and 9.1: big image of r̄ restricted to G_{Q(ζ_p)} is a standing hypothesis of the minimal modularity lifting theorem; consumers: GSp4LocalLanglandsAndGaloisRepresentations, AbelianSurfacesPotentialModularity
- Calegari–Geraghty (2020), Remark 4.12: elliptic curves over imaginary quadratic K give induced r̄ with big image for almost all p

**API.**

- `TauCeti.ResidualImage.GSp4.HasBigImage` (constructor): HasBigImage r̄ : Prop := H1 ∧ H2 ∧ H3 for continuous r̄ : G_Q → GSp₄(k).
- `TauCeti.ResidualImage.GSp4.adjointRep_eq_sp4_add_trivial` (structure): ad(r̄) ≅ ad⁰(r̄) ⊕ 1 for p > 2 (trivial action on the centre).
- `TauCeti.ResidualImage.GSp4.HasBigImage.h1` (projection): HasBigImage r̄ → ζ_p ∉ Q(ad⁰ r̄).
- `TauCeti.ResidualImage.GSp4.HasBigImage.exists_sigma` (projection): HasBigImage r̄ → ∀ m, ∃ σ ∈ G_{Q(ζ_{p^m})} with distinct eigenvalues and eigenvalue 1 on each constituent of ad⁰ r̄.
- `TauCeti.ResidualImage.GSp4.HasBigImage.isVast` (relation): With absolute irreducibility over every Q(ζ_{p^N}), big image implies vast.
- `TauCeti.ResidualImage.GSp4.hasBigImage_twist_iff` (compatibility): Big image is unchanged by twisting r̄ by a character (ad⁰ unchanged).

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.ResidualImage.GSp4.hasBigImage_of_surjective` (computation): If p ≥ 5 and r̄(G_Q) = GSp₄(F_p) then r̄ has big image.
- `TauCeti.ResidualImage.GSp4.not_hasBigImage_of_zeta_mem` (non-example): If ζ_p lies in the field cut out by ad⁰(r̄) (for example r̄ = r̄₀ ⊗ χ with ad⁰r̄₀ having image containing a cyclic quotient matching Gal(Q(ζ_p)/Q)), (H1) fails even when r̄(G_{Q(ζ_p)}) is enormous; a definition depending only on the image group fails.
- `TauCeti.ResidualImage.GSp4.adjoint_split` (compatibility): For p > 2, ad(r̄) ≅ ad⁰(r̄) ⊕ 1 with the trivial character on the second summand, not the similitude character.
- `TauCeti.ResidualImage.GSp4.hasBigImage_isVast` (characterisation): Big image together with absolute irreducibility of every r̄|G_{Q(ζ_{p^N})} implies vastness in the sense of Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni.

**Acceptance.**

- Image GSp₄(F_p), p ≥ 5, has big image (G7/cg20-big-image-examples (2)).
- An induced r̄ = Ind_K^Q ρ̄ as in Calegari–Geraghty Example 4.11(1) has big image; the element must be taken in r̄(G_{Q(ζ_{p^m})}) (E757).

**Sources.**

- cg20, §4, Assumption 4.1, arXiv v1 p. 10 (published p. 813): “Assumption 4.1 (Big Image). The restriction of r to GQ(ζp ) satisfies the following condi-” — The assumption; the text layer drops the bar on r̄.
- cg20, Assumption 4.1 (H1): “H1: The field Q(ad0 (r)) does not contain ζp ,” — (H1).
- cg20, Assumption 4.1 (H2): “H2: For any m, there exists an element σ ∈ GQ(ζpm ) such that r(σ) has four distinct” — (H2).
- cg20, Assumption 4.1 (H3): “H3: Neither the image Γ of ad0 (r) nor the image of ad0 (r)(1) admits a quotient of degree p.” — (H3).
- cg20, after Assumption 4.1: “If this assumption holds, we say that r has big image, although condition (H1) depends on” — (H1) is not group-theoretic.
- cg20, §4, before Assumption 4.1: “admits a decomposition ad(r) = ad0 (r) ⊕ ν, where ν is the similitude character of r.” — The printed decomposition, corrected by E759.

#### Examples of big image: surjective GSp₄(F_p) images and inductions from imaginary quadratic fields

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/cg20-big-image-examples`. Kind: theorem. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.ResidualImage.GSp4` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/ImageConditions/GSp4BigImage`). Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7`.

Let p ≥ 5. (1) (Calegari–Geraghty 2020, Example 4.11(1), with corrected proof) Let K/Q be imaginary quadratic with K ⊄ Q(ζ_p), and ρ̄ : G_K → GL₂(F_p) with det ρ̄ = ε̄^{1−k} for some integer k, such that for a complex conjugation c the pair (ρ̄, ρ̄^c) maps G_{K(ζ_p)} onto SL₂(F_p) × SL₂(F_p) (the fields cut out by ρ̄|G_{K(ζ_p)} and ρ̄^c|G_{K(ζ_p)} are linearly disjoint over K(ζ_p)). Then r̄ = Ind_K^Q ρ̄ preserves a symplectic form with multiplier ε̄^{1−k}·(quadratic character as in G7/gsp4-and-symplectic-induction), ad⁰(r̄)|_{G_K} ≅ (ρ̄ ⊗ ρ̄^c) ⊗ ε̄^{k−1} ⊕ ad⁰(ρ̄) ⊕ ad⁰(ρ̄^c), ad⁰(r̄) ≅ As(ρ̄) ⊗ ε̄^{k−1} ⊕ Ind_K^Q ad⁰(ρ̄) up to replacing As(ρ̄) by its quadratic twist, r̄(G_{Q(ζ_{p^m})}) = {diag(A,B) : A, B ∈ SL₂(F_p)} ⊔ {diag(A,B)·r̄(c) : det A = det B = (−1)^{k−1}} (abstractly SL₂(F_p)² ⋊ Z/2Z) for every m ≥ 1, and r̄ has big image. (2) (Example 4.11(2)) If r̄(G_Q) = GSp₄(F_p), then r̄ has big image.

**Hypotheses.**

- p ≥ 5, so that SL₂(F_p) and Sp₄(F_p) are perfect and PSL₂(F_p) is simple
- the element witnessing (H2) must lie in r̄(G_{Q(ζ_{p^m})}); c itself does not (E757)
- only the eigenvalue 1, not −1, is automatic on Ind_K^Q ad⁰(ρ̄) for elements of the index-two subgroup (E758)

**Construction and proof.**

1. (1), structure: the dual of ρ̄ is ρ̄ ⊗ ε̄^{k−1} (printed with × for ⊗, E760); compute ad⁰ over K and over Q by G7/gsp4-big-image-verification (6) and G7/tensor-induction (Asai).
2. (1), (H1) and (H3): SL₂(F_p) perfect (Mathlib Matrix.SL2.commutator_eq_top) and K ⊄ Q(ζ_p) (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/restriction-to-the-cyclotomic-field for the cyclotomic bookkeeping).
3. (1), image over Q(ζ_{p^m}): elements of G_{Q(ζ_{p^m})} ∖ G_K are σc with σ ∈ G_K, ε̄(σ) ≡ −1, so r̄(σc) = diag(ρ̄(σ), ρ̄^c(σ))·r̄(c) with det ρ̄(σ) = (−1)^{k−1}; SL₂(F_p)² is perfect and disjoint from the p-extension K(ζ_{p^m})/K(ζ_p), so every (A, B) with det A = det B = (−1)^{k−1} occurs (E757).
4. (1), (H2): take A = diag(x, (−1)^{k−1}x⁻¹), B = diag(y, (−1)^{k−1}y⁻¹), x = 2, y = 1; diag(A,B)·r̄(c) has eigenvalues ±(xy)^{1/2}, ±(xy)^{−1/2} on r̄ (distinct as (xy)² = 4 ≠ 1), eigenvalues xy, (xy)⁻¹, 1, −1 on As(ρ̄), and eigenvalue 1 on Ind ad⁰(ρ̄) (every element of GL₂ has eigenvalue 1 on ad⁰, and elements outside the index-two subgroup have both ±1, E758).
5. (2): r̄(G_{Q(ζ_{p^m})}) ⊇ Sp₄(F_p) for all m (Sp₄(F_p) perfect, GSp₄(F_p)/Sp₄(F_p) abelian); (H2) as in G7/gsp4-big-image-verification (5): 𝔰𝔭₄ is absolutely irreducible and every element with distinct eigenvalues has eigenvalue 1 on it; (H1): the projective image PGSp₄(F_p) has abelianisation of order 2 while Gal(Q(ζ_p)/Q) is cyclic of order p − 1 ≥ 4; (H3): PGSp₄(F_p) has no quotient of order p and the image of ad⁰(r̄)(1) is an extension of a quotient of PGSp₄(F_p) by a group of order prime to p. Calegari–Geraghty cite Pilloni 2012, Proposition 5.8 instead (not read in this job).

**Prerequisites.** `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/cg20-big-image-assumption`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/gsp4-big-image-verification`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/gsp4-and-symplectic-induction`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/tensor-induction`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/continuous-induction`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/restriction-to-the-cyclotomic-field`; `mathlib:Matrix.SL2.commutator_eq_top`.

**Acceptance.**

- (1) mod 13 with x = 2, y = 1 and either sign (−1)^{k−1}: the element has characteristic polynomial T⁴ + 4T² + 1 on r̄ and (T² − 1)(T − 2)(T − 2⁻¹) on As(ρ̄) (check recorded by the Calegari–Geraghty extraction, E28).
- (1) for k = 2 (Remark 4.12, elliptic curves): the printed element swap·diag(x, x⁻¹, y, y⁻¹) has blocks of determinant +1 ≠ −1 and does not lie in r̄(G_{Q(ζ_{p^m})}); the corrected element does.
- (2) for p = 5: GSp₄(F_5) surjective image gives big image although SL₂(F_5) is not enormous.

**Sources.**

- cg20, Example 4.11, arXiv v1 p. 14 (published p. 818): “Example 4.11 (Examples of representations with big image). Suppose that p ≥ 5.” — The example.
- cg20, Example 4.11(2): “(2) Suppose the image of r is GSp4 (Fp ). Then r has big image.” — (2).
- cg20, proof of Example 4.11: “and hence the image of r|GQ(ζ m ) under our assumptions is the group SL2 (Fp )2 ⋊ Z/2Z.” — The image over Q(ζ_{p^m}).
- cg20, proof of Example 4.11: “Since 1 and −1 are always eigenvalues of any element acting on IndQ” — The overstatement corrected by E758.
