#### Taylor–Wiles image conditions: adequate or enormous image over F(ζ_p) and a scalar element outside G_{F(ζ_p)}

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/taylor-wiles-image-conditions`. Kind: definition. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.ResidualImage` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/ImageConditions/TaylorWiles`). Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7`.

Let F be a number field, p a prime, n ≥ 1 and s̄ : G_F → GL_n(F̄_p) continuous; its image is finite and lies in GL_n(k) for a finite field k (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/residual-descent-to-a-finite-field). (a) s̄ satisfies the Taylor–Wiles image conditions if (TW2) the finite group s̄(G_{F(ζ_p)}) ⊆ GL_n(F̄_p) is adequate (G7/adequate-subgroup, Thorne 2012 sense) and (TW3) there is σ ∈ G_F ∖ G_{F(ζ_p)} with s̄(σ) scalar. (b) s̄ satisfies the enormous Taylor–Wiles image conditions if s̄(G_{F(ζ_p)}) is enormous (G7/enormous-image-and-its-coefficient-extension-invariance) and (TW3) holds (Allen et al. 2023, Theorems 6.1.1–6.1.2, hypotheses (3)–(4)). These are the image-theoretic parts (2) and (3) of the Taylor–Wiles big image conditions of Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Newton–Thorne, Definition 5.2.1; their condition (1), decomposed genericity, is defined at AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII:AG2.7 and the full conjunction is formed at PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure:PA.5. (TW3) is equivalent to ζ_p ∉ F̄^{ker ad s̄}, i.e. ker(ad s̄) ⊄ G_{F(ζ_p)}.

**Hypotheses.**

- (TW2) is about the image of G_{F(ζ_p)}, not of G_F
- (TW3) requires σ outside G_{F(ζ_p)}; in particular it fails when ζ_p ∈ F
- decomposed genericity is not part of this node (stage-edge: AG2.7 requires G7)

**Construction and proof.**

1. Finite image: R01.1/finite-coefficients-and-finite-quotients and R01.1/residual-descent-to-a-finite-field; restriction to G_{F(ζ_p)} via R01.1/restriction-dual-tensor-twist.
2. (TW3) ⟺ ζ_p ∉ F̄^{ker ad s̄}: s̄(σ) is scalar iff σ ∈ ker(ad s̄) (Mathlib Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.center_eq_range_scalar: the centre of GL_n is the scalars), and ker(ad s̄) ⊄ G_{F(ζ_p)} iff the fixed field of ker(ad s̄) does not contain ζ_p (Galois correspondence).
3. Twisting: s̄ ⊗ χ has the same ad and the same image up to scalars over F(ζ_p), so both conditions are invariant under twists (G7/adequate-subgroup API isAdequate_units_mul_iff; enormity is projective).

**Prerequisites.** `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/adequate-subgroup`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/enormous-image-and-its-coefficient-extension-invariance`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/residual-descent-to-a-finite-field`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/finite-coefficients-and-finite-quotients`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/restriction-dual-tensor-twist`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/adjoint-representations`; `mathlib:Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.center_eq_range_scalar`.

**Uses.**

- Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Newton–Thorne (2025), Definition 5.2.1 and Theorem 3.2.1 hypotheses (3)–(4): conditions (2) and (3) of the Taylor–Wiles big image conditions; combined with decomposed genericity at PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure:PA.5
- Allen et al. (2023), Theorems 6.1.1 and 6.1.2, hypotheses (3)–(4): enormous image of ρ̄|G_{F(ζ_p)} and a scalar ρ̄(σ) with σ ∈ G_F ∖ G_{F(ζ_p)}
- Allen et al. (2023), Lemma 7.1.6(1); Qian (2023), Lemma 2.6: (TW3) for Sym^m r̄|G_{F'} through ζ_l ∉ F̄^{ker ad Sym^m r̄}·F' (G7/taylor-wiles-image-lemmas)
- GlobalGaloisDeformations:G7/enormous-taylor-wiles-primes: the enormous image hypothesis on ρ̄(G_{F(ζ_p)})

**API.**

- `TauCeti.ResidualImage.TaylorWilesImageConditions` (constructor): TaylorWilesImageConditions s̄ : Prop := IsAdequate (s̄(G_{F(ζ_p)})) ∧ ∃ σ ∈ G_F, σ ∉ G_{F(ζ_p)} ∧ s̄ σ ∈ scalars.
- `TauCeti.ResidualImage.EnormousTaylorWilesImageConditions` (constructor): The variant with IsEnormous in place of IsAdequate.
- `TauCeti.ResidualImage.tw3_iff_zeta_not_mem` (characterisation): (∃ σ ∈ G_F ∖ G_{F(ζ_p)}, s̄ σ scalar) ↔ ζ_p ∉ F̄^{ker ad s̄}.
- `TauCeti.ResidualImage.TaylorWilesImageConditions.twist` (compatibility): Both conditions are invariant under s̄ ↦ s̄ ⊗ χ.
- `TauCeti.ResidualImage.EnormousTaylorWilesImageConditions.toTaylorWiles` (relation): If k contains all eigenvalues of s̄(G_F), the enormous variant implies (a).
- `TauCeti.ResidualImage.TaylorWilesImageConditions.restrict` (functoriality): Restriction to G_H for H/F as in Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Newton–Thorne Lemma 5.2.2 preserves both conditions (G7/taylor-wiles-image-lemmas (1)).

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.ResidualImage.twImageConditions_rank_one` (degenerate): For n = 1 and any character s̄, TaylorWilesImageConditions s̄ ↔ ζ_p ∉ F.
- `TauCeti.ResidualImage.not_twImageConditions_of_zeta_mem` (non-example): If ζ_p ∈ F then (TW3) fails for every s̄, whatever its image; a definition testing only the image group s̄(G_F) fails.
- `TauCeti.ResidualImage.twImageConditions_elliptic` (computation): For s̄ : G_Q → GL₂(F_7) surjective with det s̄ the mod 7 cyclotomic character, s̄ satisfies both (a) and (b).
- `TauCeti.ResidualImage.tw3_iff_zeta_not_mem` (characterisation): (TW3) ↔ ζ_p ∉ the fixed field of ker(ad s̄).

**Acceptance.**

- n = 1: (TW2) always holds and (TW3) holds iff ζ_p ∉ F.
- For a non-CM elliptic curve E/Q and l ≥ 7 with r̄_{E,l}(G_Q) = GL₂(F_l): r̄(G_{Q(ζ_l)}) = SL₂(F_l) is adequate and enormous, and σ with r̄(σ) = 2·I has χ̄_l(σ) = det = 4 ≠ 1, so σ ∉ G_{Q(ζ_l)}; both (a) and (b) hold.

**Sources.**

- bcgnt25, §5.2, Definition 5.2.1, arXiv v3 pp. 50–51: “Definition 5.2.1. Say that a representation s : GF → GLn (Fp ) satisfies the” — The definition; the text layer drops the bar on F_p.
- bcgnt25, Definition 5.2.1(1): “(1) The representation s is decomposed generic.” — Condition (1), routed to PA.5.
- bcgnt25, Definition 5.2.1(2): “(2) The representation s|GF (ζp ) has adequate image.” — (TW2).
- bcgnt25, Definition 5.2.1(3): “(3) There exists σ ∈ GF − GF (ζp ) such that s(σ) is scalar.” — (TW3).
- accplus-cm-potential-automorphy, Theorem 6.1.1(3)–(4), printed p. 1029: “(4) There exists σ ∈ GF − GF (ζp ) such that ρ(σ) is a scalar. We have p > n2 .” — The enormous variant (b): hypothesis (3) asks that the image of ρ̄|G_{F(ζ_p)} be enormous, (4) for the scalar element.

#### Verification lemmas for the Taylor–Wiles image conditions: disjoint base change, Sym^{n−1}r̄_A ⊗ r̄_B, induced Frobenius eigenvalues, scalar elements for Sym^m

Node: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/taylor-wiles-image-lemmas`. Kind: theorem. Declaration namespace: `TauCeti.ResidualImage` (module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/GaloisRepresentation/ImageConditions/TaylorWilesLemmas`). Realises `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7`.

(1) (Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Newton–Thorne, Lemma 5.2.2, image part) Let F/Q be Galois and s̄ : G_F → GL_n(F̄_p) satisfy the Taylor–Wiles image conditions (G7/taylor-wiles-image-conditions). If H/F is finite and its Galois closure over Q is linearly disjoint over F from the composite of F(ζ_p) and the Galois closure over Q of F̄^{ker s̄}, then s̄(G_H) = s̄(G_F), s̄(G_{H(ζ_p)}) = s̄(G_{F(ζ_p)}), and s̄|G_H satisfies the Taylor–Wiles image conditions. (2) (Lemma 5.2.4, image parts) Let F/Q be Galois, r̄_A : G_F → GL₂(F_p) and r̄_B : G_F → GU_m(F_{p²}) ⊆ GL_m(F_{p²}) with r̄_A(G_{F(ζ_p)}) = SL₂(F_p) and r̄_B(G_{F(ζ_p)}) = SU_m(F_{p²}), s̄ = Sym^{n−1}r̄_A ⊗ r̄_B, p > 2mn + 1, and if m = 2 assume the Galois closures over Q of the fixed fields of the projective representations of r̄_A and r̄_B are linearly disjoint over F(ζ_p) (E768). Then (i) s̄|G_{F(ζ_p)} has adequate image; (ii) if det r̄_A = ε̄^{−m} and r̄_B has multiplier ε̄^{1−m}, s̄ has image in GU_{mn}(F_{p²}) with multiplier ε̄^{1−mn} (E769); (iii) if moreover ε̄(G_F) = F_p^×, (TW3) holds for s̄. (3) (Lemma 5.2.5) Let E/Q be cyclic of degree m and linearly disjoint from F, L = EF, ψ : G_L → F_p^× with p ∤ m, r̄_B = Ind_{G_L}^{G_F} ψ, and q a rational prime splitting completely in F with r̄_B unramified above q and Frob_q generating Gal(E/Q). For v | q, the eigenvalues of r̄_B(Frob_v) are λ, ζλ, …, ζ^{m−1}λ with ζ a primitive m-th root of unity. (4) (Lemma 5.2.6, image parts, corrected) Let F/Q be Galois, r̄_A as in (2), r̄_B ≅ Ind_{G_L}^{G_F} ψ : G_F → GL_m(F_p) as in (3) with r̄_B|G_{F(ζ_p)} absolutely irreducible (E767), s̄ = Sym^{n−1}r̄_A ⊗ r̄_B and p > 2mn + 1. Then s̄|G_{F(ζ_p)} has adequate image, and if det r̄_A = ε̄^{−m}, det r̄_B = ε̄^{−m(m−1)/2} and ε̄(G_L) = F_p^×, (TW3) holds. (5) (Allen et al. 2023, Lemma 7.1.6(1)) Under the standing hypotheses of G7/enormous-symmetric-powers (3) (F/Q finite with normal closure F̃, l > 2m + 3, r̄(G_{F̃}) ⊇ SL₂(F_l), F'/F linearly disjoint from F̄^{ker r̄}), if l is unramified in F'/Q then ζ_l ∉ F̄^{ker ad Sym^m r̄}·F', so Sym^m r̄|G_{F'} satisfies (TW3) and, with G7/enormous-symmetric-powers (3), the enormous Taylor–Wiles image conditions.

**Hypotheses.**

- the decomposed-genericity halves of Lemmas 5.2.2, 5.2.4(1), 5.2.6(1) and of Allen et al. Lemmas 7.1.5, 7.1.6(3)–(5), 7.1.7 are not stated here (routed to PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure:PA.5)
- (4) needs r̄_B|G_{F(ζ_p)} absolutely irreducible, not merely irreducible (E767)
- (2) for m = 2 needs linear disjointness of the Galois closures, not of the fields themselves (E768)

**Construction and proof.**

1. (1): Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Newton–Thorne Lemma 5.2.2: reduce to H Galois over Q; disjointness gives Gal(H·M(ζ_p)/F) ≅ Gal(M(ζ_p)/F) × Gal(H/F), so the images of G_H and G_{H(ζ_p)} equal those of G_F and G_{F(ζ_p)}, and a scalar σ outside G_{F(ζ_p)} gives (σ, 1).
2. (2)(i): Goursat with Lemma 5.2.3 (simplicity and pairwise non-isomorphism of PSL₂(F_p) and PSU_m(F_{p²}), ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/normal-subgroups-and-automorphisms-of-psl2-pgl2 for the PSL₂ part) gives Gal(H̃/F(ζ_p)) ≅ PSL₂(F_p)^r × PSU_m(F_{p²})^s; the image of s̄|G_{F(ζ_p)} contains Sym^{n−1}SL₂(F_p) ⊗ SU_m(F_{p²}), acting absolutely irreducibly, and adequacy follows from G7/adequacy-criteria (1) as p > 2mn + 1 ≥ 2(mn + 1) − 1 (GHTT Theorem A.9). (ii): multipliers multiply (G7/polarized-representation for unitary multipliers). (iii): choose σ with r̄_A(σ) and r̄_B(σ) scalar and ε̄(σ) ≠ 1, using ε̄(G_F) = F_p^×.
3. (3): Gal(L/F) ≅ Gal(E/Q) is cyclic of order m; r̄_B ≅ r̄_B ⊗ χ for a character χ of order m through Gal(L/F), and Frob_v maps to a generator, so the eigenvalue multiset is stable under multiplication by ζ = χ(Frob_v).
4. (4): as (2)(i), with r̄_B of solvable image and order prime to p after Mackey (Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Newton–Thorne item 140; Tau Ceti RepresentationTheory/InductionRestriction layer 4) and G7/adequacy-criteria (4) (BLGG13 Lemma A.3.1) for the tensor product; absolute irreducibility of r̄_B|G_{F(ζ_p)} is needed because adequacy implies it (E767).
5. (5): reduce to m = 1 (ad Sym^m r̄ factors through ad r̄); Gal(F'(ζ_l)/F') ≅ (Z/l)^× as l is unramified in F', while ad r̄(G_{F'}) = ad r̄(G_F) is PSL₂(k) or PGL₂(k) and has no cyclic quotient of order l − 1 > 2 (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/restriction-to-the-cyclotomic-field); then apply the characterisation (TW3) ⟺ ζ_l ∉ F̄^{ker ad} of G7/taylor-wiles-image-conditions.

**Prerequisites.** `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/taylor-wiles-image-conditions`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/adequacy-criteria`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/enormous-symmetric-powers`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/symmetric-and-exterior-powers`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/polarized-representation`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/continuous-induction`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/normal-subgroups-and-automorphisms-of-psl2-pgl2`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/restriction-to-the-cyclotomic-field`; `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/dickson-classification-and-the-dyadic-refinement`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/Chebotarev#layer-10-dirichlet-density-chebotarev`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/InductionRestriction#layer-4-intertwining-numbers-and-the-mackey-irreducibility-criterion`.

**Acceptance.**

- (3) with m = 2: r̄_B = Ind ψ from a quadratic L = EF, Frob_v nontrivial on E: eigenvalues λ, −λ, i.e. trace zero.
- (4) without absolute irreducibility fails: for m = 2 with Ind ψ̄ ≅ θ ⊕ θη over F̄_p (θ F_{p²}-valued) the image of s̄|G_{F(ζ_p)} is not absolutely irreducible, hence not adequate (E767).
- (5) for E/Q non-CM with surjective mod l image, l ≥ 7, F = F' = Q: ζ_l ∉ Q̄^{ker ad r̄}, so Sym^m r̄ satisfies the enormous Taylor–Wiles image conditions for l > 2m + 3.

No atlas stage plans these; part (ii) of the reductive node (independence of the Ĝ-semisimplified reduction for general Ĝ) rests on them. The GL_n case is closed inside R01.1 without them. Needed by: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/reductive-integral-models`.
- **Larsen's lemma on hyperspecial points after a totally ramified extension.** M. Larsen, Maximality of Galois actions for compatible systems, Duke Math. J. 80 (1995), Lemma 2.4, as used in the proof of BHKT Theorem 4.8(ii): there are a totally ramified E′/E and a ρ(Γ)-stable point x ∈ B(DĜ, E) with i_{E,E′}(x) hyperspecial. Not planned by ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.2 as stated. Not needed for Ĝ = GL_n. Needed by: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/reductive-integral-models`.
- **Functional equation of Artin L-functions of number fields with global constants.** Deligne's existence proof (Théorème 4.1 via Lemmes 4.12–4.16) uses, for a Galois extension of number fields and a finite-image complex representation V of Gal(K̄/K) twisted by an idele class quasi-character χ, the meromorphic continuation of L(V, χ) = ∏_v L(V_v ⊗ χ_v), the functional equation L(V, χ) = ε(V, χ)L(V^*, ω_1χ^{-1}) with ε(V, χ) of the form A·e^{Bs}, inductivity ε(Ind V_L, χ) = ε(V_L, χ ∘ N_{L/K}) and additivity (Deligne 3.12 (A)–(D), proved from Brauer induction and Hecke's functional equation), together with idele class characters of prescribed local conductors (Lemme 4.14) and globalisation of local Galois extensions at a non-split place (Lemme 4.13). No atlas stage owns Artin L-functions of number fields (FunctionFieldArithmetic FA.5 is for function fields; AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors AL.1 stops at Hecke characters). Proposed owner: an Artin L-function stage of AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors after AL.1. Needed by: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/local-epsilon-factor`.
- **Local constants outside finite extensions of Q_p.** Deligne's Théorème 4.1 also covers archimedean local fields (W_R, W_C, Deligne 2.2.5 and Lemme 4.4) and local fields of characteristic p. The archimedean Weil groups have no owner in the atlas (Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory layer 9 is nonarchimedean; LanglandsParameterStacks LP0 is nonarchimedean), and the equal-characteristic reciprocity isomorphism is excluded from ClassFieldTheory layer 9. FSY's global ε-factor uses the archimedean factor ε_k(∞, s); this node supplies only the finite places. Needed by: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/local-epsilon-factor`.
- **Ramification filtration over a perfect infinite residue field.** LocalFieldsRamification layer 3 supplies lower and upper numbering, Herbrand's quotient theorem and Hasse–Arf only for IsNonarchimedeanLocalField (finite residue field); AlgebraicCurves layer 8 states explicitly that arbitrary-residue-field completions do not claim that supplier. Missing: the same three results for finite Galois extensions of a complete discretely valued field with perfect (e.g. algebraically closed) residue field (Serre, Local Fields IV–V), which tier (P) of R01.3 — F̄_q((t)) and the completion of K^ur, as requested by FiniteFieldsAndCharacterSums FF.2 — needs. Tier (F) is closed without it; the Artin–Schreier computation itself uses only the lower filtration. Natural owner: a 'Local fields and ramification, Part II' roadmap (see restructure). Needed by: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.3/breaks-and-swan-conductor`, `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.3/hasse-arf-integrality`, `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.3/additivity-twist-and-unramified-invariance`, `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.3/artin-schreier-swan-conductor`.
- **Saito's conductor–discriminant theorem and its inputs.** No roadmap in the atlas plans: (1) ℓ-adic étale cohomology H^i(X_K̄, Q_ℓ), H^i(X_k̄, Q_ℓ) of the fibres of a proper regular curve X over a complete DVR together with the specialisation identity dim H¹(X_k̄) = dim H¹(X_K̄)^{I_K} for the minimal regular model of an elliptic curve (LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles LPV.0 is downstream of ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations and cannot be used); (2) Deligne's discriminant Δ_{X/S} of a regular relative curve (via the Mumford isomorphism) and its identification with the minimal Weierstrass discriminant in genus one; (3) Saito's theorem −Art(X/S) = ord Δ_{X/S} (Duke Math. J. 57 (1988), Theorem 1 and Cor. 2; not freely available, statement read in Liu 1994). Consequence: R01.3/ogg-formula is closed for residue characteristic p ≥ 5 by the direct case check and open for p ∈ {2, 3}; EllipticCurveModularity R29.4's exact-conductor comparison at 2 and 3 waits on this gap. Proposed owner: a stage of NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties or a new arithmetic-surfaces stage upstream of R01.3 that owns étale cohomology of relative curves over a DVR and Deligne's discriminant. Needed by: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.3/saito-conductor-discriminant`, `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.3/ogg-formula`.
- **One-dimensional comparison with class field theory.** ClassFieldTheory layer 7 defines characterConductorExp through unit filtrations; the identity artinMap(U_K^n) ↔ G_K^n (Serre, Local Fields XV §2) that equates it with the Artin conductor of this layer is not stated by any layer; requested from ClassFieldTheory layer 7. The local and global theorems of R01.3 do not need it; only the translation of 𝔣(ψ) into the conductor of a Hecke character does. Needed by: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.3/artin-conductor-with-its-wild-part`, `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.3/induction-formula-for-conductors`.
- **Dickinson 2001, Lemma 42 (H¹(SL_2(F_{2^r}), M_2(F)) = 0, r ≥ 2) not read.** Statement (c) is quoted from Dickinson, On the modularity of certain 2-adic Galois representations, Duke Math. J. 109 (2001), through KW II Lemma 4.3(5)(i). The paper was not obtained; the proof sketch reduces it to Ext¹(V, V) = 0 for the natural SL_2(F_0)-module, which still needs a source or a computation. Needed by: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/characteristic-two-residual-image-facts`.
- **Automorphisms of PSL_2(F_q) and PGL_2(F_q) (Dieudonné / Steinberg) not read in their own source.** Statement (c) (Aut = PΓL_2) is quoted from NT26, CG20 and BCGNT, which cite Dieudonné, La géométrie des groupes classiques, Ch. IV §6, and Steinberg; those sources were not read and the normaliser of PSL_2(F_q) in Sym(q + 1) is not proved here. Needed by: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/normal-subgroups-and-automorphisms-of-psl2-pgl2`.
- **Nekovář's semisimplicity criterion [Nek18, Proposition 3.10].** BCGP25 Proposition 4.11.1 is a special case of Nekovář, Eichler–Shimura relations and semisimplicity of étale cohomology of quaternionic Shimura varieties, Ann. Sci. ÉNS 51 (2018), Prop. 3.10 (minuscule case (3)); the GL_2 version (Blasius–Rogawski) is used in 4.11.2. The paper is not on arXiv and was not read; no roadmap plans it. Needed by: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.5/gsp4-semisimplicity-criteria`.
- **Analytic subsets of compact ℓ-adic Lie groups with empty interior are Haar-null.** Serre 1981 §6.4 (p. 168, citing Bourbaki, Variétés §10.1.2) uses that a closed analytic subset with empty interior of a compact ℓ-adic Lie group has Haar measure 0. The polynomial case on open subgroups of GL_n(ℤ_ℓ) is proved in the node; the general analytic case (needed for images such as GSp_4(ℤ_ℓ) when the condition is not polynomial on GL_n-coordinates, and for Zariski-closed images) has no owner and no library support. Needed by: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.5/haar-measure-chebotarev`.
- **Integral, ℓ-independent characteristic polynomial of an endomorphism on V_ℓA (dimension > 1).** Milne AV Prop. 10.20 (P_α = det(X − V_ℓα), integer coefficients, independent of ℓ) is planned as AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A6/characteristic-polynomial-on-tate-module, whose own prerequisites (A6 degree theory, A3, A4) do not involve R01.6. But the stage AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A6 requires ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6 (only through A6/tate-module-of-a-weil-restriction), so citing it would close a stage cycle. The elliptic case (g = 1) is proved in this layer without A6. Closed by restructure proposal R01.6-RS1. Needed by: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6/good-reduction-frobenius-polynomial`, `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6/local-euler-factor-of-an-abelian-variety`, `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6/serre-independence-and-connectedness`.
- **Freeness of V_ℓA over E ⊗ Q_ℓ for a subfield E ⊆ End⁰(A), and E-characteristic polynomials.** Milne AV Prop. 10.23 (V_ℓA free of rank 2g/[E:Q] over E ⊗ Q_ℓ; trace and norm formulas) is AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A6/trace-and-degree-on-a-subfield, downstream for the same reason as the previous gap. Closed by R01.6-RS1. Needed by: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6/tate-module-with-endomorphism-coefficients`.
- **Weierstrass curves as abelian varieties of dimension one.** No packet or Tau Ceti layer located that identifies the projective closure of an elliptic Weierstrass curve W/K with a Tau Ceti AbelianVariety of dimension 1 whose L-points are W⁄L.Point functorially in L. Elliptic statements of this layer avoid it (they use Tau Ceti EllipticCurves directly); only the transfer of abelian-variety statements (isogeny cokernels, local Euler factors) to Weierstrass curves needs it. Natural owner: Tau Ceti JacobianChallenge layer E or AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A1. Needed by: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6/elliptic-tate-module-comparison`.
- **Mumford–Tate containment of the ℓ-adic images (Richard–Yafaev Theorem 4.9, third clause).** Deligne's theorem that Hodge cycles on abelian varieties are absolutely Hodge, the Galois finiteness on absolute Hodge classes (Deligne–Milne–Ogus–Shih I, Prop. 2.9) and the Mumford–Tate group as stabiliser of Hodge tensors (I.3.4) are owned by ShimuraData D1 and AutomorphicBundles B1, which consume this stage (through NeronModels R11.5, ShimuraVarieties V5 and B1), so citing them here closes a stage cycle. The clause U ⊆ M(Ẑ) is therefore not stated in R01.6; restructure proposal R01.6-RS3 plans it at a stage downstream of both owners. Needed by: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6/serre-independence-and-connectedness`.
- **Serre's independence and connectedness theorems: original proofs not read; possibly downstream inputs.** Richard–Yafaev cite Serre, Œuvres IV nos. 133, 135, 136, Serre, Comment. Math. Helv. 88 (2013) §3.1, and Larsen–Pink, Invent. Math. 107 (1992) 6.14; none was read in this pass (not freely located in time). If their proofs for abelian varieties use Faltings' semisimplicity (FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems R28.4) or Grothendieck's semistable reduction (NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties R11.3), both of which consume R01.6, parts (1)–(2) must move downstream (restructure R01.6-RS2). Needed by: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6/serre-independence-and-connectedness`.
- **Serre's complement to the specialization of Galois images (Noot Proposition 1.3).** For each ℓ there is a closed point σ with ρ_{X_η,ℓ}(G_K) = ρ_{X_σ,ℓ}(Gal(F̄/F(σ))). Its proof uses Hilbert irreducibility for compact ℓ-adic Lie quotients (Serre, Lectures on the Mordell–Weil theorem, 10.6), owned by InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups IG.2, which depends on this stage (IG.2 ← IG.1 ← IG.0 ← SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.2 … ← NeronModels R11.3 ← R01.6). Restructure proposal R01.6-RS4 plans the complement at IG.2. Needed by: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6/noot-specialization`.
- **Borel, Linear Algebraic Groups, Ch. I §§1–2 facts on Zariski closures not read in the source.** NT26 cites [Bor91, Ch. I §2.1(f), §2.4; Ch. II §7.1]. Borel was not fetched; the facts are planned in G7/zariski-closure-and-monodromy-groups with standard proofs, and the review should check them against Borel. Needed by: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/zariski-closure-and-monodromy-groups`.
- **Gan–Takeda Lemma 6.1 not read.** BCGP21 proves Lemma 2.1.3 by citing the proof of Gan–Takeda (Ann. of Math. 173 (2011)) Lemma 6.1, not fetched here; the proof sketch given is the standard isotypic-component argument. Needed by: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/gsp4-semisimple-determined-by-gl4`.
- **Guralnick–Herzig–Taylor–Thorne adequacy theorem (appendix Theorem 9 / Theorem A.9).** The proof uses Proposition 7 of the appendix, which rests on the classification of finite simple groups (Tau Ceti CFSGStatement states the classification but no layer derives the algebraic-group structure of finite linear groups generated by p-elements in small dimension), and Guralnick's 1999 theorem that small modules have no self-extensions (Ext¹ vanishing for dim W_i + dim W_j ≤ p − 2). Neither input is planned by any roadmap. Needed by: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/adequacy-criteria`, `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/gsp4-big-image-verification`, `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/taylor-wiles-image-lemmas`, `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/adequacy-of-symmetric-powers`.
- **Ext¹ computations for SL₂(F_{p^r}) behind GHT17 Corollary 9.4.** Corollary 9.4 uses Andersen–Jørgensen–Landrock's Ext¹ computations for SL₂(p^r) (r > 1), [GHT, Cor. 1.4] for r = 1, H²(SL₂(F_q), k) = 0 for q ∉ {4, 9}, and tilting-module computations for q = 4, 9. No library or roadmap plans the modular representation theory of SL₂(F_q). Needed by: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/adequacy-criteria`, `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/adequacy-of-symmetric-powers`.
- **H¹(SL₂(F_q), Sym^{2i}) = 0 for 2i < p − 3 (Cline–Parshall–Scott Lemma 2.7(c)).** Clozel–Harris–Taylor's proof of Corollary 2.5.4 cites Cline–Parshall–Scott (1975), Lemma 2.7(c), for H¹(U, Sym^{2i})^B = 0; that paper was not obtained in this job, and the printed hypothesis (l > n + 1) is too weak. Darmon–Diamond–Taylor's method (restriction to the Borel and a B-stable filtration) proves the case 2i = 2; the general case needs the weight computation of H¹(U, ·)^B. An exact source statement is still to be read; this job verified the prime-field cases p = 5, 7, 11 by computation (H¹(SL₂(F_p), Sym^a) ≠ 0 only for a = p − 3). Needed by: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/h1-of-sl2-with-adjoint-coefficients`, `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/enormous-symmetric-powers`.
- **Finite group computations of Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni §7.5.** H¹(Sp₄(F_p), 𝔰𝔭₄) = 0 for p = 3, 5, 7 (Lemma 7.5.15), the list of the 11 enormous classes among the 162 conjugacy classes of subgroups of Sp₄(F_3) (§7.5.20) and Lemma 7.5.21(1), (2), (3b), (4) are Magma computations; a formal treatment needs certified enumerations of these finite groups and their cohomology. Needed by: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/gsp4-big-image-verification`.
- **Thorne 2024, Lemma 7.3 (adequacy of symmetric powers of large SL₂ images).** Newton–Thorne quote Thorne, A p-adic approach to the existence of level-raising congruences (Proc. LMS 128, 2024), Lemma 7.3, which was not read; the node gives a proof route through GHT17 Corollary 9.4, which itself rests on the gap above. Needed by: `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7/adequacy-of-symmetric-powers`.

## Mistakes found in the sources

- **ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations/E101** (gap, cg20, §6.3, proof of Theorem 6.13, p. 843 (Duke published version); arXiv:1907.08691v1 has the same text in the proof of Theorem 6.13). Printed: “"The eigenform f_i has an associated Galois representation r_{f_i} : G_Q → GSp4(O_{K′_i}) for some finite extension K′_i/K_i, by Proposition 6.8." Proposition 6.8 (p. 839) gives only "r_f : G_Q → GSp4(K′)" ("The usual Baire category argument implies that r_f can be defined over a finite extension of K. Thus in all cases, we may take r_f : G_Q → GSp4(K′).")”. Correction: Add: since r̄ is absolutely irreducible, the G_Q-stable O_{K′}-lattices in r_f form a single homothety class; the similitude character is O_{K′}^×-valued by compactness; the dual lattice for the symplectic form is stable, hence a homothetic translate, so after rescaling the lattice (and the form by ϖ if needed) the form is perfect on it and has a symplectic basis, giving r_f : G_Q → GSp4(O_{K′}). Reason: Proposition 6.8 is a field-valued statement; the integral GSp4(O) model is an additional step (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/self-dual-lattice-for-absolutely-irreducible-residual). It holds under the standing absolute irreducibility of r̄, so the theorem is unaffected. Affects: the proof. Known: new (noted as 'used silently' in the extraction item PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20/ext-galois-rep-finite-extension-and-integral-model, which is not an erratum).
- **ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations/E201** (misprint, deligne73-constantes, 8.12, displayed formula after (8.12.4), Del-72, printed p. 572 (IAS typescript scan of LNM 349)). Printed: “Pour (ρ'N') définis par une représentation λ-adique ρ sur V, on a V^I = V^{ρ(I)}, Z(V,t) = det(1-Ft, V^{ρ(I)})”. Correction: Z(V,t) = det(1 − Ft^d, V^{ρ(I)})^{-1}, as in (8.12.2) and (3.5.1) Reason: (8.12.2) four lines above defines Z(V,t) = det(1 − Ft^d, V^I)^{-1}, and (3.5.1) has the same form; the λ-adic restatement substitutes V^I = V^{ρ(I)} and must keep the exponent −1 and t^d. Read on a zoomed rendering of the page. Affects: nothing. Known: new.
- **ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations/E202** (misprint, deligne73-constantes, proof of Lemme 8.4.3, Del-69, printed p. 569). Printed: “pour toute représentation (ρ',N') de 'W(K̄/K) sur un corps E, et tout a ∈ E, (ρ',N') ⥲ (ρ',a N')”. Correction: for every a ∈ E^× (a ≠ 0) Reason: For a = 0 and N' ≠ 0 the pairs (ρ', N') and (ρ', 0) are not isomorphic (an isomorphism conjugates N' to 0). The proof constructs A with λ(q^{-n}α) = aλ(α), which needs a invertible. Affects: nothing. Known: new (already noted in the reviewed decomposition's hypotheses).
- **ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations/E301** (misprint, ulmer16, Tate, Number theoretic background (Corvallis 1979), (4.2.4), as quoted by Ulmer 2016 §2, PDF p. 5). Printed: “a(ρ_ℓ) = dim V^{ss} − dim V_ℓ + a(ρ^{ss}) (Tate 4.2.4 as reported by Ulmer: 'missing the exponent IF on Vℓ')”. Correction: a(ρ_ℓ) = dim V^{ss, I_F} − dim V_ℓ^{I_F} + a(ρ^{ss}): the dimensions are of inertia invariants. Reason: For ρ_ℓ unramified the printed form gives a(ρ_ℓ) = 0 only because dim V^{ss} = dim V_ℓ; for the Steinberg representation the corrected form gives 2 − 1 + 0 = 1, the printed one 0. Affects: a stated result. Known: Ulmer, Conductors of ℓ-adic representations, Proc. AMS 144 (2016), §2 (arXiv:1307.4525v4).
- **ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations/E401** (gap, serre87-duke, 3.3, bracketed remark after condition (c), printed p. 198 (Duke Math. J. 54 (1987)); Collège de France PDF, page image checked). Printed: “Si alors ρ se décomposait sur F̄_p en somme directe de deux représentations de dimension 1, cette décomposition ne pourrait être que celle donnée par les vecteurs propres de ρ(c), donc serait rationnelle sur F_p, ce qui contredirait (b').”. Correction: Also treat the case where ρ ⊗ F̄_p is reducible but not a direct sum: its unique stable line is stable under ρ(c), hence is one of the two eigenlines of ρ(c), which are F_p-rational; so ρ is reducible over F_p, contradicting (b′). Equivalently: every ρ(G_ℚ)-stable line of F̄_p² is an eigenline of ρ(c). Reason: Irreducible over F_p but not absolutely irreducible only says that F̄_p² has a stable line; the remark argues only from a decomposition into a direct sum of two lines. A reducible indecomposable ρ ⊗ F̄_p (one stable line) is not covered by the sentence, although the same eigenline argument closes it. Affects: nothing. Known: new as a recorded issue; the omission is noted in the statement text of the reviewed decomposition node ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/bad-dihedral-representations-and-the-oddness-criterion (data/decompositions/ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations.json), not as a sourceIssue.
- **ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations/E501** (error, chenevier-determinants, Definition 2.19, p. 33, arXiv:0809.0415v2). Printed: “We say that D is split if it is the determinant of a representation R −→ Md (k). Equivalenty, D is split if and only if R/ ker(D) is a finite product of matrix algebras over k.”. Correction: The two conditions are not equivalent in general: R/ker(D) a product of matrix algebras over k implies D is the determinant of a k-representation, but not conversely. They agree when D is absolutely irreducible or multiplicity free (the cases used in the paper). In general D is the determinant of a k-representation iff, in Theorem 2.16, the index of S_i divides m_i for all i (with k_i/k separable). Reason: k = ℝ, R = ℝ[Q_8], D = det of the 4-dimensional real representation of Q_8 on ℍ by left multiplication. D is the determinant of R → End_ℝ(ℍ) ≅ M_4(ℝ), but R/ker(D) ≅ ℍ, a division algebra, not a product of matrix algebras over ℝ (D = Nrd² on the ℍ factor, m = 2, index 2). Affects: nothing. Known: new.
- **ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations/E502** (misprint, bcgp25, Proposition 4.11.2, proof, p. 111, arXiv:2502.20645v1). Printed: “(the eigenvalues in either case take the form 1, −1, λ, −λ for some λ)”. Correction: 1, −1, λ, λ^{-1} for an element of the determinant −1 component of O_4. Reason: Orthogonal eigenvalues pair reciprocally; det(1, −1, λ, −λ) = λ², not −1 in general. The minimal-polynomial argument goes through with the corrected list. Affects: the proof. Known: PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-PILLONI-25/E020 (atlas extraction, review verdict confirmed); no published correction.
- **ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations/E701** (error, cg20, §4, second paragraph after the display of r̄|_{G_p}, published p. 813; arXiv:1907.08691v1 §4, p. 10). Printed: “admits a decomposition ad(r) = ad0 (r) ⊕ ν, where ν is the similitude character of r.”. Correction: For p > 2, ad(r̄) = ad⁰(r̄) ⊕ k with k = k·I_4 the centre of gsp_4 and trivial Galois action. Reason: For p > 2, gsp_4 = sp_4 ⊕ k·I and X − (c/2)I ∈ sp_4 when XᵗJ + JX = cJ; Ad(g) fixes scalars, and the quotient gsp_4/sp_4 is trivial because ν(g) cancels. For odd r̄, ν(r̄(c)) = −1, so ν ∘ r̄ is nontrivial and the printed decomposition is false. Nothing downstream uses the one-dimensional summand. Carried from PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20/E18 (review: confirmed). Affects: nothing. Known: PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20/E18 (atlas extraction, confirmed by REV-PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20).
- **ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations/E702** (error, cg18, §8.4 "The invariant l_0", published p. 406; arXiv v2 §8.4 pp. 80–81). Printed: “and assume that the action of GFv is odd for each v|∞. Explicitly, this is the trivial condition for complex places, and for real places v|∞ says that the action of complex conjugation cv ∈ GFv satisfies Trace(cv ) ∈ {−1, 0, 1}.”. Correction: Odd at a real place means the ±1-eigenspaces of c_v have dimensions differing by at most one; this agrees with Trace(c_v) ∈ {−1, 0, 1} in characteristic 0 and in characteristic ℓ exactly when ℓ > n + 1 (n even) or ℓ > n (n odd). Reason: Trace(c_v) = a − b in the field, where a, b are the eigenspace dimensions; dim H^0(⟨c_v⟩, ad⁰ V) = a^2 + b^2 − 1. Over F_3 with n = 2 and c acting trivially the trace is 2 = −1 but dim H^0 = 3, not 1. No numbered statement is affected (Prop. 8.5(4) only needs the inequality). Carried from PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18/E164 (review: confirmed). Affects: a stated result. Known: PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18/E164 (atlas extraction, confirmed by REV-PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18).
- **ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations/E703** (error, bcgp21, Lemma 2.1.3 and proof, §2.1.2 (arXiv v3 p. 17; publ. p. 171)). Printed: “a semisimple representation Γ → GSp4 (L) is determined up to conjugacy by the”. Correction: Add char L ≠ 2. Reason: In characteristic 2, Γ = SL_2(F_2), V = W ⊗ L^2 with forms B_W ⊗ (0 1; 1 0) and B_W ⊗ I gives two Sp_4-valued representations, GL_4-conjugate with equal similitude, not GSp_4-conjugate. All uses in BCGP21 have odd residual characteristic. Carried from PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-PILLONI-21/E6 (review: confirmed). Affects: a stated result. Known: PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-PILLONI-21/E6.
- **ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations/E704** (misprint, nt26, Proof of Lemma 2.2, arXiv v2 p. 10). Printed: “in GL2 × GL2 contains the derived group of the Zariski closure of ρ(GF ) × ρ′ (GF )”. Correction: Read (ρ × ρ′)(G_{F(ζ_{p^∞})}) and (ρ × ρ′)(G_F), the images of the product map. Reason: With products of the separate images the Goursat argument before it would be pointless; with the images of ρ × ρ′ the argument is correct. Carried from PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-26/E13 (review: confirmed). Affects: nothing. Known: PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-26/E13.

- **ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations/E754** (error, blgg13-serre-weights, Proposition A.2.1 and its proof, Point 5 and Figure 1, arXiv v1 pp. 30–34). Printed: “We have l = 5, and the image of G in PGL2 (F5 ) is conjugate to PGL2 (F5 ) or PSL2 (F5 ). … The case where Ḡ is PGL2 (F5 ) will then also have H 1 (G, gln (Fl )) 6= (0) by [CPS75, 2.3 (g)], and again G will fail to be adequate.”. Correction: For l = 5 only the projective image PSL₂(F_5) is excluded: if the image of G in PGL₂(F̄_5) is conjugate to PGL₂(F_5), then G is adequate. Reason: By Lemmas A.1.3–A.1.4 of the same appendix, G is adequate iff GL₂(F_5) is. GL₂(F_5) has no quotient of order 5, 5 ∤ 2, its semisimple elements span M₂(F_5), and H¹(GL₂(F_5), gl₂) = H¹(GL₂(F_5), F_5) ⊕ H¹(GL₂(F_5), sl₂) = 0: the first because the abelianisation is F_5^× of order 4; the second by a direct cocycle computation over the Cayley graph of GL₂(F_5) (a direct linear-algebra computation by this job), which gives dim H¹(GL₂(F_5), sl₂ ⊗ det^j) = 0, 0, 1, 0 for j = 0, 1, 2, 3, and dim H¹ = 1 for SL₂(F_5) and for {g : det g = ±1}. So the class in H¹(SL₂(F_5), sl₂) is moved by the outer action of diag(2,1) (it lives in sl₂ ⊗ det²), and inflation–restriction gives H¹(GL₂(F_5), sl₂) = H¹(SL₂(F_5), sl₂)^{GL₂/SL₂} = 0. This agrees with the Andersen–Jørgensen–Landrock description of Ext¹_{GL₂(F_p)}(1, Sym^{p−3} ⊗ det^b) (nonzero only for b ≡ 1 mod p − 1, while sl₂ = Sym² ⊗ det⁻¹), and with Gee–Newton Lemma 3.2.3. Affects: a stated result. Known: new (Gee–Newton, Patching and the completed homology of locally symmetric spaces, Lemma 3.2.3 states the correct list without comment, citing this proposition).

Reason: BLGG13 Proposition A.2.1 lists the projective image PGL₂(F_5) among the non-adequate cases, so it does not yield the second statement of Lemma 3.2.3, which excludes only PSL₂(F_p) for p = 3, 5. The statement of Lemma 3.2.3 is correct (see E754). Affects: the proof. Known: new.

So (E3) holds. Since #Sp₄(F_3) = 51840 = 2⁷·3⁴·5, the enormous class of order 128 in §7.5.20 is this Sylow subgroup. The error affects nothing: the remark only motivates the p = 3 hypothesis. ## Structural proposals

- **rescope** (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations): gap 1; consumers FiniteFieldsAndCharacterSums FF.2 and PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology RD.6 need F̄_q((t)) Proposal: LocalFieldsRamification, Part II: ramification filtrations, Herbrand's theorem and Hasse–Arf for complete discretely valued fields with perfect (possibly infinite) residue field, and the absolute upper filtration G_K^u
- **rescope** (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli, ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations): AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A6/tate-module-of-a-weil-restriction cites R01.6 for the Tate module and G7 for induction. The first makes A6 a consumer of R01.6, so R01.6 cannot cite A6/characteristic-polynomial-on-tate-module or A6/trace-and-degree-on-a-subfield (two gaps of this layer). The second is misrouted: continuous induction is R01.1/continuous-induction; and the edge G7 → A6 it creates, together with the PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2 → G7 edge that the Patrikis lifting theorem requires (route of PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-PILLONI-21), closes the stage cycle G7 → A6 → FunctionFieldArithmetic FA.5 → DeligneWeightsAndPurity DWP.4 → … → PadicHodgeTheory R06.2 → G7. Proposal: [R01.6-RS1] Re-point AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A6/tate-module-of-a-weil-restriction from ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6 to AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A4 (the étale Tate local system over Spec K is a continuous G_K-module) plus ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/continuous-induction, or move that node to a stage downstream of R01.6. This removes the only stage edge R01.6 → A6 (checked on data/atlas.json: A6 is downstream of R01.6 only through that direct edge), after which R01.6 may require A6 and the two A6 gaps of this layer close by citation.
- **rescope** (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations): See proposal. Proposal: [R01.6-RS2] If Serre's independence/connectedness proofs need Faltings' semisimplicity or semistable reduction, move parts (1)–(2) of R01.6/serre-independence-and-connectedness to a stage downstream of FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems R28.4 and NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties R11.3 (as REV-PAPER-MASSER-ZANNIER-20 routed Serre's open image), keeping the definitions and Deligne's part (3) here.
- **rescope** (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations, AutomorphicBundles, ShimuraData): See proposal. Proposal: [R01.6-RS3] Plan the Mumford–Tate containment of Richard–Yafaev Theorem 4.9 (third clause: after a finite extension the adelic image of an abelian variety over a number field lies in M(Ẑ)) at a stage downstream of ShimuraData D1 and AutomorphicBundles B1, importing R01.6/serre-independence-and-connectedness and R01.6/tate-module-of-an-abelian-variety.
- **rescope** (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations, InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups): See proposal. Proposal: [R01.6-RS4] Plan Serre's complement to the specialization of Galois images (Noot Prop. 1.3: for each ℓ a closed point with equal ℓ-adic image) at InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups IG.2, which owns Hilbert irreducibility and already depends on R01.6; it imports R01.6/noot-specialization.
